question.en: Which of the following options most accurately expresses the meaning of the idiom "to cook the books"? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 17/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: To meticulously analyse extensive literature and academic publications to extract relevant data for a thesis.

2.en: To draft innovative, highly creative recipes for a commercial restaurant chain to maximise culinary efficiency.

3.en: To systematically preserve ancient, deteriorating manuscripts through advanced chemical restoration techniques.

4.en: To intentionally falsify corporate accounting records or balance sheets to deceive auditors and investors.

solution.en:
To cook the books is an idiom that means to manipulate, alter, or falsify accounting records and financial data fraudulently.
Options (a), (b), and (c) are literal or irrelevant distractors.
Vocab Meanings:
• To cook the books: To falsify accounts or records (हिसाब-किताब में हेराफेरी करना / खातों में गड़बड़ी करना)

question.en: Which of the following options most accurately expresses the meaning of the idiom "A Pyrrhic victory"? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 17/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: A successful outcome achieved at such a ruinous and devastating cost to the victor that it is tantamount to a strategic defeat.

2.en: A triumphant milestone achieved through a collaborative group effort, yielding equitable dividends for each participating member.

3.en: A decisive military conquest that permanently alters the geopolitical landscape by completely annihilating an enemy state.

4.en: A monumental triumph secured via the collective struggle of a populace, but whose structural benefits enrich only the elite few while marginalising the masses.

solution.en:
A Pyrrhic victory refers to a victory won at such enormous devastation or prohibitive cost that it practically amounts to a defeat.
Options (b), (c), and (d) do not describe the self-destructive nature of the victory.
Vocab Meanings:
• A Pyrrhic victory: A victory won at too great a cost (बहुत भारी कीमत चुकाकर मिली जीत / हार जैसी जीत)

question.en:
Choose the correct idiom for the word highlighted in bold.
The hospital is within a stone's throw of the railway station. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Meaning: The idiom within a stone's throw means a very short distance away or very close.
Example sentence: We live within a stone's throw of the city center.
Vocab Meanings:
• Within a stone's throw: Very close (बहुत नज़दीक / कुछ ही दूरी पर)

question.en: What does the idiom "bark up the wrong tree" mean? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: To pursue the wrong course of action

2.en: To take responsibility for a mistake

solution.en:
Meaning: Bark up the wrong tree means to pursue a mistaken line of thought or follow a completely wrong course of action.
Example sentence: If you expect him to lend you money, you are barking up the wrong tree.
Vocab Meanings:
• Bark up the wrong tree: To follow the wrong course or blame the wrong person (गलत दिशा में प्रयास करना / गलत व्यक्ति पर आरोप लगाना)

question.en: Identify the option in which the underlined idiom has been used incorrectly. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 19/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: When her uncle offered to pay her full university tuition, Sofia <u>looked a gift horse in the mouth</u> by immediately thanking him and accepting the generous check.

2.en: The newly appointed regional manager began <u>throwing his weight around</u> during his first week by demanding a larger corner office and forcing staff to log their bathroom breaks.

3.en: The network security team routinely <u>cried wolf</u> by triggering high-priority alarms for minor software updates, leaving the staff unwary when a cyberattack actually occurred.

4.en: The pioneering neuroscientist managed to <u>blaze a trail</u> in medical research by developing the world's first non-invasive neural interface for paralysed patients.

solution.en:
Meaning: Look a gift horse in the mouth means to find fault with or be ungrateful for something that has been received as a gift or favor.
Usage: Since Sofia was grateful and readily accepted the offer, the idiom is used contradictorily and incorrectly in option (a).
Vocab Meanings:
• Look a gift horse in the mouth: To find fault with a gift (उपहार में मिली चीज़ में दोष निकालना)
• Throw one's weight around: To use one's power in an unpleasant way (रौब जमाना)
• Cry wolf: To raise false alarms (झूठा खतरा बताना)
• Blaze a trail: To be the first to do something new (नई राह दिखाना / पथ-प्रदर्शक बनना)

question.en: Identify the option in which the underlined idiom has been used incorrectly. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 19/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: After the startup acquired its primary competitor's patents and secured exclusive distribution rights, the board knew they <u>held all the aces</u> in the upcoming acquisition negotiations.

2.en: Recognising that the younger team members needed leadership experience, the senior consultant decided to <u>take a back seat</u> during the project, offering guidance only when explicitly asked.

3.en: The tyrannical creative director loved to <u>lord it over</u> his junior designers, frequently mocking their portfolios in front of the entire office to assert his dominance.

4.en: Intending to reward the ambitious young politician for his absolute loyalty, the party chairman <u>clipped his wings</u> by promoting him to the prestigious position of committee chair.

solution.en:
Meaning: Clip someone's wings means to restrict someone's freedom, power, or ambitions.
Usage: Promoting someone to a prestigious leadership position empowers rather than restricts them, making the idiom incorrect in option (d).
Vocab Meanings:
• Hold all the aces: To have all the advantages (पूरी तरह लाभ की स्थिति में होना)
• Take a back seat: To take a less active role (पीछे हट जाना / कम सक्रिय भूमिका लेना)
• Lord it over: To act in a superior, bossy way (किसी पर रौब जमाना)
• Clip someone's wings: To limit someone's freedom or power (किसी की स्वतंत्रता या शक्ति सीमित करना)

question.en: What does the idiom "straw in the wind" mean? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 21/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: A small sign that suggests what might happen in the future

3.en: A situation where things are chaotic and uncontrollable

solution.en:
Meaning: Straw in the wind refers to a small indicator or hint of what might happen or how things might develop in the future.
Example: The slight drop in quarterly unemployment figures is a straw in the wind for economic recovery.
Vocab Meanings:
• Straw in the wind: A small sign of what may happen (भविष्य का छोटा सा संकेत / आने वाली घटना का आभास)

question.en:
Choose the correct option:
Richard offered to be my guide through Paris, but since he'd never been there before either, it was a case of: [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 21/09/26 Shift 1]

4.en: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder

solution.en:
Meaning: The blind leading the blind describes a situation where an unqualified, uninformed, or inexperienced person is attempting to guide another person.
Other options:
• Seeing is believing: Only physical or concrete evidence is convincing.
• A sight for sore eyes: A person or thing that is welcomed or pleasing to see.
• Beauty is in the eye of the beholder: Different people have different standards of beauty.
Vocab Meanings:
• The blind leading the blind: An ignorant person guiding another ignorant person (अंधे को अंधा राह दिखाए / अनजान का अनजान को मार्गदर्शन)
• Seeing is believing: You believe only what you see yourself (आँखों देखी पर ही विश्वास)
• A sight for sore eyes: A person or thing you are glad to see (मन को भाने वाला दृश्य / स्वागत योग्य व्यक्ति)
• Beauty is in the eye of the beholder: What is beautiful differs from person to person (सुंदरता देखने वाले की नज़र में होती है)

question.en:
Read the following sentence and ascertain whether the underlined idiom is used correctly. If the usage is incorrect, choose the correct option (A/B/C) to suitably replace it. If the usage is correct, choose Option D: "No correction required."
The evolutionary biologist expected his radical paper on genetic editing to spark a civil debate, but upon publication, he was forced to rule the roost as peers from every major research institute unleashed a barrage of harsh critiques, public reprimands, and demands for its retraction. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 22/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Meaning: To run the gauntlet means to undergo a severe ordeal, trial, or endure a barrage of criticism and hostile attacks from all sides.
The biologist faced "a barrage of harsh critiques, public reprimands, and demands for retraction."
"To rule the roost" incorrectly means to dominate or be in control, making option (b) the proper replacement.
Vocab Meanings:
• Run the gauntlet: To face severe criticism or attack from many sides (चारों ओर से आलोचना या हमले का सामना करना)
• Rule the roost: To be in charge; to dominate (वर्चस्व रखना / हुक्म चलाना)
• Drop the ball: To make a mistake (गलती करना / चूक जाना)
• The die is cast: A decision has been made that cannot be changed (निर्णय हो चुका / पासा फेंका जा चुका)

question.en: Identify the option in which the idiom "to pass the buck" has been used correctly. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 22/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The biology department passed the buck by securing an external federal grant that covered all tuition costs for their incoming doctoral candidates.

2.en: The financial committee managed to pass the buck by converting the university's surplus cash reserves into low-yield, highly secure government bonds.

3.en: Instead of taking accountability for the data breach, the chief information officer sought to pass the buck by blaming a junior contractor's outdated software patch.

4.en: The provost advised the academic senate to pass the buck by designing a highly rigorous curriculum that challenged the undergraduate students.

solution.en:
Meaning: To pass the buck means to shift responsibility or blame for something onto someone else.
In option (c), the chief information officer avoids accountability by shifting the blame to a contractor, illustrating the precise and correct usage of the idiom.
In options a, b, and d, the phrase is misused in positive administrative or financial contexts.
Vocab Meanings:
• To pass the buck: To shift responsibility to someone else (ज़िम्मेदारी दूसरों पर डालना / दोष टालना)

question.en: What does the idiom "To hit the nail right on the head" mean? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 23/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: To say or do something exactly right

solution.en:
Meaning: "To hit the nail right on the head" means to describe exactly what is causing a situation or problem, or to say/do something with precise accuracy.
Example: Her analysis of the market slowdown hit the nail right on the head.
Vocab Meanings:
• To hit the nail right on the head: To say or do exactly the right thing (बिल्कुल सही बात कहना या करना)

question.en:
Read the sentence below and determine whether the underlined idiom has been used correctly. If it is incorrect, select the appropriate option (A/B/C) to replace it. If it is correct, choose Option D: 'No correction required.'
The rogue state signed multiple non-proliferation frameworks to disarm the international weapons inspectors, completely leading them up the garden path while secretly moving its uranium enrichment facilities deep underground. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 24/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Meaning: The idiom lead someone up the garden path means to deceive or deliberately mislead someone.
The context describes deliberately misleading weapons inspectors while secretly moving enrichment facilities underground.
Thus, the idiom is used completely accurately, so No correction required is correct.
Vocab Meanings:
• Lead someone up the garden path: To deceive or mislead someone (किसी को धोखा देना / गुमराह करना)
• Steal someone's thunder: To take credit for someone else's success (किसी का श्रेय छीन लेना)
• Dance to someone's tune: To do whatever someone wants (किसी के इशारों पर नाचना)
• Play into someone's hands: To act in a way that helps your opponent (अनजाने में दूसरे को लाभ पहुँचाना)

question.en: Select the option that shows the grammatically and lexically correct form of the idiom meaning "to speak with absolute candour, describing something completely truthfully and directly, even if it is unpleasant." [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 24/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: To call a spade a spade

2.en: To call a shovel a shovel

3.en: To call a clover a clover

4.en: To call a trowel a trowel

solution.en:
Meaning: The standard, fixed English idiom is to call a spade a spade, which means to speak directly and plainly about something, even if it is unpleasant.
The other forms replace 'spade' with other tools or plants and are incorrect variants.
Vocab Meanings:
• To call a spade a spade: To speak plainly and honestly (साफ़-साफ़ / खरी-खरी बात कहना)

question.en:
Choose the correct meaning of idiom:
Keep one's powder dry [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 25/09/26 Shift 1]

4.en: Remain prepared for action while avoiding premature moves

solution.en:
Meaning: The idiom keep one's powder dry originates from keeping gunpowder dry so it is ready to fire when needed, meaning to remain prepared for action or a possible emergency while avoiding acting prematurely.
Vocab Meanings:
• Keep one's powder dry: To stay ready for action while waiting (कार्रवाई के लिए तैयार रहना पर जल्दबाज़ी न करना)

question.en:
In the following sentence, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which gives the correct meaning of the underlined idiom or phrase.
Winning the lawsuit was a pyrrhic victory, as the legal fees exceeded the settlement amount. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 16/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A victory gained at too great a cost

4.en: A celebration after a long war

solution.en:
Meaning: A pyrrhic victory refers to a success or victory that is won at such a devastatingly high cost that it is tantamount to defeat.
Example: The army achieved a pyrrhic victory, losing nearly all its soldiers in the battle.
Vocab Meanings:
• Pyrrhic victory: A victory won at too great a cost (बहुत भारी कीमत चुकाकर मिली जीत / हार जैसी जीत)

question.en:
In the following sentence, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which gives the correct meaning of the underlined idiom or phrase.
The explorer knew that entering the uncharted jungle was a Hobson's choice between certain hunger or dangerous predators. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 16/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A wide variety of excellent choices

2.en: A very difficult decision between friends

3.en: A situation with no real choice at all

4.en: A choice made with great care and time

solution.en:
Meaning: A Hobson's choice is a choice of taking what is offered or taking nothing at all; a free choice in which only one thing is actually offered, resulting in no real alternative.
Example: The employee was offered a salary cut or termination, which was purely a Hobson's choice.
Vocab Meanings:
• Hobson's choice: A situation with no real choice at all (ऐसा विकल्प जिसमें कोई वास्तविक चुनाव न हो / मजबूरी का चुनाव)

question.en:
Choose the correct idiom for the word highlighted in bold.
The boundary between their properties has been a bone of contention for years, leading to several legal disputes. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 17/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A source of disagreement or dispute.

2.en: A symbol of unity and peace.

solution.en:
Meaning: A 'bone of contention' refers to an issue, subject, or problem over which there is continuing disagreement or dispute.
Example: The division of ancestral property remained a bone of contention between the two families.
Vocab Meanings:
• Bone of contention: A cause of dispute or disagreement (विवाद का कारण / झगड़े की जड़)

question.en:
In the following sentence, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which gives the correct meaning of the underlined idiom or phrase.
The poet felt like a fish out of water when he was forced to attend the noisy corporate gala. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 17/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A person who is very thirsty or tired

2.en: A person who loves swimming and diving

3.en: A person who is very quiet and shy

4.en: A person in a strange, awkward situation

solution.en:
Meaning: 'A fish out of water' denotes a person placed in an unfamiliar, uncomfortable, or awkward situation where they do not fit in.
Example: Lacking any background in technology, she felt like a fish out of water at the developer conference.
Vocab Meanings:
• Like a fish out of water: A person in an unfamiliar or uncomfortable situation (अनजान माहौल में असहज होना / बेगानी जगह पर परेशान)

question.en:
In the following sentence, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which gives the correct meaning of the underlined idiom or phrase.
Winning the national debate was the jewel in the crown of her academic career. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 18/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A very expensive piece of jewellery

2.en: The most valuable part of something

3.en: A small metal object worn on the head

4.en: A hidden secret that no one knows

solution.en:
Meaning: The idiom 'jewel in the crown' refers to the most valuable, successful, or attractive feature or achievement of something.
Example: The new research facility is considered the jewel in the crown of the university.
Vocab Meanings:
• Jewel in the crown: The most valuable or best part of something (किसी चीज़ का सबसे मूल्यवान भाग / सबसे बड़ी उपलब्धि)

question.en:
In the following sentence, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which gives the correct meaning of the underlined idiom or phrase.
The professor warned that the new policy would be the thin end of the wedge for academic freedom. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 18/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A very useful tool for fixing furniture

2.en: A small change leading to bigger problems

3.en: A clever way to save a lot of money

4.en: A sharp object used for cutting wood

solution.en:
Meaning: 'The thin end of the wedge' is an idiom meaning an initial, seemingly minor action or change that is likely to lead to much more serious, undesirable consequences.
Example: Permitting minor censorship could be the thin end of the wedge for the free press.
Vocab Meanings:
• The thin end of the wedge: A small change likely to lead to bigger problems (छोटा बदलाव जो आगे बड़ी समस्या बन जाए)

question.en:
In the following sentence, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which gives the correct meaning of the underlined idiom or phrase.
The young professor was known to burn the midnight oil to finish his research papers. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 19/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: To set fire to his laboratory at night

2.en: To use an expensive type of lamp

3.en: To waste time doing nothing important

4.en: To stay up very late at night working

solution.en:
Meaning: Burn the midnight oil means to work or study late into the night.
Example sentence: She burned the midnight oil studying for her final examinations.
Options (a), (b), and (c) are incorrect literal or unrelated interpretations.
Vocab Meanings:
• Burn the midnight oil: To work or study late into the night (देर रात तक जागकर काम करना / पढ़ना)

question.en:
In the following sentence, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which gives the correct meaning of the underlined idiom or phrase.
The artist's sudden fame proved to be a flash in the pan as his second gallery was a total failure. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 19/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A sudden but very brief success period

2.en: A permanent change in a person's life

3.en: A dangerous fire in a kitchen area

4.en: A very bright light in a dark room

solution.en:
Meaning: A flash in the pan refers to a sudden, brief success that is not repeated or sustained.
Example sentence: His debut hit was just a flash in the pan; he never produced another successful song.
Options (b), (c), and (d) are incorrect.
Vocab Meanings:
• A flash in the pan: A sudden success that does not last (क्षणिक सफलता / चार दिन की चाँदनी)

question.en:
In the following sentence, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which gives the correct meaning of the underlined idiom or phrase.
The poet lived in an ivory tower, entirely oblivious to the struggles of ordinary people. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 22/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A magnificent white building made of expensive materials that symbolises power

2.en: A place where scientists conduct experiments

3.en: A state of mind where one is sheltered from the practical realities of life

solution.en:
Meaning: Living in an ivory tower refers to an impractical state of existence where one is secluded or detached from the harsh practical realities and everyday problems of life.
Example: Philosophers often face criticism for residing in an ivory tower rather than engaging with real-world issues.
Vocab Meanings:
• Ivory tower: A state of being cut off from practical realities (वास्तविकता से कटा हुआ जीवन / काल्पनिक दुनिया)

question.en:
In the following sentence, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which gives the correct meaning of the underlined idiom or phrase.
In the quiet village, the arrival of the famous movie star was a nine days' wonder. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 22/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A miracle that lasts for many years

2.en: An occasion that lasts for over a week

3.en: An event that creates short-lived interest

4.en: A mystery that is never truly solved

solution.en:
Meaning: A nine days' wonder refers to a person, event, or phenomenon that generates great excitement or public interest for a very short period and is then completely forgotten.
Example: The sudden viral trend proved to be merely a nine days' wonder.
Vocab Meanings:
• Nine days' wonder: Something that creates interest for a short time only (थोड़े समय की चर्चा / अल्पकालिक आकर्षण)

question.en:
In the following sentence, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which gives the correct meaning of the underlined idiom or phrase.
The novel was so exciting that I read it at one sitting. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 23/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: To read while sitting in a specific chair

2.en: To read a book very slowly over several weeks

3.en: To do something continuously without stopping

4.en: To read only the first and last chapters

solution.en:
Meaning: The idiom at one sitting (or at a sitting) means during one continuous period of time without getting up or stopping until finished.
Example: She finished painting the entire canvas at one sitting.
Vocab Meanings:
• At one sitting: Continuously, without a break (एक ही बार में / बिना रुके)

question.en:
In the following sentence, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which gives the correct meaning of the underlined idiom or phrase.
The heavy rain was a blessing in disguise as it forced us to cancel the disastrous outdoor party. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 23/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A good thing that seemed bad at first

2.en: A person wearing a very strange costume

3.en: A religious event held in a church

4.en: A lucky charm kept for good fortune

solution.en:
Meaning: A blessing in disguise refers to something that seems unfortunate, bad, or unlucky at first, but turns out to have good or advantageous results later on.
Example: Missing the bus turned out to be a blessing in disguise because the train arrived earlier and was far more comfortable.
Vocab Meanings:
• A blessing in disguise: Something good that first seems bad (छिपा हुआ वरदान / जो पहले बुरा लगे पर अंत में अच्छा निकले)

question.en:
In the following sentence, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which gives the correct meaning of the underlined idiom or phrase.
The politician's promise of a new park turned out to be a castle in the air project with no funding. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 25/09/26 Shift 2]

2.en: Plans or ideas with little hope of being realised

4.en: Goals that are easily attainable without much effort

solution.en:
Meaning: A castle in the air refers to an unrealistic or visionary plan, scheme, or daydream that has little to no chance of ever coming true.
Vocab Meanings:
• Castle in the air: A plan or dream unlikely to come true (हवाई किले / ख्याली पुलाव)

question.en:
In the following sentence, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which gives the correct meaning of the underlined idiom or phrase.
The old sailor's tale about the ghost ship was dismissed as a cock and bull story by the village elders. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 25/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A story about farm animals and nature

2.en: A very believable and honest account

3.en: An unlikely and highly improbable story

4.en: A brave tale of heroism and courage

solution.en:
Meaning: A cock and bull story is a story or explanation that is absurd, fanciful, or unlikely to be true.
Vocab Meanings:
• Cock and bull story: An unbelievable, made-up story (मनगढ़ंत कहानी / अविश्वसनीय किस्सा)

question.en:
Select the correct idiom to fill in the blank:
Despite many warnings, Rohan invested all his savings in the fake scheme and finally had to ________ [SSC Selection Post (10th) 16/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Meaning: 'Face the music' means to confront or accept the unpleasant consequences of one's actions.
Example: After ignoring sound financial advice, he had to face the music.
Other idioms: 'Spill the beans' means to reveal a secret; 'Take French leave' means an unauthorized absence; 'Call it a day' means to stop working.
Vocab Meanings:
• Face the music: To accept the unpleasant results of one's actions (अपने किए का फल भुगतना)
• Spill the beans: To reveal a secret (भेद खोल देना)
• Take French leave: To take leave without permission (बिना अनुमति छुट्टी लेना)
• Call it a day: To stop working for the day (काम बंद करना)

question.en: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'The tip of the iceberg' [SSC Selection Post (10th) 16/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: A small visible part of a much bigger issue

solution.en:
Meaning: 'The tip of the iceberg' refers to a small, noticeable part of a problem, the total extent of which is much greater and largely unseen.
Example: The complaints received were only the tip of the iceberg.
Vocab Meanings:
• The tip of the iceberg: A small visible part of a much bigger problem (किसी बड़ी समस्या का छोटा सा दिखाई देने वाला भाग)

question.en: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'By leaps and bounds' [SSC Selection Post (10th) 17/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Meaning: The idiom 'by leaps and bounds' means making rapid or dramatic progress; Very rapidly.
Example: Her spoken English skills have improved by leaps and bounds.
Vocab Meanings:
• By leaps and bounds: Very quickly; rapidly (बहुत तेज़ी से / दिन दूनी रात चौगुनी)

question.en: What does the idiom/phrase 'in the doldrums' mean? [SSC Selection Post (10th) 17/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Meaning: 'In the doldrums' is an idiom meaning sluggish, depressed, stagnant, or in a state of inactivity and low spirits.
Example: The retail sector remained in the doldrums throughout the slow quarter.
Vocab Meanings:
• In the doldrums: In a state of low spirits or inactivity (उदासी या निष्क्रियता की स्थिति में)

question.en: What does the idiom/phrase 'a storm in a teacup' mean? [SSC Selection Post (10th) 18/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: Great fuss over a trivial matter

2.en: A sudden spell of bad luck

4.en: A plan that fails at the start

solution.en:
Meaning: The idiom a storm in a teacup means a situation where people get very angry or excited about something that is not at all important.
Example: Don't worry about their minor disagreement; it is just a storm in a teacup.
Vocab Meanings:
• A storm in a teacup: A lot of anger or worry about a very small matter (छोटी सी बात पर बहुत हंगामा / राई का पहाड़ बनाना)

question.en: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Play second fiddle' [SSC Selection Post (10th) 18/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Meaning: To play second fiddle means to take a subordinate or less important position relative to someone else.
Example: He was tired of playing second fiddle to his partner and decided to start his own business.
Vocab Meanings:
• Play second fiddle: To take a less important role than someone else (कम महत्वपूर्ण / सहायक भूमिका निभाना)

question.en: What does the idiom/phrase 'set one's face against' mean? [SSC Selection Post (10th) 19/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: To show firm opposition to something

4.en: To look carefully at a problem

solution.en:
Meaning: The idiom 'set one's face against' means to resist, oppose, or disapprove of something strongly and determinedly.
Example: The committee set its face against any further delay in the project.
Vocab Meanings:
• Set one's face against: To firmly oppose something (किसी बात का दृढ़ता से विरोध करना)

question.en:
Choose the correct idiom to fill in the blank:
Everyone in the office knew that the senior accountant was honest, so the allegation against him was a ________ [SSC Selection Post (10th) 19/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Meaning: A bolt from the blue refers to a sudden, unexpected, and shocking event or piece of news.
Other options: A red-letter day is a memorable or happy day; a wild goose chase is a futile search; a storm in a teacup is great outrage over a trivial matter.
Vocab Meanings:
• Bolt from the blue: A sudden and unexpected event (अचानक आई विपत्ति / अप्रत्याशित घटना)
• Red-letter day: A memorable or special day (यादगार / शुभ दिन)
• Wild goose chase: A useless search (व्यर्थ की खोज)
• Storm in a teacup: A big fuss over a small matter (छोटी बात पर बड़ा हंगामा)

question.en: What does the idiom/phrase 'move heaven and earth' mean? [SSC Selection Post (10th) 21/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Meaning: 'Move heaven and earth' means to do everything you can in order to achieve something.
Example: He moved heaven and earth to ensure his family got through the crisis.
Vocab Meanings:
• Move heaven and earth: To make every possible effort (हर संभव प्रयास करना / एड़ी-चोटी का ज़ोर लगाना)

question.en: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Through the roof' [SSC Selection Post (10th) 21/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Meaning: 'Through the roof' means rising to an extremely high or unexpected level.
Example: Prices of essential commodities went through the roof during the shortage.
Vocab Meanings:
• Through the roof: Extremely high (बहुत अधिक / आसमान छूना)

question.en: What does the idiom/phrase 'at sixes and sevens' mean? [SSC Selection Post (10th) 22/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: In a state of confusion or disorder

solution.en:
Meaning: The idiom at sixes and sevens means in a state of total confusion, disarray, or disorder.
Example: After the sudden departure of the manager, the entire department was left at sixes and sevens.
Vocab Meanings:
• At sixes and sevens: In a state of confusion or disorder (अस्त-व्यस्त / उलझन या अव्यवस्था की स्थिति में)

question.en: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Take the bull by the horns' [SSC Selection Post (10th) 22/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Meaning: The idiom take the bull by the horns means to face, confront, or deal with a difficult situation directly and courageously.
Example: Instead of evading the issue, she decided to take the bull by the horns and speak directly to her employer.
Vocab Meanings:
• Take the bull by the horns: To deal with a problem boldly (समस्या का साहसपूर्वक सामना करना)

question.en: What does the idiom/phrase 'bell the cat' mean? [SSC Selection Post (10th) 23/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Meaning: To bell the cat means to attempt or undertake something that is extremely dangerous or difficult.
Example: Someone had to face the boss about the pay cuts, but nobody wanted to bell the cat.
Vocab Meanings:
• Bell the cat: To take on a risky task for others (जोखिम भरा काम अपने सिर लेना)

question.en: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Run out of steam' [SSC Selection Post (10th) 23/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Meaning: Run out of steam means to lose energy, enthusiasm, or momentum to continue an activity.
Example: After working fourteen hours straight, the team finally ran out of steam.
Vocab Meanings:
• Run out of steam: To lose energy or enthusiasm (ऊर्जा या उत्साह खो देना / थक जाना)

question.en: What does the idiom/phrase 'be on tenterhooks' mean? [SSC Selection Post (10th) 24/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: To be in a state of anxious suspense

solution.en:
Meaning: 'Be on tenterhooks' means to be in a state of tense anticipation, nervousness, or suspense.
Example: We were on tenterhooks all morning waiting for the exam results.
Vocab Meanings:
• Be on tenterhooks: In a state of anxious waiting (चिंतापूर्ण प्रतीक्षा में होना / बेचैन रहना)

question.en: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Wear one's heart on one's sleeve' [SSC Selection Post (10th) 24/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Meaning: 'Wear one's heart on one's sleeve' means to make one's feelings and emotions obvious and apparent to all.
Example: He is not afraid to wear his heart on his sleeve and tells everyone how much he loves his family.
Vocab Meanings:
• Wear one's heart on one's sleeve: To show one's feelings openly (अपनी भावनाएँ खुलकर प्रकट करना)

question.en: What does the idiom/phrase 'carry coals to Newcastle' mean? [SSC Selection Post (10th) 25/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: To supply something where it is already plentiful

solution.en:
Meaning: Carry coals to Newcastle means to do or provide something that is completely redundant or unnecessary because there is already an abundance of it.
Example: Exporting wine to France is like carrying coals to Newcastle.
Vocab Meanings:
• Carry coals to Newcastle: To take something to a place where it is already plentiful (जहाँ कोई चीज़ पहले से भरपूर हो वहीं उसे ले जाना / उल्टे बाँस बरेली को)

question.en: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Up in the air' [SSC Selection Post (10th) 25/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Meaning: Up in the air means unresolved, undecided, or uncertain.
Example: Our travel plans for next weekend are still up in the air.
Vocab Meanings:
• Up in the air: Uncertain; not yet decided (अनिश्चित / अधर में लटका हुआ)

tests.title: Selection Post 2026 English — HOMOPHONES AND HOMONYMS

meta.title: Selection Post 2026 English — HOMOPHONES AND HOMONYMS
meta.subject: English

question.en:
From the given options, select the homonym that corresponds to both Definition (P) and Definition (Q).
(P) The study of the internal structure of words and how they are formed using morphemes
(Q) The study of the physical form, shape, and structural characteristics of organisms or rocks [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 17/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Morphology in linguistics refers to the study of word formation and morphemes, while in biology/geology it refers to the study of the structure and form of organisms or landforms.
Phonology is the study of speech sounds; Topology relates to geometrical properties; Ontology is the philosophical study of being.
Vocab Meanings:
• Morphology: The study of the forms of words or living things (रूपविज्ञान / आकृति विज्ञान)
• Phonology: The study of speech sounds (स्वनविज्ञान / ध्वनि विज्ञान)
• Topology: The study of shapes and spaces (in mathematics) (सांस्थितिकी)
• Ontology: The study of the nature of existence (सत्तामीमांसा)

question.en:
From the given options, select the homonym that corresponds to both Definition (P) and Definition (Q).
(P) To combine, merge, or unite two separate companies or organisations into one unified corporate structure
(Q) To alloy, mix, or blend a metal alloy directly with liquid mercury [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 19/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Definition: Amalgamate means to combine or unite to form one organization or structure, and in metallurgy/chemistry, it specifically denotes combining or blending a metal with mercury.
Other options: Coagulate means to change to a solid or semi-solid state; Arbitrate means to judge a dispute; Consolidate means to combine multiple things into a single whole, but does not refer to alloying with mercury.
Vocab Meanings:
• Amalgamate: To combine into one; to mix a metal with mercury (विलय करना / मिश्रित करना; पारे के साथ मिश्रधातु बनाना)
• Coagulate: To thicken or form clots (जमना / थक्का बनना)
• Arbitrate: To settle a dispute as a judge (मध्यस्थता करना)
• Consolidate: To make stronger; to combine (सुदृढ़ करना / एकीकृत करना)

question.en:
From the given options, select the homonym that corresponds to both Definition (P) and Definition (Q).
(P) The process by which a cell or molecule absorbs and integrates an external substance into its own physical structure
(Q) The legal process of officially forming and registering a new corporation or business entity [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 22/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Meaning: The term Incorporation refers biologically/physically to combining or taking in something as part of a whole, and legally to the formation and registration of a corporate entity.
Assimilation applies only to biological or cultural absorption, not corporate registration.
Calcination and Acquisition do not satisfy both definitions.
Vocab Meanings:
• Incorporation: Including something as part of a whole; forming a legal company (समावेशन / निगमन - कंपनी का पंजीकरण)
• Assimilation: Absorbing and integrating something (आत्मसात्करण / समावेश)
• Calcination: Heating a substance to a high temperature (निस्तापन)
• Acquisition: Buying or obtaining something (अधिग्रहण)

question.en:
From the given options, select the homonym that corresponds to both Definition (P) and Definition (Q).
(P) A regular, repeating three-dimensional arrangement of atoms, ions, or molecules in a crystalline solid
(Q) A partially ordered set in which every pair of elements has a unique supremum and infimum [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 24/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Meaning: In chemistry/crystallography, a lattice is a periodic 3D arrangement of atoms or molecules.
In order theory (mathematics), a lattice is a partially ordered set in which every two elements have a unique supremum and infimum.
Hence, Lattice satisfies both definitions.
Vocab Meanings:
• Lattice: A regular repeating pattern (atoms in crystals; also a mathematical set) (जालक / जाली - क्रिस्टल संरचना; गणित में जालक)
• Matrix: A rectangular array of numbers; a surrounding medium (आव्यूह / मैट्रिक्स)
• Trellis: A frame of crossed strips for climbing plants (जाली / बेलों का मचान)
• Cicatrice: The scar of a healed wound (घाव का निशान)

question.en:
Choose the option that contains the homonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The local history museum plans to show a collection of rare 19th-century maps to the public for the first time this weekend. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 16/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: During the science fair, the students will show their experiments to the judges to explain how chemical reactions occur.

2.en: The guide was kind enough to show the tourists the hidden entrance to the ancient temple behind the waterfall.

3.en: I missed the latest episode of that reality show because I had to stay late at the office to finish my project.

4.en: When you arrive at the theater, please show your digital ticket to the usher so they can direct you to your seat.

solution.en:
Concept: A homonym is a word that shares the same spelling and pronunciation as another word but has a completely different meaning and part of speech.
In the sentence, show is used as a verb meaning to display or present.
In option (c), show is used as a noun meaning a television programme or broadcast performance, whereas options (a), (b), and (d) all use show as a verb.
Vocab Meanings:
• Show: To display or let someone see (verb) (दिखाना / प्रदर्शित करना - क्रिया)
• Show: A TV or stage programme (noun) (कार्यक्रम / शो - संज्ञा)

question.en:
Fill in the blank with an appropriate option.
My soul gets tired of repairing soles. In this sentence, soul and sole are ___ [SSC Selection Post (12th) 17/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: Words that have the same pronunciation but differ in meaning, origin, and spelling are called homophones.
Both 'soul' (the spiritual aspect of a person) and 'sole' (the underside of a shoe) are pronounced identically (/soʊl/).
Homonyms usually share spelling or pronunciation, homographs share the exact spelling, and polysemy refers to a single word carrying multiple related meanings.
Vocab Meanings:
• Soul: The spiritual part of a person (आत्मा)
• Sole: The bottom of a shoe; or only one (जूते का तला / एकमात्र)
• Homophones: Words that sound the same but differ in meaning and spelling (समध्वनि शब्द - एक जैसा उच्चारण, अलग अर्थ और वर्तनी)
• Homonyms: Words with the same spelling or sound but different meanings (समनाम / समरूपी शब्द)
• Polysemy: One word having several related meanings (बहुअर्थकता)
• Homographs: Words spelt the same but differing in meaning or sound (समवर्तनी शब्द)

question.en:
Choose the correct option to complete the sentence.
The ________ of the school is very supportive of new learning methods. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 17/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: 'Principal' functions as a noun referring to the head or chief administrator of a school.
Correct sentence: The principal of the school is very supportive of new learning methods.
'Principle' refers to a fundamental truth, law, or moral standard, while 'principel' and 'prinsipal' are incorrect spellings.

question.en:
Choose the option that contains the homonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The heavy rains caused the soil to shift, eventually cracking the concrete foundation of the house. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 17/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A solid foundation is the most important part of any building's structural integrity.

2.en: Before starting the renovation, the crew had to reinforce the crumbling foundation of the old warehouse.

3.en: Engineers inspected the damaged foundation of the bridge to assess the risk of collapse.

4.en: The makeup artist applied a thin layer of liquid foundation to even out the actor's skin tone before filming.

solution.en:
Rule: A homonym is a word that shares the same spelling and pronunciation as another word but possesses a different meaning.
In the prompt sentence, 'foundation' refers to the concrete structural substructure of a building.
In option (d), 'foundation' denotes a cosmetic product applied to facial skin.
Options (a), (b), and (c) all use 'foundation' in its original structural and architectural sense.
Vocab Meanings:
• Foundation: The base on which a building stands (नींव / आधार)
• Foundation: A cosmetic cream applied to even skin tone (मेकअप में चेहरे पर लगाई जाने वाली क्रीम / फाउंडेशन)

question.en:
Choose the option that contains the homonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The children ran across the open ground to reach the swings before the school bell rang. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 18/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The local council decided to convert the empty lot into a new sports ground for the youth.

2.en: Geologists studied the frozen ground of the Arctic to understand climate shifts.

3.en: For the traditional recipe, the chef used spices that were freshly ground into a fine aromatic powder.

4.en: The sacred cremation ground was located at the edge of the quiet village.

solution.en:
In the source sentence, 'ground' is a noun referring to the surface of the earth or land.
In option (c), 'ground' is the past participle/adjective derived from the verb 'grind' (crushed into particles).
A homonym shares the same spelling and pronunciation but has a completely distinct origin and meaning.
In options (a), (b), and (d), 'ground' retains the original noun sense of land/surface.
Vocab Meanings:
• Ground: The surface of the earth; an open area (noun) (मैदान / ज़मीन - संज्ञा)
• Ground: Crushed into powder; past tense of 'grind' (पीसा हुआ - 'grind' का भूतकाल)

question.en:
Choose the option that contains the homonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The museum curator carefully placed the ancient gold object into the glass display case to protect it from dust. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 19/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: During the deep-sea dive, the explorers spotted a metallic object partially buried in the sand near the shipwreck.

2.en: The science teacher explained that every solid object in the room is made up of millions of tiny atoms.

3.en: Although the plan seemed efficient, several board members decided to object to the high cost of the new project.

4.en: When the light hit the crystalline object on the shelf, it created a beautiful rainbow across the opposite wall.

solution.en:
In the original sentence, object is used as a noun meaning a material thing.
In option (c), object is used as a verb meaning to express disapproval or opposition, creating a homonym (same spelling, different meaning/part of speech).
In options (a), (b), and (d), object is used identically as a noun referring to a physical item.
Vocab Meanings:
• Object: A thing that can be seen or touched (noun) (वस्तु - संज्ञा)
• Object: To express disapproval or opposition (verb) (आपत्ति करना / विरोध करना - क्रिया)

question.en:
Choose the option that contains the homonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The architect visited the site daily to ensure that the construction of the skyscraper followed the safety blueprints exactly. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 21/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Heavy machinery was moved into the city centre to facilitate the construction of the new underground metro station.

2.en: The local residents complained about the loud noise coming from the construction of the luxury apartment complex nearby.

3.en: Following the earthquake, the government provided funds for the rapid construction of temporary housing for displaced families.

4.en: To improve his writing, the student focused on the grammatical construction of his essays to avoid run-on sentences.

solution.en:
Meaning: In the given sentence, construction refers to the physical building or erection of a physical structure (the skyscraper).
Options (a), (b), and (c) all use "construction" in this exact same primary physical building sense (metro station, apartment complex, temporary housing).
In option (d), construction refers to the arrangement or syntactic formation of words in a sentence (grammatical structure), representing a different meaning/sense of the homonym.
Vocab Meanings:
• Construction: The process of building something (निर्माण - भवन आदि)
• Construction: The way words are arranged in a sentence (वाक्य-रचना / संरचना - व्याकरण में)

question.en:
Choose the option that contains the homonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The scientist explained that the scale of the recent volcanic eruption was larger than anything recorded in the last century. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 22/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The global scale of the plastic pollution crisis requires immediate international cooperation.

2.en: When drawing the floor plan, the architect used a scale of one inch to four feet.

3.en: On a local scale, the new community garden has significantly improved the neighbourhood's air quality.

4.en: The project was so massive in scale that it required thousands of workers and ten years to complete.

solution.en:
In the prompt sentence, scale refers to the relative size, extent, or magnitude of an event.
In sentences (a), (c), and (d), "scale" is used in the identical sense of relative scope or extent (global scale, local scale, massive in scale).
In sentence (b), scale is used as a distinct homonym/sense denoting a graduated measurement ratio or standard for mapping and architectural drawing.
Vocab Meanings:
• Scale: The size or extent of something (पैमाना / व्यापकता - आकार)
• Scale: The ratio between a map/drawing and the real size (अनुपात / मापक - नक्शे या ड्रॉइंग का)

question.en:
Choose the option that contains the homonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The doctor instructed the patient to swallow the vitamin capsule with a full glass of water every morning. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 22/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The pharmaceutical company developed a new capsule to treat chronic pain effectively.

2.en: Because the medicine was bitter, it was encased in a gelatine capsule to make it easier for children to take.

3.en: During the final stage of the mission, the crew entered the space capsule to begin their descent back to Earth.

4.en: The herbal supplement is available in both liquid and a concentrated capsule form.

solution.en:
In the given sentence, capsule refers to a small soluble gelatin case enclosing a dose of medicine.
Options (a), (b), and (d) all use "capsule" in the medical or pharmaceutical sense.
Option (c) uses capsule in a completely different context and meaning, referring to a spacecraft compartment or vehicle designed to carry astronauts.
Vocab Meanings:
• Capsule: A small case containing medicine (दवा का कैप्सूल)
• Capsule: A small compartment of a spacecraft (अंतरिक्ष यान का कक्ष / अंतरिक्ष कैप्सूल)

question.en:
Choose the option that contains the homonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The editor reviewed the digital content of the website to ensure all the articles were accurate and up to date. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 23/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Students were advised to check the written content at the back of the novel to get the gist of the plot.

2.en: After a long day of hiking in the mountains, she sat by the campfire feeling completely content with the quiet beauty of nature.

3.en: The legal team analyzed the video content shared on social media to see if it violated any copyright regulations.

4.en: When preparing your presentation, make sure the educational content is simplified so that the younger audience can understand it.

solution.en:
A homonym (specifically a heteronym in pronunciation) is a word that shares the same spelling as another word but has a different meaning and grammatical function.
In the given sentence, content (/ˈkɒntɛnt/) is a noun meaning information, material, or substance.
In option (b), content (/kənˈtɛnt/) is an adjective meaning pleased, satisfied, and at peace.
Options (a), (c), and (d) all use 'content' in the identical noun sense of material or text.
Vocab Meanings:
• Content: The material contained in something (noun) (विषय-वस्तु / सामग्री - संज्ञा)
• Content: Satisfied; happy (adjective) (संतुष्ट - विशेषण)

question.en:
Choose the option that contains the homonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The ballistics expert examined the bullet found at the scene to determine the calibre of the weapon used. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 24/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: During the hunting trip, he was careful to keep his extra bullet casings in a secure pouch to avoid littering the forest.

2.en: For better readability, the author decided to use a small bullet before each item in the list of ingredients.

3.en: The historical museum displays a silver bullet that was allegedly used as a protective charm during the 18th century.

4.en: The high-velocity bullet shattered the glass target instantly during the precision shooting competition.

solution.en:
A homonym shares the same spelling and pronunciation but has a completely different meaning.
In the original sentence, 'bullet' refers to a projectile fired from a firearm.
In option (b), 'bullet' refers to a typographical symbol or bullet point used in formatting lists.
Options (a), (c), and (d) all use 'bullet' in the original sense of ammunition.
Vocab Meanings:
• Bullet: A metal piece fired from a gun (गोली - बंदूक की)
• Bullet: A dot used to mark items in a list (सूची में बिंदु चिह्न / बुलेट पॉइंट)

question.en:
Choose the option that contains the homonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The ozone layer acts as a massive shield that absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 25/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: During the heavy rainstorm, the thick canopy of trees provided a natural shield for the hikers.

2.en: The knight raised his iron shield to deflect the incoming arrows during the battle.

3.en: After winning the inter-school cricket tournament, the captain proudly hoisted the silver shield.

4.en: Scientists are developing a new thermal shield to protect spacecraft from extreme heat during re-entry.

solution.en:
Homonym Context:
In the given sentence, 'shield' is used in the sense of a protective barrier (as are options a, b, and d).
In option (c), shield has an entirely distinct homonymic meaning: a decorative plaque, trophy, or award presented to the winner of a competition.
Vocab Meanings:
• Shield: A protective barrier or cover (ढाल / सुरक्षा कवच)
• Shield: A trophy shaped like a shield (शील्ड / पुरस्कार में मिलने वाली ट्रॉफी)

question.en:
Choose the option that contains the homonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The biology student spent the summer studying marine ecosystems to understand the impact of rising temperatures on ocean currents. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 25/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Divers discovered a variety of colorful marine plants while exploring the deep crevices of the coral reef.

2.en: The government passed a new law to protect marine mammals, such as dolphins and whales, from industrial pollution.

3.en: After completing his rigorous training, the young soldier was proud to serve as a marine in the elite coastal division.

4.en: Specialized marine equipment is required for researchers to collect water samples from the floor of the Pacific Ocean.

solution.en:
Homonym Context:
In the prompt sentence, 'marine' is an adjective meaning relating to or found in the sea. Options (a), (b), and (d) all use this identical oceanographic definition.
In option (c), marine functions as a noun referring to a member of a military armed force trained to serve on land or at sea.
Vocab Meanings:
• Marine: Relating to the sea (adjective) (समुद्री - विशेषण)
• Marine: A soldier who serves on ships (noun) (नौसैनिक / मरीन सैनिक - संज्ञा)

question.en:
Choose the option that contains the homonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The massive naval vessel disappeared into the thick fog as it left the harbor. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 26/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: A small fishing vessel was spotted drifting aimlessly in the middle of the Atlantic.

2.en: The explorer spent years searching for the wreckage of a Spanish vessel lost at sea.

3.en: A damaged vessel carrying cargo had to be towed back to the port for urgent repairs.

4.en: Doctors explained that the blockage in the patient's coronary vessel required immediate surgery.

solution.en:
Homonym: Words sharing the same spelling and pronunciation but possessing completely different meanings.
