The correct spelling is Quiescence (a state of quietness, dormancy, or inactivity).
It derives from Latin quiescere and requires the letter sequence -scence.
Options (a), (b), and (c) contain incorrect letter arrangements.
Vocab Meanings:
• Quiescence: A state of inactivity or rest (निष्क्रियता / शांति / स्थिरता)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 16/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Sustainability is the correct spelling. It refers to the ability to be maintained at a certain rate or level, or the avoidance of the depletion of natural resources. The other options contain errors such as 'i' or missing vowels.
Vocab Meanings:
• Sustainability: The ability to continue for a long time without harming the environment (संधारणीयता / स्थिरता)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 16/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Premature is the correct spelling. It means occurring, done, or occurring before the proper or usual time. The other options contain phonetic misspellings or transposed letters.
Vocab Meanings:
• Premature: Happening before the proper or usual time (समय से पहले / अपरिपक्व)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 17/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correctly spelt word is Measurable (formed by adding the suffix '-able' to 'measure', dropping the terminal silent 'e').
Vocab Meanings:
• Measurable: That can be measured (मापने योग्य)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 17/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correctly spelt word is Elimination, which means the complete removal or destruction of something.
Vocab Meanings:
• Elimination: The act of removing or getting rid of something (उन्मूलन / निष्कासन)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 17/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correctly spelt word is Questionable, meaning doubtful as to truth or validity.
Vocab Meanings:
• Questionable: Doubtful; open to question (संदिग्ध / संदेहास्पद)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 18/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correctly spelt word is Unprecedented, which means never done or known before. The other options contain incorrect vowel substitutions: 'i' in place of 'e', 's' in place of 'c', or 'a' in place of 'e'.
Vocab Meanings:
• Unprecedented: Never done or known before (अभूतपूर्व)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 18/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correctly spelt word is Brainstorming, meaning a spontaneous group discussion to produce ideas. Option (a) incorrectly doubles the letter 'm', option (c) transposes letters to 'strom', and option (d) omits the letter 'i'.
Vocab Meanings:
• Brainstorming: A group discussion to produce new ideas (विचार-मंथन)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 19/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correctly spelt word is Hazardous, which means risky or dangerous.
The other spellings are incorrect variants.
Vocab Meanings:
• Hazardous: Dangerous; risky (खतरनाक / जोखिम भरा)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 19/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correctly spelt word is Simultaneous, meaning occurring, operating, or done at the same time.
The other options contain spelling errors.
Vocab Meanings:
• Simultaneous: Happening at the same time (एक साथ होने वाला / समकालिक)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 19/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correct spelling is Irresistible, ending in -ible.
All other options are misspelled.
Vocab Meanings:
• Irresistible: Too strong or attractive to be resisted (अप्रतिरोध्य / जिसका विरोध न किया जा सके)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 21/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Worldwide is the correct spelling, meaning extending or reaching throughout the world.
The other options contain erroneous omissions or letter substitutions.
Vocab Meanings:
• Worldwide: Spread throughout the world (विश्वव्यापी)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 21/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Characteristic is the correct spelling, referring to a feature or quality typical of a person, place, or thing.
The other options contain vowel misspellings.
Vocab Meanings:
• Characteristic: A typical quality or feature (विशेषता / लाक्षणिक गुण)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 22/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correctly spelt word is Ballistics (spelled with double 'l' and ending in '-ics'), which refers to the science of projectiles and firearms.
Vocab Meanings:
• Ballistics: The science of projectiles and firearms (प्रक्षेपिकी / प्रक्षेप्य विज्ञान)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 22/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correctly spelt word is Celestial, which means positioned in or relating to the sky, or outer space as observed in astronomy.
Vocab Meanings:
• Celestial: Relating to the sky or heaven (आकाशीय / दिव्य)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 23/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correctly spelt word is Disguise, which means to give a new appearance to a person or thing to hide its true identity.
Vocab Meanings:
• Disguise: A changed appearance to hide one's identity (भेष बदलना / छद्मवेश)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 23/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correctly spelt word is Classic, meaning judged over a period of time to be of the highest quality and outstanding of its kind.
Vocab Meanings:
• Classic: Of high quality; traditional and lasting (उत्कृष्ट / श्रेष्ठ / शास्त्रीय)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 23/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correctly spelt word is Liaison, which refers to communication or cooperation facilitating a close working relationship between people or organizations.
Vocab Meanings:
• Liaison: Communication or cooperation between groups (संपर्क / तालमेल)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 24/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Spelling: The correctly spelt word is Gallery, which refers to a room or building for the display or sale of works of art, or a balcony/upper floor in a hall. All other spellings are incorrect.
Vocab Meanings:
• Gallery: A room or building for displaying art (दीर्घा / चित्रशाला)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 24/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Spelling: The correct spelling is Connoisseur, which refers to an expert judge in matters of taste, the fine arts, or food and wine. It contains double 'n' and double 's'.
Vocab Meanings:
• Connoisseur: An expert judge in matters of taste (पारखी / विशेषज्ञ)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 25/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Spacecraft is the correct spelling, referring to a vehicle designed for travel or operation outside Earth's atmosphere.
Vocab Meanings:
• Spacecraft: A vehicle used for travel in space (अंतरिक्ष यान)

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 25/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correctly spelt word is Refrigerator. Note that while the short informal form is spelled "fridge" with a 'd', the formal word refrigerator does not contain a 'd'.
Vocab Meanings:
• Refrigerator: An appliance for keeping food cold (प्रशीतक / फ्रिज)

tests.title: Selection Post 2026 English — ACTIVE PASSIVE VOICE

meta.title: Selection Post 2026 English — ACTIVE PASSIVE VOICE
meta.subject: English

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
Please help the injured man at once. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 17/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The injured man is requested to be helped at once.

2.en: The injured man should be helped at once.

3.en: Let the injury man be helped at once.

4.en: You are requested to help the injured man at once.

solution.en:
An imperative sentence expressing a request starting with "Please" changes into passive voice using "You are requested to + V1...".
Thus, the correct passive transformation is "You are requested to help the injured man at once."

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
The mountaineers spotted an injured snow leopard lying motionless near the frozen stream. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 17/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: An injured snow leopard was spotted to lie motionless near the frozen stream by the mountaineers.

2.en: An injured snow leopard was spotted lying motionless near the frozen stream by the mountaineers.

3.en: An injured snow leopard had been spotted lying motionless near the frozen stream by the mountaineers.

4.en: An injured snow leopard was spotted to be lying motionless near the frozen stream by the mountaineers.

solution.en:
The active sentence is in Simple Past tense (spotted). The passive structure requires was/were + V3 (was spotted) while preserving the participle clause (lying motionless).
Option (c) incorrectly uses past perfect (had been spotted), while (a) and (d) introduce unidiomatic infinitive constructions.

question.en:
Choose the grammatically correct active voice form of the passive voice sentence given below.
The Charminar had not been seen by them before. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: They had not seen the Charminar before.

2.en: They did not see the Charminar before.

3.en: They have not seen the Charminar before.

4.en: They will not see the Charminar before.

solution.en:
Rule: Past perfect passive structure (had + been + V3) changes to past perfect active structure (had + V3).
• Passive: The Charminar had not been seen by them before.
• Active: They had not seen the Charminar before.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
The teacher teaches a new technique [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: A new technique is taught by the teacher

2.en: A new technique was taught by the teacher

3.en: A new technique has taught by the teacher

4.en: A new technique is taught by him

solution.en:
Rule: Simple present active tense (teaches) changes to simple present passive tense (is/am/are + V3).
• Active: The teacher teaches a new technique.
• Passive: A new technique is taught by the teacher.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
The authorities have not repaired the broken roads for months. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 19/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The broken roads were not repaired by the authorities for months.

2.en: The broken roads are not repaired by the authorities for months.

3.en: The broken roads had not been repaired by the authorities for months.

4.en: The broken roads have not been repaired by the authorities for months.

solution.en:
Rule: Active have/has + not + V3 transforms into Passive have/has + not + been + V3.
Active: The authorities have not repaired the broken roads for months.
Passive: The broken roads have not been repaired by the authorities for months.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
The defence lawyer was arguing the case of the wrongly convicted prisoner in front of the high court bench yesterday. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 19/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The case of the wrongly convicted prisoner was argued in front of the high court bench yesterday by the defence lawyer.

2.en: The case of the wrongly convicted prisoner had been argued in front of the high court bench yesterday by the defence lawyer.

3.en: The case of the wrongly convicted prisoner was being argued in front of the high court bench yesterday by the defence lawyer.

4.en: The case of the wrongly convicted prisoner has been argued in front of the high court bench yesterday by the defence lawyer.

solution.en:
Rule: Active Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing) transforms into Passive was/were + being + V3.
Active: The defence lawyer was arguing the case...
Passive: The case of the wrongly convicted prisoner was being argued in front of the high court bench yesterday by the defence lawyer.

question.en:
Select the most suitable active voice construction of the following sentence.
The visitor was pleased with the receptionist. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 21/09/26 Shift 1]

2.en: The receptionist was pleased with the visitor.

4.en: The receptionist is pleased by the visitor.

solution.en: Rule: The passive structure 'was pleased' (simple past passive) corresponds to the simple past active form 'pleased'. The object of the preposition becomes the subject: 'The receptionist pleased the visitor.'

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
The manager approved the budget proposal. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 21/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The budget proposal was approving by the manager

2.en: The budget was approved by the manager

3.en: The budget proposals were approved the manager

4.en: The budget proposal was approved by the manager

solution.en: Rule: Simple past active ('approved') changes to 'was/were + past participle' ('was approved'). The subject 'The budget proposal' is singular, yielding 'The budget proposal was approved by the manager.'

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
The supervisor checks the quality of every product carefully. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 22/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The quality of every product is being checked carefully by the supervisor.

2.en: The quality of every product has been checked carefully by the supervisor.

3.en: The quality of every product is checked carefully by the supervisor.

4.en: The quality of every product was checked carefully by the supervisor.

solution.en:
Rule: Simple Present Active: Subject + V1 (s/es) + Object converts to Passive: Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject.
Here, "the quality of every product" is singular, so it takes "is checked".
Option (a) is present continuous, (b) is present perfect, and (d) is past tense.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
Had the investigation team examined all the suspicious documents before the court hearing began? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 22/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Were all the suspicious documents examined by the investigation team before the court hearing began?

2.en: Have all the suspicious documents been examined by the investigation team before the court hearing began?

3.en: Were all the suspicious documents being examined by the investigation team before the court hearing began?

4.en: Had all the suspicious documents been examined by the investigation team before the court hearing began?

solution.en:
Rule: Past Perfect Interrogative Active: Had + Subject + V3 + Object? converts to Passive: Had + Object + been + V3 + by Subject?
The auxiliary verb "Had" remains unchanged in the past perfect passive form.
Option (d) correctly keeps the past perfect interrogative structure "Had all the suspicious documents been examined...".

question.en:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence in active voice corresponding to the one given.
The bear was spotted near the village last night. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 23/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Someone spotted the bear near the village last night.

2.en: The bear spotted someone near the village last night.

3.en: The villagers spotted the bear near the village last night.

4.en: The bear is spotting near the village last night.

solution.en: Rule: Passive voice in simple past (was/were + V3) changes to active voice (subject + V2 + object). Since the agent is omitted in the passive sentence, the indefinite pronoun someone correctly serves as the active subject without introducing unmentioned agents like 'the villagers'.

question.en:
Change the following from active to passive:
The mechanic will service the car next week. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 23/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The car will be serviced by the mechanic next week.

2.en: The car is serviced by the mechanic next week.

3.en: The car has been serviced by the mechanic next week.

4.en: The car will have been serviced by the mechanic next week.

solution.en:
Rule: Active voice with modal future (will + V1) converts into passive voice as (will + be + V3).
Active: The mechanic will service the car next week.
Passive: The car will be serviced by the mechanic next week.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
The railway department will lay new tracks along the entire route next year. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 24/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: New tracks will be being laid along the entire route by the railway department next year.

2.en: New tracks are being laid along the entire route by the railway department next year.

3.en: New tracks will have been laid along the entire route by the railway department next year.

4.en: New tracks will be laid along the entire route by the railway department next year.

solution.en:
Rule: Simple Future Active (will + V1) converts to Passive as will + be + V3.
Active: 'will lay' → Passive: will be laid.
Subject 'The railway department' becomes the agent 'by the railway department'.
Therefore, option (d) is the correct passive form.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
The accused could not have stolen the confidential files from the minister's office without inside assistance. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 24/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The confidential files from the minister's office could not have been stolen by the accused without inside assistance.

2.en: The confidential files from the minister's office could not have been stolen by the accused from the minister's office without inside assistance.

3.en: The confidential files from the minister's office should not have been stolen by the accused without inside assistance.

4.en: The confidential files from the minister's office could not be stolen by the accused without inside assistance.

solution.en:
Rule: Modal Perfect Active (could not have + V3) converts to Passive as could not have been + V3.
Active: 'could not have stolen' → Passive: could not have been stolen.
Option (a) correctly carries out this change without changing modality or adding redundant repeated phrases as in (b).

question.en:
Choose the correct Active Voice form of the given sentence:
The food has been ordered by Raj for the entire team. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 25/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Raj orders the food for the entire team.

2.en: Raj had ordered the food for the entire team.

3.en: Raj is ordering the food for the entire team.

4.en: Raj has ordered the food for the entire team.

solution.en:
Rule: Present Perfect Passive (has/have been + V3) converts to Present Perfect Active (has/have + V3).
• Passive: The food has been ordered by Raj...
• Active: Raj has ordered the food for the entire team.
• Option a is Simple Present, b is Past Perfect, and c is Present Continuous.

question.en:
Change the following from active to passive:
Someone must have changed the settings. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 25/09/26 Shift 1]

2.en: The settings must have been changed.

3.en: The settings have to be changed.

4.en: The settings must be being changed.

solution.en:
Rule: Modal perfect active (must have + V3) changes to modal perfect passive (must have been + V3).
• Active: Someone must have changed the settings.
• Passive: The settings must have been changed.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
Long hours of visually demanding work damage the eyesight of young workers. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 17/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The eyesight of young workers is damaged by long hours of visually demanding work.

2.en: The eyesight of young workers are damaged by long hours of visually demanding work.

3.en: The eyesight of young workers have been damaged by long hours of visually demanding work.

4.en: Long hours of visually demanding work is damaged by the eyesight of young workers.

solution.en:
Rule: Simple present active (Subject + V1 + Object) converts to passive (Object + is/are + V3 + by + Subject).
The grammatical object 'The eyesight' is an uncountable, singular noun phrase, requiring the singular auxiliary 'is'.
Active: Long hours of visually demanding work damage the eyesight of young workers.
Passive: The eyesight of young workers is damaged by long hours of visually demanding work.
Option (b) uses incorrect plural verb 'are', (c) shifts tense to present perfect, and (d) reverses the agent and patient.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
Helen brought groceries regularly for her elderly mother. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 17/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Groceries was brought regularly for her elderly mother by Helen.

2.en: Groceries were brought regularly for her elderly mother by Helen.

3.en: Groceries has brought regularly for her elderly mother by Helen.

4.en: Groceries was being brought regularly for her elderly mother by Helen.

solution.en:
Rule: Simple past active (Subject + V2 + Object) converts to passive (Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject).
The plural object 'Groceries' requires the plural auxiliary verb 'were'.
Active: Helen brought groceries regularly for her elderly mother.
Passive: Groceries were brought regularly for her elderly mother by Helen.
Option (a) uses singular 'was', (c) creates an incomplete perfect tense, and (d) changes the aspect to continuous.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
Employers hire children because they provide cheap and obedient labour. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 22/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Children have hired by employers because they provided cheap and obedient labour.

2.en: Children are be hired by employers because of cheap and obedient labour.

3.en: Employers are hired by children because they provide cheap and obedient labour.

4.en: Children are hired by employers because they provide cheap and obedient labour.

solution.en:
Rule: Simple present active voice (Subject + V1 + Object) changes to passive voice as (Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject).
The main clause "Employers hire children" becomes "Children are hired by employers".
The subordinate clause explaining the reason remains intact: "because they provide cheap and obedient labour".

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
The pilot announced the weather before the plane descended. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 22/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The weather are announced by the pilot before the plane descended.

2.en: The weather have been announced by the pilot before the plane descended.

3.en: The weather was announced by the pilot before the plane descended.

4.en: The weather was been announced by the pilot before the plane descended.

solution.en:
Rule: Simple past active voice (Subject + V2 + Object) changes to passive voice as (Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject).
"The pilot announced the weather" becomes "The weather was announced by the pilot".
The time clause "before the plane descended" remains unchanged.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
The writer describes the harsh realities of poverty faced by children in cities. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 25/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The harsh realities of poverty faced by children in cities have described by the writer.

2.en: The harsh realities of poverty faced by children in cities are described by the writer.

3.en: The harsh realities of poverty has being described by the writer for children in cities.

4.en: The writer is describing the harsh realities of poverty faced by children in cities.

solution.en:
Rule: Simple present active tense (\(\text{Subject} + \text{V}_1 + \text{Object}\)) changes to passive as \(\text{Object} + \text{is/are/am} + \text{V}_3 + \text{by} + \text{Subject}\).
The object "The harsh realities of poverty faced by children in cities" is plural, requiring "are described".
Option (b) correctly applies this grammatical rule.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
The committee approved the proposal after extensive discussion. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 25/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The proposal are approved by the committee after extensive discussion.

2.en: The proposal was approved by the committee after extensive discussion.

3.en: The proposal was been approved by the committee after extensive discussion.

4.en: The proposal has being approved by the committee after extensive discussion.

solution.en:
Rule: Simple past active tense (\(\text{Subject} + \text{V}_2 + \text{Object}\)) changes to passive as \(\text{Object} + \text{was/were} + \text{V}_3 + \text{by} + \text{Subject}\).
The singular subject "The proposal" takes "was approved".
Option (b) is grammatically precise.

question.en:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.
Ravi suggested to his friends that they should go for a walk. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 17/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Ravi said to his friends, "They should go for a walk."

2.en: Ravi said to his friends, "We should go for a walk."

3.en: Ravi say to his friends, "We shall go for a walk."

4.en: Ravi says to his friends, "We should go for a walk."

solution.en:
A proposal or suggestion introduced by "suggested to" in indirect narration corresponds to "said to" with a first-person plural proposal like "We should..." or "Let us...".
Options (c) and (d) incorrectly use present reporting verbs ("say", "says"). Option (a) incorrectly keeps the third-person pronoun "They" in direct address.

question.en:
Choose the option that best represents the direct narration of the given sentence.
She said that she had three sisters and one brother. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: She said, "I have three sisters and one brother."

2.en: She said, "She have had three sisters and one brother."

3.en: She said, "I had three sisters and one brother."

4.en: She said, "I have three sisters and a brother."

solution.en:
Rules: In changing indirect to direct speech:
• The past tense auxiliary/verb had in the indirect clause reverts to simple present have for a habitual/factual state.
• The third-person pronoun she changes back to first-person I.
• The exact original wording retains one brother, making option (a) the accurate direct speech.

question.en:
Choose the appropriate direct speech equivalent of the following sentence.
The laborers said that they wouldn't have enough time to complete the assigned work. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The laborers said, "They won't have enough time to complete the assigned work."

2.en: The laborers said, "We wouldn't have enough time to complete the assigned work."

3.en: The laborers said, "We don't have enough time to complete the assigned work."

4.en: The laborers said, "We won't have enough time to complete the assigned work."

solution.en:
Rules:
• The third-person pronoun they referring to the speakers becomes first-person plural we.
• The modal wouldn't in indirect narration corresponds to won't (will not) in direct speech.
• Therefore, the direct speech is: The laborers said, "We won't have enough time to complete the assigned work."

question.en:
Choose the correct indirect speech of the sentence:
She said, "Why didn't you attend the meeting?" [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: She asked why I hadn't attended the meeting.

2.en: She said why I didn't attend the meeting.

3.en: She asked that why hadn't I attended.

4.en: She said why had I not attended the meeting.

solution.en:
Rules: In changing an interrogative Wh-question into indirect speech:
• The reporting verb said changes to asked.
• Wh-words (here, why) connect the clause without the conjunction that.
• The word order changes from interrogative inversion to affirmative statement form (subject + verb).
• Simple past negative (didn't attend) backshifts to past perfect negative (hadn't attended).
• Therefore, the sentence becomes: She asked why I hadn't attended the meeting.

question.en:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.
She explained that she was watching a movie when the incident happened. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 19/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: She said, "She was watching a movie when the incident happened."

2.en: She said, "I am watching a movie when the incident happened."

3.en: She said, "I was watching a movie when the incident happened."

4.en: She says, "I was watching a movie when the incident happened."

solution.en:
Rule: The indirect pronoun she referring to the speaker changes back to first-person I in direct speech.
The reporting clause is in past tense (explained / said), maintaining the past continuous time frame of the background action in direct narration.
Sentence: She said, "I was watching a movie when the incident happened."

question.en:
Choose the correct direct speech form of the sentence below.
Anant said that he was the fastest bowler in the university. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 21/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Anant said, "He is the fastest bowler in this University."

2.en: Anant said, "I am the fastest bowler in the University."

3.en: Anant said, "I was the fastest bowler in the University."

4.en: Anant said, "He was the fastest bowler in the University."

solution.en: Rules: When converting indirect to direct speech, the third-person pronoun 'he' referring to the speaker changes to first-person 'I'. The simple past verb 'was' reverts to the simple present 'am'.

question.en:
Which of the following is the correct direct speech form of the given sentence?
Rishab said that I had not been paying attention in class the previous day. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 21/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Rishab said, "You aren't paying attention in class yesterday."

2.en: Rishab said, "You weren't paying attention in class yesterday."

3.en: Rishab said, "You weren't paying attention in class the previous day."

4.en: Rishab said, "I had not been paying attention in class yesterday."

solution.en: Rules: Past perfect continuous tense ('had not been paying') in indirect speech reverts to past continuous ('weren't paying') in direct speech. The pronoun 'I' refers to the listener addressed as 'You', and 'the previous day' changes back to 'yesterday'.

question.en:
Choose the correct indirect speech of the sentence:
The teacher said, "Who has not submitted the assignment?" [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 21/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The teacher asked who had not submitted the assignment.

2.en: The teacher said who hasn't submitted the assignment.

3.en: The teacher asked who was not submitting the assignment.

4.en: The teacher asked who didn't submit the assignment.

solution.en: Rules: In interrogative sentences, the reporting verb 'said' changes to 'asked'. The present perfect tense ('has not submitted') shifts back to the past perfect tense ('had not submitted').

question.en:
Find the grammatically sound direct speech representation of the indirect sentence from the options below.
Nandita told Abhay that if they had not hurried out of the room, they would not have come back so soon pushing those tall wire carts full of babies for him to review. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 22/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Nandita told Abhay, "If we have not hurried out of the room, we will not have come back so soon pushing those tall wire carts full of babies for you to have reviewed."

2.en: Nandita told Abhay, "If we have not hurried out of the room, we would not have come back so soon pushing those tall wire carts full of babies for you to be reviewing."

3.en: Nandita told Abhay, "If we had not hurried out of the room, we will not have come back so soon pushing those tall wire carts full of babies for you having reviewed."

4.en: Nandita told Abhay, "If we had not hurried out of the room, we would not have come back so soon pushing those tall wire carts full of babies for you to review."

solution.en:
Rules: In third conditional sentences expressing an unreal past conditional ("If + past perfect, would have + past participle"), the tense of the conditional clause remains unchanged in indirect speech reporting.
Pronoun shifts: "they" converts back to "we", and the indirect objective pronoun "him" converts to "you".
The infinitive purpose phrase "for him to review" corresponds directly to "for you to review".
Thus, option (d) is the exact, grammatically correct direct speech form.

question.en:
Choose the correct direct sentence of the following sentence.
The manager said that nothing would have gone wrong if the process had been followed correctly. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 23/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The manager said, "Nothing would go wrong if the process is followed correctly."

2.en: The manager said, "Nothing would have gone wrong if the process had been followed correctly."

3.en: The manager said, "Nothing went wrong because the process was followed."

4.en: The manager said, "The process must be followed to prevent issues."

solution.en:
Rule: In third conditional sentences (unreal past: would have + V3 ... had + V3), the tenses remain unchanged when switching between direct and indirect speech.
Direct: The manager said, "Nothing would have gone wrong if the process had been followed correctly."

question.en:
Choose the correct indirect speech of the sentence:
She said, "I might consider your proposal." [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 23/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: She said she may consider my proposal.

2.en: She said she might considered my proposal.

3.en: She said she might consider my proposal.

4.en: She said she would considered my proposal.

solution.en: Rule: The modal auxiliary might remains unchanged in indirect speech, followed by the base form of the verb (V1: consider). The first-person pronoun 'I' changes to 'she', and 'your' changes to 'my'.

question.en:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.
He said that no sooner had he arrived than the meeting began. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 23/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: "No sooner I arrived than the meeting began," he said.

2.en: "No sooner did I arrive than the meeting began," he said.

3.en: "No sooner had I arrived than the meeting began," he said.

4.en: "No sooner have I arrived than the meeting began," he said.

solution.en: Rule: The past perfect form with inverted syntax ("No sooner had + subject + V3 ... than ...") in indirect speech corresponds directly to the identical past perfect construction in direct speech with quotation marks and pronoun adjustment.

question.en:
The following sentence is given in Indirect Speech. Select the option that correctly expresses it in Direct Speech.
The wicked Montoni told Emily that if she signed the castle estates over to him, she would secure her freedom immediately. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 24/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The wicked Montoni told Emily, "that if you sign the castle estates over to me, you will secure your freedom immediately."

2.en: The wicked Montoni said, "Emily, if you signed the castle estates over to him, you would secured her freedom immediately."

3.en: The wicked Montoni said to Emily, "If you sign the castle estates over to me, you will secure your freedom immediately."

4.en: The wicked Montoni told to Emily, "If she signed the castle estates over to me, she would secure your freedom immediately."

solution.en:
Rules:
1. Reporting verb 'told Emily that' becomes said to Emily, "...".
2. Conditional clause backshift reverses: past simple 'signed' becomes present simple sign, and 'would secure' becomes will secure.
3. Pronouns shift to the second and first persons: 'she' → you, 'him' → me.
Therefore, option (c) is the grammatically correct direct speech form.

question.en:
Choose the correct direct sentence of the following sentence.
She said that he might as well have accepted the offer instead of waiting. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 25/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: She said, "He might as well have accepted the offer instead of waiting."

2.en: She said, "You should accept the offer instead of waiting."

3.en: She said, "You might accept the offer instead of waiting."

4.en: She said, "He should have accepted the offer instead of waiting."

solution.en:
Rule: The modal idiom "might as well have + past participle" remains unchanged in indirect speech when reporting in the past.
• Therefore, the direct speech retains the exact phrasing: She said, "He might as well have accepted the offer instead of waiting."
• Other options change the modal verb to "should" or "might accept", altering the meaning.

question.en:
Choose the correct indirect version:
He said, "Can you help me with this?" [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 25/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: He asked if I can help him with this.

2.en: He asked whether I could help him with that.

3.en: He said could I help him with that.

4.en: He asked that I could help him.

solution.en:
Rule:
• Reporting verb "said" changes to "asked".
• Yes/no question introduces conjunction "if" or "whether".
• Modal "can" changes to past form "could".
• Demonstrative "this" changes to "that".
• Pronouns change: "you" → "I", "me" → "him".
• Sentence: He asked whether I could help him with that.

question.en:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.
He said that he would rather not comment on the allegations. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 25/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: "I'd rather not comment on the allegations," he said.

2.en: "I would not comment on the allegations," he said.

3.en: "I will rather not speak about the allegations," said he.

4.en: "I'd prefer to stay silent," he said.

solution.en:
Rule: The phrase "would rather" corresponds directly to "would rather" (contracted as "I'd rather") in direct speech.
• Third-person pronoun "he" shifts back to first-person "I".
• Direct speech: "I'd rather not comment on the allegations," he said.

question.en:
Choose the correct direct speech form of the following sentence.
Meena inquired how she could reach the railway station. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 17/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Meena said, "How can I reach the railway station?"

2.en: Meena said, "How can she reached the railway station?"

3.en: Meena said, "How can they reach the railway station?"

4.en: Meena said, "How shall I reach the railway station?"

solution.en:
Rules: The reporting verb 'inquired' changes to 'said' in direct speech. The pronoun 'she' reverts to first person 'I' as it refers to Meena. The modal verb 'could' reverts to its present form 'can', and the inverted word order of a direct question ('How can I...') is restored.
Option (b) incorrectly uses the past form 'reached' after 'can', (c) changes the subject pronoun to 'they', and (d) unnecessarily introduces 'shall'.

question.en:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.
The interviewer asked the candidate why he had chosen that particular career path. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 17/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The interviewer said to the candidate, "Why have you chosen this particular career path?"

2.en: The interviewer said to the candidate, "Why did you chosen that particular career path?"

3.en: The interviewer said to the candidate, "Why had you choose this particular career path?"

4.en: The interviewer said to the candidate, "Why do you choose this particular career path?"

solution.en:
Rules: The reporting verb 'asked' reverts to 'said to'. The indirect past perfect 'had chosen' corresponds to the present perfect 'have you chosen' in direct speech. The pronoun 'he' changes to 'you', and demonstrative 'that' becomes 'this'.
Option (b) is grammatically malformed ('did you chosen'), (c) uses an invalid verbal pairing ('had you choose'), and (d) improperly changes the tense to simple present.

question.en:
Choose the correct direct speech form of the following sentence.
Rabinson said that he would not allow anybody to enter into the compound. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 21/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Rabinson said, "I will not allow anybody to enter to the compound."

2.en: Rabinson said, "I shall not allow anybody to enter into the compound."

3.en: Rabinson said, "I will not allow anybody entering into the compound."

4.en: Rabinson said, I shall not allow anybody to enter the compound."

solution.en:
Rules: In converting indirect speech back to direct speech, the third-person pronoun 'he' referring to the speaker becomes first-person 'I'.
The modal auxiliary 'would' in reported speech corresponds to 'shall' (or 'will') with first-person pronoun 'I' expressing future intention or determination.
The prepositional phrase "into the compound" and infinitive "to enter" remain unchanged.
Option (b) correctly retains the complete quotation punctuation and exact prepositional structure: Rabinson said, "I shall not allow anybody to enter into the compound."
Option (a) incorrectly alters "into" to "to".
Option (c) incorrectly changes the infinitive "to enter" to the participle "entering".
Option (d) misses the opening quotation mark and omits the preposition "into".

question.en:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.
The instructor said to the students, "Draw what you see in front of you." [SSC Selection Post (12th) 21/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The instructor commanded the students that they should draw what they saw in front of them.

2.en: The instructor ordered the students to draw what you saw in front of you.

3.en: The instructor asked the students to draw what they see in front of them.

4.en: The instructor told the students to draw what they saw in front of them.

solution.en:
Rules: In reporting imperative sentences, the reporting verb "said to" changes to "told" / "ordered" / "instructed", followed by the infinitive structure ("to draw").
The subordinate clause tense shifts from the simple present "see" to the simple past "saw".
The second-person pronoun "you" changes to the third-person plural pronoun "they" and the objective form "them" to match the addressee ("the students").
Option (d) correctly applies all transformations: "The instructor told the students to draw what they saw in front of them."
Option (a) unnecessarily uses a "that they should" clause.
Option (b) fails to change the second-person pronouns "you".
Option (c) fails to backshift the present tense verb "see" to the past tense "saw".

question.en:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.
The mother asked her daughter if she would help her with the laundry that evening. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 22/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The mother said to her daughter, "Will you help me with the laundry this evening?"

2.en: The mother said to her daughter, "Would you help her with the laundry that evening?"

3.en: The mother said to her daughter, "Can you help her with the laundry this evening?"

4.en: The mother said to her daughter, "Shall you help me with the laundry this evening?"

solution.en:
Rules: In indirect speech, "asked... if" derives from an interrogative direct speech clause starting with an auxiliary verb.
Modal verb would converts back to will; pronoun she (referring to daughter) converts back to you; her converts back to me.
Time adverbial that evening changes back to this evening.

question.en:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.
The officer demanded to know why I had arrived so late for the morning parade. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 22/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The officer said to me, "Why have you arrive so late for the morning parade?"

2.en: The officer said to me, "Why did you arrive so late for the morning parade?"

3.en: The officer said to me, "Why had you arrive so late for the morning parade?"

4.en: The officer said to me, "Why was you arrived so late for the morning parade?"

solution.en:
Rules: The past perfect in indirect speech ("had arrived") corresponds to a simple past tense in direct speech ("did you arrive").
Pronoun I changes back to second person you.
Option (a) and (c) use incorrect grammatical forms ("have you arrive", "had you arrive").
Thus, the correct direct question is: "Why did you arrive so late for the morning parade?"

question.en:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.
The girl said, "I can sketch a beautiful landscape." [SSC Selection Post (12th) 24/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The girl said that she can sketch a beautiful landscape.

2.en: The girl said that she could sketch a beautiful landscape.

3.en: The girl said that I could sketch a beautiful landscape.

4.en: The girl said that she could sketched a beautiful landscape.

solution.en:
Rules: In indirect speech with a past reporting verb ('said'):
1. The pronoun 'I' changes to she according to the subject 'The girl'.
2. The modal auxiliary 'can' changes to could.
3. The modal is followed by the base form of the verb (sketch).
Thus, the correct sentence is: The girl said that she could sketch a beautiful landscape.

question.en:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.
Mrs. Croft demanded to know who was speaking. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 24/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rules: When converting indirect speech to direct speech, the past continuous 'was speaking' corresponds to the present continuous is speaking in the speaker's original utterance.
The reporting verb 'demanded' is preserved.
Hence, the correct direct speech form is: Mrs. Croft demanded, "Who is speaking?"

question.en:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.
The traveler inquired of the local if he could show him the way to the inn. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 25/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The traveler said to the local, "Can you show me the way to the inn?"

2.en: The traveler said to the local, "Could you showed him the way to the inn?"

3.en: The traveler said to the local, "Would you show me the way to the inn?"

4.en: The traveler asked the local, "Can him show me the way to the inn?"

solution.en:
Rules:
1. The reporting verb "inquired of" converts back to "said to".
2. The conjunction "if" is replaced with direct speech inverted question structure.
3. The modal auxiliary "could" reverts to "Can" in present tense.
4. Pronouns shift appropriately: third-person "he" reverts to second-person "you", and objective "him" reverts to first-person "me".
Option (a) correctly formats the question: "Can you show me the way to the inn?"

question.en:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.
The spectators exclaimed with joy that their favorite team had won the championship trophy. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 25/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The spectators said, "Alas! Our favorite team has won the championship trophy."

2.en: The spectators said, "Hurrah! Our favorite team has won the championship trophy."

3.en: The spectators said, "Bravo! Their favorite team was won the championship trophy."

4.en: The spectators said, "Hurrah! Their favorite team has win the championship trophy."

solution.en:
Rules:
1. "Exclaimed with joy" indicates an interjection expressing happiness, which is typically "Hurrah!".
2. The third-person possessive pronoun "their" converts to the first-person plural "our".
3. Past perfect "had won" converts to present perfect "has won" inside direct quotations.
Option (b) correctly renders: "Hurrah! Our favorite team has won the championship trophy."

question.en:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.
The teacher said, "We will go for a picnic tomorrow." [SSC Selection Post (12th) 26/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The teacher said that they would go for a picnic tomorrow.

2.en: The teacher said that they would go for a picnic the next day.

3.en: The teacher said that we will go for a picnic the next day.

4.en: The teacher said that they will go for a picnic the following day.

solution.en:
Rules:
1. The reporting verb is in the past tense (said), so modal will changes to would.
2. Pronoun we shifts to the third-person plural they.
3. Time expression tomorrow shifts to the next day (or the following day).
Option (b) applies all shifts correctly, whereas (a) keeps tomorrow, and (c) and (d) fail to shift the modal verb to would.

question.en:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.
The narrator said that he had arrived in Boston the previous week. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 26/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The narrator said, "I arrived in Boston last week."

2.en: The narrator said, "I had arrived in Boston the previous week."

3.en: The narrator said, "I arrive in Boston last week."

4.en: The narrator said, "He arrived in Boston last week."

solution.en:
Rules:
1. Past perfect tense (had arrived) in indirect speech backshifts from the simple past (arrived) in direct speech.
2. The third-person pronoun he corresponds to first-person I spoken by the narrator.
3. Time expression the previous week converts back to last week.
Thus, option (a) provides the correct direct speech sentence.

meta.title: Selection Post 2026 English — FILL IN THE BLANKS

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate adverb.
He responded ________ to the allegations, without admitting fault. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Meaning: To respond evasively means in a way that avoids giving a direct answer or taking a firm position, perfectly matching "without admitting fault".
The other adverbs do not fit the context of dodging responsibility or blame.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with an appropriate degree of comparison.
She completed the task ________ efficiently than her colleagues, surprising everyone. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: The comparative degree of a multi-syllable adverb like efficiently is formed using more when followed by the comparative conjunction than.
• Most is used for superlative comparison.
• Much and many are not comparative markers here.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate adverb.
________ considered, the theory still leaves many questions unanswered. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 21/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Collocation/Meaning: Broadly considered is a standard idiomatic adverbial phrase meaning "taking all main aspects into account" or "in general terms."
• Summarily: Means immediately or dispensing with formalities.
• Crudely: In a rudimentary or unrefined manner.
• Cursory: An adjective, grammatically incorrect before a participle acting adverbially.

question.en:
Complete the collocation by choosing a suitable word to fill in the blank.
Given the rapid technological evolution, it is imperative for educational institutions to ________ curricula that address emerging interdisciplinary fields. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 21/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Meaning: Formulate means to create, develop, or prepare methodically. The collocation formulate curricula correctly fits educational planning.
• Extrapolate: To extend the application of an unknown situation by assuming existing trends will continue.
• Vacillate: To waver between different opinions or actions.
• IN THE TENTATIVE ANSWER KEY BOTH OPTION A AND B WERE SAME SO IT IS A BONUS QUESTION

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
The ________ nature of the coral reef makes it highly susceptible to changes in water temperature. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 22/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: Contextual vocabulary matching. The sentence states that the coral reef is "highly susceptible to changes," indicating delicacy and vulnerability.
Fragile means easily damaged or delicate, fitting the context precisely.
Robust (strong/durable) contradicts the sentence, while gigantic and noisy do not make logical sense.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate adverb.
No matter how _______ she tried, she could not solve the intricate equation. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 23/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The positive degree adverb hard (meaning with great effort or energy) correctly modifies the verb 'tried' in the structure "No matter how + adverb/adjective + subject + verb".
Other options:
• Hardly / Hardly ever: Mean scarcely or almost never, altering the intended meaning.
• Harder: Comparative degree is unnecessary here without a comparative baseline.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with an appropriate degree of comparison.
The final performance was the _______ of the entire evening. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 23/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en: Rule: The definite article the preceding the blank, together with the prepositional phrase "of the entire evening" (comparing among all performances), requires the superlative degree most spectacular.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate adverb.
He completed the negotiations ________ refusing to let emotions affect his judgments. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 25/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Context: The clause "refusing to let emotions affect his judgments" indicates an objective, calm, and unemotional manner.
• Dispassionately: In an unemotional, impartial, or calm manner.
Other options:
• Flamboyantly: In a noticeably stylish, bright, or showy way.
• Effusively: In a way that expresses feelings of gratitude, pleasure, or approval in an unrestrained or heartfelt manner.
• Mendaciously: In a dishonest, untruthful way.

question.en:
Fill in the blanks with appropriate parts of speech.
Not only ________ the hypotheses questioned, but also ________ by leading experts in the field. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 25/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: The subject "hypotheses" is plural (singular: hypothesis).
• In the first clause, negative inversion ("Not only...") requires the plural auxiliary verb were before "the hypotheses".
• In the second clause, parallel structure ("were questioned, but also [were] invalidated") requires the past participle invalidated sharing the passive auxiliary.

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
Of the two detective novels I read this weekend, the first one was definitely ________ written. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 16/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: When comparing two items, the comparative degree (better) is used rather than the superlative degree (best).
"More better" is an incorrect double comparative. Therefore, better is the correct choice.

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
Neither of the two candidates ________ invited for the interview. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 18/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: The distributive pronoun 'Neither' refers to one of two persons or things individually and takes a singular verb.
Since the sentence is in the passive voice in the past ("invited for the interview"), the singular past auxiliary was is correct.
'Were' and 'are' are plural forms; 'have' is grammatically incorrect in this construction.

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
The mountain climber ________ escaped a fatal fall after his harness caught on a jagged rock. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 18/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Collocation & Meaning: The adverbial collocation narrowly escaped means to avoid danger or death by a very small margin.
'Rarely' means seldom; 'largely' means mostly; 'highly' means to a high degree. None fit the context of avoiding an accident.

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
He was very tired, _______ he continued to work until midnight. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 19/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: The conjunction yet is used as an adversative coordinator to show contrast between being tired and continuing to work.
So shows result, because shows cause, and or shows an alternative, which do not fit the contrast.

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
The philosopher's ideas were deeply rooted _______ the traditions of Ancient Greece. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 19/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: The fixed prepositional phrase is rooted in, meaning having an origin or strong basis within something.
The prepositions 'on', 'at', and 'with' do not collocate correctly with 'rooted'.

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
The poet ________ revised his manuscript for years, seeking the perfect word for every line. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 21/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Meaning: Meticulously means in a way that shows great attention to detail and is very thorough and careful.
Seeking the perfect word for every line over several years indicates deep care and precision.
Other options:
• Haphazardly: In a manner lacking any obvious principle of organization or randomness.
• Accidentally: By chance or without intention.
• Vaguely: In an unclear or imprecise way.

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
The student solved the complex math problem ______ [SSC Selection Post (12th) 23/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: An adverb of manner is required to modify the main verb solved.
Easily is the adverb form of the adjective 'easy'.
Easy, easier, and easiest are adjectives (positive, comparative, superlative degrees) and cannot modify the verb 'solved' directly.

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
The young scientist's breakthrough was ______ par with the most significant discoveries of the decade. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 23/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: The fixed prepositional idiom is on par with, which means at the same level or standard as someone or something else.
Other prepositions ('at par with', 'in', 'above') do not form the standard idiomatic construction in this context.

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
The teacher asked the students to ________ attention to the lecture. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 24/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Collocation Rule: The standard English collocation used with 'attention' in the context of listening or concentrating is pay attention.
Therefore, pay is the most appropriate word.

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
The bunch of keys ______ lying on the table since morning. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 26/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: When a collective noun phrase like a bunch of... acts as the subject, the head noun is singular (bunch), which takes a singular verb.
Among the given options, is is the only singular present verb form that fits the blank grammatically.
Plural verbs are and were disagree with the singular subject, and past auxiliary had requires a past participle (e.g., been).

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
The ______ of the symphony was so powerful that the audience remained silent long after the music ended. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 26/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Meaning: Resonance refers to the quality in a sound of being deep, full, and reverberating, creating a lasting emotional impact.
The context describes music so profoundly impactful that silence followed.
Other options: Fragility (delicacy), discord (harsh lack of harmony), and brevity (shortness of duration) do not match the powerful emotional aftermath described.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The secretary is answerable ________ the director for all official correspondence. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 16/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The adjective 'answerable' takes the preposition to when referring to a person or authority to whom one is accountable ('answerable to someone for something').
Correct sentence: The secretary is answerable to the director for all official correspondence.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The report is based ________ data collected from rural areas. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 16/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The verb 'base' takes the preposition on (or 'upon') when indicating the foundation or underlying facts of something ('based on').
Correct sentence: The report is based on data collected from rural areas.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
He has been suffering ________ back pain for several weeks. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 16/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The verb 'suffer' takes the preposition from when followed by an illness, ailment, or condition ('suffer from an illness').
Correct sentence: He has been suffering from back pain for several weeks.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The students are preparing __ the practical examination. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 17/09/26 Shift 3]
question.hi:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The students are preparing the practical examination. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 17/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The verb prepare takes the preposition for when indicating the purpose, event, or examination being gotten ready for.
Correct sentence: The students are preparing for the practical examination.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The manager is responsible __ the safety of all workers in the factory. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 17/09/26 Shift 3]
question.hi:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The manager is responsible the safety of all workers in the factory. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 17/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The adjective responsible is followed by the preposition for when referring to an obligation, duty, or task.
Correct sentence: The manager is responsible for the safety of all workers in the factory.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
She has been waiting __ the bus for more than twenty minutes. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 17/09/26 Shift 3]
question.hi:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
She has been waiting the bus for more than twenty minutes. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 17/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The verb wait takes the preposition for when referring to the person or thing expected.
Correct sentence: She has been waiting for the bus for more than twenty minutes.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The officer was entrusted __ the confidential documents. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 18/09/26 Shift 3]
question.hi:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The officer was entrusted the confidential documents. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 18/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The verb entrust takes the preposition with when followed by the thing assigned to someone's care: entrust someone with something. Alternatively, it takes to when phrased as entrust something to someone.
Correct sentence: The officer was entrusted with the confidential documents.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The new policy will come __ effect from next Monday. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 18/09/26 Shift 3]
question.hi:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The new policy will come effect from next Monday. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 18/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The standard English idiomatic phrasal expression for a law, rule, or policy taking effect is come into effect.
Correct sentence: The new policy will come into effect from next Monday.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
He apologized __ arriving late at the interview. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 18/09/26 Shift 3]
question.hi:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
He apologized arriving late at the interview. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 18/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The verb apologize takes the preposition for when citing the fault, action, or reason (apologize for doing something). It takes to only when indicating the person receiving the apology (apologize to someone).
Correct sentence: He apologized for arriving late at the interview.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The trainees were provided __ safety helmets before entering the site. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 19/09/26 Shift 3]
question.hi:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The trainees were provided safety helmets before entering the site. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 19/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The verb provide takes the preposition with when followed by the thing provided to someone: provide someone with something.
Correct sentence: The trainees were provided with safety helmets before entering the site.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The players were confident __ their chances of winning the match. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 19/09/26 Shift 3]
question.hi:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The players were confident their chances of winning the match. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 19/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The adjective confident typically takes the preposition of when followed by an outcome or possession of certainty (e.g., confident of success/chances).
Correct sentence: The players were confident of their chances of winning the match.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
She is not accustomed __ working under pressure. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 19/09/26 Shift 3]
question.hi:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
She is not accustomed working under pressure. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 19/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The adjective accustomed is followed by the preposition to (accustomed to something / doing something).
Correct sentence: She is not accustomed to working under pressure.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
You should refrain ________ making unnecessary comments in the meeting. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 21/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The verb 'refrain' is conventionally followed by the fixed preposition from (+ gerund).
Correct sentence: You should refrain from making unnecessary comments in the meeting.
The other prepositions are grammatically incorrect in this context.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The old bridge is still capable ________ carrying heavy vehicles. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 21/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The adjective 'capable' takes the preposition of followed by a gerund or noun phrase.
Correct sentence: The old bridge is still capable of carrying heavy vehicles.
The other prepositions are grammatically incompatible with 'capable'.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The principal was pleased ________ the students' performance. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 21/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The adjective 'pleased' takes the preposition with when expressing satisfaction with a person, thing, or outcome.
Correct sentence: The principal was pleased with the students' performance.
The other prepositions are incorrect in this standard collocation.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
His remarks were contrary __ the evidence produced in court. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 22/09/26 Shift 3]
question.hi:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
His remarks were contrary the evidence produced in court. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 22/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The adjective contrary takes the fixed preposition to when indicating opposition or conflict.
Correct sentence: His remarks were contrary to the evidence produced in court.
Other prepositions ('for', 'with', 'of') are ungrammatical in this fixed phrase.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
She has no interest __ joining the family business. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 22/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The noun interest is paired with the preposition in when indicating engagement, curiosity, or concern regarding an activity.
Correct sentence: She has no interest in joining the family business.
Other prepositions ('on', 'for', 'at') are grammatically incorrect in this pattern.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The villagers appealed __ the authorities for immediate help. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 23/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The verb appeal takes the preposition to when referring to the person or authority being addressed (appeal to somebody for something).
Correct sentence: "The villagers appealed to the authorities for immediate help."

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
He was prevented __ entering the restricted zone. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 23/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The verb prevent takes the preposition from followed by a gerund (prevent someone from doing something).
Correct sentence: "He was prevented from entering the restricted zone."

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
He succeeded __ convincing the board to revise the budget. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 23/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The verb succeed is followed by the preposition in and a gerund (succeed in doing something).
Correct sentence: "He succeeded in convincing the board to revise the budget."

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The workers protested __ the sudden reduction in wages. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 24/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The verb protest when used intransitively to express opposition to something typically takes the preposition against.
Correct sentence: The workers protested against the sudden reduction in wages.
Other options: 'to', 'for', and 'with' do not correctly express opposition in this context.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The child was frightened __ the loud noise outside. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 24/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The passive construction 'was frightened by' is used to denote the agent or external cause producing the fear, especially a sudden event or sound like a loud noise.
Correct sentence: The child was frightened by the loud noise outside.
Other options: 'from' and 'with' are incorrect; 'frightened of' is generally used for ongoing phobias/fears (e.g., frightened of dogs/spiders).

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
Our teacher insisted __ regular practice before the examination. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 24/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The verb insist takes the fixed preposition on (or 'upon') when followed by a noun, noun phrase, or gerund.
Correct sentence: Our teacher insisted on regular practice before the examination.
Other options: 'for', 'to', and 'with' do not pair with the verb insist.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
She is keen _____ learning new words every day. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 25/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The adjective keen is followed by the preposition on when expressing an interest in or enthusiasm for an activity (e.g., keen on doing something).
Correct sentence: She is keen on learning new words every day.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
The committee agreed _____ the proposal after a long discussion. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 25/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: One agrees with a person, agrees to a proposal (or action), and agrees on a matter, decision, or proposal after collective discussion. Among the given alternatives, on fits appropriately.
Correct sentence: The committee agreed on the proposal after a long discussion.

question.en:
Select the correct Preposition to fill the given blank.
He is very good _____ solving complex numerical problems. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 25/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The adjective good takes the preposition at when referring to ability, skill, or proficiency in doing something (e.g., good at mathematics, good at solving problems).
Correct sentence: He is very good at solving complex numerical problems.

question.en:
Read the sentence thoroughly, with special attention to the underlined segment. Choose the most appropriate substitution from A, B, or C. If the sentence is fine as it is, select D (No improvement required).
Despite claiming a commitment to renewable energy infrastructure, the present government has been starving tidal array projects of funding for almost ten years. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 17/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: is starving tidal array projects off fund

2.en: was starving tidal array projects at funds

3.en: has starved tidal array projects on funding

solution.en:
The original phrase has been starving tidal array projects of funding correctly employs the present perfect continuous tense to indicate an ongoing action continuing over a period ("for almost ten years") and uses the correct preposition of with the verb starve ("to starve something of something").
Therefore, no improvement is required.

question.en:
Read the following sentence carefully and focus on the underlined portion. Choose the option (A, B, or C) that best substitutes the underlined segment to improve the sentence grammatically or contextually. If the sentence is correct as written, select Option D (No Improvement Required).
The economist noted that fifty sails were charting new routes across the Atlantic, each carrying a cargo that was insulated against sudden market fluctuations. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 17/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: were charting new routes across the Atlantic, all carrying cargo that were

2.en: was charting new routes across the Atlantic, each carrying cargoes that was

3.en: are charting new routes across the Atlantic, each carrying cargo that was

solution.en:
Fifty sails uses synecdoche to mean fifty ships, which takes the plural verb were charting. The distributive absolute phrase each carrying a cargo that was... correctly uses singular agreement (cargo that was).
Therefore, the sentence is grammatically correct as written, requiring no improvement.

question.en:
Read the sentence below carefully. Choose the option (A/B/C) that best improves the sentence. If the sentence is already correct, select Option D (No improvement required).
The deep underground tectonic fissure was suddenly being closed because of the massive lithospheric compression was generated by the secondary shockwaves. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 19/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The deep underground tectonic fissure suddenly closed because of the massive lithospheric compression generated by the secondary shockwaves.

2.en: The deep underground tectonic fissure was suddenly closed because of the secondary shockwaves generated massive lithospheric compression.

3.en: The massive lithospheric compression generated by the secondary shockwaves were suddenly closed of the deep underground tectonic fissure.

solution.en:
Rule: The original sentence suffers from awkward continuous passive phrasing (was suddenly being closed) and a double predicate/run-on structure (compression was generated governed by because of).
Correct sentence: Using simple past active suddenly closed followed by the participial phrase generated by the secondary shockwaves makes the sentence grammatically correct and concise.

question.en:
Read the sentence thoroughly, with special attention to the underlined segment. Choose the most appropriate substitution from A, B, or C. If the sentence is fine as it is, select D (No improvement required).
Had the lead cryptanalyst deciphered the compromised communications matrix before the strike team deployed, he would avoid the subsequent ambush altogether. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 19/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: he would avoided the subsequent ambush

2.en: he would have avoided the subsequent ambush

3.en: he had avoided the subsequent ambush

solution.en:
Rule: Third conditional inversion structure requires: Had + Subject + V3 (past participle)..., Subject + would have + V3.
Correct sentence: Had the lead cryptanalyst deciphered..., he would have avoided the subsequent ambush altogether.

question.en:
Read the sentence below carefully. Choose the option (A/B/C) that best improves the sentence. If the sentence is already correct, select Option D (No improvement required).
The institutional review board concluded that the gene-editing trial was not an insignificant breakthrough, though it was not entirely risk-free either. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 22/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: It was the institutional review board's conclusion that the gene-editing trial, though not being an insignificant breakthrough, it was not entirely risk-free either.

2.en: The institutional review board concluded that the gene-editing trial was either not entirely risk-free but not an insignificant breakthrough.

3.en: The proposed gene-editing trial was concluded by the institutional review board to be neither an insignificant breakthrough and not entirely risk-free either.

solution.en:
Rule: The original sentence is grammatically sound, concise, and stylistically balanced using litotes ("not an insignificant breakthrough") followed by a coherent concessive clause ("though it was not entirely risk-free either").
Option (a) introduces a redundant subject pronoun ("it") creating a comma splice/run-on structure.
Option (b) incorrectly pairs "either" with "but".
Option (c) incorrectly pairs "neither" with "and not... either".
Therefore, no improvement is required.

question.en:
Read the sentence thoroughly, with special attention to the underlined segment. Choose the most appropriate substitution from A, B, or C. If the sentence is fine as it is, select D (No improvement required).
Following the Supreme Council's ratification of the third-century isolationist decree, the reclusive mountain kingdom maintains a strict embargo on all foreign vessels who attempted to cross the border. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 22/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: maintained a strict embargo on all foreign vessels attempting to cross

2.en: is maintaining a strict embargo on all foreign vessel's attempt to cross

3.en: has maintained a strict embargo on all foreign vessels' attempt at crossing

solution.en:
Rule: Tense consistency and relative pronoun reference for non-human antecedents.
The action takes place following a past decree ("ratification of the third-century isolationist decree"), necessitating the simple past tense maintained.
Furthermore, "foreign vessels" are inanimate objects and cannot take the personal relative pronoun "who". Replacing the clause with the present participle phrase attempting to cross ensures clarity and conciseness.

question.en:
Read the sentence below carefully. Choose the option (A/B/C) that best improves the sentence. If the sentence is already correct, select Option D (No improvement required).
