question.en:
In the following question, six sentences from a passage are provided. The first and last sentences, S1 and S6, are fixed. The four intermediate sentences-A, B, C, and D-have been shuffled. Reorder them to form a grammatically correct and logically coherent paragraph, then select the option that represents the correct sequence.
S1. There is only one way to make sure of the validity of a chain of logical reasoning.
A. If after this anybody still raises doubts then we can only beg him to point out an error in the steps of the proof, or to think the matter over again.
B. Any empirical scientific statement can be presented (by describing experimental arrangements, etc.) in such a way that anyone who has learned the relevant technique can test it.
C. This is to put it in the form in which it is most easily testable: we break it up into many small steps, each easy to check by anybody who has learnt the mathematical or logical technique of transforming sentences.
D. In the case of the empirical sciences, the situation is much the same.
S6. If, as a result, he rejects the statement, then it will not satisfy us if he tells us all about his feelings of doubt or about his feelings of conviction as to his perceptions. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 23/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
1. S1 introduces the problem: how to make sure of the validity of a chain of logical reasoning.
2. C directly answers S1 using the demonstrative pronoun "This" ("This is to put it in the form in which it is most easily testable... break it up into many small steps...").
3. A follows C by discussing the conclusion of this logical checking process ("If after this anybody still raises doubts...").
4. D transitions from pure logical reasoning to empirical sciences ("In the case of the empirical sciences, the situation is much the same").
5. B elaborates on empirical scientific statements, explaining how they can be tested, leading directly into S6 ("If, as a result, he rejects the statement...").
Order: C, A, D, B.

question.en:
The sentences of a passage have been shuffled and labelled P, Q, R, and S. Rearrange these sentences to form the most logically coherent and meaningful paragraph. Choose the correct sequence from the options provided.

Q: Society as a whole is splitting up into two great hostile camps, into two great classes, directly facing each other: Bourgeoisie and Proletariat.
R: Our epoch, the epoch of the bourgeoisie, possesses, however, this distinctive feature: it has simplified the class antagonisms.
S: The modern bourgeois society that has sprouted from the ruins of feudal society has not done away with class antagonisms. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 24/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Order analysis:
• Sentence S introduces the theme: modern bourgeois society emerging from feudal ruins without eliminating class antagonisms.
• Sentence P continues directly from S with 'It has but established...', explaining what it did instead of eliminating them.
• Sentence R introduces a contrasting/distinctive feature ('possesses, however, this distinctive feature: it has simplified the class antagonisms').
• Sentence Q details that simplification into two opposing classes: Bourgeoisie and Proletariat.
Thus, the correct coherent sequence is S - P - R - Q.

question.en:
In the following question, the opening sentence of a passage is fixed and labelled as S1. The remainder of the passage has been split into four parts - P, Q, R and S- which are not in their proper order. Rearrange these parts to form the most logically coherent and meaningful passage starting from S1. Choose the correct sequence from the options provided.
S1: The intuitive school affirms as strongly as the inductive school that there is a science of morals.
P: They both agree that the morality of an individual action is not a question of individual perception, but of the application of a common law to an individual case.
Q: Yet to support their pretensions, there ought to be one fundamental principle or law at the root of all morality.
R: They either assume the ordinary precepts of morals as of à priori authority, or they lay down some general maxims which have never succeeded in gaining popular acceptance.
S: Although both equally hold that morality must be deduced from principles, they seldom attempt to make out a list of such principles. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 25/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Logical Sequence:
S1 introduces two schools of thought: the intuitive school and the inductive school.
Part (P) naturally follows S1 by discussing their shared ground: "They both agree that the morality of an individual action is not a question of individual perception...".
Part (S) follows by qualifying this agreement with a contrasting shortcoming: "Although both equally hold that morality must be deduced from principles, they seldom attempt to make out a list of such principles."
Part (R) expands on how they fail to provide this list: "They either assume the ordinary precepts of morals as of à priori authority, or they lay down some general maxims...".
Part (Q) concludes by stating the overarching requirement necessary to support their claims: "Yet to support their pretensions, there ought to be one fundamental principle or law...".
Order: P, S, R, Q.

In the following question, four sentences from a paragraph are provided. The sentences are jumbled and labeled A, B, C and D. Rearrange these sentences into the correct sequence to form a logically and grammatically coherent paragraph. From the given alternatives, select the option that represents the correct sequence.
A. These are Dam (blood), Balgham (phlegm), Safra (yellow bile) and Sanda (black bile).
B. The Unani medicines are given to the person suffering from a disease to promote an equilibrium of these elements in the body.
C. Unani system of medicine is also the natural way of treatment with the help of herbal medicines.
D. According to this system, the health of a person depends on the balance of four elements in the body. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 24/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Sentence structure:
C introduces the main subject: 'Unani system of medicine'.
D explains the core principle of 'this system', which relies on the balance of 'four elements'.
A names the four elements ('These are Dam, Balgham, Safra and Sanda').
B concludes with how Unani medicines help restore equilibrium among these elements.
Order: C, D, A, B.

question.en:
In the following question, four sentences from a paragraph are provided. The sentences are jumbled and labeled A, B, C and D. Rearrange these sentences into the correct sequence to form a logically and grammatically coherent paragraph. From the given alternatives, select the option that represents the correct sequence.
A. A nutritious diet favours growth.
B. Nutrition is, therefore, the most important external factor for growth.
C. In fact, at every stage, the body needs a basic level of nutrients for its sustenance.
D. Growth requires multiplication of cells or enlargement of cells, which depends on an adequate supply of nutrients. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 25/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Sentence A introduces the primary subject that a nutritious diet favours growth.
Sentence D explains how growth occurs and why nutrients are required (cell multiplication/enlargement).
Sentence C elaborates on the continuous need for nutrients at every stage for sustenance.
Sentence B logically concludes with the connecting adverb "therefore".
Order: A, D, C, B.

question.en:
In the following question, four sentences from a paragraph are provided. The sentences are jumbled and labeled A, B, C and D. Rearrange these sentences into the correct sequence to form a logically and grammatically coherent paragraph. From the given alternatives, select the option that represents the correct sequence.
A. The examples of this consistency can be seen in a person who remains friendly or a person who is generally kind or helpful in most situations.
B. It tells us what type of person one is.
C. Personality is a very common term which is used in our day-to-day life.
D. We know that each person generally behaves consistently in most of the situations. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 25/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Sentence C introduces the main concept ("Personality").
Sentence B uses the pronoun "It" to refer back to personality and explain what it reveals.
Sentence D states the premise that individuals behave consistently across situations.
Sentence A directly exemplifies "this consistency" mentioned in sentence D.
Order: C, B, D, A.

question.en:
In the following question, four sentences from a paragraph are provided. The sentences are jumbled and labeled A, B, C and D. Rearrange these sentences into the correct sequence to form a logically and grammatically coherent paragraph. From the given alternatives, select the option that represents the correct sequence.
A. Modern gymnastics is regulated by the Federation International de Gymnastique (FIG) which was founded in 1881.
B. Guts Muths, is known as the Grand Father of Modern Gymnastics and Friedrich Ludwig Jahn is known as the Father of Gymnastics.
C. The word gymnastics has been derived from the Greek word 'Gymnos' meaning "naked art".
D. In ancient Greek, the word "Gymnastics" was used to denote the exercise done with the naked body. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 25/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Sentence C introduces the origin and etymology of the term gymnastics from the Greek word 'Gymnos'.
Sentence D directly expands upon its ancient Greek usage.
Sentence B transitions into the prominent historical figures associated with gymnastics.
Sentence A brings the progression to modern regulated gymnastics.
Order: C, D, B, A.

question.en:
In contemporary cognitive science, human judgment is increasingly understood as a product of layered neural and psychological mechanisms rather than a purely rational calculus. Decisions that appear deliberate are often (A) by unconscious biases that subtly recalibrate perception before conscious deliberation even begins. This recognition has significantly undermined earlier models of rational agency, suggesting instead that cognition is dynamically constructed in real time.
Within this framework, behavioural economists argue that heuristics, while computationally efficient, can (B) systematic errors in probabilistic reasoning, particularly under conditions of uncertainty and informational overload. Such errors are not incidental but structurally embedded within the architecture of human cognition.
Clinical psychology has similarly evolved, with therapeutic paradigms increasingly encouraging individuals to (C) entrenched cognitive schemas rather than merely suppressing symptomatic expressions of distress. This shift reflects an understanding that maladaptive thought patterns are self-reinforcing and resistant to superficial correction.
Neuroscientific evidence further indicates that the brain (D) capable of extensive functional reorganization, even in adulthood, thereby challenging earlier assumptions about fixed neural circuitry. This adaptability underpins many modern rehabilitative and psychotherapeutic interventions.
Nevertheless, scholars caution that public discourse often (E) complex psychological constructs into overly simplistic explanatory frames, thereby obscuring the nuanced interplay between cognition, emotion, and environment.

Fill in the blank (A) with the correct word. [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 17/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Mediated means brought about, influenced, or conveyed as an intermediary mechanism, which perfectly describes decisions shaped by unconscious biases.
Aggravated means made worse; intensified means made more intense; obstructed means blocked.

question.en:
Good governance is essential for the stability and progress of any nation. It involves transparency, accountability, and effective delivery of public services. Policies must be designed not just for short-term gains but to ensure long-term development. A government that prioritizes public welfare must also be open to (1) __ and citizen feedback. However, even well-meaning policies can fail if poorly implemented. Coordination between departments and timely communication are (2) __ for achieving outcomes. Public awareness and access to accurate information also help in reducing (3) __ in governance. Digital platforms and e-governance tools have made it easier for citizens to track services, report grievances, and (4) __ participation. A responsive and inclusive government must constantly evaluate its policies to match the changing needs of society. Ultimately, policy-making must be guided by both data and (5) __ values.

question.en:
Electric vehicles (EVs) promise lower emissions, quieter cities, and reduced dependence on fossil fuels. However, the transition to electric mobility requires substantial investment in charging infrastructure, reliable electricity grids, and sustainable battery production. (A) ________ policymakers must recognize that technological innovation alone cannot guarantee widespread adoption. Consumer confidence depends on affordability, charging availability, battery longevity, and transparent regulatory standards.
Although EVs reduce tailpipe emissions, irresponsible mining practices may (B) ________ ecological degradation in resource-rich regions if environmental safeguards remain inadequate. Governments, industries, and research institutions must therefore develop cleaner extraction techniques and promote battery recycling and alternative materials.
If governments (C) ________ clear and consistent policy incentives, consumers would feel more confident about investing in electric vehicles despite their higher initial costs. Such confidence may encourage manufacturers to expand production and reduce prices. Equally important is the creation of an (D) ________ that rewards innovation without discouraging fair competition. Long-term industrial growth also depends on institutional credibility and predictable governance.
Ultimately, the success of electric mobility will be determined by society's willingness to invest (E) ________ a comprehensive transition that balances environmental responsibility, economic practicality, and social equity.

Identify the correct discourse marker for blank (A). [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 19/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Context: The preceding sentence states that the transition requires substantial investments; the following clause concludes that policymakers must consequently take proactive measures.
Connector: Therefore shows logical consequence/deduction based on the stated prerequisite needs.

question.en:
In increasingly interdependent ecosystems, trust is no longer a soft virtue but a strategic asset that determines institutional resilience. While many organizations profess commitment to transparency, such declarations often fail to __ (A) under scrutiny when operational opacity persists beneath performative disclosure. Moreover, stakeholders are increasingly unwilling to __ (B) rhetorical assurances, particularly when prior breaches of confidence have not been adequately redressed. This skepticism is further amplified in digital environments where information asymmetry and rapid dissemination of partial narratives distort institutional intent. In such contexts, leaders must __ (C) reputational capital with caution, as overextension of goodwill may precipitate a rapid erosion of legitimacy. Nevertheless, trust deficits, once entrenched, do not easily __ (D) through cosmetic reforms or episodic outreach initiatives. Such dynamics underscore the importance of aligning formal governance structures with informal norms of accountability. Consequently, reputational repair requires sustained behavioral consistency rather than episodic signaling exercises that merely project responsiveness without substantive change. Therefore, institutions that consistently align incentives with ethical imperatives are more likely to __ (E) enduring legitimacy across shifting socio-political landscapes. Without such alignment, even well-designed frameworks risk gradual erosion of stakeholder confidence.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (A). [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 22/09/26 Shift 1]

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (B). [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 22/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The phrasal verb buy into means to completely accept, believe, or subscribe to an idea or assertion.
The context notes that skeptical stakeholders are unwilling to "buy into rhetorical assurances."
"Buy over" and "buy off" mean to bribe someone, while "buy out" means to purchase a controlling interest in a business.

question.en:
Patience is a powerful virtue that shapes judgment, emotional stability, and long-term success. It is not passive endurance but an active mental discipline that improves decision-making and strengthens character.
Modern psychological studies, (A) ________ demonstrate that individuals who cultivate patience tend to exhibit greater resilience and better problem-solving abilities, suggest a strong link between delayed gratification and cognitive maturity. However, in a digitally accelerated world, instant outcomes are often prioritised, (B) ________ patience remains undervalued in both personal and professional life.
Many successful individuals attribute their achievements to their ability to (C) ________ short-term temptations and remain committed to long-term objectives. The capacity to endure uncertainty without frustration is a psychological skill that must be consciously developed. In this context, patience becomes (D) ________ framework through which individuals interpret setbacks as opportunities for growth rather than failures.
Cultivating patience requires consistent effort, self-awareness, and trust in processes that unfold gradually. Through such discipline, individuals place themselves (E) ________ a more thoughtful and enduring path towards success.

Choose the correct option to fill blank (A). [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 24/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Blank (A) requires a reduced relative clause (past participle modifier) modifying 'Modern psychological studies'.
Designed to correctly acts as an adjectival participle phrase meaning 'which are designed to'.
The other options are grammatically incorrect in this syntactic position.

question.en:
Complete the following passage by filling in the blanks with the most appropriate words from the options given below.
Oceanic literature has long been obscured by Western perspectives that view the sea as a vast, empty void between "significant" landmasses. In the imperial imagination, the ocean was (A)________ a highway for trade or a barrier to be conquered. This "terra-centric" view effectively erased the complex histories and cultures of the peoples who lived upon and with the water.
Modern Pacific writers, however, are reclaiming this space, asserting that the ocean is a connector (B)________ than a divider. They describe the sea not as a desert of salt, but as a "sea of islands" interconnected by ancient voyaging routes. This shift in perspective transforms the ocean from a site of transit into a site of profound cultural belonging and identity.
Had the early colonial cartographers respected the indigenous seafaring traditions and navigational charts, the maps of today might look very different. Instead of vast blue expanses labelled as "unexplored", we would see a web of ancestral pathways. The refusal to acknowledge these traditions was a deliberate act of (C)________ silencing that facilitated colonial expansion.
Though these narratives are often marginalised in global literary curricula, they provide a vital counter-history antithetical (D)________ the standard tales of discovery. They challenge the idea that history only happens on land. By centring the ocean, these authors force us to reconsider the fluidity of borders and the permanence of cultural ties.
Their prose is often (E)________ with metaphors of fluidity and currents, challenging the rigid, static borders imposed by imperial powers. This literature does not just tell a story; it performs an act of decolonisation. It reminds us that for those who call the ocean home, the water is the most solid ground they know.

Fill in the blank (A) with an adverb that indicates a diminished viewpoint in this context. [SSC Selection Post (12th) 16/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Context: The question specifically asks for an adverb indicating a diminished viewpoint.
Merely signifies "only" or "nothing more than", underscoring how imperial perspectives narrowly diminished the ocean to just a trade route or barrier.
Other options: Scarcely means barely/hardly; Negligibly means to an insignificant degree; Minimally means to the smallest extent possible.

question.en:
Complete the following passage by filling in the blanks with the most appropriate words from the options given below.
Phenomenology suggests that time is not a series of discrete, ticking moments but a continuous, indivisible flow of consciousness. We do not experience life as a succession of "nows" like beads on a string. (A) __, our consciousness "protends" and "retains", pulling the past and the future into every single instant of awareness.
Our perception of a "now" is constantly (B) __ by our memories of what has just occurred and our anticipations of what is about to happen. When you listen to a melody, you don't hear isolated notes; you hear the relationship between the note playing now and the ones that preceded it. The "now" is always pregnant with the "next".
Were we to experience a moment in total isolation, stripped of all context and memory, it (C) __ to have any human meaning. It would be a "flash" without a narrative, a sensation without a self. Our very identity is built upon the temporal continuity that phenomenology seeks to describe and analyse.
While objective clocks measure seconds with mechanical precision, the "lived time" of the individual is notoriously elastic. An hour spent in a state of flow can feel like minutes, while a minute of intense physical pain can feel like an eternity. The clock is a social (D) __ ; the experience of duration is a biological and psychological reality.
This subjective stretching of duration is what makes a moment of joy feel fleeting and a moment of dread feel interminable. We are not mere observers of time; we are the medium (E) __ which time gains its quality. To understand the human condition, we must look beyond the stopwatch and into the shifting currents of internal experience.

Choose the correct adverb to begin the sentence: (A) [SSC Selection Post (12th) 17/09/26 Shift 2]

Complete the following passage by filling in the blanks with the most appropriate words from the options given below.
Phenomenology suggests that time is not a series of discrete, ticking moments but a continuous, indivisible flow of consciousness. We do not experience life as a succession of "nows" like beads on a string. (A), our consciousness "protends" and "retains", pulling the past and the future into every single instant of awareness.
Our perception of a "now" is constantly (B) by our memories of what has just occurred and our anticipations of what is about to happen. When you listen to a melody, you don't hear isolated notes; you hear the relationship between the note playing now and the ones that preceded it. The "now" is always pregnant with the "next".
Were we to experience a moment in total isolation, stripped of all context and memory, it (C) to have any human meaning. It would be a "flash" without a narrative, a sensation without a self. Our very identity is built upon the temporal continuity that phenomenology seeks to describe and analyse.
While objective clocks measure seconds with mechanical precision, the "lived time" of the individual is notoriously elastic. An hour spent in a state of flow can feel like minutes, while a minute of intense physical pain can feel like an eternity. The clock is a social (D) ; the experience of duration is a biological and psychological reality.
This subjective stretching of duration is what makes a moment of joy feel fleeting and a moment of dread feel interminable. We are not mere observers of time; we are the medium (E) which time gains its quality. To understand the human condition, we must look beyond the stopwatch and into the shifting currents of internal experience.
Fill in the blank (B) with the word that means "to be fastened to a fixed point". [SSC Selection Post (12th) 17/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Clue: The prompt explicitly asks for a word meaning "to be fastened to a fixed point". Tethered accurately denotes being tied, anchored, or fastened to an anchor point, describing how our awareness is bound to past and future.
Other options differ in definition: 'deterred' means discouraged, 'festered' means deteriorated or become inflamed, and 'sutured' means surgically stitched.

question.en:
The Gothic cathedral was never intended to be merely a shelter or a place of assembly; it was a stone encyclopedia meant to be "read" by the illiterate masses. In an age where books were rare and literacy was a privilege (A) _______ the elite, the church used architecture to communicate theology. Every carving, window and arch was a word in a silent sermon.
Every spire reaching toward the heavens and every grotesque gargoyle perched on the eaves conveyed a specific theological or moral message. The heights inspired awe and humility, while the frightening figures served as reminders of the spiritual dangers (B) _______ outside the sacred space. It was an immersive experience designed to bypass the intellect and speak directly to the soul.
To the medieval mind, the cathedral would have represented the physical bridge between the celestial and the terrestrial. Standing in the nave, bathed in the "divine light" of stained glass, the peasant felt a proximity to the divine that was (C) _______ unavailable. The building was a portal, a physical manifestation of the Kingdom of Heaven on Earth.
Because the structural innovations, like the flying buttress, allowed for towering heights and thinner walls, the primary intent remained spiritual rather than technical. The engineering was a (D) _______ to an end the creation of a space that felt unburdened by the weight of the world. The triumph of light over stone was a metaphor for the triumph of the spirit over the flesh.
However, this intricate architectural language remains impenetrable to those who lack a (E) _______ in medieval symbolism. Modern visitors often see the beauty but miss the "text". To truly understand the Gothic style, one must learn to look at the stone not just as a material, but as a medium of complex, coded communication.

Choose the preposition to collocate with the word "privilege" and fill in the blank (A). [SSC Selection Post (12th) 19/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: The standard noun phrase is privilege of, signifying that literacy belonged exclusively to that specific group ("a privilege of the elite").
Thus, of correctly fills blank (A).

question.en:
In the modern digital age, the shift toward algorithmic governance suggests a world where human bias is replaced by the cold, mathematical precision of code. From credit scoring to judicial sentencing, automated systems are being integrated into the very fabric of institutional decision-making. The promise is one of efficiency and radical neutrality, (A) __ away the subjective whims of human administrators.
However, this perceived neutrality is often illusory; algorithms are, after all, trained on historical data that inevitably (B) __ the prejudices of the past. If the training data contains systemic biases against certain demographics, the machine learns those patterns as "truths". Far from eliminating discrimination, the algorithm may simply hide it behind a veneer of technical objectivity.
Should a predictive policing system be designed to identify high-risk neighbourhoods, it might inadvertently codify and amplify existing systemic inequalities. By targeting areas that were already over-policed due to historical bias, the system creates a feedback loop. The "math" then appears to justify the (C) __ targeting of those same communities, creating a cycle that is difficult to break.
(D) __ these tools offer undeniable efficiency in processing vast amounts of data, they lack the "moral imagination" required for true justice. A machine can identify a statistical correlation, but it cannot understand the nuance of human circumstance or the socio-economic context behind a data point. It treats humans as static variables rather than evolving individuals.
This creates a dangerous (E) __ where the pursuit of objective fairness results in the automated replication of historical harm. As we outsource our judgement to software, we risk losing the ability to hold systems accountable. We must ensure that the drive for technological progress does not come at the expense of the very equity we seek to achieve.

Which word best completes blank (A) to show the effect of 'radical neutrality'? [SSC Selection Post (12th) 21/09/26 Shift 2]
question.hi:
In the modern digital age, the shift toward algorithmic governance suggests a world where human bias is replaced by the cold, mathematical precision of code. From credit scoring to judicial sentencing, automated systems are being integrated into the very fabric of institutional decision-making. The promise is one of efficiency and radical neutrality, (A) away the subjective whims of human administrators.
However, this perceived neutrality is often illusory; algorithms are, after all, trained on historical data that inevitably (B) the prejudices of the past. If the training data contains systemic biases against certain demographics, the machine learns those patterns as "truths". Far from eliminating discrimination, the algorithm may simply hide it behind a veneer of technical objectivity.
Should a predictive policing system be designed to identify high-risk neighbourhoods, it might inadvertently codify and amplify existing systemic inequalities. By targeting areas that were already over-policed due to historical bias, the system creates a feedback loop. The "math" then appears to justify the (C) targeting of those same communities, creating a cycle that is difficult to break.
(D) these tools offer undeniable efficiency in processing vast amounts of data, they lack the "moral imagination" required for true justice. A machine can identify a statistical correlation, but it cannot understand the nuance of human circumstance or the socio-economic context behind a data point. It treats humans as static variables rather than evolving individuals.
This creates a dangerous (E) where the pursuit of objective fairness results in the automated replication of historical harm. As we outsource our judgement to software, we risk losing the ability to hold systems accountable. We must ensure that the drive for technological progress does not come at the expense of the very equity we seek to achieve.
Which word best completes blank (A) to show the effect of 'radical neutrality'? [SSC Selection Post (12th) 21/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: A present participle clause (-ing form) is required to function as a participle clause modifying the preceding clause and expressing an accompanying result or effect of "radical neutrality".
Therefore, stripping correctly completes the phrase "stripping away the subjective whims of human administrators."

In an age of instant messages and constant notifications, the ability to read deeply has become increasingly rare. Deep reading does not merely mean moving one's eyes over printed words; it requires attention, patience and the willingness to follow an argument from its beginning to its conclusion. A reader who is always (1) __ by digital alerts may gather information quickly, but he seldom understands it fully. Schools, therefore, must not treat reading as a mechanical exercise. They should encourage students to question ideas, connect them with experience and reflect (2) __ what they have read. Such habits help learners develop judgement rather than simply collect facts. When reading is practised regularly, it also improves writing, because the mind absorbs patterns of clear expression. Many students avoid difficult texts because they appear demanding at first, yet these texts often give (3) __ to the most valuable insights. The challenge is not to make every passage easy, but to teach students how to stay with complexity without giving up. A society that values serious reading is likely to produce citizens who are less (4) __ to rumours and more capable of independent thought. Thus, reading is not a luxury; it is a discipline that strengthens both language and reason. Its importance will remain (5) __ even as technology changes the ways in which people receive information.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. (1) [SSC Selection Post (12th) 22/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Collocation and meaning: The adjective prone followed by the preposition to means susceptible, vulnerable, or likely to suffer from something undesirable.

question.en:
The human brain's ability to rewire itself, a phenomenon known as neuroplasticity, is most evident during early childhood development. This period of high "synaptic pruning" allows the brain to specialise, based on the specific stimuli it receives from the environment. It is the reason children can learn multiple languages with an ease that adults often find (A) __.
It is during this "critical period" that children internalise the complex, underlying rules of abstract syntax without any formal instruction. They don't just mimic sounds; they (B) __ the deep structural logic of their native tongue. This innate capacity for grammar suggests that the human mind is biologically "pre-wired" for linguistic complexity.
If a child were deprived of linguistic input during these formative years, the window for achieving native-level fluency might close forever. Cases of "feral children" have shown that (C) __ vocabulary can be acquired later in life, the subtle mastery of syntax-the ability to weave thoughts into complex structures-is almost impossible to recover once the critical window shuts.
Since neuroplasticity continues into adulthood, it does so at a significantly diminished rate. The adult brain is more stable and less "malleable", which is beneficial for maintaining long-term memories but detrimental for the rapid acquisition of entirely new systems of thought. Learning a language at forty is a cognitive (D) __ ; at four, it is an effortless absorption.
This biological constraint highlights the (E) __ nature of language acquisition, where timing is as critical as the stimulus itself. It serves as a reminder that our cognitive architecture is not just a product of our will but a reflection of a strictly timed biological schedule. To master the mind, one must first understand the clock by which it grows.

question.en:
Complete the following passage by filling in the blanks with the most appropriate words from the options given below.
The prospect of "de-extinction" has moved from the realm of (A) __ science fiction to the high-tech laboratory, yet the moral landscape governing such ventures remains profoundly ambiguous. While the ability to sequence ancient DNA is a marvel of modern genomics, the ethical framework required to manage the consequences is still in its infancy. We are, in essence, attempting to rewrite natural history without a full grasp of the original narrative.
While the technical prowess required to revive a species is immense, the ecological ramifications are even more significant. Introducing a long-lost herbivore into a modern ecosystem could trigger a trophic (B) __ that shifts the entire balance of local flora and fauna. These environments have evolved for millennia in the absence of such creatures, and a sudden reintroduction could be more disruptive than restorative.
There is also a significant opportunity cost associated with these "vanity" projects. Critics argue that we might better spend our finite resources on protecting extant species that are currently facing (C) __ threats of extinction. Diverting funds toward the resurrection of the woolly mammoth may inadvertently accelerate the demise of the living elephant species we still have left.
Furthermore, the reintroduced species might find itself a "biological orphan", bereft (D) __ the social structures and environmental cues it once thrived upon. A mammoth born to a surrogate elephant mother would lack the ancestral knowledge of migration patterns and social hierarchies. It would be a creature displaced in time, existing as a lonely curiosity rather than a functional member of a biological community.
Ultimately, the question is not whether we possess the genetic tools to reach into the past, but whether we ought to proceed. Just because a scientific "could" exists doesn't (E) __ a moral "should" follows. We must decide if our role is to be the restorers of the past or the responsible guardians of the present.

solution.en:
Rule: After the auxiliary contraction doesn't (does not), the base form of the main verb (V1) is required.
Therefore, the base form mean correctly completes the clause "doesn't mean a moral 'should' follows."
The inflected forms means, meant, and meaning are grammatically incorrect after doesn't.

question.en:
The old lighthouse had stood on the jagged cliffs of Blackwood Bay for over a century, its lantern room long since emptied of its rotating flame. To the townsfolk below, the structure was a relic of a bygone era, yet for Elias, the retired keeper, it remained the only place where the world felt coherent. He spent his afternoons in the small circular room atop the spiral stairs, (A) the rhythmic crashing of the Atlantic against the rocks below.
He often wondered about the rapidly changing modern world. Today's sailors did not need his guidance. They relied on satellite pings and digital charts, (B) their predecessors had eagerly looked for the steady, reassuring blink of his beacon to navigate the treacherous waters. There was a certain coldness to the new technology, a lack of human connection that Elias found difficult to (C). He believed that a machine could tell you where you were, but it could never tell you that you were safe.
One evening, a storm of unprecedented ferocity swept in from the north, knocking out the town's power grid and plunging the bay into total darkness. In the sudden silence of the digital age, the people felt a (D) fear they had long-forgotten. Elias reached into his heavy oak cabinet and pulled out a rusted iron key. He knew that the emergency oil lamps were still in the cellar. As he struck a match and the first spark caught, the golden glow reflected in his eyes. For the panicking residents of the tiny coastal town, the flickering light wasn't a sign of outdated tech, but a beacon (E) hope.

Choose the grammatically correct option to fill in the blank (A). [SSC Selection Post (10th) 16/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en: Rule: The present participle phrase modifies the action of spending afternoons. 'Listen' is an intransitive verb that requires the preposition 'to' before its object ('the rhythmic crashing'). Thus, listening to is grammatically correct.

A chip ecosystem depends on a steady supply of engineers, technicians and researchers with highly_(1)_ skills. Training programmes therefore need to be aligned with industry requirements rather than designed in a purely _(2) manner. Experts also warn that policy enthusiasm must be matched by patient investment, because this sector is too capital-intensive to reward _(3). If institutions, firms and governments work in close _(4), the country can gradually reduce dependence on imports. Without such coordination, bold announcements may produce publicity, but little enduring _(5).

Choose the most suitable word for blank (1). [SSC Selection Post (10th) 19/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Semiconductor fabrication is a high-tech field that requires specific, advanced skills; thus, specialised fits contextually.
Words like casual, domestic, or redundant do not fit the requirement of technical expertise.

question.en:
Complete the following passage by filling in the blanks with the most appropriate words from the options given below.
The silent vacuum of low-Earth orbit, once the exclusive playground of superpower governments, is rapidly becoming a crowded marketplace. As private aerospace firms (A)________ down the cost of launches, the deployment of "megaconstellations", thousands of small satellites designed to provide global internet coverage, (B)________ an all-time high.
This influx of hardware is not without its consequences. For astronomers whose work depends on pristine views of the night sky, these streaks of (C)________ sunlight represent a significant barrier to deep-space observation. The legal framework governing outer space remains dangerously outdated, and there is (D)________ clear consensus on whether a corporation can claim ownership of resources extracted from celestial bodies.
The most pressing concern, however, is the accumulation of orbital debris. Every spent rocket stage and defunct satellite adds to a growing cloud of "space junk" that circles the planet at lethal speeds. If a single collision occurs, it could trigger a chain reaction, known as the Kessler Syndrome, (E)________ certain orbits inaccessible for generations. Engineers are now racing to develop "harpoon" and "net" technologies for removing the largest pieces of debris before such a catastrophe occurs.

Choose the correct word to fill in the blank (A) and complete the phrasal verb. [SSC Selection Post (10th) 21/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The phrasal verb drive down means to force down or reduce prices/costs significantly.
Here, private aerospace firms 'drive down' the launch costs.
The other verbs ('turn down', 'rope down', 'wave down') do not form the intended meaning.

solution.en:

Social media platforms have reshaped how people perceive reality. Algorithms tailor content to individual preferences, creating echo chambers where users mostly see what aligns with their views. This personalization limits exposure to diverse opinions and can distort one's understanding of events. Additionally, carefully curated posts-highlighting success, beauty, or wealth-can lead to unrealistic comparisons and lowered self-esteem. Studies show that frequent exposure to such content may affect mental health, especially among youth. What's more, misinformation spreads quickly, often blurring the line between fact and opinion. To counter this, users need digital literacy and a critical mindset. Awareness of algorithmic influence helps in making more balanced judgments. In a world where perception often shapes action, conscious media consumption is not just beneficial-it's essential.

question.en:
In a digital era saturated with information, distinguishing fact from opinion has become increasingly difficult. News is often tailored to attract attention rather than inform, blurring the line between journalism and entertainment. This trend has significant implications for public opinion, as emotionally charged headlines can shape perceptions more than verified facts. Algorithms on social media further intensify this effect by filtering content based on prior user behavior, creating echo chambers. In such environments, individuals are more likely to encounter views they already agree with, reinforcing biases instead of challenging them. Media literacy, therefore, is essential. It involves the ability to critically evaluate sources, check for credibility, and recognize manipulative techniques. Without these skills, citizens risk forming views based on partial or misleading information. An informed public is not just a democratic ideal-it's a necessity in an age where truth can easily be distorted.

What is the primary concern the passage raises about modern news? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 23/09/26 Shift 1]

3.en: News often prioritizes attention over accuracy

solution.en: The passage directly states: "News is often tailored to attract attention rather than inform, blurring the line between journalism and entertainment." Thus, the author's primary concern is that news prioritizes attention over accuracy.

question.en:
Human decision-making is rarely based on logic alone; emotion, bias, and perception play critical roles, especially in assessing risk. Psychologists have observed that people often fear unlikely events-such as airplane crashes-more than common dangers like car accidents. This "availability heuristic" leads individuals to judge risks based on how easily examples come to mind, not on actual probability. Moreover, emotions like fear or excitement can distort rational thinking. People also tend to avoid losses more strongly than they pursue gains, a concept known as "loss aversion." This is why investors might hold on to failing stocks rather than accept a small loss. Understanding these psychological patterns can improve personal and policy-level decisions. Rather than eliminating emotion, effective risk management involves recognizing how it influences choices. Awareness of these tendencies allows individuals to make more balanced, informed decisions in uncertain situations.

question.en: What does a Therapeutic Use Exemption (TUE) allow an athlete to do under anti-doping regulations? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 17/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: डोपिंग रोधी नियमों के तहत चिकित्सीय उपयोग छूट (TUE) एक एथलीट को क्या करने की अनुमति देती है? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 17/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Use any performance-enhancing drug without restriction
1.hi: बिना किसी प्रतिबंध के किसी भी प्रदर्शन बढ़ाने वाली दवा का उपयोग करना

2.en: Use a prohibited substance or method for medical treatment with official approval
2.hi: आधिकारिक अनुमोदन के साथ चिकित्सा उपचार के लिए एक प्रतिबंधित पदार्थ या विधि का उपयोग करना

3.en: Avoid undergoing doping tests during competition
3.hi: प्रतियोगिता के दौरान डोपिंग परीक्षणों से गुजरने से बचना

4.en: Transfer responsibility of doping violations to the team doctor
4.hi: डोपिंग उल्लंघनों की जिम्मेदारी टीम के डॉक्टर को हस्तांतरित करना

solution.en:
A Therapeutic Use Exemption (TUE) granted by anti-doping bodies permits an athlete suffering from an illness or medical condition to use an otherwise prohibited substance or method strictly for therapeutic treatment without committing an anti-doping rule violation.
Important Facts:
- TUEs are regulated globally under the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) International Standard for TUEs.
- Athletes must apply and provide clinical documentation from a physician demonstrating significant health impairment if untreated.
- Approval requires evidence that no reasonable non-prohibited therapeutic alternative exists.
- The use of the substance must not produce any additional enhancement of athletic performance beyond returning to normal health.
- In India, national-level TUE applications are evaluated by the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) TUE Committee.
solution.hi:
डोपिंग रोधी नियमों के तहत चिकित्सीय उपयोग छूट (TUE) किसी वैध बीमारी या चिकित्सा स्थिति से पीड़ित एथलीट को उचित चिकित्सा उपचार के लिए आधिकारिक अनुमति के साथ प्रतिबंधित पदार्थ या पद्धति का उपयोग करने की स्वीकृति देती है, जिससे वह डोपिंग उल्लंघन का दोषी नहीं माना जाता।
महत्वपूर्ण तथ्य:
- TUE को वैश्विक स्तर पर विश्व डोपिंग रोधी एजेंसी (WADA) के अंतरराष्ट्रीय मानकों के अनुसार विनियमित किया जाता है।
- एथलीट को यह प्रमाणित करने के लिए चिकित्सक से विस्तृत नैदानिक दस्तावेज प्रस्तुत करने होते हैं।
- अनुमोदन प्राप्त करने के लिए यह साबित करना अनिवार्य है कि कोई गैर-प्रतिबंधित चिकित्सीय विकल्प उपलब्ध नहीं है।
- इस छूट के तहत दवा के प्रयोग से सामान्य स्वास्थ्य बहाली के अतिरिक्त कोई अतिरिक्त खेल प्रदर्शन लाभ नहीं मिलना चाहिए।
- भारत में राष्ट्रीय स्तर पर TUE आवेदनों का मूल्यांकन राष्ट्रीय डोपिंग रोधी एजेंसी (NADA) की समिति करती है।

question.en: Raas Leela is a classical dance form of which state? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 17/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: रास लीला किस राज्य का एक शास्त्रीय नृत्य रूप है? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 17/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Manipuri Raas Leela** is one of the eight major Indian classical dance traditions, originating in the state of **Manipur**. It is deeply centered around themes of Vaishnavism, depicting the divine love and pastimes of Radha and Lord Krishna.
**Important Facts:**
- The institutionalization of Raas Leela in Manipuri dance is credited to **Maharaja Bhagyachandra** (Ningthou Ching-Thang Khomba) in the 18th century.
- Dancers wear a cylindrical, barrel-shaped stiff skirt called the **Kumil** or Potloi.
- The movements in Manipuri dance are graceful, lyrical, and fluid, avoiding sharp jerks.
- The musical accompaniment includes the **Pung** (cylindrical drum) and small kartals (cymbals).
- Raas Leela dance was designated an element of UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage through Sankirtana.
solution.hi:
**मणिपुरी रास लीला** भारत के प्रमुख आठ शास्त्रीय नृत्यों में से एक है, जो **मणिपुर** राज्य की पावन सांस्कृतिक परंपरा है। यह वैष्णव धर्म के भक्ति भाव पर आधारित है और राधा-कृष्ण के दिव्य प्रेम तथा लीलाओं का मंचन करता है।
**महत्वपूर्ण तथ्य:**
- मणिपुरी रास लीला के शास्त्रीय स्वरूप और वेशभूषा की स्थापना का श्रेय 18वीं सदी के **महाराजा भाग्यचंद्र** को जाता है।
- इस नृत्य में नृत्यांगनाएं एक विशेष बेलनाकार चमकदार घाघरा पहनती हैं जिसे **कुमिल** (पोटलोई) कहा जाता है।
- मणिपुरी नृत्य की शारीरिक गतियां अत्यंत सौम्य, सुंदर और लहरदार होती हैं, जिनमें कठोर झटकों का अभाव होता है।
- इस नृत्य का मुख्य वाद्य यंत्र **पुंग** (मणिपुरी ढोल) और करताल (मंजीरा) है।
- मणिपुर के संकीर्तन और रास लीला को यूनेस्को की अमूर्त सांस्कृतिक विरासत में विशेष मान्यता प्राप्त है।

question.en: Which of the following is a correctly matched pair of a traditional folk dance with its corresponding state? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 17/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा पारंपरिक लोक नृत्य और उसके संबंधित राज्य का सही सुमेलित युग्म है? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 17/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Kud** is a celebratory folk dance performed by the locals in the hilly regions of **Jammu and Kashmir** after the harvest. The other options are incorrect: Karma is primarily associated with Jharkhand, MP, and Chhattisgarh; Chai Lam is a folk dance of Mizoram; and Dollu Kunitha belongs to Karnataka.
**Important Facts:**
- **Kud dance** is performed during the night to thank the local Gram Devata (deity) for protecting crops and cattle.
- Traditional instruments accompanying the Kud dance include the **Narsingha**, flute, and drums.
- **Dollu Kunitha** is a famous high-energy drum dance indigenous to **Karnataka**.
- **Chheihlam** (Chhai Lam) is a traditional festive dance native to **Mizoram**.
- **Karma dance** is widely practiced by tribes like Oraon, Baiga, and Gond across central and eastern India.
solution.hi:
**कूद** लोक नृत्य **जम्मू और कश्मीर** के पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में अच्छी फसल की कटाई के बाद ग्रामीणों द्वारा किया जाने वाला एक पारंपरिक नृत्य है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि करमा मुख्यतः झारखंड/मध्य प्रदेश/छत्तीसगढ़ से, छाई लम मिजोरम से और डोल्लू कुनिथा कर्नाटक से संबंधित है।
**महत्वपूर्ण तथ्य:**
- **कूद नृत्य** मुख्य रूप से फसलों और मवेशियों की सुरक्षा के लिए ग्राम देवता के प्रति आभार व्यक्त करने हेतु रात में किया जाता है।
- इस नृत्य के दौरान **नरसिंगा**, बांसुरी और ढोलक जैसे पारंपरिक वाद्ययंत्र बजाए जाते हैं।
- **डोल्लू कुनिथा** बड़े ढोलों के साथ प्रस्तुत किया जाने वाला **कर्नाटक** का प्रसिद्ध लोक नृत्य है।
- **छाई लम** (Chheihlam) **मिजोरम** राज्य का एक अत्यंत लोकप्रिय पारंपरिक उत्सव नृत्य है।
- **करमा नृत्य** पूर्वी और मध्य भारत की उरांव, बैगा और गोंड जनजातियों द्वारा करम उत्सव पर किया जाता है।

question.en: As per 2011 census, which 'State' had the highest proportion of the Scheduled Tribe (ST) population relative to its total population? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 17/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: 2011 की जनगणना के अनुसार, अपनी कुल जनसंख्या के सापेक्ष अनुसूचित जनजाति (ST) जनसंख्या का उच्चतम अनुपात किस 'राज्य' में था? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 17/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
According to the 2011 Census of India, **Mizoram** had the highest percentage of Scheduled Tribe population among all Indian states at **$94.4\%$**.
**Important Facts:**
- Among Union Territories, **Lakshadweep** had the highest ST proportion with **$94.8\%$**.
- Nagaland ranked second among states with an ST population percentage of approximately **$86.5\%$**.
- In terms of absolute numbers of ST population, **Madhya Pradesh** ranks first in India.
- States with no notified Scheduled Tribes include **Punjab, Haryana**, and the UTs of Delhi, Chandigarh, and Puducherry.
- The Scheduled Tribes comprise approximately **$8.6\%$** of the total population of India as per the 2011 Census.
solution.hi:
2011 की जनगणना के अनुसार, भारत के सभी राज्यों में **मिजोरम** में अपनी कुल आबादी के अनुपात में अनुसूचित जनजाति (ST) का प्रतिशत सबसे अधिक था, जो **$94.4\%$** दर्ज किया गया था।
**महत्वपूर्ण तथ्य:**
- केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में **लक्षद्वीप** में अनुसूचित जनजाति की आबादी का अनुपात सबसे अधिक (**$94.8\%$**) था।
- राज्यों में नागालैंड दूसरे स्थान पर था, जहां एसटी आबादी का अनुपात लगभग **$86.5\%$** था।
- अनुसूचित जनजाति की कुल निरपेक्ष (संख्यात्मक) जनसंख्या के मामले में **मध्य प्रदेश** देश में प्रथम स्थान पर है।
- **पंजाब और हरियाणा** राज्यों तथा दिल्ली, चंडीगढ़ और पुडुचेरी केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में कोई अनुसूचित जनजाति अधिसूचित नहीं है।
- 2011 की जनगणना के अनुसार भारत की कुल जनसंख्या में अनुसूचित जनजाति (ST) की हिस्सेदारी लगभग **$8.6\%$** है।

question.en: In Indian temple architecture, which feature distinguishes a Sandhara temple? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 17/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: भारतीय मंदिर वास्तुकला में, कौन सी विशेषता सांधार मंदिर को अलग करती है? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 17/09/26 Shift 1]

2.hi: किसी भी प्रदक्षिणा पथ का अभाव होना

solution.en:
In classical Indian temple architecture, a **Sandhara** temple is classified by the presence of an enclosed **circumambulatory pathway (pradakshina patha)** around the sanctum sanctorum (garbhagriha).
**Important Facts:**
- In contrast, a temple built without an enclosed circumambulatory pathway is termed a **Nirandhara** temple.
- A temple having an open-pillared gallery or circumambulatory path that is accessible all around is known as **Sarvatobhadra**.
- The innermost chamber where the principal deity is consecrated is called the **Garbhagriha** (womb chamber).
- The ambulatory path allows devotees to perform **Pradakshina** (clockwise circumambulation) around the deity.
- This structural classification applies across both **Nagara** (North Indian) and **Dravida** (South Indian) temple styles.
solution.hi:
भारतीय मंदिर वास्तुकला के शास्त्रीय वर्गीकरण में, **सांधार** प्रकार के मंदिर की मुख्य विशेषता गर्भगृह के चारों ओर एक ढके हुए आंतरिक **प्रदक्षिणा पथ** की उपस्थिति होती है।
**महत्वपूर्ण तथ्य:**
- इसके विपरीत, जिस मंदिर में गर्भगृह के चारों ओर प्रदक्षिणा पथ नहीं होता, उसे **निरांधार** मंदिर कहा जाता है।
- जिस मंदिर में सभी दिशाओं से प्रवेश द्वार और खुला परिक्रमा गलियारा होता है, उसे **सर्वतोभद्र** मंदिर कहा जाता है।
- मुख्य मंदिर का वह आंतरिक कक्ष जहाँ मुख्य देवता की मूर्ति स्थापित की जाती है, **गर्भगृह** कहलाता है।
- प्रदक्षिणा पथ श्रद्धालुओं को अपने आराध्य की घड़ी की सुई की दिशा में परिक्रमा करने की सुविधा देता है।
- यह संरचनात्मक वर्गीकरण **नागर** (उत्तर भारतीय) और **द्रविड़** (दक्षिण भारतीय) दोनों स्थापत्य शैलियों पर समान रूप से लागू होता है।

question.en: Which of the following substances is banned by anti-doping agencies? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा पदार्थ डोपिंग रोधी एजेंसियों द्वारा प्रतिबंधित है? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS) are synthetic derivatives of testosterone banned by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) because they artificially enhance muscle growth, strength, and athletic performance.
Important Facts:
- The World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) was established in 1999 with headquarters in Montreal, Canada.
- In India, anti-doping regulations are enforced by the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA), set up in 2005.
- Common banned anabolic steroids include nandrolone, stanozolol, and boldenone.
- WADA publishes an updated Prohibited List annually, effective on January 1 of each year.
- Common dietary supplements such as vitamins and standard protein powders are not banned under WADA rules.
solution.hi:
एनाबॉलिक-एंड्रोजेनिक स्टेरॉयड (AAS) टेस्टोस्टेरोन के सिंथेटिक व्युत्पन्न हैं जिन्हें विश्व डोपिंग रोधी एजेंसी (WADA) द्वारा प्रतिबंधित किया गया है क्योंकि वे मांसपेशियों के विकास, शक्ति और प्रदर्शन को कृत्रिम रूप से बढ़ाते हैं।
महत्वपूर्ण तथ्य:
- विश्व डोपिंग रोधी एजेंसी (WADA) की स्थापना 1999 में हुई थी और इसका मुख्यालय मॉन्ट्रियल, कनाडा में है।
- भारत में, डोपिंग रोधी नियमों को राष्ट्रीय डोपिंग रोधी एजेंसी (NADA) द्वारा लागू किया जाता है, जिसकी स्थापना 2005 में हुई थी।
- प्रमुख प्रतिबंधित एनाबॉलिक स्टेरॉयड में नैंड्रोलोन, स्टैनोज़ोलोल और बोल्डेनोने शामिल हैं।
- वाडा (WADA) प्रतिवर्ष एक अद्यतन प्रतिबंधित सूची प्रकाशित करता है, जो प्रत्येक वर्ष 1 जनवरी से प्रभावी होती है।
- सामान्य आहार पूरक जैसे विटामिन और मानक प्रोटीन पाउडर वाडा के नियमों के तहत प्रतिबंधित नहीं हैं।

question.en: Which country won the highest number of gold medals in the 2023 Asian Games? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: 2023 के एशियाई खेलों में किस देश ने सर्वाधिक स्वर्ण पदक जीते? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Host nation China dominated the medal tally at the 19th Asian Games held in Hangzhou in 2023, finishing at the top with a record 201 gold medals (and 383 total medals).
Important Facts:
- The 19th Asian Games took place in Hangzhou, China from September 23 to October 8, 2023.
- Japan finished second with 52 gold medals, followed by South Korea in third with 42 gold medals.
- India ranked 4th overall, achieving its best-ever medal haul of 107 medals (including 28 gold medals).
- The official motto of the Hangzhou Asian Games was "Heart to Heart, @Future".
- The first edition of the Asian Games was hosted in New Delhi, India in 1951.


Carry-forward fact
• The 20th Asian Games — Aichi–Nagoya, Japan (19 September–4 October 2026) — will feature 43 sports; Tokyo hosts the swimming and diving events, and Aichi–Nagoya are first-time hosts.
solution.hi:
2023 में हांगझू में आयोजित 19वें एशियाई खेलों में मेजबान देश चीन ने पदक तालिका में शीर्ष स्थान हासिल किया और रिकॉर्ड 201 स्वर्ण पदक (कुल 383 पदक) जीते।
महत्वपूर्ण तथ्य:
- 19वें एशियाई खेल 2023 में 23 सितंबर से 8 अक्टूबर तक हांगझू, चीन में आयोजित किए गए थे।
- जापान 52 स्वर्ण पदकों के साथ दूसरे स्थान पर रहा, जबकि दक्षिण कोरिया 42 स्वर्ण पदकों के साथ तीसरे स्थान पर रहा।
- भारत कुल तालिका में चौथे स्थान पर रहा, जिसने 28 स्वर्ण पदक सहित अपना सर्वश्रेष्ठ प्रदर्शन करते हुए कुल 107 पदक जीते।
- हांगझू एशियाई खेलों का आधिकारिक आदर्श वाक्य "Heart to Heart, @Future" था।
- एशियाई खेलों का पहला संस्करण 1951 में नई दिल्ली, भारत में आयोजित किया गया था।.


आगे का तथ्य
• 20वें एशियाई खेल — आइची–नागोया, जापान (19 सितंबर–4 अक्टूबर 2026) — में 43 खेल होंगे; तैराकी व डाइविंग टोक्यो में होंगे, और आइची–नागोया पहली बार मेज़बान हैं।

question.en: Which of the following French architectural elements is most commonly found in Pondicherry buildings? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा फ्रांसीसी स्थापत्य तत्व पांडिचेरी की इमारतों में सबसे अधिक पाया जाता है? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]

2.hi: प्याज के आकार के गुंबद (अनियन डोम)

solution.en:
The French Quarter (White Town) of **Puducherry (Pondicherry)** features colonial French architecture characterized by **arcaded courtyards**, colonnaded verandas, tall arched windows with louvered wooden shutters, and continuous street façades.
**Important Facts:**
- Puducherry was the principal settlement of the **French East India Company** in India from **1674 to 1954**.
- The historic town is divided into two distinct zones: the French Quarter (**Ville Blanche**) and the Tamil Quarter (**Ville Noire**).
- Prominent French landmarks include the **Aフランス Monument aux Morts** (War Memorial) and the **Church of the Sacred Heart of Jesus**.
- The town plan follows a distinctive French **gridiron pattern** with perpendicular streets.
- **François Martin** served as the first Governor-General of French Pondicherry.
solution.hi:
**पुडुचेरी (पांडिचेरी)** का फ्रेंच क्वार्टर (व्हाइट टाउन) औपनिवेशिक फ्रांसीसी वास्तुकला को प्रदर्शित करता है, जिसकी प्रमुख विशेषता **मेहराबदार आंगन (आर्केडेड कोर्टयार्ड)**, खंभों वाले बरामदे, लौवर वाले लकड़ी के शटर वाली ऊंची मेहराबदार खिड़कियां और सतत अग्रभाग हैं।
**महत्वपूर्ण तथ्य:**
- पुडुचेरी **1674 से 1954** तक भारत में **फ्रेंच ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी** की मुख्य बस्ती रही थी।
- ऐतिहासिक शहर को दो अलग-अलग क्षेत्रों में विभाजित किया गया है: फ्रेंच क्वार्टर (**विले ब्लैंच**) और तमिल क्वार्टर (**विले नोइरे**)।
- प्रमुख फ्रांसीसी स्थलों में **युद्ध स्मारक (Monument aux Morts)** और **सैक्रेड हार्ट ऑफ जीसस चर्च** शामिल हैं।
- पुडुचेरी का नगर नियोजन विशिष्ट फ्रांसीसी **ग्रिडआयरन पैटर्न** पर आधारित है जिसमें समकोण पर काटती सड़कें हैं।
- **फ्रांस्वा मार्टिन** फ्रेंच पांडिचेरी के पहले गवर्नर-जनरल थे।

question.en: What was Bharatanatyam originally called? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: भरतनाट्यम को मूल रूप से क्या कहा जाता था? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Bharatanatyam**, the classical dance form of Tamil Nadu, was traditionally performed in Hindu temples by Devadasis and was historically known as **Sadir**, **Sadir Nattyam**, or **Dasi Attam**.
**Important Facts:**
- The art was revived and given the classical name "Bharatanatyam" in the 1930s by pioneers like **E. Krishna Iyer** and **Rukmini Devi Arundale**.
- Rukmini Devi Arundale founded the premier arts institution **Kalakshetra** at Adyar, Chennai, in **1936**.
- The dance form's theoretical principles trace back to the ancient treatise **Natya Shastra** attributed to Sage Bharata.
- Essential components of Bharatanatyam include **Alarippu**, **Jatiswaram**, **Shabdam**, **Varnam**, **Padam**, and **Tillana**.
- The musical accompaniment follows the **Carnatic music** system, anchored by the nattuvanar playing cymbals.
solution.hi:
तमिलनाडु का शास्त्रीय नृत्य **भरतनाट्यम** पारंपरिक रूप से देवदासियों द्वारा हिंदू मंदिरों में प्रस्तुत किया जाता था और इसे ऐतिहासिक रूप से **सादिर**, **सादिर नाट्यम** या **दासी अट्टम** के नाम से जाना जाता था।
**महत्वपूर्ण तथ्य:**
- इस कला को 1930 के दशक में **ई. कृष्ण अय्यर** और **रुक्मिणी देवी अरुंडेल** जैसे अग्रदूतों द्वारा पुनर्जीवित किया गया और "भरतनाट्यम" नाम दिया गया।
- रुक्मिणी देवी अरुंडेल ने **1936** में अडयार, चेन्नई में प्रमुख कला संस्थान **कलाक्षेत्र** की स्थापना की।
- इस नृत्य शैली के सैद्धांतिक सिद्धांत भरत मुनि द्वारा रचित प्राचीन ग्रंथ **नाट्य शास्त्र** से लिए गए हैं।
- भरतनाट्यम के प्रमुख क्रमों में **अलारिप्पु**, **जातिस्वरम**, **शब्दम**, **वर्णम**, **पदम** और **तिल्लाना** शामिल हैं।
- इसमें प्रयुक्त होने वाला संगीत **कर्नाटक संगीत** परंपरा पर आधारित होता है, जिसे नट्टुवनार द्वारा संचालित किया जाता है।

question.en: What is the term for pure dance where body movements do NOT convey any meaning or mood? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: उस शुद्ध नृत्य के लिए क्या शब्द है जिसमें शारीरिक गतियाँ कोई अर्थ या भाव व्यक्त नहीं करती हैं? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
According to the Natya Shastra, **Nritta** refers to pure dance composed of abstract, rhythmical movements, footwork, and poses that do not depict any story, meaning, or emotional expression (bhava).
**Important Facts:**
- Classical Indian dance is divided into three aspects: **Nritta** (pure abstract dance), **Nritya** (expressive dance with sentiment), and **Natya** (dramatic performance).
- **Nritya** conveys specific mood (**bhava**) and aesthetic flavor (**rasa**) through gestures and mime.
- **Natya** incorporates the elements of drama, speech, and storytelling.
- **Abhinaya** is the art of expression, classified into four types: Angika, Vachika, Aharya, and Sattvika.
- In Bharatanatyam, the **Alarippu** and **Jatiswaram** are prime examples of the **Nritta** aspect.
solution.hi:
नाट्य शास्त्र के अनुसार, **नृत्त** से तात्पर्य शुद्ध नृत्य से है जिसमें अमूर्त, लयबद्ध शारीरिक गतियां, पदचाप और मुद्राएं होती हैं जो किसी भी कहानी, अर्थ या भावनात्मक भाव (रस) को व्यक्त नहीं करती हैं।
**महत्वपूर्ण तथ्य:**
- भारतीय शास्त्रीय नृत्य को तीन अंगों में विभाजित किया गया है: **नृत्त** (शुद्ध नृत्य), **नृत्य** (भावाभिव्यक्ति युक्त नृत्य) और **नाट्य** (नाटकीय प्रस्तुति)।
- **नृत्य** हस्त मुद्राओं और चेहरे के हाव-भाव द्वारा विशिष्ट भाव और **रस** का संचार करता है।
- **नाट्य** में नाटक, संवाद और कथात्मक प्रस्तुति के तत्व शामिल होते हैं।
- **अभिनय** अभिव्यक्ति की कला है, जिसे चार भागों में वर्गीकृत किया गया है: आंगिक, वाचिक, आहार्य और सात्विक।
- भरतनाट्यम में **अलारिप्पु** और **जातिस्वरम** मुख्य रूप से **नृत्त** पहलू के प्रमुख उदाहरण हैं।

question.en: A census town, as classified in Census 2011, must satisfy all of the following conditions except [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: 2011 की जनगणना में वर्गीकृत एक जनगणना शहर (सेंसस टाउन) को निम्नलिखित में से किसे छोड़कर अन्य सभी शर्तों को पूरा करना होगा? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 18/09/26 Shift 1]

2.hi: कम से कम 50% कृषि में लगे हों

3.hi: घनत्व 400 प्रति वर्ग किमी से अधिक हो

4.hi: अधिकांश लोग गैर-कृषि कार्यों में लगे हों

solution.en:
For an area to be classified as a **Census Town**, at least **75% of the male main working population** must be engaged in **non-agricultural pursuits**; therefore, requiring "at least 50% engaged in agriculture" is contrary to the definition.
**Important Facts:**
- The criteria for a **Census Town** in India are:
  1. A minimum population of **5,000**.
  2. At least **75%** of male main working population engaged in **non-agricultural pursuits**.
  3. A population density of at least **400 persons per sq. km** (1,000 per sq. mile).
- A **Statutory Town**, by contrast, is any urban settlement notified by statute with a municipality, corporation, cantonment board, or notified town area committee.
- The 2011 Census recorded **3,894 Census Towns**, up significantly from 1,362 in 2001.
- Census towns lack municipal status and continue to be governed by rural gram panchayats despite their urban physical characteristics.
- The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India functions under the **Ministry of Home Affairs**.
solution.hi:
**जनगणना शहर (सेंसस टाउन)** के रूप में वर्गीकृत होने के लिए, **पुरुष मुख्य कार्यशील जनसंख्या का कम से कम 75% गैर-कृषि कार्यों** में संलग्न होना चाहिए; इसलिए, "कम से कम 50% कृषि में लगे हों" की शर्त इसकी परिभाषा के विपरीत है।
**महत्वपूर्ण तथ्य:**
- भारत में **जनगणना शहर** के तीन अनिवार्य मानदंड हैं:
  1. न्यूनतम जनसंख्या **5,000** होनी चाहिए।
  2. पुरुष मुख्य कार्यशील जनसंख्या का कम से कम **75%** गैर-कृषि कार्यों में लगा होना चाहिए।
  3. जनसंख्या घनत्व कम से कम **400 व्यक्ति प्रति वर्ग किमी** होना चाहिए।
- इसके विपरीत, **सांविधिक शहर (Statutory Town)** वह होता है जिसे नगर पालिका, नगर निगम, छावनी बोर्ड या अधिसूचित नगर क्षेत्र समिति के साथ अधिसूचित किया गया हो।
- 2011 की जनगणना में **3,894 जनगणना शहर** दर्ज किए गए थे, जो 2001 में 1,362 से काफी अधिक थे।
- शहरी विशेषताओं के बावजूद, जनगणना शहरों में नगर पालिका का दर्जा नहीं होता है और वे ग्राम पंचायतों द्वारा शासित होते हैं।
- भारत के महारजिस्ट्रार और जनगणना आयुक्त **गृह मंत्रालय** के अधीन कार्य करते हैं।

question.en: Which Indian female sprinter, a former 100m national record holder, is associated with a reported four-year ban beginning in late 2022? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 19/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: कौन सी भारतीय महिला धावक, जो 100 मीटर की पूर्व राष्ट्रीय रिकॉर्ड धारक हैं, 2022 के उत्तरार्ध से शुरू हुए चार साल के प्रतिबंध से जुड़ी हैं? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 19/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Indian sprinter and two-time Asian Games silver medallist Dutee Chand was handed a four-year ban by the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) after testing positive for prohibited Selective Androgen Receptor Modulators (SARMs), effective from December 2022.
Important Facts:
- Dutee Chand won silver medals in both the 100m and 200m events at the 2018 Jakarta Asian Games.
- She held the national record in women's 100 metres with a timing of 11.17 seconds set in 2021.
- In 2019, she became the first Indian woman sprinter to win a gold medal at the World Universiade.
- PT Usha currently serves as the President of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA).
- Annu Rani is an Indian track and field athlete competing in the javelin throw.
solution.hi:
भारतीय धावक और दो बार की एशियाई खेलों की रजत पदक विजेता दुती चंद पर राष्ट्रीय डोपिंग रोधी एजेंसी (NADA) द्वारा प्रतिबंधित सेलेक्टिव एण्ड्रोजन रिसेप्टर मॉड्यूलेटर (SARMs) के पॉजिटिव परीक्षण के बाद दिसंबर 2022 से प्रभावी चार साल का प्रतिबंध लगाया गया था।
महत्वपूर्ण तथ्य:
- दुती चंद ने 2018 जकार्ता एशियाई खेलों में 100 मीटर और 200 मीटर दोनों स्पर्धाओं में रजत पदक जीता था।
- उन्होंने 2021 में 11.17 सेकंड के समय के साथ महिलाओं की 100 मीटर स्पर्धा में राष्ट्रीय रिकॉर्ड बनाया था।
- 2019 में, वह वर्ल्ड यूनिवर्सिटी गेम्स में स्वर्ण पदक जीतने वाली पहली भारतीय महिला धावक बनीं।
- पीटी उषा वर्तमान में भारतीय ओलंपिक संघ (IOA) की अध्यक्ष के रूप में कार्यरत हैं।
- अन्नू रानी एक भारतीय ट्रैक और फील्ड एथलीट हैं जो भाला फेंक (जैवलिन थ्रो) में प्रतिस्पर्धा करती हैं।

question.en: Bagurumba dance is a traditional folk dance associated with which of the following communities? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 19/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: बागुरुम्बा नृत्य निम्नलिखित में से किस समुदाय से जुड़ा एक पारंपरिक लोक नृत्य है? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 19/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Bagurumba** is a prominent traditional folk dance practiced by the **Bodo community** of Assam and parts of Northeast India. Usually performed by Bodo women during the festival of Bwisagu, it mimics the graceful movements of butterflies and birds.
**Important Facts:**
- The **Bagurumba** dance is also fondly called the "butterfly dance" because dancers spread their traditional *Dokhona* like wings.
- It is performed to celebrate the arrival of spring during the **Bwisagu** festival in mid-April.
- Traditional musical instruments used include the **Kham** (drum), **Siphung** (bamboo flute), and **Jotha** (cymbals).
- The **Bodo** are an indigenous ethnolinguistic group recognized as part of the Sixth Schedule areas in Assam.
- **Ali-Aye-Ligang** is the famous agricultural spring festival associated with the **Mishing** community.
solution.hi:
**बागुरुम्बा** असम और पूर्वोत्तर भारत के **बोडो समुदाय** द्वारा किया जाने वाला एक प्रमुख पारंपरिक लोक नृत्य है। आमतौर पर बोडो महिलाओं द्वारा बैसागु उत्सव के दौरान किया जाने वाला यह नृत्य तितलियों और पक्षियों की सुंदर गतिविधियों की नकल करता है।
**महत्वपूर्ण तथ्य:**
- **बागुरुम्बा** नृत्य को "तितली नृत्य" भी कहा जाता है क्योंकि नर्तकियां अपनी पारंपरिक पोशाक *दोखोना* को पंखों की तरह फैलाती हैं।
- यह अप्रैल के मध्य में **बैसागु** उत्सव के दौरान वसंत ऋतु के आगमन के स्वागत में प्रस्तुत किया जाता है।
- इसमें उपयोग किए जाने वाले पारंपरिक वाद्ययंत्रों में **खाम** (ढोल), **सिफंग** (बांसुरी), और **जोथा** (झांझ) शामिल हैं।
- **बोडो** असम में छठी अनुसूची के तहत मान्यता प्राप्त एक प्रमुख स्वदेशी जातीय-भाषाई समुदाय हैं।
- **अली-आई-लिगांग** असम के **मिशिंग** समुदाय से जुड़ा प्रसिद्ध वसंतकालीन कृषि उत्सव है।

questions.topic: Static GK: Folk Dances and Festivals

question.en: Which of the following pairs of traditional folk dance and its associated state is correctly matched? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 19/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: पारंपरिक लोक नृत्य और उसके संबंधित राज्य का निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा युग्म सही सुमेलित है? [SSC Selection Post (Graduate) 19/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Raut Nacha** is a traditional folk dance of **Chhattisgarh**, performed mainly by the Yadav/Raut community during Diwali. Dollu Kunitha belongs to Karnataka, Bhortal Nritya belongs to Assam, and Cheraw dance belongs to Mizoram.
**Important Facts:**
- **Raut Nacha** expresses devotion to Lord Krishna and celebrates good overcoming evil.
- **Dollu Kunitha** is a popular drum-based dance form originating in **Karnataka**.
- **Bhortal Nritya** was developed by the Sattriya artist Narahari Burha Bhakat in **Assam**.
- **Cheraw Dance** (popularly known as the Bamboo Dance) is the traditional dance of **Mizoram**.
- **Pandwani** and **Panthi** are other internationally recognized performing arts from **Chhattisgarh**.
solution.hi:
**राउत नाचा** **छत्तीसगढ़** का एक पारंपरिक लोक नृत्य है, जो मुख्य रूप से यादव/राउत समुदाय द्वारा दीपावली के अवसर पर किया जाता है। डोल्लू कुनिथा कर्नाटक का, भोरताल नृत्य असम का, और चेराव नृत्य मिजोरम का पारंपरिक नृत्य है।
**महत्वपूर्ण तथ्य:**
- **राउत नाचा** भगवान कृष्ण के प्रति भक्ति व्यक्त करता है और बुराई पर अच्छाई की विजय का उत्सव मनाता है।
- **डोल्लू कुनिथा** **कर्नाटक** का एक प्रसिद्ध ढोल-आधारित लोक नृत्य है।
- **भोरताल नृत्य** की रचना **असम** में सत्रीया कलाकार नरहरि बुरहा भकत द्वारा की गई थी।
- **चेराव नृत्य** (बांस नृत्य के रूप में लोकप्रिय) **मिजोरम** का पारंपरिक लोक नृत्य है।
- **पंडवानी** और **पंथी** **छत्तीसगढ़** के अन्य अंतरराष्ट्रीय स्तर पर प्रसिद्ध लोक प्रदर्शन रूप हैं।
