Impartial [निष्पक्ष] means fair and unbiased. Its antonym is Biased.

Option meanings
Neutral — not taking sides [तटस्थ]
Fair — just [न्यायी]
Biased — prejudiced [पक्षपाती]
Just — equitable [न्यायपूर्ण]

Related words: Antonyms of impartial: partial, prejudiced, partisan.

question.en: Choose the antonym of 'contemporary': [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Contemporary [समकालीन, आधुनिक] means belonging to the present. Its antonym is Obsolete (out of date).

Option meanings
Present — current [वर्तमान]
Current — of now [चालू]
Obsolete — outdated [अप्रचलित]
Modern — of recent times [आधुनिक]

Related words: Antonyms of contemporary: outdated, archaic, antiquated.

question.en: Choose the antonym of 'discreet': [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Discreet [संयमी, सतर्क] means careful and prudent in behaviour. Its antonym is Reckless.

Option meanings
Prudent — cautious [सतर्क]
Reckless — careless [लापरवाह]
Wise — sensible [बुद्धिमान]
Tactful — diplomatic [विवेकपूर्ण]

Related words: Antonyms of discreet: indiscreet, careless, rash.

question.en:
select the most appropriate antonym of the word:
OBEDIENCE [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Obedience [आज्ञाकारिता] means compliance with orders. Its antonym is rebellion.

Option meanings
Rebellion — defiance of authority [विद्रोह]
Compliance — obedience [अनुपालन]
Discipline — controlled behaviour [अनुशासन]
Submission — yielding [समर्पण]

Related words: Antonyms of obedience: defiance, disobedience, revolt.

question.en:
Choose the one which can be substituted for the given sentence.

• Linguistic Anthropology — the study of how language influences social life and culture [भाषा मानवविज्ञान]
• Medical Anthropology — the study of human health, disease, and health care systems in cultural context [चिकित्सा मानवविज्ञान]
• Cultural Anthropology — the study of cultural variation among living human societies [सांस्कृतिक मानवविज्ञान]
• Archaeology — the study of prehistoric human societies via material remains [पुरातत्व]

Related words: Archaeology: excavation, antiquities, paleography.

question.en: Which term refers to a person who is skilled in horsemanship? [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
An equestrian [घुड़सवार] (derived from Latin equus 'horse') is a person who rides horses or is skilled in horsemanship.

Option meanings
• Aquarist — a person who maintains an aquarium or studies aquatic life [जलजीव-पालक]
• Equestrian — a person skilled in horse riding or equestrian sports [घुड़सवार]
• Cyclist — a person who rides a bicycle [साइकिल चालक]
• Linguist — a person skilled in foreign languages or linguistics [भाषाविद्]

Related words: Equestrian: jockey, cavalryman, horseman, rider.

question.en:
Choose the one which can be substituted for the given word/sentence.
One who cannot be corrected. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
An incorrigible [असुधार्य, जिसे सुधारा न जा सके] person (derived from Latin in- 'not' + corrigere 'to correct') is someone whose bad habits, behavior, or tendencies are so firmly fixed that they cannot be reformed or corrected.

Option meanings
• Incurable — impossible to cure (used primarily for diseases) [लालाज]
• Incorrigible — incapable of being reformed or corrected in character or habits [असुधार्य]
• Hardened — made callous or accustomed to hardship or crime [कठोर, पक्का]
• Vulnerable — susceptible to physical or emotional attack or harm [असुरक्षित, नाजुक]

Related words: Incorrigible: unreformable, inveterate, irredeemable, habitual.

question.en:
Choose the one which can be substituted for the given word/sentence.
The study of insects. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Entomology [कीटविज्ञान] (derived from Greek entomon 'insect' + logos 'study') is the branch of zoological science dedicated to the study of insects.

Option meanings
• Anthropology — the study of human origins, societies, and cultures [मानवविज्ञान]
• Zoology — the general scientific study of animals [जंतुविज्ञान]
• Etymology — the study of the origin and historical development of words [शब्द-व्युत्पत्ति शास्त्र]
• Entomology — the scientific study of insects [कीटविज्ञान]

question.en:
Choose the one word substitute for the below sentence.
Jacob asked his friend, a person who studies insects called? [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Entomologist – a person who studies insects (Greek entomon = insect + -logy = study).

Other options
Ornithologist – studies birds; Zoologist – studies animals in general; Botanist – studies plants.

Therefore, Entomologist.

question.en:
Choose the one word substitute for the below sentence.
Rachel asked her teacher, person who performs surgeries called? [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Surgeon – a doctor who performs surgical operations.

Other options
Physician – treats diseases with medicine (not surgery); Dentist – treats teeth; Podiatrist – treats feet.

Therefore, Surgeon.

question.en:
Choose the one word substitute for the below sentence.
Rahul asked his lecturer, a person who loves to argue called? [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Controversialist – a person who loves to argue or engages readily in disputes and controversies.

Other options
Pessimist – one who expects the worst; Debater – one who argues formally in a debate, not necessarily out of fondness for arguing; Quibbler – one who raises petty, trivial objections.

Therefore, Controversialist.

question.en:
Choose the one word substitute for the below sentence.
Siddharth dedicated his time to mastering a new trade, steadily honing his skills through practice and guidance. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Siddharth is learning a new trade through practice and guidance – i.e., learning a skilled job under an experienced person.
Such a learner is an apprentice.

Other options
Scholar – a learned academic person; Student – a general learner at school/college; Novice – any beginner, without the idea of trade training under a master.

Therefore, Apprentice.

question.en:
Choose the one word substitute for the below sentence.
Farhan faced criticism from his community after being labeled for abandoning his faith and religious beliefs. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
A person who abandons or renounces his religious faith is an apostate (the act is called apostasy).

Other options
Devotee – a deeply religious follower; Prophet – a messenger of God; Theologian – a scholar of religion.

Therefore, Apostate.

question.en:
Select the alternative that can be used as a one-word substitute for the highlighted group of words.
He specialised in the science and technology of metals at university. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Metallurgy – the science and technology of metals (extraction, properties, processing).
Archaeology – study of ancient remains; Meteorology – study of weather; Anthropology – study of human societies.

Therefore, Metallurgy.

question.en:
Select the alternative that can be used as a one-word substitute for the highlighted group of words.
The ancient tribe practised the belief that God is everything peacefully. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Pantheism – the belief that God is everything and everything is God (Greek pan = all + theos = god).
Polytheism – belief in many gods; Neologism – a newly coined word; Materialism – belief that only matter exists / love of possessions.

Therefore, Pantheism.

question.en:
Choose the one which can be substituted for the given sentence.
A person who remains calm in both pleasure and pain is called a: [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
A person indifferent to or uncomplaining in the face of pleasure and pain is known as a **Stoic**.
**Other options:** A **Mystic** seeks direct spiritual union; a **Skeptic** questions or doubts accepted beliefs; an **Atheist** disbelieves in a deity.

question.en:
Choose the one which can be substituted for the given sentence.
A detailed list of items in a library is called a: [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
A comprehensive, systematic list of all books, periodicals, and items held in a library is a **Catalogue**.
**Other options:** An **Index** is an alphabetical list of names/subjects at the back of a book; a **Diary** records personal daily events; an **Almanac** is an annual calendar of data.

question.en:
Choose the one which can be substituted for the given sentence.
A story in which animals act like humans [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
A short fictional story featuring anthropomorphic animals designed to teach a moral lesson is a **Fable**.
**Other options:** An **Allegory** conveys symbolic hidden meanings; a **Novel** is a long narrative work of fiction; a **Poem** is verse-based literature.

question.en:
Choose the one which can be substituted for the given sentence.
A disease which spreads over a large area [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
A disease prevalent over a whole country, continent, or globally is a **Pandemic** (an epidemic across extensive regions).
**Other options:** **Epidemic** affects many people within a community or localized region; **Endemic** is regularly found among particular people; **Hysteria** is uncontrolled emotion.

question.en:
Choose the one which can be substituted for the given sentence.
An act of speaking one's thoughts aloud when alone [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Speaking one's private thoughts aloud when by oneself, especially in drama, is a **Soliloquy**.
**Other options:** A **Dialogue** is a conversation between two or more people; a **Monologue** is a long speech delivered to an audience; an **Extempore** speech is given without preparation.

question.en:
Choose the one which can be substituted for the given sentence.
A person who collects and studies stamps [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
A collector and student of postage stamps is designated a **Philatelist**.
**Other options:** A **Numismatist** collects and studies coins/currency; an **Archivist** manages historical archives; a **Paleographer** studies ancient writing systems.

question.en:
Choose the one which can be substituted for the given sentence.
A person who travels on foot is called a: [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
A pedestrian [पैदल चलने वाला] is a person who travels on foot.

Option meanings
Pedestrian — one who walks [पैदल यात्री]
Cyclist — rides a bicycle [साइकिल चालक]
Passenger — travels in a vehicle [यात्री]
Pilot — flies an aircraft [पायलट]

Related words: walker, foot-passenger.

question.en:
Choose the one which can be substituted for the given sentence.
A place where clothes are washed is called a: [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
A laundry [धोबीघर] is a place where clothes are washed.

Option meanings
Laundry — washing place [धोबीघर]
Pantry — food store [भंडार]
Cloakroom — coat storage [कोटघर]
Dormitory — sleeping hall [छात्रावास]

Related words: washhouse, dry cleaner's.

question.en:
Choose the one which can be substituted for the given sentence.
A place where animals are slaughtered [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
An abattoir [कसाईखाना] is a place where animals are slaughtered.

Option meanings
Abattoir — slaughterhouse [कसाईखाना]
Aviary — bird enclosure [पक्षीशाला]
Apiary — bee house [मधुमक्खीशाला]
Aquarium — fish tank [मत्स्यालय]

Related words: slaughterhouse, butchery.

question.en:
Choose the one which can be substituted for the given sentence.
A person who believes everything easily [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
A credulous [सरलविश्वासी] person believes everything easily.

Option meanings
Credulous — gullible [आसानी से विश्वास करने वाला]
Skeptic — doubter [संदेहवादी]
Pragmatist — practical person [व्यावहारिकवादी]
Stoic — unemotional person [स्थितप्रज्ञ]

Related words: gullible, trusting, naive.

question.en:
Choose the one which can be substituted for the given sentence.
A game or contest between two teams [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
A match [मैच] is a game or contest between two teams.

Option meanings
Match — a contest between teams [खेल-मुकाबला]
Race — a speed contest [दौड़]
Duel — a fight between two individuals [द्वंद्व]
Fete — a celebration [मेला]

Related words: game, contest, fixture.

question.en:
Choose the one which can be substituted for the given sentence.
A person who is indifferent to pleasure, pain, grief or joy [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
A stoic [स्थितप्रज्ञ] is a person indifferent to pleasure, pain, grief or joy.

Option meanings
Stoic — indifferent to pleasure/pain [स्थितप्रज्ञ]
Cynic — distrustful person [निंदक]
Mystic — spiritual person [रहस्यवादी]
Pragmatist — practical person [व्यावहारिकवादी]

Related words: unemotional, impassive, phlegmatic.

question.en: What does the idiom 'Hobson's choice' mean? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Hobson’s choice [मजबूरी का एकमात्र विकल्प] is a situation in which only one option is offered: take it or leave it.

Option meanings
A free option — a choice made freely [स्वतंत्र विकल्प]
No real choice at all — only one thing is available [कोई वास्तविक विकल्प नहीं]
Two equal options — alternatives of equal value [दो बराबर विकल्प]
A sudden decision — a decision made quickly [अचानक लिया गया निर्णय]

The phrase comes from Thomas Hobson, a Cambridge stable-keeper who made customers take the horse nearest the door or none.

Related words: Contextual equivalents: take it or leave it, no alternative.

question.en:
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom:
The lion's share [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The lion’s share [सबसे बड़ा हिस्सा] means the largest part of something.

Option meanings
A tiny portion — a very small part [बहुत छोटा भाग]
Equal distribution — sharing equally [बराबर बँटवारा]
The largest part — the biggest share [सबसे बड़ा भाग]
A fair deal — just treatment [उचित व्यवहार]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: the major part, the bulk, the greater part.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To bury the hatchet [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
To bury the hatchet [पुरानी दुश्मनी भुलाकर सुलह करना] means to end a quarrel and make peace.

Option meanings
To start a fight — to begin a quarrel [झगड़ा शुरू करना]
To make peace — to end hostility [सुलह करना]
To dig a hole — literal digging [गड्ढा खोदना]
To hide a weapon — literal concealment [हथियार छिपाना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: reconcile, make up, let bygones be bygones.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To go to the dogs [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

2.en: To decline in condition or quality

solution.en:
To go to the dogs [बर्बाद हो जाना, बदहाल होना] means to decline badly in condition or quality.

Option meanings
To be successful — to achieve success [सफल होना]
To decline in condition or quality — to get worse [बदतर होना]
To get along well — to have a good relationship [अच्छा तालमेल होना]
To become an animal lover — literal and unrelated [पशु-प्रेमी बनना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: deteriorate, go downhill, go to rack and ruin.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To have too many irons in the fire [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

2.en: To be involved in too many activities at once

solution.en:
To have too many irons in the fire [एक साथ बहुत सारे कामों में उलझे रहना] means to be involved in too many activities at the same time.

Option meanings
To be very focused — concentrating on one thing [पूरी तरह एकाग्र होना]
To be involved in too many activities at once — taking on too much [एक साथ बहुत से कामों में लगे रहना]
To be lazy — unwilling to work [आलसी होना]
To be a blacksmith — literal and unrelated [लोहार होना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: spread oneself too thin, overcommit.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To flog a dead horse [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: To revive interest in a subject

2.en: To waste effort on a lost cause

solution.en:
To flog a dead horse [व्यर्थ प्रयास करना] means to waste effort on something that is already finished or hopeless.

Option meanings
To revive interest in a subject — to renew attention [रुचि फिर जगाना]
To waste effort on a lost cause — to keep trying uselessly [निरर्थक प्रयास करना]
To beat an animal — literal and unrelated [पशु को पीटना]
To work very hard — to put in great effort [कड़ी मेहनत करना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: beat a dead horse, labour in vain, waste one’s breath.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To hit the nail on the head [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
To hit the nail on the head [बिल्कुल सही बात कहना] means to be exactly right — to describe a situation or problem very accurately.

Option meanings
To miss the point — to fail to understand the main idea [मुख्य बात न समझना]
To guess correctly — to make a lucky right guess [सही अनुमान लगाना]
To be very accurate — to be exactly right [बिल्कुल सटीक होना]
To strike something hard — literal hitting [ज़ोर से मारना]

The idiom is about precision, not a lucky guess.

Related words: Contextual equivalents: be spot on, be precise, get it exactly right.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To turn over a new leaf [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

2.en: To change one's behavior for the better

solution.en:
To turn over a new leaf [नई शुरुआत करना, सुधर जाना] means to change one’s behaviour for the better.

Option meanings
To start reading a book — literal [किताब पढ़ना शुरू करना]
To change one's behavior for the better — to reform oneself [अपना आचरण सुधारना]
To keep turning pages — literal [पन्ने पलटते रहना]
To return to bad habits — to relapse [पुरानी बुरी आदतों पर लौटना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: reform, make a fresh start, mend one’s ways.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To throw in the towel [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
To throw in the towel [हार मान लेना] means to surrender or admit defeat. It comes from boxing, where a trainer throws a towel into the ring to concede.

Option meanings
To surrender or admit defeat — to give up [हार मानना]
To clean up — to tidy [साफ़ करना]
To continue fighting — to keep going [लड़ते रहना]
To start a new task — to begin something new [नया काम शुरू करना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: give up, concede, call it quits.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
A bad workman always blames his tools [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: To blame external factors for poor performance

2.en: To fix equipment before starting work

3.en: To hire assistants when a task is difficult to complete

4.en: To refuse to work without proper training

solution.en:
The proverb A bad workman always blames his tools [नाच न जाने आँगन टेढ़ा] means that people who perform poorly blame outside factors instead of their own lack of skill.

Option meanings
To blame external factors for poor performance — shifting the blame [दोष दूसरों पर डालना]
To fix equipment before starting work — preparing tools [काम से पहले औज़ार ठीक करना]
To hire assistants when a task is difficult to complete — seeking help [सहायक रखना]
To refuse to work without proper training — insisting on training [प्रशिक्षण के बिना काम न करना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: make excuses, pass the buck.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Hit the nail on the head [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: To identify the exact point or truth

2.en: To perform a difficult task with ease

3.en: To be precise in a dangerous situation

4.en: To strike a heavy object forcefully

solution.en:
Hit the nail on the head [बिल्कुल सही बात कहना] means to identify the exact point or truth of a matter.

Option meanings
To identify the exact point or truth — to be exactly right [सटीक बात पकड़ना]
To perform a difficult task with ease — to do something effortlessly [कठिन काम आसानी से करना]
To be precise in a dangerous situation — to act accurately in danger [खतरे में सटीक रहना]
To strike a heavy object forcefully — literal hitting [ज़ोर से प्रहार करना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: be spot on, put one’s finger on it.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Read somebody the Riot Act [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: To explain a rule in great detail

2.en: To participate in a public protest

3.en: To read aloud from a law textbook

solution.en:
To read somebody the Riot Act [कड़ी फटकार लगाना] means to reprimand someone very severely and warn them to stop behaving badly.

Option meanings
To explain a rule in great detail — a detailed explanation [नियम विस्तार से समझाना]
To participate in a public protest — joining a demonstration [सार्वजनिक विरोध में भाग लेना]
To read aloud from a law textbook — literal reading [कानून की किताब पढ़ना]
To reprimand someone very severely — to scold sternly [कड़ी फटकार लगाना]

The phrase comes from the British Riot Act of 1714, which was read aloud to order unruly crowds to disperse.

Related words: Contextual equivalents: give a dressing-down, haul over the coals, rebuke.

question.en:
In the following question, four alternatives are given for the Idiom/Phrase underlined in the sentence. Choose the option that best expresses its meaning.
The politician's sudden apology was clearly a face-saving measure. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Face-saving [अपनी साख या इज़्ज़त बचाने वाला] describes an action meant to avoid embarrassment or protect one's reputation.
The politician apologised suddenly to limit damage to his image, not out of sincerity.

Example: The minister's resignation was seen as a face-saving move after the scandal.

question.en:
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom:
Go the extra mile [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Go the extra mile [अतिरिक्त प्रयास करना] means to make more effort than is expected.

Example: Good teachers go the extra mile to help weak students.

question.en:
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom:
Throw cold water on [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Throw cold water on [हतोत्साहित करना, पानी फेरना] means to discourage an idea or plan.

Example: The manager threw cold water on our proposal for a new branch.

question.en: What does the idiom "On the ball" mean? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
On the ball [सतर्क और सक्षम] means alert, quick to understand and competent.

Example: Our new accountant is really on the ball; she spotted the error at once.

question.en: What does the phrase "Off the cuff" mean? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Off the cuff [बिना तैयारी के] means spoken or done without preparation.

Example: He made an off-the-cuff speech at the farewell party.

question.en: What is the meaning of the phrase "Hold your horses"? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Hold your horses [धैर्य रखो, रुको] means wait a moment and do not act too hastily.

Example: Hold your horses! Let us read the terms before signing.

question.en: What does the idiom "Go the extra mile" mean? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Go the extra mile [अपेक्षा से अधिक प्रयास करना] means to do more than what is necessary or expected.

Example: The nurse went the extra mile to comfort the patient's family.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
In the doldrums [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Feeling lost in a large crowd

2.en: A state of stagnation or depression

4.en: A period of extreme hot weather

solution.en:
In the doldrums [मंदी या उदासी की स्थिति में] means in a state of stagnation, inactivity or low spirits.

Example: The real estate market has been in the doldrums for two years.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
To go the whole hog [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: To consume a very large meal quickly

2.en: To do something fully and thoroughly

3.en: To act in an extremely greedy manner

4.en: To waste all of one's personal savings

solution.en:
To go the whole hog [पूरी तरह से करना] means to do something fully and thoroughly, without holding back.

Example: Once they decided to renovate the kitchen, they went the whole hog and replaced everything.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
To chew someone out [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: To invite someone for an expensive dinner

2.en: To mock someone behind their back

3.en: To scold or reprimand someone severely

4.en: To praise someone for doing good work

solution.en:
To chew someone out [कड़ी फटकार लगाना] means to scold or reprimand someone severely.

Example: The coach chewed the players out for arriving late to practice.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Cold feet [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Cold feet [घबराहट, हिचकिचाहट] means feeling nervous or hesitant, especially just before doing something important; it is usually used as "get cold feet".

Example: He got cold feet just before his first stage performance.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Eat humble pie [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: To admit a mistake and apologise

2.en: To eat a meal that is very cheap

4.en: To be forced to eat against your will

solution.en:
Eat humble pie [अपनी गलती मानकर माफ़ी माँगना] means to admit that one was wrong and apologise, often in a humiliating situation.

Example: After his prediction proved wrong, the critic had to eat humble pie.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Feather one's nest [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

3.en: To enrich oneself using one's position

solution.en:
Feather one's nest [अपना घर भरना] means to make oneself rich, often dishonestly, by using one's position or job.

Example: The corrupt official feathered his nest with public funds.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Get wind of something [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: To experience a sudden change in the weather

2.en: To learn about a secret or private matter

3.en: To catch a severe respiratory illness

4.en: To lose one's breath after running fast

solution.en:
Get wind of something means to hear or learn about something secret or private [भनक लगना].

Example: The press got wind of the minister's resignation before it was announced.

The idiom has nothing to do with weather, illness or losing breath.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Sail close to the wind [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: To act on the verge of illegal behaviour

2.en: To travel rapidly using a sailing ship

3.en: To choose an easy path to avoid danger

4.en: To forecast weather changes with accuracy

solution.en:
Sail close to the wind means to take a risk by doing something that is almost illegal or unacceptable [कानून/नियम की सीमा पर चलना].

Example: The company sailed close to the wind with its misleading advertisements.

It comes from sailing: steering too close to the direction of the wind risks capsizing.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Cry for the moon [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

3.en: To weep during a lunar eclipse

solution.en:
Cry for the moon means to want something that is impossible to get [असंभव वस्तु की कामना करना].

Example: Expecting to become a millionaire overnight is crying for the moon.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Tied herself up in knots [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

3.en: To complete a difficult craft project

4.en: To decorate a room with ribbons

solution.en:
Tie oneself (up) in knots means to become very confused, worried or anxious [उलझन/घबराहट में पड़ जाना].

Example: She tied herself up in knots trying to explain the delay to her boss.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Want to curl up and die [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: To suffer from a severe physical illness

2.en: To feel extreme embarrassment or shame

3.en: To prefer sleeping in a small space

4.en: To give up on a difficult goal

solution.en:
Want to curl up and die means to feel extremely embarrassed or ashamed [शर्म से गड़ जाना].

Example: When he forgot his lines on stage, he wanted to curl up and die.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Bird's eye view [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

2.en: A target seen from a great distance

3.en: A small bird flying in the sky

4.en: A wide, general view from above

solution.en:
Bird's eye view means a wide, general view seen from above, or an overall view of a subject [विहंगम दृश्य].

Example: The tower offers a bird's eye view of the city.

It is the opposite of a detailed close-up inspection.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Leave it on the back burner [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: To postpone a task or project

2.en: To cook a meal at a low heat

3.en: To store items in a kitchen cupboard

4.en: To prioritise an urgent matter immediately

solution.en:
Leave/put something on the back burner means to postpone it or give it low priority [टाल देना, बाद के लिए छोड़ देना].

Example: The expansion plan has been left on the back burner until funds are available.

Option 4 gives the opposite meaning.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Leave no stone unturned [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: To build a wall around a garden

3.en: To move heavy rocks in a field

4.en: To ignore small details in a report

solution.en:
Leave no stone unturned means to search every possible place or make every possible effort [कोई कसर न छोड़ना].

Example: The police left no stone unturned in their search for the missing child.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To give the cold shoulder [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
To give the cold shoulder [अनदेखा करना, रूखा व्यवहार करना] means to ignore or slight someone deliberately.

Option meanings
To show kindness — the opposite idea [दया दिखाना]
To ignore or slight — correct [उपेक्षा करना]
To embrace warmly — to welcome [गले लगाना]
To show support — to back someone [समर्थन करना]

Example: After the argument, she gave him the cold shoulder.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To pay through the nose [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

2.en: To pay an extremely high price

solution.en:
To pay through the nose [बहुत अधिक कीमत चुकाना] means to pay a very high or unfair price.

Option meanings
To pay a fair price — opposite idea [उचित मूल्य देना]
To pay an extremely high price — correct [बहुत महँगा चुकाना]
To pay on time — punctual payment [समय पर भुगतान]
To pay slowly — delayed payment [धीरे-धीरे भुगतान]

Example: Tourists pay through the nose for water at the airport.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Through thick and thin [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Across a varied and difficult terrain

3.en: Through a fast and sudden physical change

4.en: Under all conditions, both good and bad

solution.en:
Through thick and thin [हर परिस्थिति में] means under all conditions, both good and bad.

Option meanings
Across a varied and difficult terrain — literal, wrong
Between two very different options — wrong
Through a fast and sudden physical change — wrong
Under all conditions, both good and bad — correct [सुख-दुःख में]

Example: True friends stand by you through thick and thin.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Go against the grain [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: To act contrary to one's principles

2.en: To saw wood in the wrong direction

4.en: To define the borders of a country

solution.en:
Go against the grain [स्वभाव/सिद्धांत के विरुद्ध जाना] means to act contrary to one's principles or natural inclination.

Option meanings
To act contrary to one's principles — correct [अपने सिद्धांतों के विरुद्ध]
To saw wood in the wrong direction — literal, wrong
To be physically very strong — wrong
To define the borders of a country — wrong

Example: It goes against the grain for him to tell a lie.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Hold a candle to [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: To be a very religious person

2.en: To provide light in a dark room

3.en: To be as good as someone else

solution.en:
Hold a candle to [बराबरी करना] means to be as good as someone else; it is mostly used in the negative ("cannot hold a candle to").

Option meanings
To be a very religious person — wrong
To provide light in a dark room — literal, wrong
To be as good as someone else — correct [बराबरी का होना]
To waste time doing nothing — wrong

Example: No other singer can hold a candle to her.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Burn the candle at both ends [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: To light two candles at once to save time

2.en: To live a life of extreme luxury and waste

3.en: To balance two different jobs successfully

4.en: To exhaust oneself by working excessively

solution.en:
Burn the candle at both ends [अत्यधिक काम करके थक जाना] means to exhaust oneself by working too hard, e.g. late at night and early in the morning.

Option meanings
To light two candles at once to save time — literal, wrong
To live a life of extreme luxury and waste — wrong
To balance two different jobs successfully — wrong
To exhaust oneself by working excessively — correct [ख़ुद को थका देना]

Example: Before exams, many students burn the candle at both ends.

question.en: What is the meaning of the phrase "Elephantine task"? [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Elephantine task [बहुत बड़ा और कठिन काम] means a huge, difficult task; "elephantine" means enormous, like an elephant.

Option meanings
A huge difficult task — correct [विशाल और कठिन कार्य]
A secret mission — wrong
A simple chore — opposite
A task involving elephants — literal, wrong

Example: Rebuilding the flooded town was an elephantine task.

question.en: What does the phrase "Pass the buck" mean? [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Pass the buck [ज़िम्मेदारी दूसरे पर टालना] means to shift responsibility or blame to someone else.

Option meanings
To bet money — wrong
To evade responsibility — correct [ज़िम्मेदारी से बचना]
To speak briefly — wrong
To transfer something — literal, wrong

Example: When the project failed, the manager tried to pass the buck to his team.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To steal a march [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
To steal a march [चुपके से बढ़त हासिल करना] means to gain an advantage over someone by acting earlier or secretly.

Option meanings
To march secretly — literal, wrong
To obtain an advantage secretly — correct [चुपके से बढ़त पाना]
To move slowly — wrong
To steal something — literal, wrong

Example: Our rival stole a march on us by launching its product a month early.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To keep a stiff upper lip [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

2.en: To remain stoic and unemotional in adversity

solution.en:
To keep a stiff upper lip [विपत्ति में धैर्य रखना] means to stay calm and not show one's feelings in difficult situations.

Option meanings
To cry easily — opposite
To remain stoic and unemotional in adversity — correct [विपत्ति में शांत और धैर्यवान रहना]
To smile broadly — wrong
To talk loudly — wrong

Example: Even after losing his job, he kept a stiff upper lip.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To hang in the balance [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
To hang in the balance [अधर में लटकना] means to be in an uncertain state, with the outcome undecided.

Option meanings
To be certain — opposite
To have an uncertain outcome — correct [परिणाम अनिश्चित होना]
To be well supported — wrong
To be easily managed — wrong

Example: The patient's life hung in the balance after the accident.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To get out of hand [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
To get out of hand [नियंत्रण से बाहर होना] means to become impossible to control.

Option meanings
To be controlled — opposite
To become uncontrollable — correct [बेक़ाबू होना]
To receive a gift — literal, wrong
To give advice — wrong

Example: The protest got out of hand, and the police had to intervene.

question.en: What does the idiom 'To weather the storm' mean? [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
To weather the storm [कठिन परिस्थिति का सफलतापूर्वक सामना करना] is an idiomatic expression that means to survive, endure, or successfully come through a difficult period, crisis, or misfortune without succumbing.

Option meanings
• Face difficulties bravely — to confront hardships with resilience and successfully endure [मुश्किलों का डटकर सामना करना]
• Hide from problems — to evade or conceal oneself from adversity [समस्याओं से छिपना]
• Avoid responsibilities — to shirk duties or obligations [दायित्वों से बचना]
• Start a new project — to embark on a fresh undertaking [नई योजना शुरू करना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: ride out, pull through, withstand, hold out.

question.en: What does the idiom "Chew the fat" mean? [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
To chew the fat [अनौपचारिक गपशप करना] is an informal idiom meaning to chat leisurely, engage in friendly, prolonged conversation, or gossip idly about informal matters.

Option meanings
• To chat idly — to talk in an informal, friendly manner without serious purpose [गपशप करना]
• To chew food — the literal mastication of food [खाना चबाना]
• To complain — to express dissatisfaction [शिकायत करना]
• To eat quickly — to devour food rapidly [तेजी से खाना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: shoot the breeze, chit-chat, shoot the bull, jaw.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To put the cart before the horse [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: To do things in the wrong order

solution.en:
To put the cart before the horse [उल्टा काम करना, क्रम बिगाड़ना] is a classic idiom meaning to reverse the natural, logical, or sensible order of doing things.

Option meanings
• To do things in the wrong order — to perform tasks in reverse or illogical sequence [काम गलत क्रम में करना]
• To be very efficient — highly productive [अत्यधिक कुशल होना]
• To do things quickly — acting with speed [जल्दी करना]
• To drive an animal cart — literal driving [बैलगाड़ी चलाना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: have one's priorities wrong, get ahead of oneself.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: To hunt for rare birds in dense forests

2.en: To prefer guaranteed value over potential gain

3.en: To manage two projects at the same time

4.en: To take extreme risks to increase your wealth

solution.en:
A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush [नौ नकद न तेरह उधार, जो हाथ में है वह अनिश्चित से बेहतर है] is a proverbial idiom advising that it is much better to hold onto what one already possesses with certainty than to risk losing it by pursuing greater, uncertain prospective advantages.

Option meanings
• To prefer guaranteed value over potential gain — prioritizing assured possession over speculative prospects [निश्चित लाभ को प्राथमिकता देना]
• The other options provide literal or false interpretations.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Absence makes the heart grow fonder [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: To travel far away to forget someone

2.en: To lose interest in a long-distance relationship

3.en: To value someone more when they are away

4.en: To feel sad when meeting new people

solution.en:
Absence makes the heart grow fonder [दूर रहने पर चाहत और बढ़ती है] is a proverb meaning that being separated from a person you care about makes you appreciate and love them even more.

Option meanings
• To value someone more when they are away — distance intensifies affection and emotional appreciation [दूरी से प्रेम और कद्र बढ़ना]
• The other choices state the opposite or present unrelated scenarios.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Upset the apple cart [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: To knock over a heavy piece of furniture

2.en: To change your mind at the last minute

3.en: To transport goods in an unstable vehicle

4.en: To ruin a carefully planned arrangement

solution.en:
To upset the apple cart [बना-बनाया काम बिगाड़ देना, योजना पर पानी फेरना] is an idiom that means to disrupt, spoil, or overturn a carefully prepared plan, system, or arrangement.

Option meanings
• To ruin a carefully planned arrangement — to cause disruption and derail an established plan [योजना बिगाड़ना]
• To knock over furniture / transport goods — literal interpretations (incorrect).

Related words: Contextual equivalents: spoil the game, throw a spanner in the works, rock the boat.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To fight tooth and nail [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Idiom: To fight tooth and nail = to fight with all one's strength and determination, using every possible means.
Example: The villagers fought tooth and nail to save their land.
Little effort, fighting alone and fighting unfairly are not what the idiom means.

Therefore, To fight fiercely and determinedly.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To give a wide berth [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

2.en: To keep a safe distance from

solution.en:
Idiom: To give a wide berth = to keep a safe distance from someone or something; to avoid. (A “berth” is the space a ship needs around it.)
Example: Drivers give the damaged bridge a wide berth.
Standing close is the opposite; allowing to pass and giving permission are unrelated.

Therefore, To keep a safe distance from.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
To have an axe to grind [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: To work hard at a manual trade

2.en: To have a strong weapon for defence in war

3.en: To prepare tools for a major project

4.en: To have a hidden motive or grievance

solution.en:
Idiom: To have an axe to grind = to have a private purpose, selfish motive or grievance behind one's actions.
Example: He is praising the plan only because he has an axe to grind.
The literal meanings about manual work, weapons or tools are not what the idiom means.

Therefore, To have a hidden motive or grievance.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
To go to the dogs [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: To become severely ruined or degraded

2.en: To show a deep affection for animals

3.en: To live a luxurious and pampered life

4.en: To hunt for wild game in the forest

solution.en:
Idiom: To go to the dogs = to become ruined; to deteriorate badly.
Example: The old factory has gone to the dogs after years of neglect.
Love of animals, luxurious life and hunting are unrelated literal ideas.

Therefore, To become severely ruined or degraded.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
At loggerheads [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: To engage in a heated dispute

2.en: To agree completely on a plan

4.en: To work in a wood processing mill

solution.en:
Idiom: At loggerheads = in strong disagreement; engaged in a heated dispute.
Example: The two neighbours have been at loggerheads over the boundary wall.
Agreeing, exhaustion and a wood mill are not the meaning.

Therefore, To engage in a heated dispute.

question.en:
In the following sentence, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which gives the correct meaning of the highlighted idiom or phrase.
I heard the news of the impending theatre closure straight from the horse's mouth, so there is no reason to doubt its authenticity. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: From a public rumour spreading through the town

2.en: From a collection of conflicting reports

3.en: From the most reliable or primary source

4.en: From an anonymous and suspicious informant

solution.en:
Idiom: Straight from the horse's mouth = directly from the original, most reliable source.
The sentence confirms this: “so there is no reason to doubt its authenticity”.
Rumours, conflicting reports and anonymous informants are the opposite of a reliable source.

Therefore, From the most reliable or primary source.

question.en: What does the idiom 'In hot water' mean? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Meaning:** **In hot water** is an idiom that means in a difficult situation, facing reprimand, or in serious trouble.
**Example:** He found himself in hot water after missing the major project deadline.
Options (b), (c), and (d) take the idiom in a literal or incorrect figurative sense.

question.en: What does the idiom 'Hit the sack' mean? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Meaning:** **Hit the sack** means to go to bed or **go to sleep**.
**Example:** I am exhausted after the long shift, so I am going to hit the sack early tonight.
Options (a), (c), and (d) do not correspond to this traditional colloquial idiom.

question.en: What does the idiom 'A storm in a teacup' mean? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Meaning:** **A storm in a teacup** refers to great outrage, excitement, or worry about something trivial or unimportant (**exaggeration of a minor issue**).
**Example:** Their argument over the seating arrangement was just a storm in a teacup.
Options (a), (c), and (d) represent incorrect meanings.

question.en: What does the idiom 'Burn bridges' mean? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Meaning:** **Burn bridges** means to destroy one's path, relationships, or ties so that retreat or future reconciliation is impossible (**destroy opportunities**).
**Example:** Avoid being rude to your former employer lest you burn your bridges.
Options (a), (c), and (d) express opposing or unrelated concepts.

question.en: What does the idiom 'Blow one's own trumpet' mean? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Meaning:** **Blow one's own trumpet** means to praise one's own abilities, skills, or achievements; to **boast**.
**Example:** Rather than blowing his own trumpet, he let his excellent work speak for itself.
Options (a), (c), and (d) mean the exact opposite, emphasizing modesty and humility.

question.en: What does the idiom 'Cut the Gordian knot' mean? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Meaning:** **Cut the Gordian knot** means to solve a complex, intricate problem in a decisive, bold, and direct manner.
**Example:** The CEO cut the Gordian knot by restructuring the redundant departments overnight.
Options (b), (c), and (d) do not describe resolute decisive action.

question.en:
What does the idiom "let the cat out of the bag" mean in this sentence?

Laxman Mohan let the cat out of the bag about the surprise party before they could stop him. [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Let the cat out of the bag [राज़ खोल देना] means to reveal a secret, usually by mistake. In the sentence the surprise party was disclosed before anyone could stop it, so the idiom means to reveal a secret.

Option meanings
Release a pet — a literal reading, not the idiom
Reveal a secret — disclose hidden information [राज़ खोलना]
Chase a thief — unrelated
Lose money — unrelated

Therefore, Reveal a secret.

question.en: What does the idiom 'Make a mountain out of a molehill' mean? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Make a mountain out of a molehill [छोटी बात को बड़ा बनाना] means to exaggerate a small issue into a big problem.

Option meanings
To create a problem — too general
To exaggerate a small issue — blow it out of proportion [अतिशयोक्ति]
To climb a mountain — literal
To ignore a problem — opposite

Related words: blow out of proportion, overreact.

question.en: What does the idiom 'To smell a rat' mean? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
To smell a rat [गड़बड़ी की आशंका होना] means to suspect that something is wrong or that foul play is involved.

Option meanings
To sense danger — close but not precise
To detect a lie — narrower
To suspect foul play — suspect deceit [संदेह करना]
To avoid responsibility — unrelated

Related words: be suspicious, sense something fishy.

question.en: What does the idiom 'Keep an eye on' mean? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Keep an eye on [नज़र रखना] means to watch or monitor closely.

Option meanings
To watch closely — monitor [निगरानी करना]
To ignore — opposite
To scold — rebuke
To applaud — praise

Related words: look after, supervise, monitor.

question.en: What does the idiom 'Cut no ice' mean? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Cut no ice [प्रभाव न डालना] means to be ineffective or have no influence.

Option meanings
Be ineffective — have no effect [अप्रभावी होना]
Make things easier — opposite
Be impressive — opposite
Make someone laugh — unrelated

Related words: carry no weight, make no difference.

question.en: What does the idiom 'Play second fiddle' mean? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Play second fiddle [द्वितीय भूमिका निभाना] means to take a subordinate or supporting role.

Option meanings
Be a leader — opposite
Stay unimportant — close but not the idiom's sense
Take a supporting role — subordinate position [सहायक भूमिका]
Play an instrument — literal

Related words: take a back seat, play a subordinate part.

question.en: What does the idiom 'Hit below the belt' mean? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Hit below the belt [अनुचित तरीके से हमला करना] means to act unfairly or cruelly, like an illegal boxing blow.

Option meanings
Act fairly — opposite
Attack unfairly — unjust attack [अन्यायपूर्ण हमला]
Praise genuinely — opposite
Lose in style — unrelated

Related words: fight dirty, act unjustly.

question.en:
In the following question, four alternatives are given for the Idiom/Phrase underlined in the sentence. Choose the option that best expresses its meaning.
The manager was burning the midnight oil to finish the presentation before the board meeting. [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Burning the midnight oil [देर रात तक काम करना] means working late into the night.

Option meanings
Working late into the night — stay up working [देर रात तक मेहनत]
Complaining about work — unrelated
Ignoring responsibilities — opposite
Delegating tasks — unrelated

Related words: work late, burn the candle at both ends.

question.en:
Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted word:
The defendant was released on bail after the hearing. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: He paid bail to secure his friend's release from jail.

2.en: The judge set a high bail for the accused.

3.en: She rushed to the river to bail water out of the leaking boat.

4.en: The lawyer argued for a reduction in the client's bail.

solution.en:
In the given sentence, bail is a legal noun: the temporary release of an accused person on security [ज़मानत].

A homonym has the same spelling and sound but a different meaning. In option 3, bail means to scoop water out of a boat [नाव से पानी उलीचना].

Options 1, 2 and 4 use “bail” in the same legal sense as the question.

Answer: She rushed to the river to bail water out of the leaking boat.

question.en: Choose the correct sentence. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: She will bury the letter in the sand.

2.en: Please berry the box near the tree.

4.en: They berry the treasure every year.

solution.en:
Bury [दफनाना, गाड़ना] is a verb meaning to put something in the ground or hide it. Berry [बेर जैसा छोटा फल] is a noun — a small fruit.

Option 1 uses the verb correctly: She will bury the letter in the sand.

Options 2 and 4 use the noun “berry” as a verb, and option 3 uses the verb “bury” as something to eat.

question.en:
Which word fits the meaning in the clue?
Clue: A piece of writing or the act of forming letters. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The clue describes the act of forming letters, so the word is write [लिखना].

Option meanings
right — correct; also a direction or an entitlement [सही, दायाँ, अधिकार]
rite — a ceremonial act [संस्कार, अनुष्ठान]
write — to form letters or words [लिखना]
wright — a maker or builder, as in playwright [निर्माता, शिल्पी]

These four words are homophones: they sound alike but differ in spelling and meaning.

question.en:
Which of the following pairs of words can be used to fill in the blanks most suitably?
The _____ sorcerer upturned the _____ of poison into the goblet, his lips curling into a smirk. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Use vile, vial.

Vile [नीच, दुष्ट] is an adjective describing the sorcerer: wicked or evil.
Vial [शीशी] is a noun: a small glass container, here holding poison.

Complete sentence: The vile sorcerer upturned the vial of poison into the goblet, his lips curling into a smirk.

veil — a piece of cloth covering the face [घूँघट, परदा]
vail — an old word meaning to lower or take off (as a hat) [झुकाना (पुरातन)]

question.en: Which of the following options is NOT one of the meanings of the homonym 'compound'? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A substance formed from two or more elements chemically combined

2.en: A building or group of buildings enclosed by a barrier

3.en: To make something worse by adding to it

4.en: To subtract or reduce gradually over time

solution.en:
To subtract or reduce gradually over time is not a meaning of “compound”.

Compound can mean:
a chemical substance formed from two or more elements [यौगिक]
an enclosed area containing buildings [अहाता, परिसर]
to make a problem worse by adding to it [और बिगाड़ना]

It also means to combine, or to add interest to interest (compound interest) — the opposite of reducing.

question.en: Which of the following options is not one of the meanings of the homonym 'project'? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A planned piece of work to achieve a goal

2.en: To extend outward or stick out

3.en: A protective structure used in military defence

solution.en:
A protective structure used in military defence is not a meaning of “project”.

Project can mean:
a planned piece of work [परियोजना]
to stick out or extend outward [बाहर निकला होना]
to estimate or forecast [अनुमान लगाना]

A protective defensive structure is a bastion or rampart, not a project.

question.en: Which sentence has the correct homonym? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

2.en: They build a new capitel for the state.

4.en: They lived in the capital building.

solution.en:
Capital has several meanings; one is "punishable by death", as in capital punishment [मृत्युदंड]. Sentence 1 uses it correctly.
Sentence 2 misspells the word ("capitel"), sentence 3 should read "capital letter", and sentence 4 should use "Capitol" (a legislative building), in which people do not live.

Option meanings
Capital — (1) city where the government sits [राजधानी]; (2) large letter [बड़ा अक्षर]; (3) punishable by death [मृत्युदंड योग्य]; (4) wealth, money [पूँजी]
Capitol — a building where a legislature meets, e.g. the US Capitol [विधान भवन]

question.en: Which of the following options is NOT one of the meanings of the homonym 'current'? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The movement of a body of water or air

3.en: A small dried grape used in making buns and cakes

4.en: Happening or existing at the present time

solution.en:
Current (adjective) means happening at present; as a noun it means a flow of water or air, or a flow of electricity.
"A small dried grape used in buns and cakes" is a currant [छोटी सूखी किशमिश], a different word with a different spelling (a homophone), not a meaning of "current".

Option meanings
The movement of a body of water or air — current [धारा]
Electricity flowing through a wire — electric current [विद्युत धारा]
A small dried grape — currant, not current [छोटी सूखी किशमिश]
Happening or existing at the present time — current [वर्तमान]

question.en: Which of the following options is NOT one of the meanings of the homonym 'contract'? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

2.en: A written or spoken agreement enforceable by law

solution.en:
Contract can mean a legal agreement [अनुबंध], to shrink or become smaller [सिकुड़ना], or to catch a disease [रोग से ग्रस्त होना].
"To express disapproval or disappointment" is not a meaning of "contract"; that idea is expressed by words like deplore or frown on.

Option meanings
To express disapproval — not a meaning of contract [अस्वीकृति व्यक्त करना]
A written or spoken agreement enforceable by law — contract (noun) [अनुबंध]
To shrink or become smaller — contract (verb) [सिकुड़ना]
To catch or develop (a disease) — contract (verb) [रोग लगना]

question.en: Which of the following options is NOT one of the meanings of the homonym 'obscure'? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: To make something unclear or difficult to understand

2.en: Not well-known or not easily seen

3.en: To hide or conceal something partially

4.en: To look at something from an alternative perspective

solution.en:
Obscure can mean not well known or not easily seen (adjective) [अज्ञात, अस्पष्ट], to make unclear or difficult to understand (verb) [अस्पष्ट करना], or to hide partially (verb) [ढक देना].
"To look at something from an alternative perspective" is not a meaning of "obscure".

Option meanings
To make something unclear — obscure (verb) [अस्पष्ट करना]
Not well-known or not easily seen — obscure (adjective) [गुमनाम, अस्पष्ट]
To hide or conceal partially — obscure (verb) [छिपाना]
To look at something from another perspective — not a meaning of obscure [दूसरे दृष्टिकोण से देखना]

question.en: Which of the following is NOT a meaning of the homonym 'recess'? [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

2.en: A break or pause in proceedings, especially in school or court

3.en: A remote, secluded, or inner part of something

4.en: A hollow space or indentation in a wall

solution.en:
"Slow backward movement and disappearance" is the meaning of recession/receding, not of recess [अवकाश, आला].

Meanings of recess
Break — a pause in proceedings, e.g. a school or court recess [मध्यावकाश]
Remote part — a secluded or inner part, e.g. the recesses of the mind [गहन भाग]
Hollow — an indentation or alcove in a wall [आला, ताख]

Related words: Recess: interval, niche, alcove.

question.en: Which of the following options is NOT one of the meanings of the homonym 'tender'? [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: An offer to carry out work or supply goods at a stated price

3.en: A legal document authorizing someone to conduct a trial

4.en: A small boat used to ferry people or supplies to a larger ship

solution.en:
"A legal document authorizing someone to conduct a trial" is not a meaning of tender.

Meanings of tender
Offer — a formal offer to supply goods or do work at a stated price [निविदा]
Gentle — showing gentleness or concern [कोमल, स्नेही]
Boat — a small boat that ferries people or supplies to a larger ship [छोटी नौका]

Related words: Tender also appears in legal tender, meaning currency that must be accepted as payment.

question.en:
Find the homonym error.
Sentence: She will insure that everyone is invited. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The wrongly used word is "insure".

Insure [बीमा कराना] means to protect against loss through insurance.
Ensure [सुनिश्चित करना] means to make certain.
Assure [आश्वासन देना] means to promise someone.

Correct sentence: She will ensure that everyone is invited.

question.en:
Which of the following pairs of homonyms can be used to fill in the blanks most suitably?
Her slow ______ through the company ranks came only after earning the ______ of every senior executive. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Ascent [चढ़ाई, उन्नति] means a rise — her rise through the company ranks.
Assent [सहमति, स्वीकृति] means approval — she earned the approval of the executives.

Correct sentence: Her slow ascent through the company ranks came only after earning the assent of every senior executive.

question.en:
Which of the following pairs of words can be used to fill in the blanks most suitably?
The artist's refined ______ for subtle tones matched the delicate hues on her ______. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Palate [तालु; रुचि/परख] — the sense of taste; figuratively, a person's taste or appreciation (here, for subtle tones).
Palette [रंग-पट्टिका] — the board on which an artist mixes colours (where the delicate hues are).

Correct sentence: The artist's refined palate for subtle tones matched the delicate hues on her palette.

"Palatte" is misspelt. (Pallet [लकड़ी का तख़्ता] is a wooden platform for goods.)

question.en: Pick the odd Homonym from the following. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Homophones (words sharing identical pronunciation but differing in spelling and meaning):
• Flee (/fliː/) — to run away from danger [भाग जाना]
• Flea (/fliː/) — a small wingless jumping insect [पिस्सू]
Both 'flee' and 'flea' are exact homophones sharing identical pronunciation. 'Flees' is simply the 3rd person singular of flee.
• Free (/friː/) has a completely distinct consonant sound (/fr/ instead of /fl/) and does not share phonetics with 'flee/flea'.
Therefore, Free is the odd word out.

question.en: Which of the following is NOT the meaning of the homonym 'resort'? [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: A place frequently visited for a specific purpose

2.en: A popular holiday or vacation destination

3.en: To arrange things again in a particular order

4.en: To adopt a strategy, especially as a last option

solution.en:
Examine the standard polysemous meanings of the noun/verb resort:
1. Noun: A popular vacation or holiday destination with amenities [विश्राम स्थल, सैरगाह] (Option 2).
2. Noun: A place frequently visited for recreation or a specific activity (Option 1).
3. Verb: To turn to and adopt a course of action, typically an undesirable or last-choice measure ('resort to violence') [सहारा लेना] (Option 4).
• The definition 'To arrange things again in a particular order' corresponds to re-sort (with a hyphen, meaning to sort again), which is NOT a meaning of the single word 'resort'.
Therefore, Option 3 is NOT a meaning of the homonym 'resort'.

question.en: Which of the following options is NOT one of the meanings of the homonym 'restraint'? [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: A measure or condition that keeps someone or something under control

3.en: A device used to limit movement

4.en: The ability to control one's own emotions or actions

solution.en:
Examine the standard semantic meanings of restraint:
1. The act of holding back, or self-control over impulses/emotions (e.g., 'show restraint') [आत्म-नियंत्रण] (Option 4).
2. A physical device that restricts movement (e.g., seatbelts, handcuffs) [बंधन, रोकने वाला उपकरण] (Option 3).
3. A rule, measure, or condition that regulates freedom of action (Option 1).
• 'An extremely stressful situation' refers to duress, distress, or strain, NOT 'restraint'.
Therefore, Option 2 is NOT one of the meanings of 'restraint'.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate homonym.
I will bear all the expenses. [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Meaning:** In the context of enduring, managing, or sustaining financial responsibility, the verb **bear** means to carry or **tolerate** a burden or cost.
**Other options:** Animal refers to the noun bear; accept and send do not match the core definition of bearing expenses.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate homonym.
This is a beautiful rose. [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Meaning:** In the given sentence, **rose** functions as a noun naming a fragrant, thorny flowering shrub or blossom (**Flower**).
**Other options:** Stood up is the past tense of the verb *rise*; red color describes a hue; pet denotes a domestic animal.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate homonym.
The soldiers will bear arms. [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Meaning:** The phrase **bear arms** means to equip oneself with or **carry** weapons for combat.
**Other options:** Animal is the noun bear; attack and support do not represent the primary literal meaning of *bear* (to carry/hold).

question.en:
Select the most appropriate homonym.
She used a scale to measure. [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Meaning:** A **scale** used for measuring linear distance or drawing lines is commonly referred to as a **Ruler**.
**Other options:** Climb is the verbal homonym (to scale a wall); size is a dimension; balance refers to a weighing instrument.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate homonym.
They needed to date the document. [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Meaning:** To **date** a document means to affix or write the current date upon it, often done by using a date **Stamp** or seal.
**Other options:** Romance refers to social/romantic dating; record and mark do not capture the formal process of official document dating.

question.en:
Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted word:
The cobbler replaced the rubber sole with a leather one. [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: She bought a pair of leather soles for her sandals.

2.en: The sole of his shoe was worn out.

3.en: Mud had caked on the sole of her hiking shoe.

4.en: He has sole responsibility for the outcome.

solution.en:
In the prompt sentence, **sole** refers to the underside of footwear.
In option (d), **sole** functions as a different homonym meaning *only* or *exclusive* (**sole responsibility**).
Options (a), (b), and (c) all use the word in the exact same meaning as the bottom of footwear.

question.en: Choose the correctly spelt word: [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct spelling is environment [पर्यावरण].

It keeps the “n” before “-ment”: e-n-v-i-r-o-n-m-e-n-t.
“Enviroment” drops that n, “Enviornment” swaps o and r, and “Environmant” ends in -mant.

Related words: surroundings, ecosystem, habitat.

question.en: Choose the correctly spelt word: [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct spelling is disease [रोग, बीमारी].

It is dis- + ease: d-i-s-e-a-s-e.
The other options misplace or drop vowels.

Related words: illness, ailment, malady.

question.en: Choose the correctly spelt word: [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct spelling is archetypal [आदर्श-रूप, विशिष्ट नमूने जैसा].

It is archetype + -al, with the final e of “type” dropped: a-r-c-h-e-t-y-p-a-l.
The other options add an extra e or drop the e after “arch”.

Related words: typical, classic, quintessential.

question.en: Which word is spelled incorrectly? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The misspelt word is Reconnassance; the correct spelling is reconnaissance [टोही, सैन्य सर्वेक्षण].

It has “ai” and a double s: r-e-c-o-n-n-a-i-s-s-a-n-c-e.
Conscientious, indispensable and entrepreneur are spelt correctly.

Related words: survey, scouting, exploration.

question.en: One of these words is spelled incorrectly. Pick it: [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The misspelt word is Paraphanalia; the correct spelling is paraphernalia [साज़-सामान, आवश्यक सामग्री].

The middle is “-pher-”: p-a-r-a-p-h-e-r-n-a-l-i-a.
Camouflage, vicissitude and magnanimous are spelt correctly.

Related words: equipment, apparatus, accessories.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the correctly spelt word.
The _____ principle explains the limits of precision for quantum measurements. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct spelling is Heisenberg, after the German physicist Werner Heisenberg.

Letter pattern: H-e-i-s-e-n-b-e-r-g — “ei” after H and a single s.
The Heisenberg uncertainty principle [अनिश्चितता का सिद्धांत] states that position and momentum cannot both be measured with unlimited precision.

Related words: uncertainty principle, quantum mechanics.

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correctly spelt word is breathe [साँस लेना].

Letter pattern: b-r-e-a-t-h-e; the final e makes it the verb (“breath” is the noun).
The correct forms of the others are breath, brilliant, bruise.

Related words: inhale, respire, exhale.

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correctly spelt word is captain [कप्तान].

Letter pattern: c-a-p-t-a-i-n.
The correct forms of the others are burglar, campaign, careful.

Related words: leader, commander, skipper.

question.en: Select the wrongly spelt word. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The wrongly spelt word is Narow; the correct spelling is narrow [संकरा].

It has a double r: n-a-r-r-o-w.
Liquid, manage and others are spelt correctly.

Related words: slender, tight, confined.

question.en: Select the wrongly spelt word. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The wrongly spelt word is Woker; the intended word is worker [कामगार].

The letter r is missing: w-o-r-k-e-r.
Useful, velvet and yearly are spelt correctly.

Related words: labourer, employee, workman.

question.en:
Which part of the following sentence contains a spelling error?
The manager (1) was applauded for his diplomatic approach (2) and consiliatory tone (3) during the heated negotiations (4). [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Part (3) has the error: consiliatory should be conciliatory [मेल-मिलाप वाला, सुलहकारी].

It is spelt with “c” after “n”, like “conciliate”: c-o-n-c-i-l-i-a-t-o-r-y.

Correct sentence: The manager was applauded for his diplomatic approach and conciliatory tone during the heated negotiations.

Related words: placatory, appeasing, peacemaking.

question.en:
Which part of the following sentence contains a spelling error?
He received commendation (1) for his meticulous (2) work on the restoration (3) of the ancient monastry (4). [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Part (4) has the error: monastry should be monastery [मठ].

It has an “e” before “ry”: m-o-n-a-s-t-e-r-y.

Correct sentence: He received commendation for his meticulous work on the restoration of the ancient monastery.

Related words: abbey, friary, cloister.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the correctly spelt word.
The astronomer studied the ______ movement of newly discovered celestial bodies. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The correct spelling is circumstellar [तारे के चारों ओर का].

It is circum- (around) + stellar (of stars): c-i-r-c-u-m-s-t-e-l-l-a-r.

Complete sentence: The astronomer studied the circumstellar movement of newly discovered celestial bodies.

Related words: stellar, interstellar, circumplanetary.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the correctly spelt word.
The scientist was known for her ______ adherence to ethical standards. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The correct spelling is unassailable [अटल, जिस पर प्रश्न न उठ सके].

It has a double s and ends in -able: u-n-a-s-s-a-i-l-a-b-l-e.

Complete sentence: The scientist was known for her unassailable adherence to ethical standards.

Related words: unquestionable, invulnerable, irrefutable.

question.en: Select the option which is incorrectly spelt. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The incorrectly spelt word is Counttermoove; the correct form is countermove [प्रति-चाल].

It has one t and one o in “move”: c-o-u-n-t-e-r-m-o-v-e.
Contemporary, countermarch and counteroffensive are spelt correctly.

Related words: counteraction, riposte, response.

question.en: Choose the option with the correct spelling. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The correct spelling is Worcestershire, a county in England (also known for Worcestershire sauce).

Letter pattern: W-o-r-c-e-s-t-e-r-s-h-i-r-e; it is pronounced roughly “WOOS-ter-sher”, so the spelling has to be memorised.

Related words: Worcester, shire (county).

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The correct spelling is entrepreneur [उद्यमी].

It is a French borrowing: e-n-t-r-e-p-r-e-n-e-u-r — “entre” + “pre” + “neur”.
The other options misplace the “r” or change the vowels.

Related words: businessperson, industrialist, founder.

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The correct spelling is bourgeoisie [मध्यम वर्ग, पूँजीपति वर्ग].

It comes from French: b-o-u-r-g-e-o-i-s-i-e — “bourgeois” + “-ie”.
The other options drop the “e” after g or the “i” after “s”, or change “ou” to “oo”.

Related words: middle class, capitalists, propertied class.

question.en: Select the wrongly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The wrongly spelt word is ameliarate; the correct spelling is ameliorate [सुधारना, बेहतर बनाना].

It has “io”: a-m-e-l-i-o-r-a-t-e (from Latin “melior”, better).
Perseverance, conscience and magnanimity are spelt correctly.

Related words: improve, enhance, alleviate.

question.en: Select the wrongly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The wrongly spelt word is exasperete; the correct spelling is exasperate [बहुत चिढ़ाना, खिझाना].

It ends in “-ate”: e-x-a-s-p-e-r-a-t-e.
Separate, equivalent and temperature are spelt correctly.

Related words: irritate, infuriate, annoy.

question.en: Choose the correctly spelt word: [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Reminiscence [पुरानी यादें, संस्मरण] is the correct spelling: re-mi-nis-cence ("sc" in the middle and ending "-cence").
It means the act of recalling past experiences.

Reminicense misses the "s" before "c", Reminicens is incomplete, and Reminance drops a whole syllable.

question.en: Choose the correctly spelt word: [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Epitome [प्रतीक, आदर्श उदाहरण] is the correct spelling: e-pi-to-me (single "t", ending "-ome").
It means a perfect example of a quality or type, e.g. "She is the epitome of kindness."

Epitomi ends in "i", Epittome has a double "t", and Epittomi has both errors.

question.en: Select the correct spelling of a word meaning 'falsely attractive or showy'. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Meretricious [भड़कीला, दिखावटी] is the correct spelling: mer-e-tri-cious.
It means apparently attractive but having no real value.

Meretritious uses "t" for "c", Meretriscious adds an extra "s", and Merritricious has a double "r".

question.en: Select the correct spelling of a word meaning 'using few words, concise'. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Laconic [संक्षिप्त, कम शब्दों वाला] is the correct spelling: la-con-ic, ending in "-ic".
It means using very few words, e.g. "a laconic reply".

Laconique is the French form, and Laconick and Laconik use wrong endings.

question.en: Identify the misspelt word. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:

Prodigy — a young person with exceptional talent [विलक्षण प्रतिभा]
Ineffable — too great to be expressed in words [अवर्णनीय]

question.en: Identify the misspelt word. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Antedeluvean is misspelt; the correct spelling is Antediluvian [अत्यंत पुराना]: ante-dil-u-vian.

Option meanings
Sesquipedalian — using long words [लंबे शब्दों वाला]
Antediluvian — extremely old-fashioned [अत्यंत पुराना]
Cacophony — a harsh mixture of sounds [कर्कश ध्वनि]
Triskaidekaphobia — fear of the number 13 [13 अंक का भय]

question.en: Identify the misspelt word. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Committment is misspelt; the correct spelling is Commitment [प्रतिबद्धता], with a double "m" but a single "t".

Option meanings
Farrago — a confused mixture [घालमेल]
Imbroglio — a complicated, embarrassing situation [उलझन]

question.en: Identify the misspelt word. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

Option meanings
