Rendezvous — a meeting at an agreed time and place [पूर्वनिर्धारित भेंट]

question.en: Choose the correct spelling of a word meaning: 'refusing to change opinion'. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Obstinate [हठी, ज़िद्दी] is the correct spelling: ob-sti-nate.
It means stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion.

Obstenate uses "e" for "i", Obstinatte has a double "t", and Obstinete ends in "-ete".

question.en: Choose the correct spelling of a word meaning: 'lacking interest or excitement'. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Insipid [फीका, नीरस] is the correct spelling: in-si-pid.
It means lacking flavour, interest or excitement.

Insepid uses "e" for the first "i", Insypid uses "y", and Insippid has a double "p".

question.en: One of these words is spelled incorrectly. Which one is it? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Irredescent is misspelt; the correct spelling is Iridescent [इंद्रधनुषी, रंग बदलती चमक वाला]: i-ri-des-cent (single "r", "i" after "r").

Option meanings
Perspicacious — having sharp insight [सूक्ष्मदर्शी, कुशाग्र]
Remuneration — payment for work [पारिश्रमिक]
Intransigent — refusing to change one's views [अड़ियल]
Iridescent — showing shimmering rainbow colours [इंद्रधनुषी]

question.en: Select the wrongly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Harbingar is misspelt; the correct spelling is Harbinger [अग्रदूत]: har-bin-ger, ending in "-ger".
It means a sign that something is going to happen.

Assessment, passenger and adjustment are spelt correctly.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the correctly spelt word.
The biologist studied _________ organisms found deep underwater. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Abyssopelagic [गहरे समुद्री क्षेत्र से संबंधित] is the correct spelling: abyss-o-pelagic, with a double "s" in abyss and a single "l" in pelagic.
It refers to the deep-ocean zone, about 4,000–6,000 m below the surface.

Abissopelagic uses "i" for "y", abysopelagic has a single "s", and abyssopellagic has a double "l".

Correct sentence:
The biologist studied abyssopelagic organisms found deep underwater.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the correctly spelt word.
The king ruled with _________ authority. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Antediluvian [अत्यंत पुराना, पुराने ज़माने का] is the correct spelling: ante (before) + diluvian (flood), literally "before the Flood", i.e. very old-fashioned.

Correct sentence:
The king ruled with antediluvian authority.

Antidiluvian uses "anti" for "ante", antedeluvian has "e" for "i" in "diluv", and antediluvean ends wrongly in "-ean".

question.en: Select the option which is incorrectly spelt. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Bourgoeis is incorrectly spelt; the correct spelling is Bourgeois [मध्यमवर्गीय, पूँजीवादी] (b-o-u-r-g-e-o-i-s).

Option meanings
Baccalaureate — a bachelor's degree or a school-leaving examination [स्नातक उपाधि]
Anemone — a flowering plant; also a sea animal (sea anemone) [एनीमोन पुष्प]
Bourgeois — relating to the middle class, often materialistic [मध्यमवर्गीय]
Aisle — a passage between rows of seats [गलियारा]

question.en: Select the option which is incorrectly spelt. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Prerequesite is incorrectly spelt; the correct spelling is Prerequisite [पूर्व-शर्त]: pre-requ-i-site.

Option meanings
Participate — to take part [भाग लेना]
Hardiness — the ability to endure difficult conditions [सहनशक्ति]
Prerequisite — something required beforehand [पूर्व-शर्त]
Hideaways — secret or secluded places [छिपने के स्थान]

question.en: Choose the option with the correct spelling. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Defibrillator [हृदय की धड़कन सामान्य करने वाला उपकरण] is the correct spelling: de-fib-rill-ator.
It is a device that gives an electric shock to restore the normal rhythm of the heart.

Defibrilater has a single "l" and ends in "-ater"; Difribrillater begins with "Di", adds an extra "r" and ends in "-ater"; Defribrillator adds an extra "r" after "f".

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Mellifluous [मधुर, कर्णप्रिय] is the correct spelling: mell-i-flu-ous (double "l", "flu", ending "-ous").
It means sweet and smooth-sounding, e.g. "a mellifluous voice".

Melifluous has a single "l", Mellifluas ends in "-as", and Melliflouous adds an extra "o".

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Resuscitation [पुनर्जीवन] is the correct spelling: re-sus-ci-ta-tion.
It means reviving someone from unconsciousness or apparent death, as in "cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR)".

Resussitation uses "ss" for "sc", Resuscetation has "e" for "i", and Rezuscitation uses "z" for "s".

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Surveillance [निगरानी] is the correct spelling: sur-veil-lance ("ei", double "l", "-ance").
It means close observation of a person or place, especially by the police or security agencies.

Survaillance has "ai" for "ei", Surveillence ends in "-ence", and Surveliance drops the "i" of "veil" and has a single "l".

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Trepidation [घबराहट, भय] is the correct spelling: tre-pi-da-tion.
It means a feeling of fear or anxiety about something that may happen.

Trepedation has "e" for "i", Treppidation has a double "p", and Trepidacion ends in "-cion".

question.en: Select the wrongly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Impertubable is wrongly spelt; the correct spelling is Imperturbable [अविचलित, शांत], with "r" in "-tur-" (im-per-tur-bable).
It means calm and not easily upset.

Option meanings
Maintenance — the process of keeping something in good condition [रखरखाव]
Sovereignty — supreme power or authority [संप्रभुता]
Imperturbable — calm, not easily upset [अविचलित]
Lieutenant — a junior officer rank in the armed forces [लेफ़्टिनेंट]

question.en: Select the wrongly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:

Option meanings

Questionnaire — a set of written questions [प्रश्नावली] (double "n")

question.en: Choose the correctly spelt word: [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Obfuscation [अस्पष्ट या भ्रमित करना] is the correct spelling: obf-u-s-c-a-tion.
It means making something deliberately unclear or confusing.

Obfescation has "e" in place of "u", Obfusication adds an extra "i", and Obfuscasion ends wrongly in "-sion".

question.en: Select the correct spelling of a word meaning 'to free someone from blame'. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The word meaning "to free someone from blame" is exonerate [दोषमुक्त करना], spelt e-x-o-n-e-r-a-t-e (no "h", single "r").

Exhonorate adds "h" and changes the vowels, Exonerrate doubles the "r", and Exhonoratte has three errors.

Related words: Exonerate: acquit, absolve, vindicate.

question.en:
Select the correctly spelt word to complete the below given sentence.
India is located on the continent of ______. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The name of the continent is spelt A-s-i-a.
India is located on the continent of Asia.

Aisa swaps the letters, Ashia adds "h", and Asiya adds "y".

question.en:
Select the correctly spelt word to complete the below given sentence.
The government provides ______ subsidies to support farmers in India. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correct spelling is agricultural [कृषि-संबंधी]: a-g-r-i-c-u-l-t-u-r-a-l.
The government provides agricultural subsidies to support farmers in India.

Aggricultural doubles the "g", agricultral misses the "u" after "t", and agricutural misses the "l".

question.en: One of these words is spelled incorrectly. Which one is it? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Malapropismm is misspelt; the correct spelling is Malapropism (single "m" at the end).

Option meanings
Obsequious — too eager to please or obey [चापलूस]
Unassailable — that cannot be attacked or questioned [अजेय, अकाट्य]
Misanthrope — a person who dislikes humankind [मानवद्वेषी]

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the correctly spelt word.
The scientist used ______ techniques to analyze the molecular structure. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correct spelling is spectroscopy [स्पेक्ट्रमिकी]: spectr-o-sc-o-py.
It is the study of how matter absorbs or emits light and other radiation.

Spectroscapy and spectrascopy change a vowel, and spectrascoppy also doubles the "p".

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the correctly spelt word.
The insects displayed ______ behavior before migration. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correct spelling is crepuscular [गोधूलि-कालीन, संध्या/भोर में सक्रिय]: c-r-e-p-u-s-c-u-l-a-r.
It describes animals or insects that are active at twilight (dawn and dusk).

Related words: Nocturnal — active at night [निशाचर]; diurnal — active by day [दिवाचर].

question.en:
Which part of the following sentence contains a spelling error?
The panellists (1) engaged in a thought-provoking dialogue (2) on post-modern ethics, but one speaker's argumentation (3) lacked coherance (4). [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Part (4) contains the error: "coherance" should be "coherence" [सुसंगतता], meaning the quality of being logical and consistent.

"Panellists" (British spelling), "thought-provoking dialogue" and "argumentation" are correctly spelt.

Correct sentence:
The panellists engaged in a thought-provoking dialogue on post-modern ethics, but one speaker's argumentation lacked coherence.

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correct spelling is Hemorrhage [रक्तस्राव]: h-e-m-o-rr-h-a-g-e (British spelling: haemorrhage).
It means heavy bleeding from a damaged blood vessel.

Hemorage misses one "r" and the "h", Hemmorhage doubles the "m" and has a single "r", and Hemorrhagee adds an extra "e".

question.en: Select the wrongly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

question.en:

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the correctly spelt word.
The geology professor explained the formation of ______ rock layers. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct spelling is schistose [शिस्ट जैसी परतदार], meaning having the layered structure of schist rock.

Pattern: s-c-h-i-s-t-o-s-e (single s after "schi").

Related words: Schistose: foliated, laminated, layered.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the correctly spelt word.
The desert's ______ landscape stretched endlessly. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct spelling is xerophytic [शुष्कता-सहिष्णु], meaning adapted to very dry conditions.

Pattern: xero (dry) + phyt (plant) + ic.

Related words: Xerophytic: arid, drought-resistant, desert-adapted.

question.en: Select the option which is incorrectly spelt. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Embarass is misspelt; the correct spelling is embarrass [शर्मिंदा करना], with double r and double s.

Archaeology, Bellwether and Colloquial are spelt correctly.

question.en: Choose the option with the correct spelling. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct spelling is surveillance [निगरानी].

Pattern: sur-veil-lance (the word "veil" + double l).

Related words: Surveillance: monitoring, observation, scrutiny.

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct spelling is treacherously [विश्वासघात से, ख़तरनाक ढंग से].

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:

Pattern: sil-hou-ette (single l, "hou", double t, final e).

question.en: Select the wrongly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:

Miscellaneous, millennium and hierarchy are spelt correctly.

Related words: Quixotic: idealistic, impractical, romantic.

question.en: Select the wrongly spelt word out of the four alternatives. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:

Temperature, meticulously and preliminary are spelt correctly.

question.en: Choose the correctly spelt word: [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Successful [सफल] is the correct spelling: double c, double s and a single l at the end.

Succesful misses one s, Successfull adds an extra l, and Succesfull has both errors.

question.en: Choose the correctly spelt word: [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Idiosyncrasy [व्यक्तिगत विशेषता, सनक] — a habit or way of behaving peculiar to one person — is the correct spelling: idio + syn + crasy.

Ideosyncrasy has "e" for "i", Idiosynchrasy adds an "h", and Idiosyncresy has "e" for "a".

question.en:
Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence with the correct spelling of the word:
The company's core values are ______ and do not change over time. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Immutable [अपरिवर्तनीय] means unchanging over time, which fits "do not change over time", and it is spelt correctly.

Mutable (changeable [परिवर्तनशील]) is spelt correctly but gives the opposite meaning; immuatable and Immutible are misspelt.

Related words: Immutable: unchangeable, fixed, permanent.

question.en: Which of the following words is spelled incorrectly? [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Mischievious is misspelt; the correct spelling is mischievous [शरारती], with no "i" after "v".

Embellishment [अलंकरण], Discrepancy [विसंगति] and Catastrophe [आपदा] are spelt correctly.

question.en: Which word is spelled incorrectly? [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Disenfranchize is misspelt; the correct spelling is disenfranchise [मताधिकार या अधिकार से वंचित करना], always with -ise.

Surreptitious [चोरी-छिपे], Magniloquent [आडंबरपूर्ण भाषा वाला] and Connoisseur [पारखी] are spelt correctly.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the correctly spelt word.
The DNA strands were separated through ______ methods. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Electrophoresis [वैद्युत कण-संचलन] — the technique that separates DNA fragments using an electric field — is spelt with "ph", a single "r" and the ending -esis.

Electroforesis uses "f", electrophorresis doubles the "r", and electrophoreses is the plural form.

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Answer [उत्तर] is spelt correctly.

The others should be analyse/analyze [विश्लेषण करना], annual [वार्षिक] and annoyed [नाराज़].

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Choose [चुनना] is spelt correctly.

The others should be cashier [खज़ांची], celery [सेलेरी, एक पत्तेदार सब्ज़ी] and character [चरित्र].

question.en: Select the wrongly spelt word. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Priviledge is misspelt; the correct spelling is privilege [विशेषाधिकार], with no "d".

Dinner, Entire and Golden are spelt correctly.

question.en: Select the wrongly spelt word. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Ziper is misspelt; the correct spelling is zipper [ज़िप], with double "p".

Answer, Butter and Carbon are spelt correctly.

question.en:
Select the option that correctly completes the quote with the correct spelling of the word.
Quote: "True _____ consists of helping others without expecting anything in return." [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correctly spelt word is altruism [परोपकारिता, निःस्वार्थ सेवा].

Spelling Rule: Derived from the Italian altrui ('others', from Latin alter), the standard spelling is: a-l-t-r-u-i-s-m.
• 'Alturism', 'altrusim', and 'altruisum' are all phonetically distorted misspellings.

Related words: philanthropy, benevolence, selflessness, unselfishness.

question.en:
Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence with the proper spelling of the word:
Sentence: The philosopher's writings often contrast strict self-discipline with pure _____ [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correctly spelt word is hedonism [सुखवाद, भोगवाद].

Spelling Rule: Derived from the Greek hedone ('pleasure'), the correct spelling is: h-e-d-o-n-i-s-m (single 'd', single 'n').
• The other options incorrectly double the 'n', add an 'a', or corrupt the vowel structure.

Related words: sensualism, epicureanism, self-indulgence, debauchery.

question.en: Which of the following words is spelled incorrectly? [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The incorrectly spelt word is Truculance (Option 3); the correct standard spelling is truculence [आक्रामकता, उद्दंडता, क्रूरता].

Spelling Analysis:
• The suffix is -ence, not -ance: t-r-u-c-u-l-e-n-c-e (adjective: truculent).
• Soliloquy (the act of speaking one's thoughts aloud when alone) is spelt correctly.
• Metamorphosis (transformation) is spelt correctly.
• Juxtaposition (placing close together for contrast) is spelt correctly.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the correctly spelt word.
The patient's _____ behavior indicated a severe disorder of thought processes. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correctly spelt word is idiosyncratic [अजीब, विशिष्ट, स्वभावगत].

Spelling Rule: Derived from Greek idios ('one's own') + synkrasis ('temperament/mixture'):
• The initial vowel is i-d-i-o- (not 'ideo-').
• The medial syllables are -s-y-n-c-r-a-t-i-c.
• Combining gives: i-d-i-o-s-y-n-c-r-a-t-i-c.

Related words: eccentric, peculiar, anomalous, distinctive.

question.en: Select the option which is incorrectly spelt. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The incorrectly spelt word is Manuever (Option 3); the correct standard spelling is maneuver (US) or manoeuvre (UK) [रणनीतिक चाल, युक्ति].

Spelling Analysis:
• The letter 'u' comes AFTER the 'e': m-a-n-e-u-v-e-r (the option mistakenly places 'u' before 'e': 'manuever').
• Macabre (disturbing and horrifying because of death) is spelt correctly.
• Mnemonic (a memory aid system) is spelt correctly.
• Maelstrom (a powerful whirlpool or confused state) is spelt correctly.

question.en: Choose the option with the correct spelling. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
"The architect could have been designing the building." [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

2.en: The building could have been designed.

3.en: The building could be being designed.

4.en: The building could have been being designed.

solution.en:
Rule
Modal perfect continuous (could have been + V-ing) becomes could have been being + past participle in the passive.

Explicit changes
The object “the building” becomes the subject.
“could have been designing” becomes “could have been being designed”.
The agent “by the architect” may be dropped, as in the options.

Final sentence
The building could have been being designed.

Options 1 and 2 lose the continuous aspect, and option 3 loses the perfect aspect.

question.en:
Select the correct active form.
"Such mistakes are not expected to be made by trained professionals." [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Trained professionals are not making such mistakes.

2.en: Trained professionals are not expected to make such mistakes.

3.en: Trained professionals should not have made such mistakes.

solution.en:
Rule
In “are not expected to be made by…”, only the infinitive is passive; make the infinitive active and keep “are not expected”.

Explicit changes
The agent “trained professionals” becomes the subject.
“to be made” becomes “to make”.
“Such mistakes” becomes the object of “make”.

Final sentence
Trained professionals are not expected to make such mistakes.

The other options change the meaning (a present action, a past criticism or a habit) instead of converting the voice.

question.en:
Identify the correct active voice transformation of the following sentence:
"Her routine work has been completed by my mother." [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: My mother has completing her routine work.

2.en: my mother has completed routine work

3.en: My mother has completed her routine work

4.en: My mother has been completed her routine work

solution.en:
Rule
Present perfect passive (has been + V3) becomes present perfect active (has + V3).

Explicit changes
The agent “my mother” becomes the subject.
“has been completed” becomes “has completed”.
“Her routine work” becomes the object.

Final sentence
My mother has completed her routine work.

Option 1 uses “has completing”, option 2 drops “her” and the capital letter, and option 4 wrongly keeps “been”.

Keep the rest of the sentence unchanged, including “in this case”.

Correct sentence: The witness chose to stay silent in this case.

Option 1 drops “this”, option 3 has no finite verb (“choosing”), and option 4 wrongly uses “to staying”.

question.en:
Change the following active voice sentence into passive voice by selecting the correct option.
The district education officer monitors school infrastructure. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: School infrastructure has been monitored by the district education officer.

2.en: School infrastructure is monitored by the district education officer.

3.en: School infrastructure was monitored by the district education officer.

4.en: School infrastructure will be monitored by the district education officer.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple present active (V1 / V1-s) becomes is/are + past participle in the passive.

Explicit changes
The object “school infrastructure” becomes the subject.
“monitors” becomes “is monitored” (singular subject).
The subject becomes the agent: “by the district education officer”.

Final sentence
School infrastructure is monitored by the district education officer.

The other options change the tense.

question.en:
Change the following active voice sentence into passive voice by selecting the correct option.

2.en: New welfare schemes have been introduced by the central government.

3.en: New welfare schemes were introduced by the central government.

4.en: New welfare schemes will be introduced by the central government.

solution.en:
Rule
Present perfect active (has/have + V3) becomes has/have been + past participle.

Explicit changes
“new welfare schemes” becomes the subject.
“has introduced” becomes “have been introduced” (plural subject).
Add the agent “by the central government”.

Final sentence
New welfare schemes have been introduced by the central government.

The other options change the tense.

question.en:
Change the following passive voice sentence into active voice by selecting the correct option.
Laws against poaching are enforced rigorously by the Wildlife Protection Act. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The Wildlife Protection Act enforces laws against poaching rigorously.

2.en: Laws against poaching were enforced rigorously by the Wildlife Protection Act.

3.en: Laws against poaching will be enforced rigorously by the Wildlife Protection Act.

4.en: The Wildlife Protection Act is enforcing laws against poaching rigorously.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple present passive (are + V3) becomes simple present active (V1 / V1-s).

Explicit changes
The agent “the Wildlife Protection Act” becomes the subject.
“are enforced” becomes “enforces” (singular subject).
“laws against poaching” becomes the object; “rigorously” stays with the verb.

Final sentence
The Wildlife Protection Act enforces laws against poaching rigorously.

Options 2 and 3 remain passive, and option 4 changes the tense.

question.en:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.
The new policy was announced to the public. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Someone announced the new policy to the public.

2.en: The new policy had been announced to the public.

3.en: The public announced the new policy.

4.en: They are announcing the new policy to the public.

solution.en:
Rule
When the passive sentence names no agent, use a general subject such as “someone” or “they” in the active voice; keep the tense.

Explicit changes
Supply the subject “Someone”.
Simple past passive “was announced” becomes simple past active “announced”.
“The new policy” becomes the object; “to the public” stays.

Final sentence
Someone announced the new policy to the public.

Option 2 stays passive, option 3 makes the public the announcer, and option 4 changes the tense.

question.en:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.
His application had been looked over by a special committee for weeks. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: A special committee has looked over his application for weeks.

2.en: A special committee was looking over his application for weeks.

3.en: A special committee had been looking over his application for weeks.

4.en: His application was looked over by a special committee.

solution.en:
Rule
Past perfect passive (had been + V3) corresponds to the past perfect in the active; with “for weeks”, the action is a continuing one up to a past point.

Explicit changes
The agent “a special committee” becomes the subject.
“His application” becomes the object of “looking over”.
The past perfect time frame is kept with “had”; “for weeks” shows duration, which the continuous form expresses.

Final sentence
A special committee had been looking over his application for weeks.

The strict form “had looked over” is not offered; options 1 and 2 change the time frame and option 4 is still passive.

question.en:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:
He will write a novel next year. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: A novel will have been written by him next year.

2.en: A novel would be written by him next year.

3.en: A novel is going to be written by him next year.

4.en: A novel will be written by him next year.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple future active (will + V1) becomes will be + past participle.

Explicit changes
“a novel” becomes the subject.
“will write” becomes “will be written”.
“he” becomes the agent “by him”; “next year” stays.

Final sentence
A novel will be written by him next year.

Options 1, 2 and 3 change the tense or the modal.

question.en:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:
We will not open the store until 9 a.m. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The store will not open until 9 a.m.

2.en: The store is not opened by us until 9 a.m.

3.en: The store would not be opened by us until 9 a.m.

4.en: The store will not be opened by us until 9 a.m.

solution.en:
Rule
“will not + V1” becomes will not be + past participle.

Explicit changes
“the store” becomes the subject.
“will not open” becomes “will not be opened”.
“we” becomes “by us”; “until 9 a.m.” stays.

Final sentence
The store will not be opened by us until 9 a.m.

Option 1 is an active intransitive sentence, and options 2 and 3 change the tense or the modal.

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
Take a pair of binoculars with you lest you all should miss the chance of looking at the distant scenes. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you lest the chance of looking at the distant scenes would missed by you all.

2.en: Let a pair of binoculars taken with you lest the chance of looking at the distant scenes should be missed by you all.

3.en: Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you otherwise the chance of looking at the distant scenes would be missed by you all.

4.en: Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you lest the chance of looking at the distant scenes should be missed by you all.

solution.en:
Rule
An imperative becomes Let + object + be + past participle; the “lest … should” clause also turns passive: lest + new subject + should be + past participle.

Explicit changes
“Take a pair of binoculars with you” → “Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you”.
“you all should miss the chance” → “the chance … should be missed by you all”.
Keep “lest”; it is followed by “should”.

Final sentence
Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you lest the chance of looking at the distant scenes should be missed by you all.

Option 1 has “would missed”, option 2 omits “be”, and option 3 replaces “lest … should” with “otherwise … would”.

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
The tiger ate all the flesh that the zoo-keeper had kept in the enclosure. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: All the flesh that had been kept by the zoo-keeper in the enclosure was eaten by the tiger.

2.en: All the flesh that was kept by the zoo-keeper in the enclosure was eaten by the tiger.

3.en: All the flesh that had been kept by the zoo-keeper in the enclosure had been eaten by the tiger.

4.en: All the flesh that was kept by the zoo-keeper in the enclosure had been eaten by the tiger.

solution.en:
Rule
Change both clauses: simple past (ate) → was/were + V3; past perfect (had kept) → had been + V3.

Explicit changes
“all the flesh” becomes the subject of the main clause: “was eaten by the tiger”.
The relative clause becomes “that had been kept by the zoo-keeper in the enclosure”.

Final sentence
All the flesh that had been kept by the zoo-keeper in the enclosure was eaten by the tiger.

Option 2 changes the past perfect, and options 3 and 4 change the simple past of the main clause.

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
The cheetah chased the wild boar with lightening speed. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The wild boar has been chased with lightening speed by the cheetah.

2.en: The wild boar was chased with lightening speed by the cheetah.

3.en: The wild boar had been chased with lightening speed by the cheetah.

4.en: The wild boar was being chased with lightening speed by the cheetah.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple past active (V2) becomes was/were + past participle.

Explicit changes
“the wild boar” becomes the subject.
“chased” becomes “was chased”.
“the cheetah” becomes the agent “by the cheetah”.

Final sentence
The wild boar was chased with lightening speed by the cheetah.

The other options change the tense. [The standard spelling is “lightning speed”.]

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
Suruchi exclaimed that the fish possessed a very big dorsal fin. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: It was exclaimed by Suruchi that a very big dorsal fin was possessed by the fish.

2.en: It was exclaimed by Suruchi that a very big dorsal fin had been possessed by the fish.

3.en: Suruchi exclaimed that a very big dorsal fin is possessed by the fish.

4.en: It exclaimed Suruchi that a very big dorsal fin was possessed by the fish.

solution.en:
Rule
Both clauses are in the simple past. The main clause becomes “It was exclaimed by Suruchi that…”, and the that-clause becomes “was + past participle”.

Explicit changes
“Suruchi exclaimed” → “It was exclaimed by Suruchi”.
“the fish possessed a very big dorsal fin” → “a very big dorsal fin was possessed by the fish”.

Final sentence
It was exclaimed by Suruchi that a very big dorsal fin was possessed by the fish.

Option 2 changes the tense of the that-clause, option 3 changes it to the present, and option 4 is ungrammatical.

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
The usher must have made the guests sit by the time the dinner was ready. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The guests must have been made sit by the usher by the time the dinner was ready.

2.en: The guests must have been made to sit by the usher by the time the dinner was ready.

3.en: The guests must have been made to sit by the usher by the time the dinner had been ready.

4.en: The guests must have made to sit by the usher by the time the dinner had been ready.

solution.en:
Rule
Active make + person + base verb becomes person + be made + to-infinitive in the passive; “must have made” becomes “must have been made”.

Explicit changes
“the guests” becomes the subject.
“must have made … sit” becomes “must have been made to sit”.
Add the agent “by the usher”; the time clause “by the time the dinner was ready” stays unchanged.

Final sentence
The guests must have been made to sit by the usher by the time the dinner was ready.

Option 1 omits “to”, and options 3 and 4 wrongly change the time clause (option 4 also omits “been”).

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
A table was reserved for the family at the restaurant. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: They reserved a table for the family at the restaurant.

2.en: The family reserved a table for them at the restaurant.

3.en: The restaurant reserved a table for the family by them.

4.en: They were reserving a table for the family at the restaurant.

solution.en:
Rule
If the passive sentence names no agent, supply a general subject such as “they” and keep the tense.

Explicit changes
Add the subject “They”.
“was reserved” becomes “reserved”.
“a table” becomes the object; “for the family at the restaurant” stays.

Final sentence
They reserved a table for the family at the restaurant.

Option 2 changes who reserved the table, option 3 is confused, and option 4 changes the tense.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
The cake was decorated by the children for the party. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The children decorated the cake for the party.

2.en: The children were decorating the cake for the party.

3.en: The children decorate the cake for the party.

4.en: The cake decorated the children for the party.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple past passive (was + V3) becomes simple past active (V2).

Explicit changes
The agent “the children” becomes the subject.
“was decorated” becomes “decorated”.
“the cake” becomes the object; “for the party” stays.

Final sentence
The children decorated the cake for the party.

Options 2 and 3 change the tense, and option 4 reverses the roles.

question.en:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.
The construction of the skyscraper is scheduled to have been completed by the end of the year. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The skyscraper will have completed the construction by the end of the year.

2.en: They are scheduling to have completed the construction of the skyscraper by the end of the year.

3.en: The construction of the skyscraper will be completed by the end of the year.

4.en: They are scheduled to complete the construction of the skyscraper by the end of the year.

solution.en:
Rule
In “is scheduled to have been completed”, the infinitive is passive. Make it active with a general subject (“they”), keeping “are scheduled”.

Explicit changes
Supply the subject “They”.
“is scheduled” becomes “are scheduled” (plural subject).
The passive infinitive becomes active; among the options, “to complete” expresses it.
“The construction of the skyscraper” becomes the object.

Final sentence
They are scheduled to complete the construction of the skyscraper by the end of the year.

Option 1 makes the skyscraper the doer, option 2 uses “are scheduling”, and option 3 is still passive.

question.en:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.
The new theory is said to have been developed over decades. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: They say that the new theory has been developed over decades.

2.en: They say that the new theory was developed over decades.

3.en: Someone is said to have developed the new theory over decades.

4.en: The new theory developed over decades.

solution.en:
Rule
“Is said to have been + V3” is a passive reporting structure. In the active, use “Someone is said to have + V3”, keeping the perfect infinitive.

Explicit changes
The unknown doer becomes “someone”.
“to have been developed” becomes “to have developed”.
“The new theory” becomes the object.

Final sentence
Someone is said to have developed the new theory over decades.

Options 1 and 2 are still passive, and option 4 changes the meaning.

question.en:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.
The decision will have been announced before the meeting concludes. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Someone was announced the decision before the meeting concludes.

2.en: They will have announced the decision before the meeting concludes.

3.en: The decision will be announced before the meeting concludes.

4.en: The meeting will have announced the decision.

solution.en:
Rule
Future perfect passive (will have been + V3) becomes future perfect active (will have + V3); supply “they” for the unnamed agent.

Explicit changes
Add the subject “They”.
“will have been announced” becomes “will have announced”.
“the decision” becomes the object.

Final sentence
They will have announced the decision before the meeting concludes.

Option 1 is ungrammatical, option 3 is passive, and option 4 makes the meeting the doer.

question.en:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.
"The heavy bag was carefully carried across the room by Jonathan." [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Jonathan carefully carring the heavy bag across the room.

2.en: Jonathan carefully have carried the heavy bag across the room.

3.en: Jonathan carefully carried the heavy bag across the room.

4.en: Jonathan carefully carried the heavy bag the room.

solution.en:
Rule
Passive (simple past): object + was/were + V3 + by + subject
Active (simple past): subject + V2 + object

Explicit changes
by Jonathan → Jonathan becomes the subject
was carried → carried (V2, simple past)
The heavy bag → the heavy bag becomes the object
"carefully" and "across the room" stay unchanged

Final sentence
Jonathan carefully carried the heavy bag across the room.

Option 1 uses the wrong form "carring", option 2 changes the tense to "have carried" with the wrong auxiliary, and option 4 drops "across".

question.en:
Change the following sentence from active to passive:
By the end of the semester, the professors will have been evaluating the thesis papers. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The thesis papers were evaluated by the professors by the end of the semester.

2.en: The professors have been evaluating the thesis papers by the end of the semester.

3.en: The thesis papers will be evaluated by the professors by the end of the semester.

4.en: The thesis papers will have been being evaluated by the professors by the end of the semester.

solution.en:
Rule
Active (future perfect continuous): will have been + V-ing
Passive: will have been being + V3

Explicit changes
the thesis papers (object) → subject
will have been evaluating → will have been being evaluated
the professors → by the professors
"By the end of the semester" stays unchanged

Final sentence
The thesis papers will have been being evaluated by the professors by the end of the semester.

Options 1 and 3 change the tense to simple past and simple future, and option 2 is not passive at all.

question.en:
Change the following sentence from active to passive:
The supervisor would have been checking the report drafts overnight. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The report drafts were being checked overnight by the supervisor.

2.en: The supervisor had been checking the report drafts overnight.

3.en: The report drafts would have been being checked overnight by the supervisor.

4.en: The report drafts would have checked overnight by the supervisor.

solution.en:
Rule
Active (perfect continuous with "would"): would have been + V-ing
Passive: would have been being + V3

Explicit changes
the report drafts (object) → subject
would have been checking → would have been being checked
the supervisor → by the supervisor

Final sentence
The report drafts would have been being checked overnight by the supervisor.

Option 1 changes the tense to past continuous, option 2 is not passive, and option 4 ("would have checked") lacks "been" and is not passive.

question.en:
Change the following sentence from active to passive:
The deliberation team may have been outlining alternative scenarios during the session. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The deliberation team outlined alternative scenarios during the session.

2.en: Alternative scenarios were outlined during the session by the deliberation team.

3.en: Alternative scenarios have been outlined during the session by the deliberation team.

4.en: Alternative scenarios may have been being outlined during the session by the deliberation team.

solution.en:
Rule
Active (perfect continuous with "may"): may have been + V-ing
Passive: may have been being + V3

Explicit changes
alternative scenarios (object) → subject
may have been outlining → may have been being outlined
the deliberation team → by the deliberation team

Final sentence
Alternative scenarios may have been being outlined during the session by the deliberation team.

Option 1 is active, and options 2 and 3 drop the modal "may" and change the tense.

question.en:
Change the following active voice sentence into passive voice by selecting the correct option.
The Prime Minister inaugurates new highways annually in India. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: New highways in India were inaugurated by the Prime Minister annually.

2.en: New highways are inaugurated by the Prime Minister annually in India.

3.en: The Prime Minister will inaugurate new highways annually in India.

4.en: New highways in India are being inaugurated by the Prime Minister annually.

solution.en:
Rule
Active (simple present): subject + V1/V5 + object
Passive: object + is/are + V3 + by + subject

Explicit changes
new highways (object) → subject (plural, so "are")
inaugurates → are inaugurated
The Prime Minister → by the Prime Minister
"annually in India" stays unchanged

Final sentence
New highways are inaugurated by the Prime Minister annually in India.

Option 1 changes the tense to past, option 3 is active future, and option 4 changes it to present continuous.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
How often is he praised by his teachers! [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: His teachers praise him so often!

2.en: He praises his teachers so often!

3.en: He is praising his teachers so often!

4.en: How often does he praise his teachers!

solution.en:
Rule
Passive: is + V3 + by + agent → Active: agent + V1/V5 + object.
The agent "his teachers" becomes the subject, and "he" becomes the object "him".

Explicit changes
by his teachers → His teachers (subject)
is praised → praise (simple present, plural subject)
he → him (object)

Final sentence
His teachers praise him so often!

Options 2, 3 and 4 wrongly make "he" the one who praises.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
Let the work be finished by tonight. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

3.en: You finish the work by tonight.

4.en: The work has to finish by tonight.

solution.en:
Rule
A passive imperative "Let + object + be + V3" becomes an active imperative: V1 + object.

Explicit changes
Let the work be finished → Finish the work
"by tonight" stays unchanged

Final sentence
Finish the work by tonight.

question.en:
Change the following active voice sentence into passive voice by selecting the correct option.
They will have completed the railway electrification by next year. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The railway electrification has been completed by next year.

2.en: The railway electrification will have been completed by next year.

3.en: The railway electrification will have been completing by next year.

4.en: The railway electrification will have completed by next year.

solution.en:
Rule
Future perfect active (will have + V3) → passive will have been + V3.

Explicit changes
Object "the railway electrification" → subject The railway electrification
will have completed → will have been completed
They → dropped (a general subject is usually omitted)
by next year → unchanged

Final sentence
The railway electrification will have been completed by next year.

Option 1 changes the tense, option 3 uses "completing", and option 4 is not passive (no "been").

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
People say that the outlaw had helped the destitutes at the time of need. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: It was said that the destitutes had been helped at the time of need by the outlaw.

2.en: It is said that the destitutes had been being helped at the time of need by the outlaw.

3.en: It was said that the destitutes had been being helped at the time of need by the outlaw.

4.en: It is said that the destitutes had been helped at the time of need by the outlaw.

solution.en:
Rule
For "People say that + clause", the passive is It is said that + passive clause. The reporting verb "say" (present) → is said; the past perfect "had helped" → had been helped.

Explicit changes
People say → It is said
Object "the destitutes" → subject the destitutes
had helped → had been helped
the outlaw → by the outlaw

Final sentence
It is said that the destitutes had been helped at the time of need by the outlaw.

Options 1 and 3 change "say" to "was said", and options 2 and 3 use the wrong form "had been being helped".

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
The poor children are shouting slogans in the election campaign of the local minister. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Slogans are being shouted by the poor children in the election campaign of the local minister.

2.en: Slogans were being shouted by the poor children in the election campaign of the local minister.

3.en: Slogans were being shouted at by the poor children in the election campaign of the local minister.

4.en: Slogans have been shouted by the poor children in the election campaign of the local minister.

solution.en:
Rule
Present continuous active (is/are + V-ing) → passive is/are + being + V3.

Explicit changes
Object "slogans" → subject Slogans (plural → are)
are shouting → are being shouted
The poor children → by the poor children

Final sentence
Slogans are being shouted by the poor children in the election campaign of the local minister.

Options 2 and 3 change the tense to past ("were"), option 3 also adds a wrong "at", and option 4 uses the present perfect.

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
The producer has made a biopic on Amitabh Bachchan covering his college days. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A biopic on Amitabh Bachchan covering his college days has been made by the producer.

2.en: A biopic on Amitabh Bachchan covering his college days have been made by the producer.

3.en: A biopic on Amitabh Bachchan covering his college days have made the producer.

4.en: Biopic on Amitabh Bachchan has been made by the producer covering his college days.

solution.en:
Rule
Present perfect active (has/have + V3) → passive has/have been + V3.

Explicit changes
Object "a biopic on Amitabh Bachchan covering his college days" → subject (singular → has)
has made → has been made
The producer → by the producer

Final sentence
A biopic on Amitabh Bachchan covering his college days has been made by the producer.

Option 2 uses plural "have" with the singular subject "a biopic", option 3 is not passive, and option 4 drops the article and misplaces "covering his college days".

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
The visitors photographed the children flying kites in the park. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The children flying kites in the park was photographed by the visitors.

2.en: The children flying kites were photographed by the visitor in the park.

3.en: The children flying kites in the park were photographed by the visitors.

4.en: The children flying kites in the park had been photographed by the visitors.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple past active (V2) → passive was/were + V3.

Explicit changes
Object "the children flying kites in the park" → subject (plural "children" → were)
photographed → were photographed
The visitors → by the visitors

Final sentence
The children flying kites in the park were photographed by the visitors.

Option 1 uses singular "was", option 2 changes "visitors" to "visitor" and moves "in the park", and option 4 changes the tense to past perfect.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
The students are made to clean the classroom every day. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The teacher makes the students clean the classroom every day.

2.en: The students clean the classroom every day.

3.en: The classroom is cleaned by the students every day.

4.en: The students are cleaning the classroom every day.

solution.en:
Rule
With make, the active uses a bare infinitive (make + object + V1), while the passive uses "to" (be made + to + V1). The doer is not stated in the passive, so a suitable subject (the teacher) is supplied in the active.

Explicit changes
are made (simple present passive) → makes (simple present active, singular subject)
Doer supplied → The teacher
The students → object the students
to clean → clean ("to" is dropped after "make" in the active)

Final sentence
The teacher makes the students clean the classroom every day.

Options 2 and 4 lose the sense of being made (forced) to clean, and option 3 is still passive.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
This work needs to be finished today. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: They need finish this work today.

2.en: They need to finish this work today.

3.en: They needed to finish this work today.

solution.en:
Rule
"needs to be + V3" (passive infinitive) → active "need to + V1". The doer is not stated, so the general subject They is supplied, and "this work" becomes the object.

Explicit changes
Doer supplied → They
needs to be finished → need to finish
This work → object this work

Final sentence
They need to finish this work today.

Option 1 drops "to", option 3 changes the tense to past, and option 4 loses "need to".

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
Not a word was spoken by any of the witnesses during the trial. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Any of the witnesses did not speak a word during the trial.

2.en: None of the witnesses spoke a word during the trial.

3.en: No witnesses had spoken a word during the trial.

4.en: No witness has spoken a word during the trial.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple past passive (was + V3) → simple past active (V2). A negative passive with "Not a word … by any of" becomes "None of … + V2" in the active; starting a sentence with "Any … not" is incorrect.

Explicit changes
by any of the witnesses → subject None of the witnesses (the negative moves to the subject)
was spoken → spoke
Not a word → object a word
during the trial → unchanged

Final sentence
None of the witnesses spoke a word during the trial.

Option 1 wrongly begins with "Any … did not", option 3 changes the tense to past perfect, and option 4 changes it to present perfect.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
The letter should have been mailed by John yesterday. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: John should have mailed the letter yesterday.

2.en: John should mail the letter yesterday.

4.en: John ought to have mailed the letter yesterday.

solution.en:
Rule
Modal perfect passive (should have been + V3) → active should have + V3.

Explicit changes
by John → subject John
should have been mailed → should have mailed
The letter → object the letter
yesterday → unchanged

Final sentence
John should have mailed the letter yesterday.

Options 2 and 3 change the verb form (and clash with "yesterday"), and option 4 changes the modal "should" to "ought to".

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
The stolen painting was recovered by the police. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The police recovered the stolen painting.

2.en: The police recovers the stolen painting.

3.en: The police had recovered the stolen painting.

4.en: The stolen painting recovers the police.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple past passive (was + V3) → simple past active (V2).

Explicit changes
by the police → subject The police
was recovered → recovered
The stolen painting → object the stolen painting

Final sentence
The police recovered the stolen painting.

Option 2 uses the present tense, option 3 uses the past perfect, and option 4 reverses the doer and the object.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
"He bought a new car." [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: A new car was bought by him.

2.en: A new car is bought by him.

3.en: A new car has been bought.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple past active → was/were + V3 in the passive.

Explicit changes
Object "a new car" → subject
bought → was bought
He → by him

Final sentence
A new car was bought by him.

Option 2 uses the present tense, option 3 changes the tense and drops the doer, and option 4 ("had bought") is not a passive form.

question.en:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.
"The notorious thief had been caught red-handed by the police in Hyderabad." [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: The police has caught the notorious thief red-handed in Hyderabad.

2.en: The police have caught the notorious thief red-handed in Hyderabad.

3.en: The police had caught the notorious thief red-handed in Hyderabad.

4.en: The police had caught the thief red-handed in Hyderabad.

solution.en:
Rule
Past perfect passive (had been + V3) → past perfect active (had + V3).

Explicit changes
by the police → subject The police
had been caught → had caught
The notorious thief → object the notorious thief
red-handed, in Hyderabad → unchanged

Final sentence
The police had caught the notorious thief red-handed in Hyderabad.

Options 1 and 2 change the tense to present perfect, and option 4 drops the word "notorious".

question.en:
Change the following sentence from active to passive:
By the deadline, the students must have been submitting their assignments electronically. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: The assignments must have submitted electronically by the students.

2.en: The students submitted the assignments electronically by the deadline.

3.en: The assignments have been submitted by the students by the deadline.

4.en: The assignments must have been being submitted electronically by the students by the deadline.

solution.en:
Rule
Modal perfect continuous active (must have been + V-ing) → passive must have been being + V3.

Explicit changes
Object "their assignments" → subject The assignments
must have been submitting → must have been being submitted
the students → by the students
electronically, by the deadline → retained

Final sentence
The assignments must have been being submitted electronically by the students by the deadline.

Such passives are rare in everyday English, but this is the only option that keeps the modal perfect continuous structure. Option 1 lacks "been" before "submitted", option 2 is an active sentence in a different tense, and option 3 drops the modal and changes the tense.

question.en:
Change the following active voice sentence into passive voice by selecting the correct option.
The Election Commission is conducting re-polling in Kerala today. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: The Election Commission has conducted re-polling in Kerala today.

2.en: Re-polling in Kerala will be conducted by the Election Commission today.

3.en: Re-polling in Kerala was being conducted by the Election Commission today.

4.en: Re-polling in Kerala is being conducted by the Election Commission today.

solution.en:
Rule
Present continuous active → passive is/am/are + being + V3.

Explicit changes
Object "re-polling in Kerala" → subject Re-polling in Kerala
is conducting → is being conducted
The Election Commission → by the Election Commission
today → retained

Final sentence
Re-polling in Kerala is being conducted by the Election Commission today.

Option 1 is active and in the present perfect, option 2 is in the future tense, and option 3 is in the past continuous.

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
The Wright Brothers made the first aeroplane. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: The first aeroplane was made by the Wright Brothers.

2.en: The first aeroplane is made by the Wright Brothers.

3.en: The first aeroplane has been made by the Wright Brothers.

4.en: The first aeroplane was making the Wright Brothers.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple past active → passive was/were + V3.

Explicit changes
Object "the first aeroplane" → subject The first aeroplane
made → was made
The Wright Brothers → by the Wright Brothers

Final sentence
The first aeroplane was made by the Wright Brothers.

Option 2 is in the present tense, option 3 is in the present perfect, and option 4 is not a passive form.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
The house was cleaned by Mary every weekend. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: Mary cleans the house every weekend.

2.en: Mary cleaned the house every weekend.

3.en: Mary has cleaned the house every weekend.

4.en: Mary is cleaning the house every weekend.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple past passive (was/were + V3) → simple past active (V2).

Explicit changes
by Mary → subject Mary
was cleaned → cleaned
The house → object the house
every weekend → retained

Final sentence
Mary cleaned the house every weekend.

Options 1, 3 and 4 change the tense to the simple present, present perfect and present continuous respectively.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
Was the letter written by John? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule
Simple past interrogative passive (Was + object + V3 + by …?) → active Did + subject + V1 + object?

Explicit changes
by John → subject John
Was … written → Did … write
the letter → object

Final sentence
Did John write the letter?

Option 1 wrongly uses "wrote" after "did", option 2 is in the present perfect, and option 3 is in the simple present.

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
The pundit wrote a psalm on the goddess when he saw a miraculous incident on the occasion of Kumbh Mela. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: A psalm on the goddess was being written by the pundit when a miraculous incident was seen by him on the occasion of Kumbh Mela.

2.en: A psalm on the goddess was written by the pundit when a miraculous incident was seen by him on the occasion of Kumbh Mela.

3.en: A psalm on the goddess was written by the pundit when a miraculous incident had been seen by him on the occasion of Kumbh Mela.

4.en: A psalm on the goddess has been written by the pundit when a miraculous incident seen by him on the occasion of Kumbh Mela.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple past active → was/were + past participle in the passive. Both clauses are in the simple past.

Explicit changes
wrote a psalm → a psalm ... was written by the pundit
he saw a miraculous incident → a miraculous incident was seen by him

Final sentence
A psalm on the goddess was written by the pundit when a miraculous incident was seen by him on the occasion of Kumbh Mela.

Options 1 (was being written), 3 (had been seen) and 4 (has been written) change the tense.

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
Somebody has broken the side lamps which had been installed by the municipal corporation last year. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The side lamps have been broken which were installed by the municipal corporation last year.

2.en: The side lamps which had been installed by the municipal corporation last year have been broken.

3.en: The side lamps which were being installed by the municipal corporation last year have been broken.

4.en: The side lamps which had been installed by the municipal corporation last year had been broken.

solution.en:
Rule
Present perfect active → has/have been + past participle. The subject "somebody" is dropped in the passive.

Explicit changes
has broken the side lamps → the side lamps have been broken
The relative clause "which had been installed by the municipal corporation last year" stays unchanged and stays next to "side lamps".

Final sentence
The side lamps which had been installed by the municipal corporation last year have been broken.

Option 1 separates the clause from its noun and changes its tense; options 3 and 4 change the tenses.

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
The culprit finally accepted that he had been guilty. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: It was finally accepted by the culprit that he had been guilty.

2.en: It had been finally accepted by the culprit that was guilty.

3.en: That he had been guilty accepted the culprit finally.

4.en: That he had been guilty was accepted the culprit finally.

solution.en:
Rule
When the object is a that-clause, the passive begins with It + was + past participle + that-clause.

Explicit changes
The culprit accepted → It was accepted by the culprit
The that-clause "that he had been guilty" remains unchanged.

Final sentence
It was finally accepted by the culprit that he had been guilty.

Option 2 changes the tense and drops "he"; options 3 and 4 are ungrammatical.

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
He said that he would not tolerate such nuisance in the office. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: That such nuisance in the office would not be tolerated had been said by him.

2.en: It was said by him that such nuisance in the office would not be tolerated.

3.en: It had been said by him that such nuisance in the office would not be tolerated.

4.en: That such nuisance in the office would not be tolerating had been said by him.

solution.en:
Rule
For "said that ...", the passive uses It was said by + agent + that-clause; the verb inside the clause also becomes passive: would tolerate → would be tolerated.

Explicit changes
He said → It was said by him
he would not tolerate such nuisance → such nuisance would not be tolerated

Final sentence
It was said by him that such nuisance in the office would not be tolerated.

Options 1 and 3 use "had been said" (wrong tense), and option 4 uses "would not be tolerating".

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
The wife advised the husband to maintain silence when she was practising yoga. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The husband was advised to maintain silence by the wife when yoga was practised by her.

2.en: The husband was advised by the wife to maintain silence when yoga was being practised by her.

3.en: The husband was advised by the wife to maintain silence by her when yoga was being practised.

4.en: The husband was advised to maintain silence when yoga was being practised by her by the wife.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple past → was + past participle; past continuous → was being + past participle. The infinitive "to maintain silence" stays unchanged.

Explicit changes
The wife advised the husband → The husband was advised by the wife
she was practising yoga → yoga was being practised by her

Final sentence
The husband was advised by the wife to maintain silence when yoga was being practised by her.

Option 1 uses "was practised" (wrong tense); options 3 and 4 misplace the agents.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
No decision has been taken yet. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: They did not take any decision yet.

2.en: They have not taken any decision yet.

3.en: Nobody had taken any decision yet.

4.en: Nobody will take any decision yet.

solution.en:
Rule
Passive present perfect (has been taken) → active present perfect (have taken). The negative "no decision" becomes not ... any decision, with an implied subject "They".

Explicit changes
No decision has been taken → They have not taken any decision

Final sentence
They have not taken any decision yet.

Options 1 (did not take), 3 (had taken) and 4 (will take) change the tense.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
Instructions will be given to the candidates. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

2.en: Someone gives instructions to the candidates.

3.en: Someone will give instructions to the candidates.

solution.en:
Rule
Passive simple future (will be given) → active simple future (will give). The unknown doer is expressed as "Someone".

Explicit changes
Instructions will be given to the candidates → Someone will give instructions to the candidates

Final sentence
Someone will give instructions to the candidates.

Options 1 and 2 use the present tense; option 4 makes "instructions" the doer.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
What a beautiful painting has been made by her! [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

2.en: How beautiful painting she has made!

3.en: What a beautiful painting she has made!

4.en: She has been making a beautiful painting!

solution.en:
Rule
In an exclamatory sentence, keep the exclamatory phrase (What a beautiful painting) at the start and change "has been made by her" to she has made.

Explicit changes
has been made by her → she has made

Final sentence
What a beautiful painting she has made!

Options 1 and 4 change the tense and form, and option 2 wrongly uses "How beautiful painting".

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
Guests are not permitted to enter the kitchen. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: They do not permit guests to enter the kitchen.

2.en: They did not permit guests to enter the kitchen.

3.en: They have not permitted guests to enter the kitchen.

4.en: They are not permitting guests to enter the kitchen.

solution.en:
Rule
Passive simple present (are not permitted) → active simple present (do not permit) with the implied subject "They".

Explicit changes
Guests are not permitted → They do not permit guests

Final sentence
They do not permit guests to enter the kitchen.

Options 2, 3 and 4 change the tense.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
The tourists were guided through the forest by a local ranger. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: A local ranger is guiding the tourists through the forest.

2.en: A local ranger was guided through the forest by tourists.

3.en: A local ranger guides the tourists through the forest.

4.en: A local ranger guided the tourists through the forest.

solution.en:
Rule
Passive simple past (were guided by) → active simple past; the agent "a local ranger" becomes the subject.

Explicit changes
The tourists were guided by a local ranger → A local ranger guided the tourists

Final sentence
A local ranger guided the tourists through the forest.

Options 1 and 3 change the tense, and option 2 reverses the meaning.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
"The scientist discovered a new planet." [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A new planet was discovered by the scientist.

2.en: A new planet is discovered by the scientist.

3.en: A new planet had discovered by the scientist.

4.en: A new planet was being discovered.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple past active → was/were + V3 in the passive.

Explicit changes
Object "a new planet" → subject
discovered → was discovered
The scientist → by the scientist

Final sentence
A new planet was discovered by the scientist.

Option 2 uses the present tense, option 3 wrongly uses "had discovered" (an active form) and option 4 changes the tense and drops the doer.

question.en:
Change the following active voice sentence into passive voice by selecting the correct option.
The Indian Space Research Organisation will launch the Gaganyaan mission next year. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Gaganyaan mission is being launched by ISRO next year.

2.en: Gaganyaan mission will be launched by ISRO next year.

3.en: The Gaganyaan mission has been launched by ISRO next year.

4.en: The Gaganyaan mission is launched by ISRO next year.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple future active (will + V1) → will be + V3 in the passive.

Explicit changes
Object "the Gaganyaan mission" → subject
will launch → will be launched
The Indian Space Research Organisation → by ISRO
next year → no change

Final sentence
Gaganyaan mission will be launched by ISRO next year.

Options 1, 3 and 4 use the wrong tenses (present continuous, present perfect and simple present).

question.en:
Change the following passive voice sentence into active voice by selecting the correct option.
The Railways Ministry has been upgrading railway stations across India over the last decade. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Railway stations across India have been being upgraded by the Railways Ministry over the last decade.

2.en: Railway stations have been upgraded by the Railways Ministry over the last decade.

3.en: Railway stations across India have been upgraded by the Railways Ministry over the last decade.

4.en: Railway stations across India are being upgraded by the Railways Ministry over the last decade.

solution.en:
Note: The given sentence is in the active voice (the doer, the Railways Ministry, is the subject), so it has to be changed into the passive voice.

Rule
Present perfect continuous active (has/have been + V-ing) → has/have been being + V3 in the passive.

Explicit changes
Object "railway stations across India" → subject (plural → have)
has been upgrading → have been being upgraded
The Railways Ministry → by the Railways Ministry
over the last decade → no change

Final sentence
Railway stations across India have been being upgraded by the Railways Ministry over the last decade. (option 1)

Option 2 drops "across India", option 3 changes the tense to present perfect ("have been upgraded") and option 4 changes it to present continuous.
The answer key, however, marks option 3, treating the present perfect passive as the usable form because the perfect continuous passive is rarely used.

question.en:
Change the following passive voice sentence into active voice by selecting the correct option.
Public expenditure has been being audited closely by the Finance Ministry for the past six months. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Public expenditure has been audited closely by the Finance Ministry for the past six months.

2.en: The Finance Ministry has been auditing public expenditure closely for the past six months.

3.en: Public expenditure is being audited closely by the Finance Ministry for the past six months.

4.en: The Finance Ministry is auditing public expenditure closely for the past six months.

solution.en:
Rule
Passive "has/have been being + V3" is the present perfect continuous; in the active it becomes has/have been + V-ing.

Explicit changes
by the Finance Ministry → subject The Finance Ministry
has been being audited → has been auditing
Public expenditure → object
closely, for the past six months → no change

Final sentence
The Finance Ministry has been auditing public expenditure closely for the past six months.

Options 1 and 3 are still passive, and option 4 changes the tense to present continuous.

question.en:
Change the following active voice sentence into passive voice by selecting the correct option.
They have been constructing the new metro line in Pune for two years. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The new metro line in Pune is constructed for two years.

2.en: The new metro line in Pune has been constructed for two years.

3.en: The new metro line in Pune has been being constructed for two years.

4.en: The new metro line in Pune will be constructed for two years.

solution.en:
Rule
Present perfect continuous active (have/has been + V-ing) → has/have been being + V3 in the passive.

Explicit changes
Object "the new metro line in Pune" → subject (singular → has)
have been constructing → has been being constructed
They → dropped (a vague doer is usually omitted)
for two years → no change

Final sentence
The new metro line in Pune has been being constructed for two years.

Options 1, 2 and 4 change the tense (simple present, present perfect and simple future).

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
The report must have been completed by the team before the deadline. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The team must have completed the report before the deadline.

2.en: The team must complete the report before the deadline.

3.en: The team should complete the report before the deadline.

4.en: The team must had completed the report before the deadline.

solution.en:
Rule
Modal perfect passive must have been + V3 → active must have + V3.

Explicit changes
by the team → subject The team
must have been completed → must have completed
The report → object

Final sentence
The team must have completed the report before the deadline.

Options 2 and 3 change the modal and time, and option 4 wrongly uses "must had".

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
The injured man was given first aid by the volunteers. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The volunteers gave the injured man first aid.

2.en: The volunteers were given first aid by the injured man.

3.en: The injured man gave the volunteers first aid.

4.en: The injured man was giving first aid to the volunteers.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple past passive "was given" → active gave; the doer becomes the subject and the person returns as the indirect object.

Explicit changes
by the volunteers → subject The volunteers
was given → gave
The injured man → indirect object; first aid → direct object

Final sentence
The volunteers gave the injured man first aid.

Options 2 and 3 reverse the roles, and option 4 changes the meaning.

question.en:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.
The novel was written by an author who had traveled extensively. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: An author who had traveled extensively wrote the novel.

2.en: The novel was written by an author who had traveled extensively.

3.en: The author wrote the novel, and he traveled extensively.

4.en: Writing the novel was done by an author who had traveled extensively.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple past passive "was written" → active wrote; the doer after "by" becomes the subject.

Explicit changes
by an author who had traveled extensively → subject
was written → wrote
The novel → object

Final sentence
An author who had traveled extensively wrote the novel.

Option 2 repeats the passive sentence, option 3 changes the structure and meaning, and option 4 is still passive.

question.en:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.
The project is rumored to be finished ahead of schedule. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Someone is rumored to finish the project ahead of schedule.

2.en: They are rumored that the project will be finished ahead of schedule.

3.en: People say that the project will be finished ahead of schedule.

4.en: They rumor that the project was finished ahead of schedule.

solution.en:
Rule
"Subject + is rumored + to be + V3" is an impersonal passive; in the active it takes a general doer: People say (that) …

Explicit changes
is rumored → People say that
to be finished → will be finished (the rumour is about a future event)

Final sentence
People say that the project will be finished ahead of schedule.

Option 1 changes the meaning, option 2 ("They are rumored that") is ungrammatical and option 4 changes the tense ("was finished").

question.en:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:
Has she left the apartment? [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Is the apartment left by her?

2.en: Had the apartment been left by her?

3.en: Has the apartment been left by her?

4.en: Have the apartment been left by her?

solution.en:
Rule
Present perfect question "Has + subject + V3 + object?" → Has/Have + object + been + V3 + by + subject?

Explicit changes
the apartment → subject (singular → has)
Has … left → Has … been left
she → by her

Final sentence
Has the apartment been left by her?

Option 1 uses the present tense, option 2 the past perfect, and option 4 wrongly uses "have" with a singular subject.

question.en:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:
The teacher gave the students a difficult assignment. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A difficult assignment were given the students by the teacher.

2.en: The students were given a difficult assignment by the teacher.

3.en: The students were giving a difficult assignment by the teacher.

4.en: A difficult assignment was given to the students by the teacher.

solution.en:
Rule
"Give" has two objects. In the passive, the indirect object (the person) usually becomes the subject; simple past → was/were + V3.

Explicit changes
the students → subject (plural → were)
gave → were given
a difficult assignment → retained object
The teacher → by the teacher

Final sentence
The students were given a difficult assignment by the teacher.

Option 4 (direct object as subject) is also grammatically possible, but the standard passive of such sentences makes the person the subject, as in option 2. Option 1 has "assignment were" and option 3 ("were giving") is not passive.

question.en:
Change the following active voice sentence into passive voice by selecting the correct option.
They have announced that the school will reopen after Pongal holidays. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: It was announced that the school will reopen after Pongal holidays.

2.en: That the school will reopen was announced by them after Pongal holidays.

3.en: It has been announced that the school will reopen after Pongal holidays.

4.en: The school has announced that it will reopen after Pongal holidays.

solution.en:
Rule
In sentences where an active subject introduces a statement with a reporting verb followed by a that-clause (Subject + have + V3 + that-clause), the standard impersonal passive construction uses: 'It + has been + V3 + that-clause'.

Explicit changes
• The dummy pronoun 'It' is introduced as the grammatical subject.
• Present perfect active 'have announced' transforms to present perfect passive 'has been announced' (agreeing with singular 'It').
• The that-clause remains intact.

Final sentence
It has been announced that the school will reopen after Pongal holidays.

Option 1 incorrectly shifts the tense to simple past ('was announced').

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
