Many people in this city rush to their offices due to the fear that their salaries will be deducted. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Their offices were rushed to in this city due to the fear that their salaries will be deducted.

2.en: Their offices were rushed to by many people in this city due to the fear that their salaries be deducted.

3.en: Their offices were rushed by many people in this city due to the fear that their salaries will be deducted.

4.en: Their offices are rushed to by many people in this city due to the fear that their salaries will be deducted.

solution.en:
Rule
The main clause verb 'rush to' is in the simple present tense. In the passive voice, simple present becomes: are + past participle (V3) + preposition ('rushed to').

Explicit changes
• The prepositional object 'their offices' becomes the subject.
• Present tense auxiliary 'are' is used with plural subject 'offices': 'are rushed to'.
• The agent 'by many people in this city' is included.

Final sentence
Their offices are rushed to by many people in this city due to the fear that their salaries will be deducted.

Options 1 and 2 incorrectly use past tense 'were', and Option 3 drops the vital preposition 'to'.

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
The corrupt officials will realize that they have misappropriated a large amount of money from the common people causing doubt and fear in their minds. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: It will be realized by the corrupt officials that a large amount of money has been misappropriated by them from the common people causing doubt and fear in their minds.

2.en: It will be realized by the corrupt officials that a large amount of money have been misappropriated by them from the common people causing doubt and fear in their minds.

3.en: It would be realized by the corrupt officials that a large amount of money has been misappropriated by them from the common people causing doubt and fear in their minds.

4.en: It will be realized by the corrupt officials that a large amount of money has been misappropriated by him from the common people causing doubt and fear in their minds.

solution.en:
Rule
• The main clause 'will realize' transforms to 'will be realized'.
• The noun phrase 'a large amount of money' is singular and uncountable ('money'), requiring the singular verb 'has been misappropriated'.
• The plural agent pronoun must remain 'them' (corresponding to 'officials'), not 'him'.

Analysis of Options:
• Option 2 incorrectly uses plural 'have been'.
• Option 3 incorrectly changes modal 'will' to 'would'.
• Option 4 incorrectly changes pronoun to singular 'him'.
Therefore, Option 1 is the grammatically correct passive sentence.

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
They used 1,45,000 eggs to make the largest omelette in the world. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The 1,45,000 eggs were used to make the largest omelette in the world.

2.en: 1,45,000 eggs were used to make the largest omelette in the world.

3.en: 1,45,000 eggs had been used to make the largest omelette in the world.

4.en: 1,45,000 eggs were used to be made the largest omelette in the world.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple past active (Subject + V2 + Object) transforms to passive: Object + were + V3 ('were used').

Explicit changes
• Object '1,45,000 eggs' becomes the subject.
• Simple past verb 'used' transforms to 'were used' (agreeing with plural 'eggs').
• The infinitive purpose clause 'to make the largest omelette in the world' remains active and unamended.

Final sentence
1,45,000 eggs were used to make the largest omelette in the world.

Option 1 inserts an uncalled-for definite article 'The', Option 3 incorrectly alters tense to past perfect ('had been used'), and Option 4 creates an ungrammatical infinitive ('used to be made').

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
It is believed that the suspect has fled the country. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The suspect believed to have fled the country.

2.en: They believe the suspect has fled the country.

3.en: It believes the suspect has fled the country.

4.en: Believing the suspect has fled the country.

solution.en:
Rule
The impersonal passive construction 'It is believed that...' converts into active voice by supplying an active plural indefinite subject such as 'They' or 'People', followed by the simple present verb 'believe'.

Explicit changes
• Supply general active subject 'They'.
• Passive 'is believed' transforms into active simple present 'believe'.
• The subordinate clause 'the suspect has fled the country' follows directly.

Final sentence
They believe the suspect has fled the country.

Option 1 lacks an auxiliary verb, Option 3 absurdly makes dummy pronoun 'It' believe something, and Option 4 is an incomplete sentence fragment.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
The child was made to apologize by his mother. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The mother made the child apologize.

2.en: The mother made the child to apologize.

3.en: The mother was making the child apologize.

4.en: The mother was made to apologize to the child

solution.en:
Rule: Causative Verbs in Active vs. Passive
• When the causative verb make is used in the passive voice, it takes a full to-infinitive: 'was made to apologize'.
• When converted to the active voice, 'make' takes a bare infinitive (infinitive without 'to'): 'made + object + V1 (apologize)'.

Explicit changes
• Agent 'his mother' becomes the active subject 'The mother'.
• Passive 'was made to apologize' becomes active 'made the child apologize'.

Final sentence
The mother made the child apologize.

Option 2 incorrectly retains 'to', Option 3 changes tense to continuous, and Option 4 reverses the roles.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
The complaint has been registered by the customer. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

2.en: The customer has registered the complaint.

solution.en:
Rule
Present perfect passive (has/have been + V3) transforms to active: Subject + has/have + V3.

Explicit changes
• Agent 'the customer' becomes the active subject.
• Passive 'has been registered' transforms to active 'has registered'.
• 'The complaint' becomes the direct object.

Final sentence
The customer has registered the complaint.

Option 1 uses simple present ('registers'), Option 3 uses simple past ('registered'), and Option 4 reverses agent and object.

question.en:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.
The door has been locked. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule
When converting an agentless passive in the present perfect tense (has been + V3) to the active voice, an indefinite pronoun such as 'Someone' or 'Somebody' is supplied as the active subject, followed by 'has + V3'.

Explicit changes
• Supply active subject 'Someone'.
• 'has been locked' becomes active present perfect 'has locked'.
• 'the door' becomes the object.

Final sentence
Someone has locked the door.

Option 1 and 4 remain passive descriptions of state, and Option 3 shifts tense to simple past ('locked').

question.en:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.
The winning goal was scored by the team captain in the final minute of the game. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The winning goal was scored by the team captain in the final minute of the game.

2.en: The team captain scored the winning goal in the final minute of the game.

3.en: In the final minute of the game, the winning goal was scored by the team captain.

4.en: The winning goal is scored in the final minute of the game by the team captain.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple past passive (Subject + was/were + V3 + by agent) transforms into active: Agent + V2 + Object.

Explicit changes
• The agent 'the team captain' becomes the active subject.
• Passive verb 'was scored' becomes simple past active 'scored'.
• 'the winning goal' becomes the direct object.
• Prepositional phrase 'in the final minute of the game' remains unchanged.

Final sentence
The team captain scored the winning goal in the final minute of the game.

Options 1 and 3 are still passive; Option 4 changes tense to simple present.

question.en:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.
The employee was made to hand over all company files before his termination was announced. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The employee handed over all company files before his termination was announced.

2.en: They made the employee hand over all company files before his termination was announced.

3.en: Before his termination was announced, the employee had to hand over all company files.

4.en: The termination was announced and they made the employee hand over all company files.

solution.en:
Rule on Causative 'Make':
• In the passive voice, 'make' takes a to-infinitive: 'was made to hand over'.
• In the active voice, 'make' takes a bare infinitive: 'made + person + bare infinitive (hand over)'.
• Since no explicit agent is mentioned in the passive, supply generic plural subject 'They'.

Final sentence
They made the employee hand over all company files before his termination was announced.

Option 1 alters the causative meaning; Option 3 replaces causation with obligation ('had to').

question.en:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:
Sanya always pays the dinner bills. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The dinner bills were always paid by Sanya.

2.en: The dinner bills always get paid by Sanya.

3.en: The dinner bills have always been paid by Sanya.

4.en: The dinner bills are always paid by Sanya.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple present active (Subject + V1-s + Object) transforms to passive: Object + is/are + adverb + V3 + by agent.

Explicit changes
• Direct object 'the dinner bills' becomes the plural subject.
• Simple present auxiliary for plural subject is 'are'.
• 'pays' becomes past participle 'paid', retaining the frequency adverb 'always': are always paid.
• Sanya becomes the agent: by Sanya.

Final sentence
The dinner bills are always paid by Sanya.

Option 1 uses simple past ('were'), Option 2 uses colloquial 'get paid', and Option 3 uses present perfect ('have been').

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
A person cannot connect the dots looking forward. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The dots cannot be connected by a person looking forward.

2.en: The dots could not be connected by a person looking forward.

3.en: The dots cannot have to be connected by a person looking forward.

4.en: The dots cannot have been connected by a person looking forward.

solution.en:
Rule: cannot + V1 (active) → cannot be + V3 (passive). Object “the dots” becomes the subject.
Active: A person cannot connect the dots looking forward.
Passive: The dots cannot be connected by a person looking forward.

Why other options are wrong
Option 2 changes the tense (could not); Options 3 and 4 add “have to be” / “have been”, which are not in the original.

Therefore, The dots cannot be connected by a person looking forward.

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
Sooraj may accomplish the tasks with his hands down. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The tasks might be accomplished by Sooraj with his hands down.

2.en: The tasks may be accomplished by Sooraj with his hands down.

3.en: The tasks may have to be accomplished by Sooraj with his hands down.

4.en: The tasks may have been accomplished by Sooraj with his hands down.

solution.en:
Rule: may + V1 (active) → may be + V3 (passive).
Active: Sooraj may accomplish the tasks with his hands down.
Passive: The tasks may be accomplished by Sooraj with his hands down.

Why other options are wrong
Option 1 changes may to might; Option 3 adds “have to”; Option 4 changes to the perfect form “may have been”.

Therefore, The tasks may be accomplished by Sooraj with his hands down.

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
Deepak must not have given the unnecessary things on Raghav's wedding anniversary. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The unnecessary things had not have been given on Raghav's weeding anniversary by Deepak.

2.en: The unnecessary things had not to have been given on Raghav's weeding anniversary by Deepak.

3.en: The unnecessary things must not have been given on Raghav's weeding anniversary by Deepak.

4.en: The unnecessary things must not have given on Raghav's weeding anniversary by Deepak.

solution.en:
Rule: must not have + V3 (active) → must not have been + V3 (passive).
Active: Deepak must not have given the unnecessary things …
Passive: The unnecessary things must not have been given … by Deepak.

Why other options are wrong
Options 1 and 2 wrongly use “had not (to) have been”; Option 4 omits “been”, so it is not passive.

Therefore, The unnecessary things must not have been given on Raghav's weeding anniversary by Deepak.

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
The young artist demanded a good story for the film he was going to act in. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A good story for the film he was going to act in was demanded by the young artist.

2.en: A good story for the film he had been going to act in was demanded by the young artist.

3.en: A good story for the film he was going to act in had been demanded by the young artist.

4.en: A good story for the film he had been going to act in had been demanded by the young artist.

solution.en:
Rule: Simple past (demanded) → was/were + V3 (was demanded). The clause “he was going to act in” describes the film and stays unchanged.
Passive: A good story for the film he was going to act in was demanded by the young artist.

Why other options are wrong
Options 2 and 4 needlessly change “was going” to “had been going”; Options 3 and 4 change the main verb to past perfect “had been demanded”.

Therefore, A good story for the film he was going to act in was demanded by the young artist.

question.en:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
The manager forced the employees to stop using mobiles. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The employees to stop using mobiles were forced by the manager.

2.en: The employees were forced to stop by the manager using mobiles.

3.en: The employees were forced by the manager to stop using mobiles.

4.en: The employees by the manager were forced to stop using mobiles.

solution.en:
Rule: Simple past (forced) → were forced. The infinitive phrase “to stop using mobiles” stays attached to the verb it completes.
Passive: The employees were forced by the manager to stop using mobiles.

Why other options are wrong
Option 1 places the infinitive before the verb; Option 2 splits “stop using mobiles”; Option 4 puts “by the manager” before the verb awkwardly.

Therefore, The employees were forced by the manager to stop using mobiles.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
The meeting is to be held tomorrow. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

2.en: They have to hold the meeting tomorrow.

3.en: They are to hold the meeting tomorrow.

4.en: They must hold the meeting tomorrow.

solution.en:
Rule: is/are to be + V3 (passive) → is/are to + V1 (active). “is to be held” expresses an arrangement or plan.
Active: They are to hold the meeting tomorrow.

Why other options are wrong
Option 1 loses the sense of arrangement; “have to” and “must” express obligation, not a scheduled plan.

Therefore, They are to hold the meeting tomorrow.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
The culprit is believed to have fled the country. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: People believe the culprit fled the country.

2.en: People are believing the culprit to flee the country.

3.en: It believes the culprit has fled the country.

4.en: People believe the culprit has fled the country.

solution.en:
Rule: “X is believed to have + V3” → People believe (that) X has + V3. The perfect infinitive “to have fled” shows an action completed before the believing, i.e., present perfect “has fled”.
Active: People believe the culprit has fled the country.

Why other options are wrong
Option 1 uses simple past “fled”; Option 2 uses the wrong continuous form “are believing … to flee”; Option 3 uses “It believes”, which has no sensible subject.

Therefore, People believe the culprit has fled the country.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
It is said that the company will launch a new product next month. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: They said the company will launch a new product next month.

2.en: People say that the company launches a new product next month.

3.en: People say the company will launch a new product next month.

4.en: They say the company launched a new product next month.

solution.en:
Rule: “It is said that …” → People say (that) … in the same tense; the reported clause stays unchanged.
Active: People say the company will launch a new product next month.

Why other options are wrong
Option 1 changes “say” to past “said”; Option 2 changes “will launch” to “launches”; Option 4 changes it to “launched”.

Therefore, People say the company will launch a new product next month.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
The truth ought to be told to the manager. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Someone ought to tell the truth to the manager.

2.en: Someone must have told the truth to the manager.

3.en: Someone should tell the truth to the manager.

4.en: The manager ought to tell the truth.

solution.en:
Rule: ought to be + V3 (passive) → ought to + V1 (active). Since no doer is named, use “someone”.
Active: Someone ought to tell the truth to the manager.

Why other options are wrong
Option 2 changes to “must have told”; Option 3 changes “ought to” to “should”; Option 4 makes the manager the one who tells, changing the meaning.

Therefore, Someone ought to tell the truth to the manager.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
"They speak French at home." [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: French is spoken at home by them.

2.en: French was spoken by them at home.

3.en: French was being spoken at home.

solution.en:
**Rule:** Simple present active form (\(V_1\)) changes to **is/am/are + \(V_3\)** in the passive voice.
**Active:** They speak French at home.
**Passive:** French is spoken at home by them.
Options (b) and (c) incorrectly use past tenses (**was spoken**, **was being spoken**), while option (d) remains active and ungrammatical.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
"He had completed the task." [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The task had been completed by him.

solution.en:
**Rule:** Past perfect active voice (**had + \(V_3\)**) converts into **had + been + \(V_3\)** in the passive voice.
**Active:** He had completed the task.
**Passive:** The task had been completed by him.
Options (b), (c), and (d) alter the tense or drop the mandatory passive auxiliary verb **been**.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
"They play cricket every Sunday." [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Cricket is played by them every Sunday.

solution.en:
**Rule:** Simple present active verb (**play**) converts to **is/am/are + \(V_3\)** (**is played**) in passive voice with a singular object.
**Active:** They play cricket every Sunday.
**Passive:** Cricket is played by them every Sunday.
Option (c) changes the tense to simple past (**was played**), while options (b) and (d) lack passive structure.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
"The kids are decorating the hall." [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The hall is being decorated by the kids.

2.en: The hall was decorated by the kids.

3.en: The hall will be decorated by the kids.

4.en: The hall has decorated by the kids.

solution.en:
**Rule:** Present continuous active tense (**is/am/are + \(V\)-ing**) converts to **is/am/are + being + \(V_3\)** in the passive voice.
**Active:** The kids are decorating the hall.
**Passive:** The hall is being decorated by the kids.
Options (b), (c), and (d) incorrectly change the tense to past, future, and present perfect respectively.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
"The engineer is testing the system." [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The system is being tested by the engineer.

2.en: The system is tested by the engineer.

solution.en:
**Rule:** Present continuous active voice (**is testing**) converts into **is being + \(V_3\)** (**is being tested**) in passive voice.
**Active:** The engineer is testing the system.
**Passive:** The system is being tested by the engineer.
Option (b) converts to simple present, option (c) uses past continuous, and option (d) is grammatically incorrect.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
"We had arranged all the files neatly." [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: All the files had been arranged neatly by us.

3.en: All the files has been arranged.

4.en: All the files are arranged neatly.

solution.en:
**Rule:** Past perfect active voice (**had arranged**) transforms into **had been + \(V_3\)** (**had been arranged**) in passive voice.
**Active:** We had arranged all the files neatly.
**Passive:** All the files had been arranged neatly by us.
Options (b) and (d) shift the tense to past simple and present simple, while option (c) uses an incorrect auxiliary verb.

question.en:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.
Before locking up, all the lights were switched off by the guard. [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The guard before locking up, switched off all the lights.

2.en: All the lights before locking up, the guard switched off.

3.en: Before locking up, the guard switched off all the lights.

4.en: Before locking up, the guard is switched off all the lights.

solution.en:
**Rule:** The passive past simple construction **were switched off by the guard** transforms into the active past simple verb **switched off**, keeping the initial adverbial clause positioned naturally.
**Active:** Before locking up, the guard switched off all the lights.
Options (a) and (b) introduce awkward syntax, and (d) adds an ungrammatical auxiliary verb *is*.

question.en:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.
"The email was quickly drafted and sent to her manager by Jasmin." [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Jasmin sends and drafted the email to her manager.

2.en: Jasmin has sent the email and drafted to her manager.

3.en: Jasmin quickly drafted and sent the email to her manager.

solution.en:
**Rule:** Simple past passive voice (**was drafted and sent**) converts into active past simple verbs (**drafted and sent**).
**Active:** Jasmin quickly drafted and sent the email to her manager.
Options (a), (b), and (d) distort the parallel past tense or change the aspect into continuous/present perfect.

question.en:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence:
"The answer papers were thoroughly reviewed by the principal." [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The principal is throughly reviewed the answer papers.

2.en: The principal reviewed the answer papers.

3.en: The principal thoroughly reviewed the answer papers.

4.en: The principal thoroughly has reviewed the answer papers.

solution.en:
**Rule:** Simple past passive voice (**were thoroughly reviewed**) reverts to simple past active (**thoroughly reviewed**), retaining the adverb of manner.
**Active:** The principal thoroughly reviewed the answer papers.
Option (a) is ungrammatical; option (b) drops the adverb *thoroughly*; option (d) introduces present perfect *has*.

question.en:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.
"The food is promptly served to the guests with a smile by the waiter." [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The waiter serves the food to the guests with a smile.

2.en: The waiter promptly serves the food to the guests with a smile.

3.en: The waiter promptly serving the food to the guests with a smile.

4.en: The waiter is promptly serves the food to the guests with a smile.

solution.en:
**Rule:** Simple present passive (**is promptly served**) converts to simple present active (**promptly serves**) for a singular subject (**The waiter**).
**Active:** The waiter promptly serves the food to the guests with a smile.
Option (a) omits *promptly*; options (c) and (d) contain grammatical errors (*serving*, *is serves*).

question.en:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.
"The social media content was being eagerly followed by teenagers." [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Teenagers waseagerly following the social media content.

2.en: Teenagers were eagerly following the social media content.

3.en: Teenagers are being eagerly following the social media content.

4.en: Teenagers were eagerly following the media content.

solution.en:
**Rule:** Past continuous passive (**was being eagerly followed**) transforms into past continuous active (**were eagerly following**) with the plural subject **Teenagers**.
**Active:** Teenagers were eagerly following the social media content.
Option (a) has a run-on typo and incorrect singular verb *was*; option (c) is present tense; option (d) omits the word *social*.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
"She writes a letter." [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A letter is written by her.

2.en: A letter was wrote by her.

3.en: A letter has written by her.

4.en: A letter had been written by her.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple present active (writes) becomes simple present passive (is/are + past participle).

Explicit changes
The object “a letter” becomes the subject.
“writes” becomes “is written”.
“She” becomes the agent “by her”.

Final sentence
A letter is written by her.

Option 2 uses “was wrote”, option 3 lacks the auxiliary, and option 4 wrongly shifts to past perfect.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
"She sang a beautiful song." [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: A beautiful song was sung by her.

2.en: A beautiful song is sung by her.

4.en: A beautiful song sung by her.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple past active (sang) becomes simple past passive (was/were + past participle).

Explicit changes
“A beautiful song” becomes the subject.
“sang” becomes “was sung”.
The agent is “by her”.

Final sentence
A beautiful song was sung by her.

Option 2 wrongly uses present “is sung”; options 3 and 4 lack a proper passive auxiliary.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
"She cooks delicious meals." [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Delicious meals are cooked by her.

3.en: Delicious meals were cooked by her.

solution.en:
Rule
Simple present active (cooks) becomes simple present passive (are + past participle) with a plural subject.

Explicit changes
“Delicious meals” (plural) becomes the subject.
“cooks” becomes “are cooked”.
The agent is “by her”.

Final sentence
Delicious meals are cooked by her.

Option 2 uses singular “is”, option 3 shifts to past, and option 4 uses wrong auxiliary and no agent.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
"She is sending the documents now." [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The documents are being sent by her now.

2.en: The documents were sent by her now.

3.en: The documents have been sent now.

solution.en:
Rule
Present continuous active (is sending) becomes present continuous passive (are being + past participle).

Explicit changes
“The documents” becomes the subject.
“is sending” becomes “are being sent”.
“now” is retained and the agent is “by her”.

Final sentence
The documents are being sent by her now.

Options 2, 3 and 4 either change the tense or lack the continuous passive form.

question.en:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
"He has written an article on education." [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: An article on education has been written by him.

2.en: An article is written on education.

3.en: An article had written by him.

4.en: An article has wrote by him.

solution.en:
Rule
Present perfect active (has written) becomes present perfect passive (has/have been + past participle).

Explicit changes
“An article on education” becomes the subject.
“has written” becomes “has been written”.
The agent is “by him”.

Final sentence
An article on education has been written by him.

Options 2, 3 and 4 omit the perfect passive auxiliary or use the wrong participle.

question.en:
Select the correct active form of the following sentence:
"A fresh coat of paint is given to the house by Rahul every year to keep it looking new." [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Rahul gives the house a fresh coat of paint every year to keep it looking new.

2.en: Rahul gives the house a fresh paint every year to keep it looking new.

3.en: Rahul gives the house a fresh coat of paint every year to keep looking new.

4.en: Rahul gives the house a fresh coating of paint every year to keep it looking new.

solution.en:
Rule
Present simple passive (is given) becomes present simple active (gives).

Explicit changes
The agent “Rahul” becomes the subject.
“is given” becomes “gives”.
“A fresh coat of paint” becomes the object; the rest is unchanged.

Final sentence
Rahul gives the house a fresh coat of paint every year to keep it looking new.

Option 2 drops “coat of”, option 3 drops “it”, and option 4 changes “coat” to “coating”.

question.en:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.
"The car has been successfully repaired by the mechanic to get it back on the road." [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The mechanic has repaired the car to get it back on the road.

2.en: The mechanic have successfully repaired the car to get it back on the road.

3.en: The mechanic has successfully repaired the car to get it back on the road.

4.en: The mechanic has been successfully repaired the car to get it back on the road.

solution.en:
Rule
Present perfect passive (has been repaired) becomes present perfect active (has repaired).

Explicit changes
The agent “the mechanic” becomes the subject.
“has been successfully repaired” becomes “has successfully repaired”.
“The car” becomes the object.

Final sentence
The mechanic has successfully repaired the car to get it back on the road.

Option 1 omits “successfully”, option 2 uses “have”, and option 4 wrongly keeps “been”.

question.en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in Direct to Indirect Speech.
She said, "I cannot attend the class today." [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: She said that she cannot attend the class that day.

2.en: She said that she would not attend the class.

3.en: She said that she could not attend the class that day.

4.en: She said that she might not attend the class.

solution.en:
Rule
With a past reporting verb, the reported clause moves one step back in tense, and pronouns and time words change.

Explicit changes
“I” becomes “she”.
“cannot” becomes “could not”.
“today” becomes “that day”.

Final sentence
She said that she could not attend the class that day.

Option 1 keeps “cannot”; options 2 and 4 change the meaning with “would” and “might” and drop “that day”.

question.en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in Direct to Indirect Speech.
She said, "I used to live in Delhi." [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: She said that she used to live in Delhi.

2.en: She said that she was living in Delhi.

3.en: She said that she had lived in Delhi.

4.en: She said that she has lived in Delhi.

solution.en:
Rule
“Used to” (a past habit or state) has no further past form, so it does not change in indirect speech.

Explicit changes
“I” becomes “she”.
“used to live” stays unchanged.

Final sentence
She said that she used to live in Delhi.

“Was living”, “had lived” and “has lived” change the meaning of a past habit.

question.en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in Direct Speech.
She said that she might have left her purse at the café. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: She said, "I might have left my purse at the café."

2.en: She said, "I may have left my purse at the café."

3.en: She said, "I could have left my purse at the café."

4.en: She said, "I must have left my purse at the café."

solution.en:
Rule
While converting indirect speech to direct speech, restore the speaker’s own pronouns and put the words in inverted commas; “might have + past participle” stays unchanged.

Explicit changes
“that she” becomes “I” inside the quotation.
“her purse” becomes “my purse”.
“might have left” is kept as it is.

Final sentence
She said, "I might have left my purse at the café."

“Could” and “must” change the degree of possibility; “may” assumes a back-shift that the reported sentence does not require.

question.en:
Convert the following direct speech sentence into indirect speech by selecting the correct option.
The Education Secretary said, "The new curriculum will focus on skill development." [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The Education Secretary said that the new curriculum focused on skill development.

2.en: The Education Secretary said that the new curriculum has focused on skill development.

3.en: The Education Secretary said that the new curriculum will focus on skill development.

4.en: The Education Secretary said that the new curriculum would focus on skill development.

solution.en:
Rule
With a past reporting verb, “will” becomes “would” in indirect speech.

Explicit changes
Remove the inverted commas and add “that”.
“will focus” becomes “would focus”.

Final sentence
The Education Secretary said that the new curriculum would focus on skill development.

Option 3 keeps “will”, and options 1 and 2 change the time reference.

question.en:
Convert the following direct speech sentence into indirect speech by selecting the correct option.
The Minister of State said, "The government has resolved the farmers' issues amicably." [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The Minister of State said that the government had resolved the farmers' issues amicably.

2.en: The Minister of State said that the government has resolved the farmers' issues amicably.

3.en: The Minister of State said that the government resolves the farmers' issues amicably.

4.en: The Minister of State said the farmers' issues were resolved amicably by the government.

solution.en:
Rule
With a past reporting verb, the present perfect becomes the past perfect.

Explicit changes
Add “that” after “said”.
“has resolved” becomes “had resolved”.

Final sentence
The Minister of State said that the government had resolved the farmers' issues amicably.

Options 2 and 3 are not back-shifted correctly, and option 4 changes the voice and drops “that”.

question.en:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:
Ruby said, "Wow! You have secured 95% of marks in the annual examination!" [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Ruby exclaimed with grief that he had secured 95% of marks in the annual examination.

2.en: Ruby exclaimed with delight that he had secured 95% of marks in the annual examination.

3.en: Ruby exclaimed with delight that he has secured 95% of marks in the annual examination.

4.en: Ruby exclaimed with grief that he has secured 95% of marks in the annual examination.

solution.en:
Rule
An exclamation is reported with “exclaimed” plus the feeling it shows; with a past reporting verb, the tense moves back.

Explicit changes
“Wow!” shows joy, so use “exclaimed with delight”.
“You” becomes “he” (the listener).
“have secured” becomes “had secured”.

Final sentence
Ruby exclaimed with delight that he had secured 95% of marks in the annual examination.

“With grief” gives the wrong feeling, and “has secured” is not back-shifted.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.
He asked her whether she wanted tea or coffee with her breakfast. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: He asked her, "You want tea or coffee with your breakfast?"

2.en: He said, "Whether you want tea or coffee with your breakfast?"

3.en: He asked, "Did you want tea or coffee with your breakfast?"

4.en: He said to her, "Do you want tea or coffee with your breakfast?"

solution.en:
Rule
“Asked … whether” reports a yes/no question. In direct speech, use “said to”, inverted commas, question order with an auxiliary and a question mark, and move the tense forward.

Explicit changes
“asked her” becomes “said to her”.
“whether she wanted” becomes the question “Do you want”.
“her breakfast” becomes “your breakfast”.

Final sentence
He said to her, "Do you want tea or coffee with your breakfast?"

Option 1 lacks question order, option 2 keeps “whether” inside the quotation, and option 3 keeps the back-shifted past tense.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.
The librarian requested us to maintain silence in the reading room. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The librarian said to us, "Maintain silence in the reading room."

2.en: The librarian said, "Please maintain silence in the reading room."

3.en: The librarian told us, "Silence should be maintained in the reading room."

4.en: The librarian requested, "You can maintain silence in the reading room."

solution.en:
Rule
“Requested … to” reports a polite imperative; in direct speech, use “said” and begin the command with “Please”.

Explicit changes
“requested us” becomes “said”.
“to maintain” becomes the imperative “Please maintain”.

Final sentence
The librarian said, "Please maintain silence in the reading room."

Option 1 loses the polite tone, option 3 turns the request into a passive statement, and option 4 turns it into a statement of ability.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.
She said that they would have left the town and moved to Pune by the following week. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: She said, "They will have left the town and moved to Pune by next week."

2.en: She said, "That they would leave the town and move to Pune by next week."

3.en: She said, "They have left the town and moved to Pune by the following week."

4.en: She said, "They will leave the town and move to Pune by the following week."

solution.en:
Rule
While converting to direct speech, move the tense forward and restore the original time words.

Explicit changes
Remove “that” and add inverted commas.
“would have left … moved” becomes “will have left … moved” (future perfect).
“the following week” becomes “next week”.

Final sentence
She said, "They will have left the town and moved to Pune by next week."

Option 2 keeps “that” inside the quotation, option 3 changes the tense, and option 4 loses the perfect aspect and keeps “the following week”.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.
She said that she has started attending yoga classes because she wants to lose weight. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: She said, "I started attending yoga classes because I wants to lose weight."

2.en: She said, "I have started attending yoga classes because I want to lose weight."

3.en: She said, "I started attending yoga classes because I wanted to lose weight."

4.en: She said, "I had started attending yoga classes because I want to lose weight."

solution.en:
Rule
The reported clause is still in the present (not back-shifted), so keep the tenses and restore the first-person pronouns.

Explicit changes
“she” becomes “I” in both clauses.
“has started” becomes “have started” to agree with “I”.
“wants” becomes “want”.

Final sentence
She said, "I have started attending yoga classes because I want to lose weight."

Option 1 uses “I wants”, while options 3 and 4 change the tenses.

question.en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.
The teacher said to the students, "Why are you making so much noise?" [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The teacher asked the students why they were making so much noise.

2.en: The teacher asked the students why were they making so much noise.

3.en: The teacher asked the students why they are making so much noise.

4.en: The teacher demanded the students why they were making so much noise.

solution.en:
Rule
For a wh-question, “said to” becomes “asked”, the wh-word joins the clauses, the word order becomes that of a statement, and the tense moves back.

Explicit changes
“said to” becomes “asked”.
“you” becomes “they”.
“are you making” becomes “they were making” (statement order, past continuous).

Final sentence
The teacher asked the students why they were making so much noise.

Option 2 keeps question order, option 3 is not back-shifted, and “demanded” does not take the listener as an object in this way.

question.en:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:
Riyaz said, "I will be there by tomorrow morning." [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Riyaz said that he would be there by tomorrow morning.

2.en: Riyaz said that he will be there by the following morning.

3.en: Riyaz said that he will be there by tomorrow morning.

4.en: Riyaz said that he would be there by the following morning.

solution.en:
Rule
With a past reporting verb, “will” becomes “would”, and time words change.

Explicit changes
“I” becomes “he”.
“will be” becomes “would be”.
“tomorrow morning” becomes “the following morning”.

Final sentence
Riyaz said that he would be there by the following morning.

Options 1 and 3 keep “tomorrow”, and options 2 and 3 keep “will”.

question.en:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:
William said to Margaret, "You are now twenty-one years old and you cannot behave like a child." [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: William told Margaret that she was then twenty-one years old and she could not behave like a child.

2.en: William told Margaret that she is then twenty-one years old and she could not behave like a child.

3.en: William told Margaret that she is now twenty-one years old and she could not behave like a child.

4.en: William told Margaret that she was now twenty-one years old and she could not behave like a child.

solution.en:
Rule
“Said to” becomes “told”; with a past reporting verb, tenses move back and “now” becomes “then”.

Explicit changes
“You are” becomes “she was”.
“now” becomes “then”.
“you cannot” becomes “she could not”.

Final sentence
William told Margaret that she was then twenty-one years old and she could not behave like a child.

Options 2 and 3 keep “is”, and option 4 keeps “now”.

question.en:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:
The trainer said to the trainees, "Go on writing this paragraph till you understand it very clearly." [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The trainer asked the trainees going on writing that paragraph till they understood it very clearly.

2.en: The trainer asked the trainees to go on writing that paragraph till they understood it very clearly.

3.en: The trainer asked the trainees to go on writing that paragraph till they understand it very clearly.

4.en: The trainer asked the trainees to went on writing that paragraph till they understood it very clearly.

solution.en:
Rule
An imperative is reported with “asked/told + object + to-infinitive”; tenses in the dependent clause move back.

Explicit changes
“said to” becomes “asked”.
“Go on writing” becomes “to go on writing”.
“this paragraph” becomes “that paragraph”.
“till you understand” becomes “till they understood”.

Final sentence
The trainer asked the trainees to go on writing that paragraph till they understood it very clearly.

Option 1 uses “going”, option 3 keeps “understand”, and option 4 uses “to went”.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.
The teacher reminded the students to submit their assignments by Friday. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The teacher said to the students, "Your assignments must be submitted by Friday."

2.en: The teacher reminded, "You have to submit your assignments by Friday."

3.en: The teacher reminded the students, "Submit your assignments by Friday."

4.en: The teacher said to the students, "You should submitted your assignments by Friday."

solution.en:
Rule
“Reminded … to submit” reports an instruction; in direct speech it becomes an imperative inside inverted commas, addressed to the students.

Explicit changes
Keep the reporting verb with its object: “The teacher reminded the students,”.
“to submit their assignments” becomes “Submit your assignments”.

Final sentence
The teacher reminded the students, "Submit your assignments by Friday."

Option 1 turns the instruction into a passive statement, option 2 drops the listeners, and option 4 has the error “should submitted”.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.
He said that he had been waiting for that opportunity for years. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: He said, "I have been waiting for the opportunity for years."

2.en: He said, "I am waiting for that opportunity for years."

3.en: He said, "I have been waiting for this opportunity for years."

4.en: He said, "I waited for that opportunity for years."

solution.en:
Rule
While converting to direct speech, move the tense forward and restore the speaker’s words: past perfect continuous → present perfect continuous, “that” → “this”.

Explicit changes
“he had been waiting” becomes “I have been waiting”.
“that opportunity” becomes “this opportunity”.

Final sentence
He said, "I have been waiting for this opportunity for years."

Option 1 uses “the” instead of “this”, option 2 wrongly uses “am waiting … for years”, and option 4 changes the tense.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.
The professor admitted that he had never delivered a lecture on that particular topic in any of his classes. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The professor said, "I've never delivered a lecture on this particular topic in any of my classes."

2.en: The professor admitted, "I'd never delivered a lecture on this particular topic in any class."

3.en: The professor admitted, "I have not deliver a lecture on that particular topic in any of my classes."

4.en: The professor said, "I have never delivered a lecture on this particular topic in none of my classes."

solution.en:
Rule
While converting to direct speech, use “said”, restore first-person pronouns, move the past perfect forward to the present perfect and change “that” to “this”.

Explicit changes
“admitted that he had never delivered” becomes said, "I've never delivered".
“that particular topic” becomes “this particular topic”.
“his classes” becomes “my classes”.

Final sentence
The professor said, "I've never delivered a lecture on this particular topic in any of my classes."

Option 2 keeps the past perfect, option 3 has “have not deliver”, and option 4 has a double negative (“never … none”).

question.en:
From the given alternatives, select the correct indirect narration of the given direct narration.
Pari said to Nirvaan, "He admitted that he had made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invest all his money in that risky startup company." [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Pari told Nirvaan that he had admitted that he had made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invest all his money in that risky startup company.

2.en: Pari told Nirvaan that he admitted that he had made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invest all his money in that risky startup company.

3.en: Pari told Nirvaan that he had admitted that he made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invest all his money in that risky startup company.

4.en: Pari told Nirvaan that he had admitted that he had made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invested all his money in that risky startup company.

solution.en:
Rule
With “said to” → “told … that”, a reported simple past moves back to the past perfect; a verb already in the past perfect stays unchanged.

Explicit changes
“said to Nirvaan” becomes “told Nirvaan that”.
“He admitted” becomes “he had admitted”.
“he had made” stays “had made”.
“to invest” keeps the base form after “to”.

Final sentence
Pari told Nirvaan that he had admitted that he had made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invest all his money in that risky startup company.

Option 2 does not back-shift “admitted”, option 3 changes “had made”, and option 4 has “to invested”.

question.en:
From the given alternatives, select the correct indirect narration of the given direct narration.
Sarthak said to Reyansh, "I believe that every single person deserves a second chance to make things right after making a mistake." [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Sarthak told Reyansh that he had believed that every single person deserved a second chance to make things right after making a mistake.

2.en: Sarthak told Reyansh that he believes that every single person deserved a second chance to make things right after making a mistake.

3.en: Sarthak told Reyansh that he believed that every single person deserving a second chance to make things right after making a mistake.

4.en: Sarthak told Reyansh that he believed that every single person deserved a second chance to make things right after making a mistake.

solution.en:
Rule
With “said to” → “told … that”, present tenses move back to the past.

Explicit changes
“I believe” becomes “he believed”.
“deserves” becomes “deserved”.

Final sentence
Sarthak told Reyansh that he believed that every single person deserved a second chance to make things right after making a mistake.

Option 1 over-shifts to “had believed”, option 2 keeps “believes”, and option 3 has no finite verb (“deserving”).

question.en:
From the given alternatives, select the correct direct narration of the given indirect narration.
Sanvi told Prakash that the coach had announced that practice would be cancelled for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Sanvi said to Prakash, "The coach is announcing that practice would be cancelled for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields."

2.en: Sanvi said to Prakash, "The coach announced that practice would have been cancelled for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields."

3.en: Sanvi said to Prakash, "The coach announced that practice would be cancelled for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields."

4.en: Sanvi said to Prakash, "The coach announced that practice would be cancelling for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields."

solution.en:
Rule
While converting to direct speech, “told … that” becomes “said to” with inverted commas, and the speaker’s own tense is restored: “had announced” → “announced”.

Explicit changes
“Sanvi told Prakash that” becomes Sanvi said to Prakash, "…".
“the coach had announced” becomes “The coach announced”.
The coach’s reported words, “practice would be cancelled”, remain unchanged.

Final sentence
Sanvi said to Prakash, "The coach announced that practice would be cancelled for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields."

Option 1 uses “is announcing”, option 2 uses “would have been cancelled”, and option 4 uses “would be cancelling”.

question.en:
From the given alternatives, select the correct direct narration of the given indirect narration.
Shivi told Rahul that he had realized that the mysterious footprints in the snow were actually made by a very large neighborhood dog. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Shivi said to Rahul, "He realized that the mysterious footprints in the snow were actually made by a very large neighborhood dog."

2.en: Shivi said to Rahul, "He realizes that the mysterious footprints in the snow were actually made by a very large neighborhood dog."

3.en: Shivi said to Rahul, "He realized that the mysterious footprints in the snow had been actually made by a very large neighborhood dog."

4.en: Shivi said to Rahul, "He realized that the mysterious footprints in the snow were actually made from a very large neighborhood dog."

solution.en:
Rule
While converting to direct speech, “told … that” becomes “said to”, and the past perfect “had realized” returns to the simple past.

Explicit changes
“Shivi told Rahul that” becomes Shivi said to Rahul, "…".
“he had realized” becomes “He realized”.
“were actually made by” stays unchanged.

Final sentence
Shivi said to Rahul, "He realized that the mysterious footprints in the snow were actually made by a very large neighborhood dog."

Option 2 uses “realizes”, option 3 changes “were made” to “had been made”, and option 4 uses “made from”.

question.en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in Direct Speech.
He said that he had gone to the doctor by the time I called. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: He said, "I have gone to the doctor by the time you called."

2.en: He said, "I had gone to the doctor by the time you called."

3.en: He said, "I went to the doctor by the time you called."

4.en: He said, "I go to the doctor by the time you called."

solution.en:
Rule
To change indirect speech into direct speech, remove "that", put the spoken words in inverted commas and change the pronouns back to the speaker's (he → I, I → you).
The clause "by the time you called" shows that going to the doctor was completed before another past action, so the speaker himself used the past perfect (had + V3), which stays unchanged.

Explicit changes
said that → said, " … ."
he had gone → I had gone (past perfect retained)
by the time I called → by the time you called

Final sentence
He said, "I had gone to the doctor by the time you called."

"By the time + past" needs the past perfect in the main clause, so "have gone", "went" and "go" are all incorrect here.

question.en:
Convert the following indirect speech sentence into direct speech by selecting the correct option.
The Minister said that the new policy would be effective from next month. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The Minister said, "The new policy is effective from next month."

2.en: The Minister said, "The new policy was effective from next month."

3.en: The Minister said, "The new policy will be effective from next month."

4.en: The Minister said, "The new policy would be effective from next month."

solution.en:
Rule
While converting indirect speech into direct speech, remove "that", add inverted commas and reverse the back-shift of tense: would → will.
Nothing in the sentence shows a condition, so the Minister's original words were in the simple future.

Explicit changes
said that → said, " … ."
would be → will be

Final sentence
The Minister said, "The new policy will be effective from next month."

question.en:
Convert the following indirect speech sentence into direct speech by selecting the correct option.
The police officer asked whether the suspects had fled the city by then. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The police officer asked, "Did the suspects flee the city by now?"

2.en: The police officer asked, "Had the suspects fled the city by now?"

3.en: The police officer asked, "Have the suspects been fleeing the city by now?"

4.en: The police officer asked, "Have the suspects fled the city by now?"

solution.en:
Rule
While converting an indirect question into a direct question, remove "whether", use question order and add a question mark.
The indirect "by then" goes back to the speaker's "by now". "By now" refers to the present moment, so it needs the present perfect: had fled → have fled.

Explicit changes
asked whether → asked, " … ?"
the suspects had fled → Have the suspects fled
by then → by now

Final sentence
The police officer asked, "Have the suspects fled the city by now?"

"Did … flee by now" (simple past) and "Had … fled by now" (past perfect) do not go with "by now", and "have been fleeing" would become "had been fleeing" in indirect speech.

question.en:
Convert the following indirect speech sentence into direct speech by selecting the correct option.
The Minister said that the government had allocated additional funds for education by then. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The Minister said, "The government allocated additional funds for education by now."

2.en: The Minister said, "The government had allocated additional funds for education by now."

3.en: The Minister said, "The government has allocated additional funds for education by now."

4.en: The Minister said, "The government will allocate additional funds for education by now."

solution.en:
Rule
While converting indirect speech into direct speech, remove "that", add inverted commas and reverse the back-shift of tense.
The indirect "by then" goes back to the speaker's "by now". "By now" refers to the present moment, so it needs the present perfect: had allocated → has allocated.

Explicit changes
said that → said, " … ."
had allocated → has allocated
by then → by now

Final sentence
The Minister said, "The government has allocated additional funds for education by now."

The simple past "allocated" and the past perfect "had allocated" do not go with "by now", and "will allocate" changes the meaning to future.

question.en:
Convert the following direct speech sentence into indirect speech by selecting the correct option.
The Principal said, "Students must submit their projects by Friday." [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The Principal said that students had to submit their projects by Friday.

2.en: The Principal said that students must submit their projects by Friday.

3.en: The Principal said that students should submit their projects by Friday.

4.en: The Principal said that students will submit their projects by Friday.

solution.en:
Rule
In indirect speech with a past reporting verb, "must" expressing a present or immediate obligation changes to "had to". "Must" stays unchanged only for permanent truths, rules or prohibitions.
Submitting projects by Friday is a particular obligation, so "must" becomes "had to".

Explicit changes
said, "…" → said that
must submit → had to submit

Final sentence
The Principal said that students had to submit their projects by Friday.

question.en:
Convert the following direct speech sentence into indirect speech by selecting the correct option.
The police officer asked, "Have you witnessed the incident?" [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The police officer asked have I witnessed the incident.

2.en: The police officer asked if I had witnessed the incident.

3.en: The police officer asked if I have been witnessing the incident.

4.en: The police officer asked whether I have witnessed the incident.

solution.en:
Rule
A yes/no question is reported with if/whether, in statement order, without a question mark.
The present perfect changes to the past perfect, and "you" changes to "I" (the listener is the reporter).

Explicit changes
asked, "Have you witnessed" → asked if I had witnessed
the question mark → a full stop

Final sentence
The police officer asked if I had witnessed the incident.

question.en:
Convert the following direct speech sentence into indirect speech by selecting the correct option.
The Principal said, "Submit your assignments by Monday." [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The Principal instructed us to submit our assignments by Monday.

2.en: The Principal ordered us to submit assignments by Monday.

3.en: The Principal requested us to submit assignments by Monday.

4.en: The Principal told us to submit assignments by Monday.

solution.en:
Rule
An imperative sentence is reported with a verb such as told, ordered, instructed, advised or requested + object + to-infinitive. Pronouns change according to the listener (your → our).

Explicit changes
said, "Submit" → instructed us to submit
your assignments → our assignments

Final sentence
The Principal instructed us to submit our assignments by Monday.

Options 2, 3 and 4 drop the possessive "our", and "requested" does not suit a principal's instruction.

question.en:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:
He said to me, "I will send you a picture postcard when I visit the Sun Temple." [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: He told me that he would send me a picture postcard when he visited the Sun Temple.

2.en: He told me that he would send me a picture postcard when he had visited the Sun Temple.

3.en: He told me that he would send me a picture postcard when he would visit the Sun Temple.

4.en: He told me that he would have sent me a picture postcard when he visited the Sun Temple.

solution.en:
Rule
"Said to me" → told me that. The pronouns change (I → he, you → me), will → would, and the simple present in the "when" clause changes to the simple past (visit → visited).

Explicit changes
He said to me → He told me that
I will send you → he would send me
when I visit → when he visited

Final sentence
He told me that he would send me a picture postcard when he visited the Sun Temple.

question.en:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:
Sonika said to Sailesh, “If you were in my place in the party now, you would cry like a child.” [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Sonika told Sailesh that if he had been in her place in the party then, he would have cried like a child.

2.en: Sonika told Sailesh that if he were in her place in the party now, he would cry like a child.

3.en: Sonika told Sailesh that if she had been in his place in the party then, she would have cried like a child.

4.en: Sonika told Sailesh that if she were in her place in the party now, she would cry like a child.

solution.en:
Rule
said to → told; the reported clause is joined by that.
Pronouns change according to the speaker and the listener: you → he (Sailesh), my → her (Sonika).
now → then.
The imaginary condition is shifted back: were → had been and would cry → would have cried.

Explicit changes
said to Sailesh → told Sailesh that
If you were → if he had been
in my place → in her place
now → then
you would cry → he would have cried

Final sentence
Sonika told Sailesh that if he had been in her place in the party then, he would have cried like a child.

Option 2 keeps "now" unchanged, and options 3 and 4 use the wrong pronouns (she/his, she/her).

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.
The philosopher said that truth is often more elusive than fiction. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The philosopher said, "Truth was often more elusive than fiction."

2.en: The philosopher said, "Truth is often more elusive than fiction."

3.en: The philosopher said, "Truth had often been more elusive than fiction."

4.en: The philosopher said, "Truth will always be more elusive than fiction."

solution.en:
Rule
When indirect speech is changed to direct speech, "said that" becomes said, "…", and the reported words are placed within inverted commas.
A universal truth or general statement keeps the present tense in both forms.

Explicit changes
said that → said, "
truth is → "Truth is (present tense kept; capital letter inside the quotation)
full stop placed inside the closing inverted comma

Final sentence
The philosopher said, "Truth is often more elusive than fiction."

Options 1 and 3 wrongly change the tense of a general truth, and option 4 changes the meaning to "will always be".

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.
The general commanded the troops to hold their positions until further orders. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The general said to the troops, "Hold your positions until further orders."

2.en: The general told to the troops, "Hold your positions until further orders."

3.en: The general commanded the troops, "Hold their positions until further orders."

4.en: The general said to the troops, "You must hold your position until further orders."

solution.en:
Rule
A command in indirect speech ("commanded + object + to + V1") becomes an imperative sentence in direct speech: said to + listener, "V1 …". The pronoun changes to the listener's point of view: their → your.

Explicit changes
commanded the troops → said to the troops
to hold → "Hold (imperative)
their positions → your positions

Final sentence
The general said to the troops, "Hold your positions until further orders."

Option 2 uses "told to", option 3 keeps "their", and option 4 changes the command to "You must…" and "positions" to singular.

question.en:
From the given alternatives, select the correct indirect narration of the given direct narration.
Sneha says, "We have already achieved success in our lives." [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Sneha says that they had already achieved success in their lives.

2.en: Sneha said that they had already achieved success in their lives.

3.en: Sneha says that they have already achieved success in their lives.

4.en: Sneha says that we have already achieved success in our lives.

solution.en:
Rule
When the reporting verb is in the present tense ("says"), the tense of the reported speech does not change.
Only the pronouns change according to the reporter: we → they, our → their.

Explicit changes
says, "…" → says that
We have already achieved → they have already achieved (tense unchanged)
our lives → their lives

Final sentence
Sneha says that they have already achieved success in their lives.

Options 1 and 2 wrongly change the tense to "had achieved" (option 2 also changes "says" to "said"), and option 4 keeps "we" and "our" unchanged.

question.en:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence:
He asked her if he might use her phone for a moment. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: He said, “Might I use your phone for a moment?”

2.en: He said, “May have use your phone for a moment?”

3.en: He said, “Couldn't I use your phone for a moment?”

4.en: He said, “Should I use your phone for a moment?”

solution.en:
Rule
A yes/no question reported with "asked … if" becomes a direct question (auxiliary before subject) within inverted commas, ending with a question mark. Pronouns change back to the speaker's point of view: he → I, her → your.

Explicit changes
asked her if → said, " … ?"
he might use → Might I use (question order)
her phone → your phone

Final sentence
He said, "Might I use your phone for a moment?"

Option 2 ("May have use") is ungrammatical, and options 3 and 4 change the modal and the meaning of the polite request.

question.en:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence:
The judge commanded them to call the first witness. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The judge said, "You call the first witness."

2.en: The judge said, "Call the first witness."

3.en: The judge said to them, "He call the first witness."

4.en: The judge said, "He should call the first witness."

solution.en:
Rule
"Commanded + object + to + V1" becomes an imperative sentence in direct speech; it begins with the verb (V1), and the subject "you" is understood.

Explicit changes
commanded them → said, "
to call → Call (imperative)
full stop placed inside the closing inverted comma

Final sentence
The judge said, "Call the first witness."

Option 1 adds "You", which weakens the command form, option 3 uses "He call" (wrong pronoun and verb form), and option 4 changes the command into advice with "should".

question.en:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence:
The policeman enquired where we were going. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The policeman said, "Where were we going?"

2.en: The policeman said, "Where were you going?"

3.en: The policeman said to us, "Where are we going?"

4.en: The policeman said, "Where are you going?"

solution.en:
Rule
"Enquired + wh-word + clause" becomes a direct wh-question (auxiliary before subject) with a question mark. The past tense of the reported clause goes back to the present, and we → you, because the policeman addresses the listeners.

Explicit changes
enquired → said, " … ?"
where we were going → Where are you going

Final sentence
The policeman said, "Where are you going?"

Options 1 and 2 keep the past tense, and option 3 keeps "we", which would mean the policeman is asking about his own group.

question.en:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.
He said to me, “When are you going to submit your assignment?” [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: He asked me when I was going to submit my assignment.

2.en: He asked me when was I going to submit my assignment.

3.en: He told me if when I was going to submit my assignment.

4.en: He asked me when I am going to submit my assignment.

solution.en:
Rule
said to → asked; the wh-word "when" acts as the connector; the question becomes a statement (subject before verb); the tense back-shifts, are going → was going; pronouns change, you → I and your → my.

Explicit changes
He said to me → He asked me
When are you going → when I was going
your assignment → my assignment

Final sentence
He asked me when I was going to submit my assignment.

Option 2 keeps the question order ("was I"), option 3 wrongly uses "told" and "if when", and option 4 does not back-shift the tense.

question.en:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.
“Please lend me your book for two days,” said Rohan to me. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Rohan asked me if lend him my book for two days.

2.en: Rohan requested me that I should lend him my book for two days.

3.en: Rohan requested me to lend him my book for two days.

4.en: Rohan told me to please lend him my book for two days.

solution.en:
Rule
A request with "Please" is reported with requested + object + to + V1, and "please" is dropped. Pronouns change: me → him (Rohan), your → my.

Explicit changes
said Rohan to me → Rohan requested me
Please lend → to lend
me your book → him my book

Final sentence
Rohan requested me to lend him my book for two days.

Option 1 uses "if" for a request, option 2 uses "requested … that I should", which is not the standard form, and option 4 keeps "please" with "told".

question.en:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.
“If you don’t keep quiet, I shall send you out,” said the teacher to the students. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The teacher warned the students that if they didn't keep quiet, he would send them out.

2.en: The teacher told the students that if they don't kept quiet, he shall send them out.

3.en: The teacher warned the students that if they didn't keep quiet, he shall send them out.

4.en: The teacher asked the students if they didn't keep quiet, he would send them out.

solution.en:
Rule
A threat is reported with warned. The tense back-shifts: don't keep → didn't keep, shall → would. Pronouns change: you → they, I → he, you → them.

Explicit changes
said to the students → warned the students that
If you don't keep quiet → if they didn't keep quiet
I shall send you out → he would send them out

Final sentence
The teacher warned the students that if they didn't keep quiet, he would send them out.

Option 2 uses "don't kept" and "shall", option 3 keeps "shall", and option 4 uses "asked … if", which does not suit a warning.

question.en:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.
He said to the scientist, "How long will it take to reach Mars with this propulsion system?" [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: He asked the scientist how long it will take to reach Mars with this propulsion system.

2.en: He told the scientist how long it would take to reach Mars with that propulsion system.

3.en: He asked the scientist how long it would take to reach Mars with that propulsion system.

4.en: He asked the scientist that how long it would take to reach Mars with that propulsion system.

solution.en:
Rule
A wh-question is reported with asked, the wh-word acts as the connector (no "that"), the question becomes a statement (subject before verb), and the tense is back-shifted.

Explicit changes
said to → asked
"How long will it take" → how long it would take
this → that
question mark → full stop

Final sentence
He asked the scientist how long it would take to reach Mars with that propulsion system.

Option 1 keeps "will" and "this", option 2 uses "told" for a question, and option 4 wrongly adds "that" before the wh-word.

question.en:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Indirect Speech. Choose the correct Direct Speech form.
The meteorologist said that it might rain heavily in the hills. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: The meteorologist said, "It might rain heavily in the hills."

2.en: The meteorologist said, "It will rain heavily in the hills."

3.en: The meteorologist said, "It may rain heavily in the hills."

4.en: The meteorologist said, "It rained heavily in the hills."

solution.en:
Rule
While changing indirect speech to direct speech, "said that" becomes said, "…" and the reported words are placed within inverted commas. The modal might does not change in reported speech, so the direct speech that matches the reported sentence keeps might.

Explicit changes
said that → said, "…"
it might rain → "It might rain …"
in the hills → unchanged

Final sentence
The meteorologist said, "It might rain heavily in the hills."

Option 2 turns a possibility into a certainty ("will"), option 4 changes it into a past event ("rained"), and option 3 alters the modal given in the sentence.

question.en:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Indirect Speech. Choose the correct Direct Speech form.
The doctor said that too much sugar can harm the liver. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: The doctor said, "Too much sugar can harm the liver."

2.en: The doctor said, "Too much sugar may harm the liver."

3.en: The doctor said, "Too much sugar could harm the liver."

4.en: The doctor said, "Too much sugar harms the liver."

solution.en:
Rule
A general truth or scientific fact keeps its tense and modal in reported speech, so the direct speech also keeps can.

Explicit changes
said that → said, "…"
too much sugar can harm the liver → "Too much sugar can harm the liver."

Final sentence
The doctor said, "Too much sugar can harm the liver."

Options 2, 3 and 4 change the modal ("may", "could") or the verb form ("harms"), which alters the meaning.

question.en:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Indirect Speech. Choose the correct Direct Speech form.
The coach told the players that they must give their best during the finals. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: The coach said, "You must give your best during the finals."

2.en: The coach said, "They must give their best during the finals."

3.en: The coach told them, "They had to give their best during the finals."

4.en: The coach told them, "You have to give your best during the finals."

solution.en:
Rule
"told + object + that" becomes said (to …), "…"; pronouns change back to the speaker's point of view. Must stays must.

Explicit changes
told the players that → said, "…"
they → you
their → your
must → must

Final sentence
The coach said, "You must give your best during the finals."

Options 2 and 3 keep the third-person pronouns inside the quotation, and option 4 changes "must" to "have to".

question.en:
Convert the following direct speech sentence into indirect speech by selecting the correct option.
The director said, "The film has been screened at international festivals." [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: The director said that the film had been screened at international festivals.

2.en: The director said that the film has been screened at international festivals.

3.en: The director said that the film is being screened at international festivals.

4.en: The director said that the film was screened at international festivals.

solution.en:
Rule
When the reporting verb is in the past, the present perfect changes to the past perfect.

Explicit changes
said, "…" → said that
has been screened → had been screened
inverted commas removed

Final sentence
The director said that the film had been screened at international festivals.

Option 2 does not back-shift the tense, option 3 changes the meaning to the present continuous, and option 4 uses the simple past.

question.en:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:
I said to the mechanic, "Repair the bike as soon as possible." [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: I told the mechanic repair the bike as soon as possible.

2.en: I told the mechanic to repaired the bike as soon as possible.

3.en: I told the mechanic to repair the bike as soon as possible.

4.en: I said the mechanic to repaired the bike as soon as possible.

solution.en:
Rule
An imperative sentence is reported with told/ordered/requested + object + to + V1.

Explicit changes
said to → told
"Repair" → to repair
inverted commas removed

Final sentence
I told the mechanic to repair the bike as soon as possible.

Option 1 misses "to", options 2 and 4 use "to repaired", and option 4 also uses "said the mechanic" without "to".

question.en:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:
Niyati said, "I did not believe my eyes when I saw him dance." [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: Niyati said that she did not believed her eyes when she had seen him dance.

2.en: Niyati said that she did not believe her eyes when she had seen him dance.

3.en: Niyati said that she did not believe her eyes when she saw him dance.

4.en: Niyati said that she had not believed her eyes when she had seen him dance.

solution.en:
Rule
When the reporting verb is in the past, the simple past changes to the past perfect; first-person pronouns change to match the speaker.

Explicit changes
said, "…" → said that
I → she, my → her
did not believe → had not believed
saw → had seen

Final sentence
Niyati said that she had not believed her eyes when she had seen him dance.

Option 1 uses "did not believed" (wrong), option 2 changes only one verb, and option 3 does not back-shift the tenses.

question.en:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.
He said that he had been trying to book the tickets since the previous morning. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

1.en: He said, "I have been trying to book the tickets since yesterday morning."

2.en: He said, "I had been trying to book the tickets since yesterday morning."
