D. easier to leave all baggage here on the roadside and walk on into the blackness. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Correct order: CABD

C opens with the subject: "He listened to them all … as he tested the Hoover's suction"
C "suction" + A "against pieces of newspaper, until … Life was an enormous"
A "an enormous" + B "rucksack so impossibly heavy that … it was infinitely"
B "infinitely" + D "easier to leave all baggage here on the roadside and walk on into the blackness."

Final sentence: He listened to them all for another fifteen minutes, mute as he tested the Hoover's suction against pieces of newspaper, until he was overcome by the sensation that Life was an enormous rucksack so impossibly heavy that, even though it meant losing everything, it was infinitely easier to leave all baggage here on the roadside and walk on into the blackness.

question.en:
Arrange the following sentences in the correct order to form a logically sound and coherent paragraph.
The parts are:
A. changed their sleeping pattern.
B. Experts are unable
C. to explain why the
D. owls have suddenly [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Syntactic & Logical Flow:
1. Part B: 'Experts are unable' establishes the main subject and predicate adjective.
2. Part C: 'to explain why the' provides the dependent infinitive complement ending in the definite article 'the'.
3. Part D: 'owls have suddenly' supplies the subject noun ('owls') and adverb ('suddenly') following 'the'.
4. Part A: 'changed their sleeping pattern.' completes the transitive verb phrase 'have suddenly changed' and its direct object.

Complete coherent sentence: Experts are unable to explain why the owls have suddenly changed their sleeping pattern.
Therefore, the correct sequence is BCDA.

question.en:
Arrange the following sentences in the correct order to form a logically sound and coherent paragraph.
The parts are:
A. in our profession, whatever
B. There existed in those
C. the small differences in our approach.
D. days a true camaraderie [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Syntactic & Logical Flow:
1. Part B: 'There existed in those' requires a temporal noun following the demonstrative determiner 'those'.
2. Part D: 'days a true camaraderie' supplies the noun 'days' and introduces the existential subject 'a true camaraderie'.
3. Part A: 'in our profession, whatever' qualifies the field of camaraderie and introduces the concession 'whatever'.
4. Part C: 'the small differences in our approach.' supplies the object of concession.

Complete coherent sentence: There existed in those days a true camaraderie in our profession, whatever the small differences in our approach.
Therefore, the correct sequence is BDAC.

question.en:
Given below are four jumbled parts of a sentence. Select the option that gives their correct order and forms a meaningful sentence.
A. while dining
B. we enjoyed
C. at the cafe
D. listening to jazz music [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Sentence Structure Analysis:
1. Part B: 'we enjoyed' establishes the subject and transitive verb.
2. Part D: 'listening to jazz music' provides the required gerund direct object following 'enjoy'.
3. Part A: 'while dining' introduces the adverbial temporal participle clause.
4. Part C: 'at the cafe' provides the prepositional phrase of place modifying 'dining'.

Complete meaningful sentence: We enjoyed listening to jazz music while dining at the cafe.
Therefore, the correct order is BDAC.

question.en:
Given below are four jumbled parts of a sentence. Select the option that gives their correct order and forms a meaningful sentence.
A. brought back many warm memories of
B. long summer afternoons
C. re-reading my favourite childhood story
D. spent in the quiet garden [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Sentence Structure Analysis:
1. Part C: 're-reading my favourite childhood story' acts as the gerund subject of the sentence.
2. Part A: 'brought back many warm memories of' is the main predicate verb phrase taking a prepositional object.
3. Part B: 'long summer afternoons' acts as the noun object of the preposition 'of'.
4. Part D: 'spent in the quiet garden' is a past-participial modifier describing the afternoons.

Complete meaningful sentence: Re-reading my favourite childhood story brought back many warm memories of long summer afternoons spent in the quiet garden.
Therefore, the correct order is CABD.

question.en:
Given below are four jumbled parts of a sentence. Select the option that gives their correct order and forms a meaningful sentence.
A. last-minute trip and ended up
B. leaving my favourite sweater
C. on the bedroom chair
D. I was rushing to pack for a [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Sentence Structure Analysis:
1. Part D: 'I was rushing to pack for a' introduces the subject, past continuous verb, and indefinite article 'a'.
2. Part A: 'last-minute trip and ended up' provides the singular count noun ('trip') and the coordinated verb 'ended up'.
3. Part B: 'leaving my favourite sweater' provides the gerund phrase following 'ended up'.
4. Part C: 'on the bedroom chair' provides the concluding prepositional phrase of location.

Complete meaningful sentence: I was rushing to pack for a last-minute trip and ended up leaving my favourite sweater on the bedroom chair.
Therefore, the correct order is DABC.

question.en:
Given below are four jumbled parts of a sentence. Select the option that gives their correct order and forms a meaningful sentence.
A. the quiet neighbourhood
B. ray of sunlight illuminated the streets
C. this morning, I walked through
D. absorbing the calm as the first [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Sentence Structure Analysis:
1. Part C: 'this morning, I walked through' establishes the temporal adverbial and main clause with transitive preposition 'through'.
2. Part A: 'the quiet neighbourhood' provides the noun phrase object governed by 'through'.
3. Part D: 'absorbing the calm as the first' introduces a participial clause and the temporal conjunction 'as the first'.
4. Part B: 'ray of sunlight illuminated the streets' completes the subject ('first ray of sunlight') and subordinate clause verb phrase ('illuminated the streets').

Complete meaningful sentence: This morning, I walked through the quiet neighbourhood, absorbing the calm as the first ray of sunlight illuminated the streets.
Therefore, the correct order is CADB.

Sentence: Heavy rains disrupted traffic across several parts of the national capital.

Sentence: The kittens played happily with the colourful yarn in the room.

question.en:
In the following question, the first and last parts of the sentence (1 and 6) are given. The rest of the sentence is split into four parts and named P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence and find out which of the four combinations is correct.

P. but also destroys habitats
Q. accelerates soil erosion
R. for countless species
S. living in tropical rainforest
6. regions. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
“not only … but also” must link two parallel verbs.
1. Deforestation not only – Q accelerates soil erosion – P but also destroys habitats – R for countless species – S living in tropical rainforest – 6. regions.
Sentence: Deforestation not only accelerates soil erosion but also destroys habitats for countless species living in tropical rainforest regions.
Order: Q, P, R, S.

Therefore, QPRS.

question.en:
Given below are four jumbled parts of a sentence. Select the option that gives their correct order and forms a meaningful sentence.

Infinitive: D – to be confident while facing
Object: B – difficult social settings
Sentence: True confidence is entirely different from merely pretending to be confident while facing difficult social settings.
Order: A, C, D, B.

Therefore, ACDB.

question.en:
Given below are four jumbled parts of a sentence. Select the option that gives their correct order and forms a meaningful sentence.

Sentence: The moon appears to whisper secrets to the restless ocean while the tide reflects the enduring silent rhythm of their perpetual interaction.

question.en:
Given below are four jumbled parts of a sentence. Select the option that gives their correct order and forms a meaningful sentence.
A. would surely tell stories
B. of our forgotten kinship

Sentence: If humans could communicate with nature, the earth would surely tell stories of our forgotten kinship.

question.en:
Choose the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence:
(A) she was (B) known (C) for her kindness (D) in the town [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule
Arrange subject + verb + complement + modifiers into a natural order.

Explicit changes
A (she was) + B (known) + D (in the town) + C (for her kindness).

Final sentence
She was known in the town for her kindness.

The sequence ABDC gives the most natural order among the options.

question.en:
Choose the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence:
(A) with red flowers (B) bloomed (C) the garden (D) beautifully [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule
Put subject + verb + complement + adverb in order.

Explicit changes
C (the garden) + B (bloomed) + A (with red flowers) + D (beautifully).

Final sentence
The garden bloomed with red flowers beautifully.

CBAD is the only option that yields a meaningful sentence.

question.en:
Arrange the sentence parts:
(A) in the evening (B) the guests (C) arrived (D) at the venue [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule
Arrange as subject + verb + place + time — the natural English order.

Explicit arrangement
B “the guests” — the subject opens the sentence.
C “arrived” — the verb follows the subject.
D “at the venue” — the place phrase follows the verb.
A “in the evening” — the time phrase closes the sentence.

Final sentence
The guests arrived at the venue in the evening.

BACD gives “The guests in the evening arrived at the venue”, which breaks the subject–verb flow; BADC and ACBD are also unnatural.
Therefore, BCDA.

question.en:
Arrange the sentence parts:
(A) the workers (B) completed (C) the project (D) on time [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule
The parts already read in natural order: subject + verb + object + adverbial.

Explicit changes
A (the workers) + B (completed) + C (the project) + D (on time).

Final sentence
The workers completed the project on time.

ABCD is the correct sequence.

question.en:
Arrange the sentence parts:
(A) for her success (B) congratulated (C) they (D) the candidate [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule
Arrange as subject + verb + object + reason.

Explicit arrangement
C “they” — the subject opens the sentence.
B “congratulated” — the verb follows.
D “the candidate” — the object of “congratulated”.
A “for her success” — the reason phrase closes the sentence.

Final sentence
They congratulated the candidate for her success.

CBAD gives “They congratulated for her success the candidate”, separating the verb from its object; ABDC and DBAC do not start with the subject.
Therefore, CBDA.

question.en:
In the following question, the sentence has been split into four parts. These parts are jumbled and not in the correct order. Select the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence.
A. She loves to read
B. during the evening
C. by the window
D. old mystery novels [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule
Arrange as subject + verb + object + time + place.

Explicit arrangement
A “She loves to read” — subject and verb open the sentence.
D “old mystery novels” — the object must come directly after “read”.
B “during the evening” — the time phrase.
C “by the window” — the place phrase completes the sentence.

Final sentence
She loves to read old mystery novels during the evening by the window.

ABDC gives “She loves to read during the evening old mystery novels…”, wrongly separating the verb “read” from its object “old mystery novels”; DABC and CBAD do not begin with the subject.
Therefore, ADBC.

question.en:
Choose the part of the sentence that contains an error:
She is senior than me by five years. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error is senior than; use senior to.

Latin comparatives ending in -ior (senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior) take “to”, not “than”.

Correct sentence: She is senior to me by five years.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The novelist who her editor had praised (1)/ for stylistic ingenuity and metaphorical clarity (2)/ was yet to submit (3)/ the final chapters of the manuscript. (4) [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error is in part (1): who should be whom.

In the relative clause, “her editor” is the subject, and the relative pronoun is the object of “had praised”; the object form is “whom”.

Correct sentence: The novelist whom her editor had praised for stylistic ingenuity and metaphorical clarity was yet to submit the final chapters of the manuscript.

Check: “her editor had praised her” — an object form, so “whom”.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Scholars in postcolonial studies (1)/ often disputes the neutrality (2)/ of archival records (3)/ and the politics of naming. (4) [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error is in part (2): disputes should be dispute.

The subject is the plural noun “scholars”; “in postcolonial studies” only describes them. A plural subject takes a plural verb.

Correct sentence: Scholars in postcolonial studies often dispute the neutrality of archival records and the politics of naming.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
Qatar has extended strict quarantine rules having required travellers to isolate for up to 14 days upon their arrival in the country. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error is having required travellers; use requiring travellers.

“Having required” shows an action completed before the main verb, but the rules require isolation now, at the same time as the extension. A present participle (or “that require”) expresses this.

Correct sentence: Qatar has extended strict quarantine rules requiring travellers to isolate for up to 14 days upon their arrival in the country.

question.en:
Spot the error in the below-given sentence.
"I wish I am taller than my brother". [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error is I am; use I were (informally, “I was”).

After wish about a present situation that is not true, English uses the past subjunctive.

Correct sentence: I wish I were taller than my brother.
[काश मैं अपने भाई से लंबा होता।]

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
There isn't much time to spare. You'd better buy your ticket with the train. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The error is with the train; use on the train (or “for the train”).

A ticket is bought for a journey or on board a train; “with the train” expresses neither idea.

Correct sentence: There isn't much time to spare. You'd better buy your ticket on the train.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
The person with who Maya shared the flat had not paid his rent. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The error is who Maya shared the flat; use whom.

After a preposition (“with”), the relative pronoun takes the object form: with whom.

Correct sentence: The person with whom Maya shared the flat had not paid his rent.

question.en: Identify the incorrect sentence. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Did they sent me any books for preparation of examination.

2.en: Reactions to the annual play have been favorable.

3.en: The author of the stories in these books is Mary Gomes.

4.en: Many lines in the poem are especially good.

solution.en:
Sentence 1 is incorrect: Did they sent should be Did they send.

After the auxiliary “did”, the main verb takes its base form. As a question, the sentence also needs a question mark.

Correct sentence: Did they send me any books for preparation of the examination?

The other sentences are grammatically correct.

question.en: Identify the incorrect sentence. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: All of the cities in California can to be affected by the rain yesterday.

2.en: Seven people were rescued from the fire yesterday.

3.en: Half of the boxes are empty as the children have eaten the chocolates.

4.en: Each packet can have a variable number of chocolates.

solution.en:
Sentence 1 is incorrect.

“Can” is followed by a bare infinitive (no “to”), and “can” cannot describe a past event such as “yesterday”.

Correct sentence: All of the cities in California may have been affected by the rain yesterday. (Or: …were affected by the rain yesterday.)

The other sentences are grammatically correct.

question.en:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts, namely A, B, C and D, which are given in the alternatives. Select the alternative that contains the part of the sentence with an error.
The child requested his mother to gave him a big chocolate because he had been very good all day long and deserved a treat. [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The child requested his mother to

2.en: gave him a big chocolate because he

3.en: had been very good all day

solution.en:
The error is in part B: to gave should be to give.

The infinitive marker “to” is followed by the base form of the verb: requested his mother to give.

Correct sentence: The child requested his mother to give him a big chocolate because he had been very good all day long and deserved a treat.

question.en:
Find the incorrect part of the sentence:
He told to me about the incident. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: "Tell" takes a direct object without "to" (tell someone something). "Say" is the verb that takes "to" (say to someone).
So the error is in the part "to me".

Correct sentence:
He told me about the incident.

question.en:
Identify the part containing a grammatical or structural error:
Ten miles are a long distance to walk. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: A plural expression of distance, time, money or weight taken as one amount takes a singular verb.
"Ten miles" is a single distance, so "are" must be "is".

Correct sentence:
Ten miles is a long distance to walk.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The psychological bareness (1)/ of her narrative (2)/ precludes any embellishment, yet render (3)/ the structure more profoundly intimate. (4) [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: The subject "The psychological bareness" is singular, so both verbs joined by "yet" must be singular: "precludes … yet renders".
So the error is in part (3): "render" should be "renders".

Correct sentence:
The psychological bareness of her narrative precludes any embellishment, yet renders the structure more profoundly intimate.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The paradigm of rational choice theory (1)/ postulate that agents act consistently (2)/ to maximize utility, often ignoring (3)/ the constraints imposed by affective reasoning. (4) [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: The subject is "The paradigm" (singular); "of rational choice theory" only describes it. A singular subject takes a singular verb.
So the error is in part (2): "postulate" should be "postulates".

Correct sentence:
The paradigm of rational choice theory postulates that agents act consistently to maximize utility, often ignoring the constraints imposed by affective reasoning.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
Can you borrow your book to me just for one day? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: Lend means to give something for a time; borrow means to take something for a time. When you ask someone to give you their book, the correct verb is lend ("lend something to someone").
So the error is in "borrow your".

Correct sentence:
Can you lend your book to me just for one day?

Related words: lend [उधार देना]; borrow [उधार लेना], as in "Can I borrow your book?"

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
Britains towns were given a new and elegant appearance between 1700 and 1830. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: Possession is shown with an apostrophe + s ('s). The towns belong to Britain, so "Britains towns" must be "Britain's towns".
So the error is in "Britains".

Correct sentence:
Britain's towns were given a new and elegant appearance between 1700 and 1830.

Note: when two adjectives describe the same noun, the article is used only once, as in "a new and elegant appearance".

question.en:
The following sentence has been divided into three parts. Identify the part which contains a grammatical error (ignore any punctuation errors, if any). If there is no error in the sentence, then select 'No Error'.
(A) The investigation revealed that the culprit, / (B) rather than being remorseful, was insolent enough / (C) to have been taunted the victims during the trial. / (D) No Error [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The investigation revealed that the culprit

2.en: rather than being remorseful, was insolent enough

3.en: to have been taunted the victims during the trial

solution.en:
Rule: "The victims" is the object of "taunt", so the active perfect infinitive (to have + V3) is needed. The passive "to have been taunted" cannot take an object here.
So the error is in part (C).

Correct sentence:
The investigation revealed that the culprit, rather than being remorseful, was insolent enough to have taunted the victims during the trial.

question.en:
The following sentence has been divided into three parts. Identify the part which contains a grammatical error (ignore any punctuation errors, if any). If there is no error in the sentence, then select 'No Error'.
(A) The strategy adopted by the administration / (B) is far superior than / (C) the one implemented by the previous committee. / (D) No Error [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The strategy adopted by the administration

3.en: the one implemented by the previous committee

solution.en:
Rule: Superior is a Latin comparative and takes "to", not "than". "Far" correctly strengthens the comparison.
So the error is in part (B).

Correct sentence:
The strategy adopted by the administration is far superior to the one implemented by the previous committee.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
While the algorithm claims objectivity (1)/, it inadvertently reify bias (2)/ embedded in its training data, (3)/ perpetuating systemic inequities across demographics. (4) [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: A singular subject takes a singular verb in the simple present (verb + s/es).

The subject of part (2) is "it" (the algorithm), which is singular, so "reify" must be "reifies".
Reify [अमूर्त को मूर्त/वास्तविक रूप देना] means to make something abstract appear concrete or real.

Correct sentence:
While the algorithm claims objectivity, it inadvertently reifies bias embedded in its training data, perpetuating systemic inequities across demographics.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Much of the guidelines (1)/ pertaining to AI governance (2)/ were based on speculative models (3)/ and industry projections. (4) [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: Much is used with uncountable nouns; many is used with plural countable nouns.

"Guidelines" is a plural countable noun, so "Much of the guidelines" must be "Many of the guidelines". The plural verb "were" then agrees correctly.

Correct sentence:
Many of the guidelines pertaining to AI governance were based on speculative models and industry projections.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
What troubled the evaluators most (1)/ was not the complexity of the argument (2)/ but that its logic (3)/ and conclusions were fundamentally flawed. (4) [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The correlative pair not … but … must join grammatically parallel elements.

Part (2) gives a noun phrase — "the complexity of the argument" — but part (3) begins a that-clause — "but that its logic …". This is faulty parallelism.
Part (3) should also begin with a noun phrase, e.g., "but the fact that its logic …".

Correct sentence:
What troubled the evaluators most was not the complexity of the argument but the fact that its logic and conclusions were fundamentally flawed.

question.en:
Spot the error in the below-given sentence.
"She can sings very well". [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: A modal verb (can, could, may, must, will, shall …) is always followed by the base form of the verb.

"can sings" is wrong; it should be "can sing".

Correct sentence:
She can sing very well.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
The people here have nothing. Their poverty's extreme. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error is poverty's; use poverty is.

Rule: The contraction 's after a noun is informal and can be read as a possessive (poverty's = of poverty). In a formal sentence, write the verb in full.

Correct sentence: The people here have nothing. Their poverty is extreme.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
The palace is heavily guarded, because inside it's walls sit the European leaders. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error is inside it's walls; use inside its walls.

Rule: It's means "it is/it has". The possessive form of "it" is its (without an apostrophe).

Correct sentence: The palace is heavily guarded, because inside its walls sit the European leaders.

question.en: Identify the incorrect sentence. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Mitali's hair is long and black.

2.en: Either of the alternatives seems to present major difficulties.

3.en: One of the cars in the garage is fifty years old.

4.en: Sharon has shared her devastating grief after the sudden death of her 57-year-old brother.

solution.en:
The sentence marked incorrect is "Either of the alternatives seems to present major difficulties."

Rule: Either means "one of two". When the number of choices is not limited to two, any of is used instead: "Any of the alternatives seems to present major difficulties."

Sentence 1 (hair takes a singular verb), sentence 3 (one of + plural noun + singular verb) and sentence 4 are correct.

question.en: Identify the incorrect sentence. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Beautiful furniture make the house elegant and looks sophisticated at the same time.

2.en: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) is thousands of years old and has changed little over the centuries.

3.en: Folktales can be used to help children develop strong reading skills, study other cultures, and discover a love of stories.

4.en: Clothing is expensive because of the financial shakeup it received during the COVID-19 pandemic.

solution.en:
The incorrect sentence is "Beautiful furniture make the house elegant and looks sophisticated at the same time."

Rule: Furniture is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb: makes. The two actions must also be parallel.

Correct sentence: Beautiful furniture makes the house elegant and sophisticated at the same time.

The other three sentences are grammatically correct.

question.en:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts, namely A, B, C and D, which are given in the alternatives. Select the alternative that contains the part of the sentence with an error.
The ancient ruins attract thousands of tourists every year who are fascinating by the rich history and culture of the place. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

2.en: of tourists every year who are

solution.en:
The error is in part C: fascinating by should be fascinated by.

Rule: The past participle (fascinated) describes how a person feels; the -ing form describes the thing that causes the feeling.

Correct sentence: The ancient ruins attract thousands of tourists every year who are fascinated by the rich history and culture of the place.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Fewer of the experimental designs (1)/ was compatible with the theoretical model (2)/ proposed by the research team (3)/ in their meta-analysis. (4) [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Part (2) has the error: was should be were.

Rule: Fewer of + plural noun is plural (fewer is used with countable plural nouns), so the verb must be plural.

Correct sentence: Fewer of the experimental designs were compatible with the theoretical model proposed by the research team in their meta-analysis.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
We don't have to go to the party, don't we? We can stay at home. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The error is "don't we".

Rule: A negative statement takes a positive question tag. "We don't have to go" is negative, so the tag must be "do we?"

Correct sentence: We don't have to go to the party, do we? We can stay at home.

question.en:
The sentence below has errors in two parts which are highlighted in bold. Identify the same.
The reef is on risk of (A) losing its coveted World Heritage Status on occasion of (B) ocean warming, fuelled by (C) climate change, which is damaging its health(D). [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The errors are in parts A and B.

A: "on risk of" → at risk of (fixed phrase meaning "in danger of").
B: "on occasion of" → on account of / because of; a cause is needed here, while "on the occasion of" means "at the time of an event".

Correct sentence: The reef is at risk of losing its coveted World Heritage Status on account of ocean warming, fuelled by climate change, which is damaging its health.

Parts C and D are correct, so the answer is BA.

question.en:
Identify the error in the below-given sentence.
"The police has arrested the suspect in the case". [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The error is "has".

Rule: Police is a collective noun always used in the plural, so it takes have. (Similarly: cattle, people, clergy.)

Correct sentence: The police have arrested the suspect in the case.

question.en:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts, namely A, B, C and D, which are given in the alternatives. Select the alternative that contains the part of the sentence with an error.
The insightful documentary explored the profound impact of social media on mental health between young adults globally today. [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Part (3) has the error: between should be among.

Rule: Between is used for two persons or things; among is used for more than two or a group. "Young adults globally" is a large group.

Correct sentence: The insightful documentary explored the profound impact of social media on mental health among young adults globally today.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
The news that the plane had crashed will be coming as a terrible shock. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error lies in part 3: will be coming.

Rule & Explanation: The future continuous tense ('will be coming') expresses an action in progress at a specific time in the future. However, receiving news and experiencing emotional shock occurs as a punctual event, not a continuous process. When stating the predictable effect of dramatic news, English uses the simple future: 'will come as a terrible shock' (or 'came as a terrible shock').

Correct sentence: The news that the plane had crashed will come as a terrible shock.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
The bank will be continued to transfer the interest to your account unless instructed otherwise. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error lies in part 2: will be continued.

Rule & Explanation: The subject 'The bank' is the active agent performing the action of transferring interest, not the recipient of the action. The passive construction 'will be continued to transfer' is grammatically incorrect. The verb must be in the active voice: 'will continue to transfer'.

Correct sentence: The bank will continue to transfer the interest to your account unless instructed otherwise.

question.en: Identify the incorrect sentence. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: She has got cold and cough.

2.en: Only a few people came to the party.

3.en: Could you lend me some of your books today?

4.en: He has more sense than you have.

solution.en:
The incorrect sentence is Option 1.

Rule & Explanation: In standard English idiom, the illnesses 'cold' and 'cough' are singular countable nouns that require indefinite articles: one catches or suffers from 'a cold' and 'a cough'. Thus, the correct idiomatic expression is 'She has got a cold and a cough'.
• Option 2 correctly uses 'a few' with countable 'people'.
• Option 3 correctly uses 'some' in a polite request expected to elicit an affirmative response.
• Option 4 correctly uses the comparative 'more sense than'.

question.en:
Identify the error in the below-given sentence.
"The government have decided to increase taxes". [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error is in have (Option 2).

Rule: In standard grammar (especially in standardized examination syntax), collective nouns like 'government', 'committee', or 'jury' acting as a unified singular entity take a singular verb ('has decided').

Correct sentence: The government has decided to increase taxes.

question.en:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts, namely A, B, C and D, which are given in the alternatives. Select the alternative that contains the part of the sentence with an error.
The antique grandfather clock in the hallway have not worked properly for over a decade now, which is a real shame for the family. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

3.en: properly for over a decade now,

4.en: which is a real shame for the family.

solution.en:
The error is in part 2: the hallway have not worked.

Subject-Verb Agreement Rule:
• Identify the true grammatical subject: 'The antique grandfather clock' (singular noun).
• The prepositional phrase 'in the hallway' simply modifies the clock and does not affect grammatical number.
• A singular subject takes the singular auxiliary verb has, not 'have'.

Correct sentence: The antique grandfather clock in the hallway has not worked properly for over a decade now...

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
He was imprisoned for many years, without many occasions, in both South Africa and India. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Error: “without many occasions” gives no sense. The intended idea is that he was jailed repeatedly, which is expressed as “on many occasions”.
Correct sentence: He was imprisoned for many years, on many occasions, in both South Africa and India.
“imprisoned for”, “many years” and “in both” are used correctly.

Therefore, without many occasions.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
The village is very isolated, their being no bus service. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Error: “their” is a possessive pronoun (their house). The sentence needs the adverb “there” in the absolute phrase “there being no bus service”.
Correct sentence: The village is very isolated, there being no bus service.
The other parts are grammatically correct.

Therefore, their being.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
It is a fact that there are most cars in Los Angeles than people. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Error: “most” is a superlative and cannot be followed by “than”. A comparison between cars and people needs the comparative “more”.
Correct sentence: It is a fact that there are more cars in Los Angeles than people.
“than people”, “a fact that” and “It is a fact” are correct.

Therefore, most cars.

question.en:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts, namely A, B, C and D, which are given in the alternatives. Select the alternative that contains the part of the sentence with an error.
Please provide a detailing explanation of the research methodology used in your recent scientific paper for clarification purposes requested by the board. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

2.en: of the research methodology used in

4.en: clarification purposes requested by the board.

solution.en:
Error: A noun (explanation) must be described by an adjective. “Detailing” is a verb form; the adjective is “detailed”.
Correct: Please provide a detailed explanation …
The other parts are correct.

Therefore, Please provide a detailing explanation.

question.en:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts, namely A, B, C and D, which are given in the alternatives. Select the alternative that contains the part of the sentence with an error.
Remember to brush your teeth thorough before you go to bed every single night without fail as instructed by the dentist. [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

2.en: thorough before you go to bed

solution.en:
Error: “brush” is a verb, so it must be modified by an adverb. “Thorough” is an adjective; the adverb is “thoroughly”.
Correct: Remember to brush your teeth thoroughly before you go to bed …
The other parts are correct.

Therefore, thorough before you go to bed.

question.en:
The following sentence has been divided into three parts. Identify the part which contains a grammatical error (ignore any punctuation errors, if any). If there is no error in the sentence, then select 'No Error'.
(A) Little did the CEO realise that the proposed restructuring / (B) would be met with such vehemence by the labour unions / (C) as to force a complete abandonment of the project. / (D) No Error [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: Little did the CEO realise that the proposed restructuring

2.en: would be met with such vehemence by the labour unions

3.en: as to force a complete abandonment of the project

solution.en:
Check each part
(A) “Little did the CEO realise …” – correct inversion after the negative adverb “little” (auxiliary “did” + subject + base verb).
(B) “would be met with such vehemence …” – correct passive with “would”.
(C) “as to force …” – correct, because “such … as to” expresses a result.
All parts are correct, so there is no error.

Therefore, No error.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
In Woolf's imaginary legacy (1)/, the room functions not just as sanctuary (2)/ but also as a discursive axis (3)/ where womanhood collapse into multiplicity. (4) [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Rule:** The subject **womanhood** is an uncountable singular noun and requires a singular verb (**collapses**) in the present simple tense.
**Correction:** "...where womanhood **collapses** into multiplicity."
Parts (1), (2), and (3) are grammatically sound.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Despite its ostensible neutrality (1)/, the bureaucratic apparatus (2)/ enact normative controls (3)/ that homogenize diverse expressions of identity. (4) [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Rule:** The subject **apparatus** is singular in this context and requires the singular present verb form **enacts**.
**Correction:** "...the bureaucratic apparatus **enacts** normative controls..."
The remaining clauses are constructed correctly.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Within postcolonial discourse (1)/, hybridity operate not as a passive amalgamation (2)/ but as a site of contestation (3)/ and negotiated subjectivity. (4) [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Rule:** The abstract noun **hybridity** is singular and must take the singular verb form **operates**.
**Correction:** "...hybridity **operates** not as a passive amalgamation..."
Parts (1), (3), and (4) contain no grammatical errors.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The researcher who the panel had nominated (1)/ for the ethics award (2)/ were present at the plenary session (3)/ but declined to speak. (4) [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Rule:** The head subject of the sentence is the singular noun **The researcher**, which demands the singular past verb **was** rather than the plural **were**.
**Correction:** "...**was** present at the plenary session..."
Parts (1), (2), and (4) are grammatically correct.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
None except the top-ranked researchers (1)/ has received invitations (2)/ for the closed-door summit (3)/ scheduled next quarter. (4) [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Rule:** When *none* refers to plural countable items (here, *researchers* governed by *except*), modern standard usage treats it as plural, taking **have received**, or creates an agreement mismatch.
**Correction:** "...**have received** invitations..."
Parts (1), (3), and (4) are grammatically well-formed.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The researchers insisted (1)/ on replacing the control group (2)/ by another cohort (3)/ with matched characteristics. (4) [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Rule:** The standard collocation for replacing one entity with an alternative is **replace X with Y** (not *replace by*).
**Correction:** "...**with** another cohort..."
Parts (1), (2), and (4) correctly handle standard verbs and phrases.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
You must to ensure that (1)/ all parameters are recorded (2)/ before the simulation (3)/ can be rerun. (4) [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Rule:** Modal auxiliary verbs such as **must** are followed directly by a bare infinitive without the particle *to*.
**Correction:** "You **must ensure** that..."
Parts (2), (3), and (4) are grammatically correct.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The narrator's resistance to patriarchal hermeneutics (1)/ are not simply polemical (2)/ but deeply embedded in the rhythm (3)/ and counterpoint of her syntax. (4) [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The error is in part (2): “are” should be “is”.

The subject is the singular noun “resistance” (to patriarchal hermeneutics); a singular subject takes a singular verb.

Correct sentence: The narrator's resistance to patriarchal hermeneutics is not simply polemical but deeply embedded in the rhythm and counterpoint of her syntax.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The philosopher's reluctance to endorse a universal ethic (1)/ stem from his conviction (2)/ that moral principles are always mediated (3)/ by cultural and historical particularities. (4) [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The error is in part (2): “stem” should be “stems”.

The subject is the singular “reluctance” (to endorse a universal ethic); a singular subject takes a singular verb.

Correct sentence: The philosopher's reluctance to endorse a universal ethic stems from his conviction that moral principles are always mediated by cultural and historical particularities.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Language, in its performative function, (1)/ shape the very ontology (2)/ of social relations and categories (3)/ that structure human perception. (4) [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The error is in part (2): “shape” should be “shapes”.

The subject is the singular “Language” (the phrase “in its performative function” is only a modifier); a singular subject takes a singular verb.

Correct sentence: Language, in its performative function, shapes the very ontology of social relations and categories that structure human perception.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Only in the final manuscript (1)/ did the theorist (2)/ acknowledges the limitations (3)/ of his earlier hypothesis. (4) [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The error is in part (3): “acknowledges” should be “acknowledge”.

The auxiliary “did” (inversion after “Only in the final manuscript”) already carries the past tense, so the main verb must be the base form.

Correct sentence: Only in the final manuscript did the theorist acknowledge the limitations of his earlier hypothesis.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The philosopher's idea (1)/ that reality is constructed through language, (2)/ was refuted not by logic (3)/ but emotion and intuition. (4) [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The error is in part (4): the correlative “not by logic ... but” must be completed with “by”, i.e. “but by emotion and intuition”.

The second limb of “not ... but” must repeat the preposition “by” for parallelism.

Correct sentence: The philosopher's idea that reality is constructed through language was refuted not by logic but by emotion and intuition.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Not only each participant's response (1)/ but also his metadata (2)/ was collected (3)/ and cross-validated. (4) [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule
“Not only … but also …” agrees with the second subject. Here the second subject is “his metadata”, which is treated as plural in this item, so the verb must be “were”.

Explicit changes
“their” in part (2) is replaced by “his”, which agrees with the singular “each participant’s” reference, so part (2) is no longer an error.
“was collected” (part 3) should be “were collected”.

Final sentence
Not only each participant’s response but also his metadata were collected and cross-validated.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

solution.en:

Training data is cleaned and normalized to ensure consistency. Feature selection is guided by domain knowledge and statistical relevance. 4. Discounted prices attract large crowds. [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Sequence:** Sentence 3 introduces the event and exhibitors (**The Delhi Book Fair features national and international publishers**).
Sentence 2 describes attendees exploring offerings (**Readers browse the latest titles**).
Sentence 4 explains the attraction factor (**Discounted prices attract large crowds**).
Sentence 1 mentions supplementary cultural activities held concurrently (**Workshops and author sessions are held alongside**).
**Order:** 3, 2, 4, 1.

question.en:

question.en:
Read the passage and answer the question:
Sleep is a vital biological process that restores the body and mind. However, for millions of people worldwide, this natural rhythm is disrupted by sleep disorders. These conditions can range from insomnia, where (4) person struggles to fall or stay asleep, to sleep apnea, a potentially serious condition where breathing repeatedly stops and starts during sleep.
Chronic sleep problems (3) have far-reaching consequences. They impair concentration, weaken the immune system, and increase the risk of conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, and depression. The cumulative effect of poor sleep over time can be as harmful as a poor diet or lack of exercise.
Causes of sleep disorders vary (5). Stress, irregular schedules, excessive screen time before bed, and underlying medical conditions are common triggers. Modern lifestyles, with their relentless pace and constant connectivity, have only worsened the problem.
Treatment depends on the underlying cause. For some, improving (1) sleep hygiene such as maintaining a regular sleep schedule, limiting caffeine, and creating a calm bedtime routine can make a significant difference. In more severe cases, medical intervention or therapy may be necessary.
Ultimately, addressing sleep disorders is not just about avoiding fatigue; it's about protecting overall health and ensuring that the body's (2) restorative processes function as they should.

Question: The word "restorative" in the passage is closest in meaning to: [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Restorative [पुनः स्वस्थ करने वाला, नवीनीकरण करने वाला] means able to bring back health, strength or freshness. The passage says sleep “restores the body and mind”, so the body’s restorative processes are its healing or renewing processes.

[नींद के दौरान शरीर की वे प्रक्रियाएँ जो थकान दूर करके उसे फिर से स्वस्थ और तरोताज़ा करती हैं।]

Damaging — causing harm [हानिकारक]
Healing or renewing — making healthy or fresh again [उपचार या नवीनीकरण करने वाला]
Weakening — making weaker [कमज़ोर करने वाला]
Boring — dull [उबाऊ]

Simple alternatives for restorative here: refreshing, rejuvenating, curative.

Select the correct modal verb for blank (3) in the cloze passage:
"Chronic sleep problems (3) have far-reaching consequences." [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Can expresses general possibility or capacity: chronic sleep problems are capable of causing serious effects.

“Chronic sleep problems can have far-reaching consequences.”
[लंबे समय तक चलने वाली नींद की समस्याओं के दूरगामी परिणाम हो सकते हैं।]

Will — certainty about the future [निश्चित रूप से होगा]

The next sentences state the effects as known facts, so the general-possibility modal fits best.

"These conditions can range from insomnia, where (4) person struggles to fall or stay asleep..." [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Use a.

“Person” is a singular countable noun beginning with a consonant sound, and it refers to any person in general, not a particular one.

“…insomnia, where a person struggles to fall or stay asleep.”
[अनिद्रा, जिसमें व्यक्ति को सोने या नींद बनाए रखने में कठिनाई होती है।]

“An” is used before a vowel sound, and “the” would point to a specific person already known.

solution.en:
Widely [व्यापक रूप से] means over a wide range. The next sentence lists many different causes, so the causes “vary widely”.

[नींद संबंधी विकारों के कारण बहुत अलग-अलग होते हैं।]

Read the cloze passage and answer the question:
Swimming is one of the most popular recreational and competitive activities worldwide, valued for both its fitness benefits and its ability to provide relaxation. Unlike many forms of exercise, swimming is (1) low-impact, making it ideal for people of all ages and fitness levels. The buoyancy of water supports the body, reducing strain on joints while still (3) resistance to build muscle strength and endurance.
Beyond its physical advantages, swimming is also a valuable life skill. Knowing how to swim can be (2) "life-saving" in emergencies and helps individuals enjoy other water-based activities such as boating, diving, and surfing. Competitive swimming, on the other hand, demands rigorous training, discipline, and excellent technique.
Different strokes-freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, and butterfly-engage various muscle groups and require distinct breathing patterns. Regular swimming improves cardiovascular health, increases lung capacity, and promotes overall well-being. It's also an effective way to reduce stress, as the rhythmic movements and sensation of being in water can have a calming effect on the mind.
However, safety is crucial. Swimmers should always be aware of (4) environment, whether in pools, lakes, or the ocean, and follow proper safety guidelines. Learning under supervision (5) using appropriate gear ensures a safe and enjoyable experience.

Question: In the passage, what does "low-impact" most nearly mean? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

2.en: Causing minimal stress or strain on the body

solution.en:
Low-impact [शरीर पर कम दबाव डालने वाला] describes exercise that puts little stress on the joints and bones. The passage adds that buoyancy reduces strain on joints, so it means causing minimal stress or strain on the body.

[तैराकी में जोड़ों पर बहुत कम दबाव पड़ता है।]

It does not mean ineffective or boring: the same passage says swimming builds strength and endurance.

solution.en:
Use providing.

“While still providing resistance” is a participle phrase parallel to “reducing strain”; after “while”, the -ing form shows an action happening at the same time.

[पानी का उत्प्लावन शरीर को सहारा देता है, जोड़ों पर दबाव घटाता है और साथ ही मांसपेशियों की ताकत बढ़ाने के लिए प्रतिरोध भी देता है।]

Provide / Provides — finite verbs; they would need a subject after “while” [प्रदान करना]
Provided — past participle, or “on condition that” [प्रदान किया गया / यदि]
Providing — present participle showing a simultaneous action [प्रदान करते हुए]

question.en:
In the given passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage intently and choose the most appropriate option to fill in each blank:

Education is usually seen as the pillar of a successful society. It provides people with the necessary information and skills to advance their lives and serve their communities. Apart from studies, education develops critical thinking and (1)______ making people analyse issues and make sound decisions.
One of the difficulties with education today is achieving equal access for everyone. Socioeconomic inequality tends to form obstacles, leaving disadvantaged groups lacking resources. To address this, investment must be made in infrastructure and (2)______ policies that are focused on inclusivity.
Technology has also revolutionized education, and learning has become more accessible with the help of online platforms. This change brings concerns regarding the (3)______ of typical classroom experiences, which focus on direct interaction and collaboration.
Finally, learning is not simply the process of gaining knowledge; it's about the molding of values and instilling a sense of (4)______ and (5)______.
By giving equal weight to academic success and social responsibility, societies can build a future that is both innovative and (5)______.

What should come in the place of blank number 1? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Creativity [रचनात्मकता] completes the pair of thinking skills that education develops along with critical thinking: thinking critically and creatively helps people analyse issues from fresh angles and make sound decisions.

[शिक्षा आलोचनात्मक सोच के साथ रचनात्मकता भी विकसित करती है, जिससे लोग मुद्दों का विश्लेषण कर सही निर्णय ले पाते हैं।]

Memory — the ability to retain and recall information [स्मरण-शक्ति]; merely recalling facts does not by itself make people analyse issues
Creativity — the ability to produce new ideas [रचनात्मकता]
Physical strength — bodily power [शारीरिक शक्ति]
Athletic ability — skill in sports [खेल-कौशल]

“Critical thinking and creativity” is the natural pair of mental skills; physical strength and athletic ability have nothing to do with analysing issues.

By giving equal weight to academic success and social responsibility, societies can build a future that is both innovative and (5)______.

What should come in the place of blank number 4? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Responsibility [उत्तरदायित्व] fits. The next sentence speaks of giving weight to “social responsibility”, so education should instil a sense of responsibility.

[शिक्षा मूल्यों को गढ़ती है और उत्तरदायित्व की भावना जगाती है।]

Competition — rivalry [प्रतिस्पर्धा]
Responsibility — a sense of duty [उत्तरदायित्व]
Ambition — a strong desire to succeed [महत्वाकांक्षा]
Self-Interest — concern for one’s own advantage [स्वार्थ]

“Values” and “social responsibility” rule out self-centred choices.

Unlike traditional text-only books, they tell a complete story using comic-strip formats, illustrations, and dialogue bubbles. This unique blend makes reading highly engaging and easier to understand, especially for students who find long blocks of text (1)______. It also helps capture their attention for longer than text-only books do. Graphic novels gained popularity because of their ability to (2)______ rather than just tell. A single drawing can instantly express deep emotions, set a mysterious mood, or showcase a complex action scene that might otherwise take pages to describe. Furthermore, graphic novels are not just for children; they tackle serious, mature themes like history, mental health, and social justice. What should come in blank 1? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Intimidating [डराने वाला, भयभीत करने वाला] fits: some students find long blocks of text daunting, which is why graphic novels make reading easier for them.

Intimidating — frightening or overwhelming [भयभीत करने वाला]
Exciting — causing eager enthusiasm [रोमांचक]
Interesting — holding attention [रोचक]
Transforming — changing completely [रूपांतरित करने वाला]

Only a negative feeling explains why these students need an easier format.

In the given passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage intently and choose the most appropriate option to fill in each blank:

In a time characterized by deep ideological divides and epistemic uncertainty, the role of intellectuals has become increasingly (1)______. No longer confined to the ivory towers of academia, public thinkers are now thrust into digital arenas, where their ideas are subjected to the volatile currents of public sentiment and algorithmic amplification. This (2)______ from cloistered contemplation to performative intellectualism has raised concerns about the erosion of nuanced debate in favor of ideological branding.

The commodification of knowledge production, particularly within neoliberal structures, has reoriented scholarship toward metrics of visibility rather than depth. Consequently, the pursuit of truth is often (3)______ by the need for marketability, leaving complex ideas diluted to conform to audience expectations. Amid this shift, academic institutions themselves have become entangled in bureaucratic inertia, frequently adopting managerial logics that prioritize efficiency over (4)______.

To counter this drift, there must be a recommitment to critical inquiry as a mode of civic responsibility. Intellectual labor must resist assimilation into spectacle and instead cultivate spaces for deliberation that are both inclusive and rigorous. Only by embracing such an ethic of care can the academy preserve its (5)______ in shaping public reason.

solution.en:
Contested [विवादित] fits blank 1. The passage begins with "deep ideological divides and epistemic uncertainty", so the role of intellectuals has become a matter of dispute.

Option meanings
Unequivocal — clear, leaving no doubt [असंदिग्ध]
Contested — disputed, argued over [विवादित]
Triumphant — victorious [विजयी]
Peripheral — of minor importance, on the edge [गौण, परिधीय]

question.en:
In the given passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage intently and choose the most appropriate option to fill in each blank:

A plethora of cognitive and affective factors shape the intricate process of human decision-making. Even though we often believe that our choices are rationalized entirely, studies have shown that heuristics—or implicit bias and mental shortcuts—play a significant role. For example, the (1)________ effect leads people to put great weight on the first bit of information they gather, even if it is irrelevant. This can mislead judgment and result in faulty conclusions.

Another usual bias is (2)________, in which individuals search for information that validates their current assumptions while overlooking opposing evidence. This trend perpetuates stereotypes and might inhibit critical thinking. Emotional states also influence choices; an anxious person might become more cautious, while someone who is euphoric might take (3)________ risks.

In addition, social pressures must not be ignored. The need to follow group norms, referred to as (4)________, can cause people to make decisions they would not otherwise make. This is particularly clear in high-stress situations such as corporate boardrooms or political campaigns.

Knowing these psychological processes is critical to enhancing decision-making. Through increased awareness of our own biases and the ability to challenge our assumptions, we can make more (5)________ decisions that balance logic with empathy.

What should come in the place of blank number 1? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Anchoring [आरंभिक जानकारी पर अत्यधिक निर्भरता] fits: the anchoring effect is the tendency to rely too heavily on the first piece of information received.
The passage says the effect "leads people to put great weight on the first bit of information they gather, even if it is irrelevant".

Option meanings
Anchoring — over-reliance on the first information received [प्रथम सूचना पर टिक जाना]
Confirmation bias — seeking only information that supports one's beliefs [पुष्टि पूर्वाग्रह]
Availability bias — judging by examples that come easily to mind [उपलब्धता पूर्वाग्रह]
Overconfidence bias — overestimating one's own ability or knowledge [अति-आत्मविश्वास पूर्वाग्रह]

question.en:
Read the cloze passage and answer the following questions:

Millets, a group of small-seeded grains, ______(3) for thousands of years in India and other parts of Asia and Africa. Once considered the “poor man’s food,” they are now gaining recognition for their (1) nutritional value and environmental benefits. Rich in fibre, protein, vitamins, and minerals, millets are a powerhouse of health, aiding digestion, improving heart health, and helping regulate blood sugar levels.

Unlike rice and wheat, millets require far less water to grow and can thrive in arid and semi-arid regions. This makes them not only a healthy choice but also a (2) sustainable one, particularly important in the face of climate change and depleting water resources.

There are _____(4) varieties of millets, including finger millet (ragi), pearl millet (bajra), and foxtail millet, each with its unique taste and health benefits. These grains can be used in a wide range of dishes from traditional rotis and porridges to modern snacks and desserts.

Despite their benefits, millets had fallen out of favour for decades due to changing food preferences and the dominance of rice and wheat in markets. However, with increasing health awareness ______(5) government campaigns, they are making a comeback on urban menus and in packaged food products.

In the passage, what does “nutritional” most nearly mean? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

3.en: Related to value of food for health

solution.en:
Nutritional [पोषण संबंधी] means relating to the value of food for health and growth.
The passage supports this: millets are "rich in fibre, protein, vitamins, and minerals" and "a powerhouse of health".

Option meanings
Related to flavor — about taste [स्वाद से संबंधित]
Related to cooking speed — about how fast food cooks [पकने की गति से संबंधित]
Related to value of food for health — nutritional [पोषण संबंधी]
Related to farming — agricultural [कृषि संबंधी]

Rich in fibre, protein, vitamins, and minerals, millets are a powerhouse of health, aiding digestion, improving heart health, and helping regulate blood sugar levels.

Choose the correct auxiliary verb and main verb: (3) [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: An action that began in the past and continues up to now, with "for thousands of years", takes the present perfect. The subject "Millets" is plural and the grains are grown by people, so the passive have been + V3 is needed.

Correct sentence:
Millets, a group of small-seeded grains, have been cultivated for thousands of years in India and other parts of Asia and Africa.

"Has been cultivated" is singular, "Having cultivated" is not a finite verb, and "Had cultivated" is active and places the action entirely in the past.

question.en:
Fill numbered blank with the most appropriate word to complete the passage.

Inland Waterways Development: India is promoting inland water transport to decongest roads and railways while reducing transportation costs. The Jal Marg Vikas Project focuses on the National Waterway-1 along the Ganga between Haldia and Varanasi. Modern terminals are being built, and mechanised vessels are encouraged. The project aims to shift a portion of cargo movement from road to river, which is more (1)______ friendly. Skill development programmes are training local youth as (2)______ operators. By easing traffic congestion, the project can reduce (3)______ costs and carbon emissions. The success of this initiative relies on maintaining adequate river (4)______ for navigation. Ultimately, improving inland waterways can make freight transport more sustainable and (5)______.

Fill (1) numbered blank with the most appropriate word to complete the passage. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Environmentally friendly [पर्यावरण-अनुकूल] means causing little harm to the environment. River transport uses less fuel and causes less pollution than road transport, and the passage later mentions reducing carbon emissions.

Option meanings
Economically — in terms of money [आर्थिक रूप से]
Environmentally — in terms of the environment [पर्यावरण की दृष्टि से]
Politically — in terms of politics [राजनीतिक रूप से]
Socially — in terms of society [सामाजिक रूप से]

"Economically friendly", "politically friendly" and "socially friendly" are not standard collocations.

In the following question, some of the words in the passage have been left out. Read the passage carefully and choose the correct answer to each question out of the four alternatives and fill in the blanks.

Aeroplane mode is a built-in smartphone feature that (1)______ all cellular, wireless, and Bluetooth signals. When passengers leave their cellular devices active during air travel, these devices continuously scan for network connections at full intensity. This intense scanning emits strong electromagnetic interference that can (2)______ the aircraft's critical communication and navigation systems. Pilots frequently report hearing a distinct buzzing sound in their headsets. This sound may affect the clarity of communication during (3)______ flight phases, when pilots rely heavily on instructions from the ground support team. These sounds can mask urgent radio commands from air traffic control. Moreover, cumulative signals from dozens of active devices can compromise the accuracy of flight deck instruments, such as altimeters and radar. While modern aircraft are engineered with advanced (4)______, the potential for technology to fail under unexpected signal interference remains a reality. Compliance with aeroplane mode is not something to be taken lightly by the passengers. It is a vital safety (5)______ that ensures pilots maintain a clear, uninterrupted line of communication with ground support, ensuring a safe journey for everyone on board.

What should come in blank 1? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Aeroplane mode switches off all signals, so it disconnects [संपर्क काट देता है] all cellular, wireless and Bluetooth signals.

Amplifies — makes stronger [बढ़ाता है]
Broadway — a street and theatre district in New York; meaningless here
Maintains — keeps going [बनाए रखता है]

Amplifies and maintains give the opposite meaning.

Aeroplane mode is a built-in smartphone feature that (1)______ all cellular, wireless, and Bluetooth signals. When passengers leave their cellular devices active during air travel, these devices continuously scan for network connections at full intensity. This intense scanning emits strong electromagnetic interference that can (2)______ the aircraft's critical communication and navigation systems. Pilots frequently report hearing a distinct buzzing sound in their headsets. This sound may affect the clarity of communication during (3)______ flight phases, when pilots rely heavily on instructions from the ground support team. These sounds can mask urgent radio commands from air traffic control. Moreover, cumulative signals from dozens of active devices can compromise the accuracy of flight deck instruments, such as altimeters and radar. While modern aircraft are engineered with advanced (4)______, the potential for technology to fail under unexpected signal interference remains a reality. Compliance with aeroplane mode is not something to be taken lightly by the passengers. It is a vital safety (5)______ that ensures pilots maintain a clear, uninterrupted line of communication with ground support, ensuring a safe journey for everyone on board.

What should come in blank 3? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
The flight phases in which pilots "rely heavily on instructions from the ground support team" (such as take-off and landing) are crucial [अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण].

Option meanings
Trivial — unimportant [तुच्छ]
Leisurely — relaxed, unhurried [आरामदायक]
Crucial — extremely important [अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण]
Predictable — expected [पूर्वानुमेय]

question.en:
In the following question, some of the words in the passage have been left out. Read the passage carefully and choose the correct answer to each question out of the four alternatives and fill in the blanks.

Scribes were highly respected, elite intellectuals in ancient Egypt who served as the (1)______ of the entire civilisation's administration. In a society where the vast majority of people could not read or write, scribes spent years in specialised temple schools mastering hieroglyphs-the complex picture-writing system-and hieratic script, a quicker cursive form used for daily business. It is because of their rare and (2)______ skills that the scribes held immense social power and were exempt from paying taxes, performing forced labour, or serving in the military. Their daily tasks included recording grain harvests, calculating taxes, writing legal documents, and (3)______ military victories. They also copied sacred religious spells onto papyrus rolls, which were buried inside tombs to guide the dead. Scribes used wooden (4)______ holding black and red ink cakes, writing with brushes made from reeds. Ultimately, they were the keepers of history; without their (5)______ record-keeping, much of our knowledge about ancient Egypt would be entirely lost.

What should come in blank 1? [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The answer is Backbone [रीढ़, मुख्य आधार]: scribes were the main support of Egypt's administration.

[हिंदी: लेखक (scribes) पूरी सभ्यता के प्रशासन की रीढ़ थे।]

Option meanings
Backbone — the main support [मुख्य आधार]
Obstacle — a hindrance [बाधा]
Margin — an edge [किनारा]
Bounty — a reward [इनाम]

The passage presents scribes as essential, so only "backbone" fits.

In the following question, some of the words in the passage have been left out. Read the passage carefully and choose the correct answer to each question out of the four alternatives and fill in the blanks.

An education loan, or student loan, is the amount of money borrowed by a student from a bank, specifically to pay for (1)______ education. It helps them to cover tuition fees, books, laptops, and living expenses at national or international universities. The process of how they work is (2)______. First, you apply to a lender by providing proof of college admission, a co-applicant (usually a parent), and (3)______ if borrowing a large amount. Once approved, the bank pays the money directly to your college each semester. The biggest advantage is the moratorium period, which is a repayment holiday. Lenders do not force you to repay the loan while you are still studying. Instead, repayment begins six months to a year after graduation, giving you time to secure a (4)______. Once this grace period ends, you repay the total borrowed amount plus interest through (5)______ monthly payments over several years. Knowing these terms and conditions helps you to choose a loan with competitive interest rates and flexible repayment schedules, preventing heavy financial stress at the outset of your career.

What should come in Blank 1? [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The answer is Higher [उच्च]: education loans pay for university-level (higher) education.

[हिंदी: शिक्षा ऋण विशेष रूप से उच्च शिक्षा का खर्च उठाने के लिए लिया जाता है।]

Option meanings
Higher — college/university level [उच्च]
Primary — first stage of schooling [प्राथमिक]
Basic — elementary [बुनियादी]
General — not specialised [सामान्य]

The passage mentions universities, so "higher" fits.

question.en:
Read the cloze passage and answer the following questions:

The life of a writer is often romanticized as a journey (3) inspiration, creativity, and quiet reflection. While moments of artistic brilliance do exist, the reality is far more (1) arduous than it appears. Writers spend countless hours drafting, revising, and battling self-doubt. The blank page can be both an open canvas and an intimidating void, demanding discipline as much as imagination.

A writer's routine (4) greatly. Some work in the early hours of the morning, when the world is still, while others find their rhythm late at night. Many rely on rituals such as a specific desk, a cup of tea, or a walk in the park to spark their creativity. However, inspiration alone is rarely enough; persistence is the real driving force behind completed works.

The profession also comes with emotional highs and lows. The joy of finishing a manuscript or receiving praise from readers is often tempered by the sting of rejection letters or critical reviews. Still, writers persevere, fuelled by the belief that (5) words can inform, entertain, or even change lives.

For many, writing is not merely a career but (2) a calling a lifelong pursuit that shapes the way they see and interact with the world. It is a path that demands patience, resilience, and an unwavering commitment to the craft.

In the passage, what does "arduous" most nearly mean? [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Arduous [कठिन, श्रमसाध्य] means difficult and requiring great effort. The passage supports this: writers spend "countless hours drafting, revising, and battling self-doubt".

Option meanings
Easy and quick — opposite [आसान और शीघ्र]
Difficult and requiring great effort — correct [कठिन और परिश्रमपूर्ण]
Boring and repetitive — wrong [उबाऊ और दोहराव वाला]
Short and simple — wrong [छोटा और सरल]

Related words: Arduous: strenuous, gruelling, laborious.

The life of a writer is often romanticized as a journey (3) inspiration, creativity, and quiet reflection. While moments of artistic brilliance do exist, the reality is far more (1) arduous than it appears. Writers spend countless hours drafting, revising, and battling self-doubt. The blank page can be both an open canvas and an intimidating void, demanding discipline as much as imagination.

A writer's routine (4) greatly. Some work in the early hours of the morning, when the world is still, while others find their rhythm late at night. Many rely on rituals such as a specific desk, a cup of tea, or a walk in the park to spark their creativity. However, inspiration alone is rarely enough; persistence is the real driving force behind completed works.

The profession also comes with emotional highs and lows. The joy of finishing a manuscript or receiving praise from readers is often tempered by the sting of rejection letters or critical reviews. Still, writers persevere, fuelled by the belief that (5) words can inform, entertain, or even change lives.

For many, writing is not merely a career but (2) a calling a lifelong pursuit that shapes the way they see and interact with the world. It is a path that demands patience, resilience, and an unwavering commitment to the craft.

Choose the correct verb form: (4) [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The subject "A writer's routine" is singular and the passage is in the simple present, so the verb is varies.

Correct sentence: A writer's routine varies greatly.

question.en:
Read the cloze passage and answer the following questions:

Journalism is often called the fourth pillar of democracy, alongside the legislature, executive, and judiciary. Its primary role is to inform the public, (1) scrutinize those in power, and ensure that citizens can make informed decisions. A free and responsible press serves as a watchdog, exposing corruption, amplifying marginalized voices, and holding institutions accountable.

However, this role is neither simple nor without challenges. Journalists frequently operate under intense pressure, balancing the need for (2) objectivity with the realities of deadlines, editorial bias, and, in some cases, censorship. In countries with restricted press freedom, the pursuit of truth can even put reporters' lives at risk.

The rise of digital media has transformed (3), making information more accessible but also creating new problems like misinformation and "fake news." In such an environment, the credibility of journalists depends heavily on rigorous fact-checking and ethical reporting standards.

A vibrant and independent press (4) essential to the health of any democracy. Without it, power can go unchecked, public debate may wither, and citizens risk being left in the dark. Journalism is not merely a profession; it is a civic responsibility that (5) the very foundation of democratic life.

The word "scrutinize" in the passage is closest in meaning to: [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Scrutinize [बारीकी से जाँचना] means to examine closely; the press closely examines the actions of those in power.

Option meanings
Ignore — pay no attention [अनदेखा करना]
Announce publicly — declare openly [सार्वजनिक घोषणा करना]
Approve quickly — sanction at once [शीघ्र स्वीकृति देना]
Examine closely — correct [बारीकी से जाँचना]

Related words: Scrutinize: inspect, probe, analyse.

solution.en:
Objectivity [निष्पक्षता, वस्तुनिष्ठता] means being impartial and fair, not influenced by personal feelings — which journalists must balance against deadlines and bias.

Option meanings
Personal opinion — opposite [व्यक्तिगत राय]
Impartiality and fairness — correct [निष्पक्षता और न्याय]
Harsh criticism — wrong [कठोर आलोचना]
Legal authority — wrong [कानूनी अधिकार]

Related words: Objectivity: neutrality, detachment, even-handedness.
