question.en:
Read the cloze passage and answer the following questions:
South India, known for its tropical climate, (3) heavy rainfall during both the southwest and northeast monsoons. While rain is essential for agriculture and replenishing water sources, excessive downpours can cause widespread disruption. Cities like Chennai, Kochi, and Bengaluru often face flooding, traffic standstills, and an interruption to daily life during intense monsoon spells.

One major consequence of heavy rainfall is waterlogging, which damages roads, slows transportation, and increases the risk of accidents. (1) Prolonged wet conditions can also lead to the spread of waterborne diseases. Rural areas face (4) own challenges, with farmlands getting inundated, affecting crops and the livelihoods of farmers.

The (2) infrastructure in many urban centres is not adequately prepared to handle sudden and intense showers. Poor drainage systems, encroachment on waterways, and unplanned construction exacerbate the problem. Authorities often resort to emergency measures such as pumping out water, diverting traffic, and issuing weather advisories.

While heavy rainfall is a natural part of South India’s climate, climate change is making weather patterns more unpredictable. This has led to both unusually intense rains and prolonged dry spells in some years. Effective urban planning, investment in drainage infrastructure, and community awareness are (5) to mitigating the impact of these events.

In the passage, the opposite of "prolonged" is: [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Prolonged [लंबे समय तक चलने वाला, दीर्घकालिक] means continuing for a long time or extended in duration. The antonym is Brief [संक्षिप्त, अल्पकालिक].

Option meanings
• Extended — lengthened in duration (synonym) [विस्तारित]
• Lengthy — long, protracted (synonym) [लंबा]
• Brief — lasting only for a short period of time (antonym) [संक्षिप्त]
• Delay — to make late; a noun/verb [देरी]

Related words: Prolonged: protracted, sustained, chronic, long-drawn-out.

4.en: Basic physical systems and facilities needed for a society

solution.en:
Infrastructure [बुनियादी ढाँचा, अवसंरचना] refers to the foundational physical and organizational systems, facilities, and networks (such as roads, bridges, drainage systems, water supply, and electrical grids) necessary for the operation of a community or enterprise.

Option Analysis:
• Option 4 ('Basic physical systems and facilities needed for a society') provides the precise, standard definition.
• The context of the passage specifically mentions drainage systems, waterways, and urban planning, confirming physical civic structures.

Select the correct verb form for blank (3) in the cloze passage:
"South India, known for its tropical climate, (3) heavy rainfall during both the southwest and northeast monsoons." [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Subject-Verb Agreement Rule:
• The subject is the singular geographical proper noun 'South India' (the appositive phrase 'known for its tropical climate' is set off by commas and does not change the subject number).
• A singular subject in the simple present tense (stating a recurring climatic fact) requires a third-person singular verb ending in -s: experiences.

Complete sentence: South India, known for its tropical climate, experiences heavy rainfall...

"Effective urban planning, investment in drainage infrastructure, and community awareness are (5) to mitigating the impact of these events." [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Grammatical Category Rule:
• In the predicate construction 'Subject + linking verb (are) + Predicate Adjective + prepositional phrase', a predicate adjective is required to describe the compound subject.
• Crucial [अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण, अनिवार्य] is the adjective.
• 'Crucially' is an adverb, while 'cruciality' and 'crucialness' are awkward noun forms.

Complete sentence: ...community awareness are crucial to mitigating the impact of these events.

question.en:
Read the cloze passage and answer the following questions:
Meditation is an ancient practice that (3) mental clarity, emotional stability, and overall well-being. Rooted in spiritual traditions, it has evolved into a widely recognized method for reducing stress and improving focus. By sitting quietly and focusing on the breath, a mantra, or simply observing thoughts without judgment, individuals can achieve (1) a state of deep tranquillity.

Modern science supports the benefits of meditation, linking it to reduced anxiety, lower blood pressure, and enhanced (2) cognitive function. It helps train the mind to stay present, countering the constant distractions of modern life. Many people incorporate it into their daily routines as a way to restore mental energy and improve decision-making.

However, developing a consistent meditation habit (4) be challenging. Beginners often struggle with restlessness or impatience, expecting instant results. Like any skill, meditation requires practice, patience, and persistence to experience its full benefits.

From Buddhist monasteries to corporate wellness programs, meditation is now practiced in diverse settings. It bridges ancient wisdom with modern lifestyle needs, (5) it a timeless tool for inner peace in a fast-paced world.

The phrase "state of deep tranquility" most nearly means: [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Tranquility [परम शांति, स्थिरता] denotes the state or quality of being serene, calm, and free from disturbance or mental agitation. Hence, a 'state of deep tranquility' means a period of extreme calmness.

Option meanings
• Moment of excitement — a period of high emotional arousal [उत्तेजना का क्षण]
• Period of extreme calmness — a state of profound peace and serenity [गहरी शांति की अवस्था]
• Phase of confusion — a period of perplexity or disorientation [भ्रम की स्थिति]
• Feeling of tiredness — physical exhaustion or fatigue [थकान की भावना]

Contextual Vocabulary & Agreement:

• 'Disrupts' (disturbs), 'neglects' (ignores), and 'diminishes' (reduces) express negative meanings contrary to the passage.

Complete sentence: Meditation is an ancient practice that promotes mental clarity...

"However, developing a consistent meditation habit (4) be challenging." [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Modal of Theoretical Possibility:
• The modal verb can is used to express general, theoretical possibility or potential difficulty (can be challenging) [चुनौतीपूर्ण हो सकता है].

question.en:
In the following question, some of the words in the passage have been left out. Read the passage carefully and choose the correct answer to each question out of the four alternatives and fill in the blanks.

The REM (Rapid Eye Movement) cycle is a sleep stage (1)______ by rapid eye movements, low muscle tone throughout the body, and vivid dreaming. It is a deeply fascinating stage of our sleep that plays a (2)______ role in brain development and mental health. During a normal night, our body cycles through different sleep stages every ninety minutes. REM sleep is the final stage of this cycle, occurring mostly in the early morning hours. It gets its name because our eyes rapidly dart back and forth behind our closed eyelids, signalling (3)______ brain activity. To protect us from physically acting out these wild dreams and hurting ourselves, our brain temporarily (4)______ our major muscles. This temporary lockdown is called muscle atonia. Neurologists view the REM cycle as the brain's ultimate overnight cleanup crew; it (5)______ our daily emotions, sharpens our memory, and stores everything we learned during the day.

What should come in blank 1? [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Blank 1: “a sleep stage ______ by rapid eye movements, low muscle tone … and vivid dreaming.”
The features listed are what mark or define this stage – “characterised by”.
Simplified, Criticised and Threatened do not fit “a stage … by its features”.

Therefore, Characterised.

What should come in blank 2? [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Blank 2: “plays a ______ role in brain development and mental health.”
The passage calls REM “deeply fascinating” and the brain's “cleanup crew”, so its role is very important – “crucial”.
Minor and Optional contradict the passage; Sudden does not describe a role.

Therefore, Crucial.

In the following question, some of the words in the passage have been left out. Read the passage carefully and choose the correct answer to each question out of the four alternatives and fill in the blanks.

Sowa-Rigpa, literally means the "Knowledge of Healing". It is one of the world's oldest and best-documented traditional medical systems, (1)______ practised in Tibet and the Himalayan regions of India, Bhutan, Nepal, and Mongolia. Its practitioners are traditionally known as Amchis. Similar to Ayurveda, Sowa-Rigpa is built on the (2)______ that everything in the universe, including the human body, is made of five basic elements: Earth, Water, Fire, Wind, and Space. In the body, these elements form three primary internal energies that (3)______ respiration, metabolism, and fluid balance. When these energies are perfectly balanced, a person enjoys good health; an (4)______ caused by a bad diet, stress, or seasonal changes leads to illness. To diagnose diseases, Amchis use highly (5)______ non-invasive methods such as checking a patient's pulse and analysing urine.

What should come in blank 1? [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Blank 1: “one of the world's oldest … medical systems, ______ practised in Tibet and the Himalayan regions …”
The regions listed are where the system is mainly followed – “primarily practised”.
Rarely, Accidentally and Secretly contradict its status as a well-documented, established system.

Therefore, Primarily.

question.en:
The architecture of modern policymaking increasingly reflects a shift from dialogic consensus to technocratic unilateralism. Public consultation, once a hallmark of democratic ethos, is now frequently (1) ______ by algorithmic forecasting and data-driven mandates. While such models brag precision, they risk sustaining systemic (2) ______ by embedding pre-existing prejudices into ostensibly neutral code. This evolution is further complicated by the political spectacle, where performative symbolism often supplants substantive reform. Leaders indulge in rhetorical grandstanding, constructing narratives that are (3) ______ rather than transformative. Consequently, public trust erodes, not due to apathy but from acute (4) ______ -a recognition that participation no longer guarantees influence. To reclaim legitimacy, institutions must reimagine governance not as a procedural mechanism but as an iterative, dialogical act. This demands epistemic humility, the willingness to engage multiple worldviews without defaulting to technocratic (5) ______. Only then can policy transcend compliance and cultivate authentic democratic agency.

Q1: What should come in the place of blank number 1? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Superseded** means replaced or supplanted by something newer.
The passage contrasts traditional democratic consultation with modern unilateral data mechanisms that replace it.
Options (b), (c), and (d) do not convey complete technological replacement.

question.en:
Contemporary governance will typically disguise itself in terms of agility and crisis response. From climate early warning systems to pandemic dashboards, there is a rapidly increasing apparatus that promises the vision of being in control. Such aids, while useful, tend to (1) ______ the public eye away from structural disparities by concentrating on short-term metrics. What looks like responsiveness tends to be mere reactivity in a system that is optimized for optics, not results. Governments implement short-term programs, presented as "emergency relief," but too frequently without vision or representation in the long term. These measures are hailed not for their depth but for their urgency. The theatrics of governance are most visible, while the slow violence of underfinance of healthcare, food insecurity, and housing abandonment goes on and on. Policymaking is performative in this environment and is not evaluated by what it achieves but by how visible it is. The outcome is an administration style that (2) ______ true change by replacing announcements with action. This is particularly true in the way that disasters are framed. The media cycle dramatizes, politicians act out urgency, and citizen complaints are quantified into abstraction. Gradually, this storytelling method (3) ______ distress into consumable portions reducing complexity for dissemination. Crisis is a stage; the state, its actor. To meet this, we need to question how emergencies are constructed, not merely how they are governed. Otherwise, the instruments we construct to deal with suffering risk inadvertently (4) ______ it, locking people in situations they are assured are being rectified. Resilience, without responsibility, is a code for abandonment. Unless governance examines its own aesthetics, it will be a simulation everywhere, but (5) ______ where it is needed most.

Q1: What should come in the place of blank number 1? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The collocation **divert ... away from** means to distract or redirect attention elsewhere.
The dashboards draw attention away from structural deep-rooted inequalities.
Options (b), (c), and (d) do not match the construction with "away from".

question.en:
In the given passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage intently and choose the most appropriate option to fill in each blank:

As post-industrial societies gravitate towards algorithmic governance, the contours of democratic deliberation are being steadily (1)______. What was once a domain of slow-paced, participatory engagement has now been supplanted by platforms that privilege immediacy and spectacle. The metrics of influence-likes, shares, and impressions-act as a surrogate for rational consensus, creating a new epistemic environment where the distinction between knowledge and propaganda becomes increasingly (2)______. This metamorphosis is not merely technological but ontological, reshaping how individuals perceive their agency. The citizen morphs into a data node, his behavior quantified and curated to feed predictive models of consumption and compliance. Amid this shift, traditional norms of accountability and transparency are often rendered (3)______, buried under technical jargon and opaque algorithms. Efforts to reclaim civic integrity must contend with this techno-political apparatus that simultaneously empowers and ensnares.

For those committed to revitalizing public discourse, the challenge lies in cultivating (4)______ practices-ones that resist the homogenizing tendencies of digital systems. Rather than acquiesce to algorithmic flattening, democratic actors must foreground plurality and dissent, embracing complexity over coherence. In this regard, ethical resistance becomes not an act of rebellion but of (5)______, an assertion of human interpretive agency against machinic determinism.

What should come in the place of blank number 1? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Blank (1) needs a verb meaning the contours are being erased/diminished. Effaced (wiped out) fits: democratic deliberation is being steadily effaced.

Option meanings
emblazoned — displayed brightly
effaced — erased, wiped out [मिटाया गया]
extolled — praised
exacerbated — worsened

The context (supplanted by platforms) supports “effaced”.

As post-industrial societies gravitate towards algorithmic governance, the contours of democratic deliberation are being steadily (1)______. What was once a domain of slow-paced, participatory engagement has now been supplanted by platforms that privilege immediacy and spectacle. The metrics of influence-likes, shares, and impressions-act as a surrogate for rational consensus, creating a new epistemic environment where the distinction between knowledge and propaganda becomes increasingly (2)______. The citizen morphs into a data node, his behavior quantified and curated to feed predictive models of consumption and compliance. Amid this shift, traditional norms of accountability and transparency are often rendered (3)______, buried under technical jargon and opaque algorithms. Efforts to reclaim civic integrity must contend with this techno-political apparatus that simultaneously empowers and ensnares.

For those committed to revitalizing public discourse, the challenge lies in cultivating (4)______ practices-ones that resist the homogenizing tendencies of digital systems. Rather than acquiesce to algorithmic flattening, democratic actors must foreground plurality and dissent, embracing complexity over coherence. In this regard, ethical resistance becomes not an act of rebellion but of (5)______, an assertion of human interpretive agency against machinic determinism.

What should come in the place of blank number 3? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Blank (3) needs an adjective for norms that are becoming outdated/ignored, “buried under jargon”. Obsolescent (becoming obsolete) fits.

Option meanings
obsolescent — going out of use [अप्रचलित होता]
impregnable — unassailable
consequential — important
reified — made into a thing

The sense of norms being sidelined supports “obsolescent”.

question.en:
In the given passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage intently and choose the most appropriate option to fill in each blank:

In contrast to earthquakes or wars, other violence is insidious, playing itself out over decades smog, poisoned water, eroded soil. These are not shocks but creeping disasters. Such damage has been described as "slow violence," not because it is less profound, but because it is less spectacular. It does not have the dramatic images that grab the public eye. It is therefore frequently (1)______ in media reporting, policy action, and public debate.

This invisibility is not an accident. Economies that profit from such destruction spend a lot on public relations, lobbying, and research camouflage. They present agony as the byproduct of progress or a technical glitch and not as systemic neglect. Agony is reported to victims as having no connection, their contexts misinterpreted. This repetitive denial (2)______ the very possibility for acknowledgment.

What makes slow violence so insidious is its unequal distribution. It hurts most those who have the least political power-rural poor, indigenous peoples, urban minorities. The privileged will never lay eyes on the toxins, but the marginalized inhale them. Without so much as a mention of this violence, resistance will continue to be fragmented and justice delayed. It takes more than policy to solve it-it takes a new kind of attention: slow noticing, slow journalism, slow solidarity. These are not positions of passivity but radical acts of care. They (3)______ the rhythms of harm and provide room for grief, witness, and repair.

Most legal systems are, however, constructed to address the spectacular, rather than the smoldering. At the point when damage is apparent, accountability mechanisms usually have not worked. Thus, we need to rethink time, evidence, and harm in law and science. Otherwise, the engine of justice will go on to (4)______ perpetuate the same harm it is meant to heal, oblivious to what happens too slowly to be noticed. Only by reimagining violence itself not as a high-drama event but as an erosive force can we start to map courses toward healing that are strong, equitable, and (5)______ resilient.

What should come in the place of blank number 1? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Blank (1) needs a verb for how slow harm is treated - it is overlooked. Ignored fits: slow, smoldering harm is ignored while the spectacular is addressed.

Option meanings
amplified — increased
ignored — overlooked [अनदेखा]
emphasized — stressed
canonized — declared sacred

The passage's theme (too slow to be noticed) supports “ignored”.

question.en:
Read the passage and answer the question:
Popular culture, often called "pop culture," refers to the trends, ideas, images, and activities that are widely accepted and enjoyed by the general public. It includes music, movies, television shows, fashion, social media trends, and celebrity lifestyles. Pop culture constantly evolves, shaped by changing tastes, technological advances, and global influences.
One of the defining features of pop culture is its ability to bring people together. Whether it's discussing a hit song, binge-watching a new series, or following viral internet challenges, pop culture creates a shared experience among diverse groups. It also plays a key role in shaping opinions, spreading awareness, and influencing behavior, especially among young people.
However, pop culture is not without criticism. Some argue that it promotes consumerism, encourages superficial values, and overshadows traditional cultural practices. Despite this, it continues to be a powerful force, reflecting society's hopes, concerns, and identity.
Today, social media platforms like Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube have made it easier than ever for trends to spread quickly and for individuals to influence pop culture themselves. As a result, pop culture is now more interactive, fast-paced, and global than ever before.

Question: Which part of speech is the word "viral" in the sentence below?
"Whether it's discussing a hit song, binge-watching a new series, or following viral internet challenges..." [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Viral is an adjective here.

It describes the noun phrase “internet challenges”, telling what kind of challenges they are: ones that spread rapidly online.

[“viral internet challenges” = इंटरनेट पर तेज़ी से फैलने वाली चुनौतियाँ]

It is not a verb (it shows no action), a noun or an adverb.

Identify the type of sentence:
"Pop culture constantly evolves, shaped by changing tastes, technological advances, and global influences." [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

4.en: Simple sentence with a participial phrase

solution.en:
It is a simple sentence with a participial phrase.

There is only one finite clause: “Pop culture constantly evolves”.
“shaped by changing tastes, technological advances, and global influences” is a past-participle phrase describing “pop culture”; it has no finite verb.

With no second independent clause and no subordinate clause, it is neither compound nor complex. Option 4 is more precise than the bare “Simple sentence”.

question.en:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:

Yann Martel's Life of Pi explores deep ideas concerning survival, faith, and how we construct the realities we tell ourselves. At its core, the story examines how people handle raw, natural struggles for survival, such as when Pi shares a lifeboat with the fearsome Richard Parker after their voyage goes horribly wrong. This experience shows Pi's split self-the sophisticated part of him and his raw survival instincts clashing while he fights to stay alive. Moreover, Martel questions what someone can believe during desperate times. Pi takes comfort by exploring three religions- Hinduism, Christianity, and Islam-to shield himself from hopelessness. In the end, though, Pi plays with the definition of truth. He ends up telling two entirely different versions of his tale and urges the reader to ponder which is more truthful. So, Martel asserts that we shape our truths based on the accounts we latch onto rather than on cold, hard facts. Such stories help us find purpose in our lives and make sense of everything that happens to us.

According to the passage, what does Richard Parker's presence on the lifeboat signify in Pi's internal struggle? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The conflict between Pi's refined side and his basic survival instincts.

2.en: The real threat is animals disappearing from the Pacific Ocean.

3.en: The historic change in how zoos were run during colonial India.

4.en: The actual need to keep the tiger alive to stay safe on the lifeboat.

solution.en:
The passage says the lifeboat experience “shows Pi’s split self — the sophisticated part of him and his raw survival instincts clashing”.

So Richard Parker’s presence signifies the conflict between Pi’s refined side and his basic survival instincts.

The passage says nothing about animals disappearing, zoo history or a practical need to keep the tiger alive.

1.en: Truth is only based on facts that can be proven and checked.

2.en: Truth is impossible to determine because Pi suffered from permanent memory loss.

3.en: Truth is a malleable concept shaped by the narratives we choose to believe.

4.en: The investigators who record the shipwreck always find out the truth.

solution.en:
The passage says Martel asserts that “we shape our truths based on the accounts we latch onto rather than on cold, hard facts”.

So truth is malleable — shaped by the narratives we choose to believe.

The passage rejects the idea that truth rests only on provable facts, and it mentions neither memory loss nor infallible investigators.

question.en:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:

Yann Martel's Life of Pi explores deep ideas concerning survival, faith, and how we construct the realities we tell ourselves. At its core, the story examines how people handle raw, natural struggles for survival, such as when Pi shares a lifeboat with the fearsome Richard Parker after their voyage goes horribly wrong. This experience shows Pi's split self-the sophisticated part of him and his raw survival instincts clashing while he fights to stay alive. Moreover, Martel questions what someone can believe during desperate times. Pi takes comfort by exploring three religions- Hinduism, Christianity, and Islam-to shield himself from hopelessness. In the end, though, Pi plays with the definition of truth. He ends up telling two entirely different versions of his tale and urges the reader to ponder which is more truthful. So, Martel asserts that we shape our truths based on the accounts we latch onto rather than on cold, hard facts. Such stories help us find purpose in our lives and make sense of everything that happens to us.

What is the author's primary goal in presenting two different versions of Pi's survival story? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: To mislead the reader so they lose interest in the plot.

2.en: To demonstrate that the second version is the only historically accurate one

3.en: To reveal that Pi lied to conceal a crime

4.en: To compel the reader to evaluate the meaning and purpose behind storytelling.

solution.en:
Pi tells two versions of his tale and “urges the reader to ponder which is more truthful”; such stories “help us find purpose in our lives”.

So the goal is to make the reader evaluate the meaning and purpose of storytelling.

The passage does not say that the author wants to mislead readers, that the second version alone is accurate, or that Pi concealed a crime.

question.en:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:

Gustave Flaubert, in his novel Madame Bovary, exposes the fate of his female protagonist. Emma-The fictional character of Flaubert was constructed around a feminist centre to expose the author's viewpoint on the role and position of French women in nineteenth-century society. Since childhood, Emma had been reading books; she used to develop her intellectual capacity so that, after her marriage, this dimension would not be altered. Emma learned the world from books because she was very constrained by the patriarchal system. She was an orphan, so when she chose her peace of mind by taking refuge in reading novels, she was safer from the unkind world. Due to her unhappy married life, she dreamt of the life she read about in her books. Instead of the traditional, boring routine she was supposed to follow, she wanted more from life. Emma wanted someone she could talk to, and with whom she could share her intellectual knowledge in some way; she wanted to know more, read more and talk more. She was unable to get used to the idea of staying at the same stage; she wanted to change, to develop, to be a better person.

According to the passage, what was the primary reason Emma turned to books during her childhood? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: To seek refuge from an unkind world and patriarchal limitations.

2.en: To prepare for a future professional career as a scholar.

3.en: To impress potential suitors within nineteenth-century French society.

4.en: To avoid the responsibilities associated with domestic chores.

solution.en:
The passage says Emma was “very constrained by the patriarchal system” and, as an orphan, took refuge in novels, where “she was safer from the unkind world”.

So she turned to books to seek refuge from an unkind world and patriarchal limits.

A scholarly career, suitors or escaping domestic chores are not mentioned.

question.en:
Read the passage and answer the following question:

In today's digital world, social media platforms have become an inseparable part of daily life for millions of people. While these platforms help people stay connected, share information, and express their opinions, they also raise serious concerns about data privacy.

Every time a user uploads photos, shares posts, or likes content, they leave behind a digital footprint. Social media companies collect this data to show targeted advertisements and improve user experience. However, this information can also be misused if it falls into the wrong hands or if companies fail to protect it properly.

Recent cases of data breaches have made people more aware of how vulnerable their personal information can be online. Experts suggest that users should read privacy policies, use strong passwords, and limit the amount of personal information they share on these platforms. Maintaining data privacy is crucial to ensure that social media remains a safe space for everyone.

Which word in the passage is a past participle? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
"Connected" is a past participle (V3). It appears in "help people stay connected", where it works as a participle adjective after "stay".

"Staying" and "Using" are present participles or gerunds (-ing forms), and "limit" is a base verb.

In the sentence "Recent cases of data breaches have made people more aware of how vulnerable their personal information can be online," what is the tense of the verb phrase "have made", and what does it indicate? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Past simple – a completed action in the past

2.en: Present perfect – an action that has relevance to the present

4.en: Past perfect – an action completed before another past action

solution.en:
"Have made" = have + past participle (V3), so it is the present perfect tense.
It shows a past action (the data breaches) whose result continues in the present: people are more aware now.

Why other options are wrong
Past simple would be "made".
Present continuous would be "are making".
Past perfect would be "had made".

question.en:
Read the passage and answer the following question:

India and the United Kingdom have shared a strong economic relationship for decades. In recent years, both countries have been working towards finalising a comprehensive trade agreement to boost economic growth and cooperation. This proposed trade deal aims to reduce tariffs, encourage investments, and create new opportunities for businesses in sectors like technology, education, pharmaceuticals, and manufacturing.

Negotiations for the agreement have not always been easy. Issues like market access, labour mobility, and regulatory standards have led to lengthy discussions. However, leaders from both sides believe that a fair and balanced trade agreement will benefit millions by generating employment, increasing exports, and strengthening diplomatic ties.

Experts say that if successful, the India-UK trade agreement could become a model for future partnerships with other nations. It could help India expand its global reach and attract more foreign investors, while the UK could gain access to India's vast market, which is one of the fastest-growing in the world.

In the sentence:
"India and the United Kingdom have shared a strong economic relationship for decades,"
what is the tense of the verb phrase "have shared"? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
"Have shared" = have + past participle (V3), so it is the present perfect tense.
With "for decades", it shows an action that began in the past and continues up to the present.

Simple past would be "shared", past perfect "had shared", and present continuous "are sharing".

In the sentence:
"Negotiations for the agreement have not always been easy,"
why is the plural verb "have" used instead of "has"? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 1]

3.en: Because it is in passive voice

4.en: Because the sentence is in future tense

solution.en:
Rule: The verb agrees with the real subject. In "Negotiations for the agreement have not always been easy", the subject is "Negotiations" (plural). "For the agreement" is only a prepositional phrase.
So the plural verb "have" is used.

"Agreement" is the object of the preposition "for", not the subject. The sentence is neither passive nor in the future tense.

question.en:
The theory of evolution, first systematically articulated by Charles Darwin, provides a comprehensive explanation for how species gradually change and diversify over time through the process of natural selection. Organisms possessing traits that are better adapted to their specific environments are more likely to survive, reproduce successfully and pass these advantageous traits on to subsequent generations. Over extended periods, minor variations accumulate, leading to remarkable adaptations and the emergence of entirely new species. Extensive evidence supporting evolutionary theory comes from the fossil record, comparative anatomy and modern genetic studies. Evolutionary principles illuminate the vast diversity of life, the intricate relationships among organisms and the development of complex biological traits. Although initially controversial, the concept of evolution is now widely accepted within the scientific community and serves as a foundational framework in biology, medicine and ecology. Understanding evolution enables humans to fully appreciate the profound interconnectedness of life and the natural mechanisms driving ongoing biological change.

The theory of evolution explains how species change over ______. [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The passage states that the theory explains "how species gradually change and diversify over time through the process of natural selection".
Evolution is a slow process spread over long periods, not minutes, hours or days.

Time management is an essential skill in both academic and professional life. People who manage their time effectively are better able to balance responsibilities, meet deadlines and reduce stress. Instead of reacting to tasks at the last minute, effective planners set priorities and create realistic schedules. This approach allows them to focus on important goals without feeling overwhelmed. Poor time management, on the other hand, often leads to missed deadlines, rushed work and frustration. Technology can either help or hinder time management. Digital calendars and task-management apps can improve organization, but constant notifications may distract users from their priorities. Developing good time-management habits requires self-discipline and regular reflection. When individuals learn to control how they spend their time, they gain greater productivity and a stronger sense of control over their daily lives.

What is the main focus of the passage? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The passage is entirely about time management: its importance, the benefits of good planning, the problems of poor management, the role of technology and the habits needed.
So the main focus is Management (of time). Technology, stress and productivity are only sub-points.

question.en:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on it

To reduce Kalamkari to "fabric painting" is to mistake the surface for the story. What appears today as an artisan's motif was, at one time, a traveling archive of storytelling, myth, faith, and rebellion-etched in dye, not ink. The word "Kalamkari" literally means "pen work," derived from the Persian kalam (pen) and kari (craftsmanship). Yet its essence lies not in the instrument but in the ritual. Traditionally practiced in Andhra Pradesh and some parts of Tamil Nadu, the art form was once temple-centric, used to narrate episodes from epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana through scrolls, canvas and textiles. These were not merely decorative items but didactic tools in a largely oral culture. Over time, Kalamkari migrated from temple to marketplace, from sacred wall to saree border, shaped by both Islamic and Hindu aesthetic vocabularies. Each region gave it a different grammar-Machilipatnam preferred block-printing, while Srikalahasti developed freehand drawing with a bamboo pen. Ironically, its survival today owes much to global demand and government emporiums, even as many practitioners face economic precarity. Chemical dyes now compete with natural ones; storytelling scrolls give way to mass-produced wall hangings. But within this aesthetic compromise remains a stubborn lineage-lines that still echo the hands of ancestors. Kalamkari is less a static tradition than a palimpsest: erased, rewritten, restored-always negotiating between the sacred and the saleable.

Q1. What does the author imply by calling Kalamkari a "palimpsest"? [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

2.en: It is layered, evolving through erasure and rewriting

3.en: It is written with ink, not dye

4.en: It is valued only by historians

solution.en:
A palimpsest [पुनर्लिखित पांडुलिपि] is a manuscript whose earlier writing has been erased and written over, so traces of older layers remain.
The passage states: Kalamkari is "less a static tradition than a palimpsest: erased, rewritten, restored".
So the author implies that Kalamkari is layered and keeps evolving through erasure and rewriting.

Option 1 contradicts "less a static tradition", option 3 contradicts "etched in dye, not ink", and option 4 is not suggested.

Read the passage and answer the following question:

In the modern medical world, robotic surgeries are becoming increasingly common. With the help of advanced technology, surgeons can now perform complex procedures with greater precision and control. Robotic surgical systems allow doctors to make smaller incisions, which often means less pain, minimal blood loss, and faster recovery for patients.

Hospitals across the globe are investing in robotic surgery equipment to provide better healthcare services. Although robotic surgeries can be more expensive than traditional methods, many believe the benefits justify the cost. Surgeons also need special training to handle these sophisticated machines effectively.

However, there are concerns too. Some critics argue that over-reliance on robotic systems might reduce surgeons' manual skills over time. Others worry that the high costs may limit access for poorer patients. Despite these challenges, experts agree that robotic surgeries will continue to grow and transform the medical field in the coming years.

The word "precision" means: [SSC Steno 10/09/26 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Precision [सटीकता] means the quality of being accurate and exact. The passage says surgeons can perform complex procedures "with greater precision and control".

Option meanings
Carelessness — lack of attention [लापरवाही]
Strength — physical power [शक्ति]
Accuracy and exactness — being correct in every detail [सटीकता]
Wastefulness — careless use of resources [फिजूलखर्ची]

Related words: Precision: exactness, meticulousness, correctness.

solution.en:
Rule: The present continuous tense is formed with is/am/are + V-ing and shows an action or trend in progress.

Simple present would be "become", present perfect "have become" and past continuous "were becoming".

Jack Finney's fascinating story, The Third Level, follows Charley, an ordinary thirty-one-year-old clerk who unexpectedly discovers a portal to the past within Grand Central Station. Hurrying home to his wife, Louisa, on a hot summer evening, Charley takes a wrong turn down an unfamiliar, sloping subterranean corridor. Instead of returning to the standard platforms, he emerges onto a mysterious third level. Here, the room is visibly smaller, dim open-flame gaslights flicker, and commuters are dressed in late-nineteenth-century attire. Factual verification occurs when he notices an 1894 edition of The World newspaper that reports on President Cleveland. Seeking a peaceful escape from the intense insecurities, anxieties, and stresses of modern life, Charley attempts to buy two railway tickets to Galesburg, Illinois. However, the ticket clerk rejects his modern currency, warning him that it is not legal tender. Although Charley escapes arrest and later buys vintage bills, he can never locate the entrance to the elusive third level again.

What is the main idea of the passage? [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The psychological desire to escape modern stress with historical nostalgia.

2.en: The planning and engineering challenges of growing city transit systems.

3.en: The financial currency of investing in rare or vintage currencies of the economy.

4.en: Direct political rivalries among public servants in America in the nineteenth century.

solution.en:
The main idea is the psychological desire to escape modern stress with historical nostalgia.

The passage says Charley was "seeking a peaceful escape from the intense insecurities, anxieties, and stresses of modern life" and found a portal to 1894.

Transit engineering, investing in vintage currency and political rivalries are not discussed.

The Kite Runner is a story of love, faith, loss, betrayal, guilt, and redemption written by the Afghan-American writer Khaled Hosseini and first published in 2003. Though honest, it is a painful story, and that pain stems from a cowardly and cruel act committed in childhood. A hint of the author's own childhood can be studied in his writing. Like Amir, he left Afghanistan as a child and returned only as an adult. The novel is a work of historical fiction and drama; it depicts the political and social landscape of then-contemporary Afghanistan. Themes of betrayal, love, family relations, discrimination, and violence prevail throughout the book. What inspired Hosseini to write this novel is the cruelty of the Taliban inflicted on the people of Afghanistan. Hosseini grew up flying kites in Kabul, but when he heard that the Taliban had banned the activity of flying kites, and that's how he came up with The Kite Runner. The novel beautifully depicts two different lives that coexist yet are so different from each other. The divide between the high class and the low class, the oppression of the minority community by the majority community. It is a story about "to be good again" and overcoming evil despite adverse circumstances. The idea is to atone for past sins and make the necessary sacrifice to redeem yourself.

What is the central driving force behind the redemption arc in the novel? [SSC Steno 11/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: The protagonist's attempt to atone for a cowardly and cruel act from his childhood.

2.en: The author wants to record the history of kite-flying competitions in Kabul.

3.en: The government orders the removal of class divisions between different social groups.

4.en: The need to get financial compensation for losses suffered during the Taliban era.

solution.en:
The driving force is the protagonist's attempt to atone for a cowardly and cruel act from his childhood.

The passage says the pain "stems from a cowardly and cruel act committed in childhood" and the idea is "to atone for past sins... to redeem yourself."

Kite-flying history, government orders and financial compensation are not mentioned.

Climate change has emerged as one of the most urgent and far-reaching global challenges of the twenty-first century. Rising global temperatures, rapidly melting glaciers and increasingly unpredictable weather patterns profoundly affect delicate ecosystems, agricultural productivity and human societies worldwide.

Greenhouse gas emissions, primarily from the burning of fossil fuels, widespread deforestation and intensive industrial activities, are the main drivers of accelerating global warming. These changes contribute to extreme and destructive weather events, including hurricanes, prolonged droughts and catastrophic floods, threatening food security, freshwater availability and the livelihoods of millions.

Effectively addressing climate change requires robust international cooperation, widespread adoption of renewable energy, large-scale reforestation and the promotion of sustainable and environmentally responsible lifestyle practices. A clear understanding of the science behind climate change, combined with decisive, coordinated action, is essential to protect the planet and secure a sustainable future for coming generations.

Passage Reference: The second sentence of the passage states verbatim: 'Rising global temperatures, rapidly melting glaciers and increasingly unpredictable weather patterns profoundly affect delicate ecosystems...'
Therefore, climate change leads directly to rising temperatures.

question.en:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:

The recent surge in power demand across North India, driven by record-breaking heatwaves, has brought the fragility of our energy infrastructure into sharp focus. As temperatures soar, the grid faces unprecedented pressure, leading to frequent outages that disrupt essential services. While the government has ramped up coal supply and increased solar energy integration, the underlying issue remains a lack of long-term storage solutions. Reliance on traditional grids, which were designed for more temperate climates, is no longer sufficient to handle the modern reality of extreme weather events.

True energy security in this era of climate volatility requires more than just generation capacity; it demands a radical overhaul of distribution networks and the adoption of smart-grid technology. Relying solely on short-term fixes-like diverting power from industrial sectors to domestic users-is a precarious strategy that hampers economic growth. Authorities must prioritise investment in large-scale battery storage and decentralised power systems to buffer against inevitable supply shocks. If the grid does not evolve to accommodate these shifts, the "cool comfort" of modern life will become an increasingly fragile luxury for millions, turning summer peaks into seasonal crises of public health and economic stability.

(Source: Editorial, "The heat and the grid: Powering through the crisis", published in The Indian Express on June 01, 2026.)

What is the central theme of the editorial? [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The urgent need to modernise grids for climate resilience.

2.en: The environmental impact of coal-based energy generation.

3.en: The economic benefits of prioritising industrial power supply.

4.en: The history of energy policy in North India over decades.

solution.en:
The passage says old grids built for temperate climates cannot cope with extreme weather, and calls for “a radical overhaul of distribution networks”, smart grids, battery storage and decentralised systems.
So the central theme is the urgent need to modernise the grid for climate resilience.

Why other options are wrong
Coal's environmental impact is not discussed; prioritising industry is not praised (diverting power is called “precarious”); there is no history of energy policy.

Therefore, The urgent need to modernise grids for climate resilience.

Which of the following can be inferred about the government's current approach to power shortages? [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: It is primarily based on permanent, long-term infrastructure improvements.

2.en: It has successfully eliminated the need for coal-based energy generation.

3.en: It focuses heavily on short-term adjustments to manage peak demand.

4.en: It intentionally restricts domestic power use to boost industrial growth.

solution.en:
The passage says the government has “ramped up coal supply and increased solar integration”, yet the “underlying issue remains a lack of long-term storage”. It criticises “relying solely on short-term fixes – like diverting power from industrial sectors to domestic users”.
Hence the current approach focuses heavily on short-term adjustments to manage peak demand.

Why other options are wrong
Option 1 is the opposite; Option 2 is false (coal supply was increased); Option 4 reverses the direction (power is diverted from industry to homes).

Therefore, It focuses heavily on short-term adjustments to manage peak demand.

1.en: Heatwaves are driving up power demand (Fact); The grid is fragile (Opinion).

2.en: Solar energy is being integrated (Opinion); Smart grids are the only solution (Fact).

Therefore, Heatwaves are driving up power demand (Fact); The grid is fragile (Opinion).

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:

William Shakespeare's famous tragedy, King Lear, explores what happens when pride, misplaced trust, and family problems go unchecked. The story follows Lear, an old King of Britain, who gives up his throne and divides his kingdom among his three daughters, based on how much they flatter him. The two older sisters flatter Lear to get the biggest share, but the youngest, Cordelia, refuses to exaggerate her love and chooses to be honest. Lear, upset by her response, sends Cordelia away and dismisses the wise advisers who tried to help him. But then, the conniving sisters get hold of all that power and kick their father out, treating him disgustingly in his old age. Stripped of everything, Lear ends up outside during a fierce storm. Madness sets in as reality hits him hard-he's lost everything due to his silly fantasies. At its core, this tale warns us about how the ego can shatter a family and cause total destruction.

What is the main theme of the passage? [SSC Steno 12/09/26 Shift 2]

1.en: The destructive impact of ego and false trust on family.

2.en: The political strategies used to expand early British territories.

3.en: The historical lifestyle differences between royal siblings.

4.en: The economic advantages of retiring early from public office.

solution.en:
The passage ends: “this tale warns us about how the ego can shatter a family and cause total destruction”, and begins with “pride, misplaced trust, and family problems”.
So the main theme is the destructive impact of ego and false trust on the family.
Political strategy, royal lifestyle and early retirement are not discussed.

Therefore, The destructive impact of ego and false trust on family.

question.en:
The inheritance of culture is rarely obvious. What we call tradition is often just repetition with reverence, and what we call structure is more often sediment-settled behaviors shaped by forgotten motives. No individual wakes up conscious of the script they perform daily: the deference coded into language, the hierarchy in who speaks and who listens, the legitimacy given to one dialect over another. These scripts are learned by doing, not by knowing. Structures do not enforce themselves through law alone; they linger in weddings, gestures, floor plans, and silence. The most enduring hierarchies don't shout they whisper, hiding in rituals too familiar to question. When efforts are made to 'preserve culture,' they often freeze one version of the past, assuming it pure and unchanging. However, culture never stood still. It changes, not by denial, but by negotiation. To honor a legacy is not to protect its shape, but to confront what it excludes. If history is architecture, then culture is weather - it reshapes even stone, slowly, insistently. A society unwilling to interrogate its inherited rhythms is not preserving culture it is embalming it.

1.en: It is taught consciously through education

2.en: It is reinforced by formal institutions only

3.en: It is practiced unconsciously through daily behavior

4.en: It is dictated directly by written tradition

solution.en:
The passage directly states: "No individual wakes up conscious of the script they perform daily... These scripts are learned by doing, not by knowing."
This demonstrates that cultural inheritance is largely internalized and performed unconsciously in ordinary everyday conduct.
Options (a), (b), and (d) are refuted by the passage's insistence that culture is not limited to formal laws or conscious schooling.

question.en:
In modern leadership models, emotional intelligence (EI) has come not as an ancillary characteristic but as a fundamental axis upon which successful leadership rotates. As compared to the classical models that placed importance on technical competence, decisiveness, and power, the progressively complex, interdependent, and people-oriented nature of organizations has emphasized relational competencies as crucial to influence, adaptability, and long-term performance. Emotional intelligence, in general terms, is the ability to perceive, regulate, and respond appropriately to one's own and other people's emotions. Applied to the context of leadership, it means empathetic communication, measured reaction in a crisis, and being able to build trust among diverse groups. High EI leaders are not just charismatic figures; they possess a consistent calm demeanor that enables them to soak up criticism, manage conflict without awkwardness, and motivate others without tyranny. Most importantly, emotional intelligence also serves as a bulwark against toxic leadership behaviors impulsiveness, narcissism, and authoritarian inflexibility. It promotes psychological safety, which is a requirement in innovation-intensive environments where vulnerability, criticism, and experimentation need to be fostered instead of stifled. While EI may be innate, more people increasingly consider it to be a trainable competency. As such, forward-thinking organizations are embedding EI assessments and coaching into executive development programs since leadership is as much about emotional calibration as it is about strategic execution. Overall, emotional intelligence is not an add-on trait but a leadership structural imperative for the time that intellect no longer has the capacity to navigate complexity. Leaders who do not develop EI can be technically brilliant but emotionally irrelevant.

2.en: Their calm presence, openness to criticism, and motivational style

4.en: Their strict control over performance metrics

solution.en:
The passage states that high EI leaders "possess a consistent calm demeanor that enables them to soak up criticism, manage conflict without awkwardness, and motivate others without tyranny."
This distinguishes them from merely charismatic figures.
Options (a), (c), and (d) describe authoritarian or detached models rejected by the author.

question.en:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on it:

In no previous century has the boundary between machinic execution and human agency been so imperceptibly redrawn as in our own. Machines no longer reside merely in factories or data farms; they have diffused into cognition itself-through pattern detection, affect analysis, and probabilistic reasoning. Yet amid this silent migration of authority, a peculiar question lingers beneath the efficiency rhetoric: what becomes of judgment when its form is preserved but its source displaced? It is not that machines err-they err differently. They do not forget, but neither do they forgive. A calculus-driven output, in a medical tribunal or parole board, bears no malice-but neither does it carry grace. This absence of interiority of remorse, doubt, or ethical conflict-renders such systems unsettling not because they are inhuman, but because they mimic our structures while bypassing our struggles. The specter of neutrality seduces us with promises of impartiality, yet what is more dangerous than a system that believes itself objective without capacity for self-questioning? The issue is not merely epistemic but civilizational: do we measure justice by consistency alone, or by its responsiveness to suffering? To reduce ethics to outputs is to mechanize mercy-and in so doing, abandon it. We must not aspire to human-like machines, but to machine-aware humans, vigilant not only of what machines can do, but of what we too readily surrender.

Why is machine judgment described as "unsettling" in the passage? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

2.en: It mimics systems without internal moral conflict

solution.en:
The passage says such systems are unsettling because they mimic our structures while bypassing our struggles - they lack interiority, remorse, doubt or ethical conflict. So machine judgment mimics systems without internal moral conflict.

Option meanings
It commits factual errors frequently — the text says it is not that machines err
It mimics systems without internal moral conflict — matches the passage
It violates constitutional law — not stated
It responds emotionally — opposite of the passage

Therefore, It mimics systems without internal moral conflict.

What rhetorical device is used in "They do not forget, but neither do they forgive"? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Antithesis is the rhetorical device of contrasting ideas in a balanced form: “do not forget” vs “do not forgive”.

Option meanings
Irony — saying the opposite of what is meant
Euphemism — a mild expression for a harsh one
Antithesis — parallel contrast [विरोधाभासी तुलना]
Personification — giving human traits to non-humans

The balanced opposition of “forget” and “forgive” is antithesis.

The author warns that “the specter of neutrality seduces us with promises of impartiality” and calls a system that believes itself objective without self-questioning dangerous. So algorithmic neutrality is dangerous when assumed to be objective.

Option meanings
It ensures justice by removing emotions — opposite of the author's view
It is dangerous when assumed to be objective — matches
It should guide all legal systems — opposite
It is preferable to subjective human opinion — opposite

Therefore, It is dangerous when assumed to be objective.

question.en:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on it:

In no previous century has the boundary between machinic execution and human agency been so imperceptibly redrawn as in our own. Machines no longer reside merely in factories or data farms; they have diffused into cognition itself-through pattern detection, affect analysis, and probabilistic reasoning. Yet amid this silent migration of authority, a peculiar question lingers beneath the efficiency rhetoric: what becomes of judgment when its form is preserved but its source displaced? It is not that machines err-they err differently. They do not forget, but neither do they forgive. A calculus-driven output, in a medical tribunal or parole board, bears no malice-but neither does it carry grace. This absence of interiority of remorse, doubt, or ethical conflict-renders such systems unsettling not because they are inhuman, but because they mimic our structures while bypassing our struggles. The specter of neutrality seduces us with promises of impartiality, yet what is more dangerous than a system that believes itself objective without capacity for self-questioning? The issue is not merely epistemic but civilizational: do we measure justice by consistency alone, or by its responsiveness to suffering? To reduce ethics to outputs is to mechanize mercy-and in so doing, abandon it. We must not aspire to human-like machines, but to machine-aware humans, vigilant not only of what machines can do, but of what we too readily surrender.

What does the phrase "mechanize mercy" metaphorically criticize? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

solution.en:
“Mechanize mercy” criticises reducing ethics to outputs - handing compassion over to emotionless systems, thereby abandoning genuine mercy.

Option meanings
Delegating compassion to emotionless systems — matches
Machines learning human kindness — opposite
Human programming errors — unrelated
Excessive empathy in coding — opposite

Therefore, Delegating compassion to emotionless systems.

question.en:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on it:

Innovation, usually romanticized as the result of sudden inspiration or individual brilliance, is actually based on psychological processes that are cumulative, social, and context dependent. Creativity is a necessary condition, but innovation has more to it, including the execution of ideas, persistence through doubt, and navigation of institutional resistance. At the psychological heart of innovation is cognitive flexibility the capacity for divergent and convergent thinking. Divergent thinking propels the examination of new associations, while convergent thinking helps in refining and executing viable solutions. Innovative people show a high ambiguity tolerance, intrinsic motivation, and an ability to reframe failures as feedback instead of as terminus. Emotions also have a contradictory function. Excitement and curiosity drive experimentations, but frustration and discomfort can be indicative of periods of creative tension. Innovators thus need to be emotionally resilient, able to remain interested even when results are uncertain, and have a mental disposition that finds constraints to be catalysts, not barriers. Additionally, the psychology of innovation is not limited to individuals alone. Social environments organizational cultures, peer feedback loops, leadership models have a profound influence on whether or not creativity is fostered or stifled. Psychological safety, in which people can share unorthodox ideas without fear of ridicule, is a repeated predictor of innovative outcomes in teams and institutions. Finally, innovation is less a matter of revolutionary leaps than of enduring psychological preparedness to question assumptions, bear ambiguity, and translate fantasy into reality even when faced with initial failure or disregard.

According to the passage, what distinguishes innovation from mere creativity? [SSC Steno 15/09/26 Shift 2]

2.en: It includes execution and persistence beyond idea generation.

4.en: It is mostly based on sudden inspiration.

solution.en:
The passage says innovation “has more to it” than creativity, “including the execution of ideas, persistence through doubt” - i.e. execution and persistence beyond idea generation.

Option meanings
It involves artistic talent — not stated
It includes execution and persistence beyond idea generation — matches
It excludes emotional influence — opposite
It is mostly sudden inspiration — opposite

question.en: Which of the following features is most characteristic of Meitei Traditional Architecture associated with Sanamahism in Manipur? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: मणिपुर में सनामही धर्म (Sanamahism) से संबंधित मीतेई पारंपरिक स्थापत्य की सबसे विशिष्ट विशेषता कौन-सी मानी जाती है? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: Use of large granite blocks with intricate stone carvings depicting Hindu epics.
1.hi: विशाल ग्रेनाइट शिलाखंडों का प्रयोग, जिन पर हिंदू महाकाव्यों को चित्रित करती सूक्ष्म शिल्पकारी होती है

2.en: Predominantly wooden construction with raised platforms and open-air sanctuaries dedicated to nature deities.
2.hi: मुख्यतः लकड़ी से निर्मित संरचनाएँ जिनमें उच्च मंच और प्राकृतिक देवताओं को समर्पित खुले अभयारण्य होते थे।

3.en: Pyramid-shaped stupas with golden spires influenced by Tibetan Buddhism.
3.hi: पिरामिडनुमा स्तूप जिनके शीर्ष पर तिब्बती बौद्ध प्रभाव से प्रेरित सुनहरी कलश होते हैं।

4.en: Fortified palaces with Mughal-style domes and minarets reflecting medieval Islamic influence.
4.hi: मुग़ल शैली के गुम्बदों और मीनारों से युक्त दुर्गनुमा महल, जो मध्यकालीन इस्लामी प्रभाव को दर्शाते हैं

solution.en:
Traditional Meitei sacred architecture linked with Sanamahism is vernacular and nature-centred: timber, bamboo and thatch structures on raised plinths, with shrines and sacred groves for ancestral and nature deities. Granite epic carvings, Tibetan stupas and Mughal domes belong to other traditions.


Related exam facts
1. A Laishang is the shrine or house of a deity (lai) in Meitei tradition.
2. Sanamahi is worshipped in every Meitei household at the south-west corner, called the Sanamahi Kachin, together with his mother Leimaren.
3. Umang Lai are forest deities; sacred groves are associated with their worship.
4. Lai Haraoba is the festival held to please the traditional deities (Umang Lai).
solution.hi:
सनामहीवाद से जुड़ी पारंपरिक मैतेई पवित्र वास्तुकला स्थानीय और प्रकृति-केंद्रित है: ऊँचे चबूतरों पर लकड़ी, बाँस और छप्पर की संरचनाएँ, पूर्वज और प्रकृति-देवताओं के लिए देवस्थान तथा पवित्र उपवन। ग्रेनाइट पर महाकाव्य-नक्काशी, तिब्बती स्तूप और मुगल गुंबद अन्य परंपराओं के हैं।


संबंधित परीक्षा-तथ्य
1. मैतेई परंपरा में लाइशांग का अर्थ देवता (लाई) का देवस्थान या घर है।
2. प्रत्येक मैतेई घर के दक्षिण-पश्चिम कोने में, जिसे सनामही काचिन कहते हैं, सनामही की पूजा उनकी माता लेइमरेन के साथ होती है।
3. उमंग लाई वन-देवता हैं; पवित्र उपवन उनकी पूजा से जुड़े हैं।
4. लाई हराओबा पारंपरिक देवताओं (उमंग लाई) को प्रसन्न करने का उत्सव है।

question.en: Which of the following characteristics best distinguishes Kamsale from other devotional dance forms in Karnataka, particularly in terms of its musical instrumentation, religious significance, and performance context? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: कर्नाटक के अन्य भक्ति-प्रधान नृत्य रूपों की तुलना में कंसाले को सबसे अलग पहचान देने वाली विशेषताएँ कौन-सी हैं, विशेषतः इसके वाद्ययंत्र, धार्मिक महत्व और प्रस्तुति संदर्भ को लेकर? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: It is a temple dance performed silently by women, emphasizing stillness and subtle hand gestures to invoke goddess Durga
1.hi: यह एक मंदिर नृत्य है जो स्त्रियों द्वारा मौन में किया जाता है, जिसमें स्थिरता और सूक्ष्म हस्त मुद्राओं द्वारा देवी दुर्गा का आह्वान किया जाता है

2.en: It involves rhythmic clashing of metal cymbals called 'Kamsale' by male performers, who sing praises of Lord Male Mahadeshwara, combining martial dance movements with devotional fervor during pilgrimage and festival rituals.
2.hi: यह नृत्य पुरुष कलाकारों द्वारा किया जाता है, जिसमें वे कंसाले नामक धातु की झांझ बजाते हैं और माले महादेश्वर की स्तुति गाते हैं; इसमें युद्ध नृत्य और भक्ति भावनाओं का अद्वितीय मेल होता है और यह तीर्थयात्रा व उत्सवों के दौरान किया जाता है।

3.en: It is a purely theatrical folk drama without any musical instruments, narrating mythological stories through dialogue and facial expressions.
3.hi: यह एक शुद्ध रूप से नाटकीय लोक नाटक है जिसमें किसी भी प्रकार का वाद्य प्रयोग नहीं होता, और संवाद एवं चेहरे के भावों के माध्यम से पौराणिक कथाओं को प्रस्तुत करता है।

4.en: It is a harvest dance performed during the festival of Sankranti, primarily focused on celebrating agricultural prosperity with group formations and colorful costumes.
4.hi: यह संक्रांति पर्व के दौरान किया जाने वाला फसल उत्सव नृत्य है, जिसका मुख्य उद्देश्य कृषि समृद्धि का उत्सव मनाना है, समूह नृत्य संरचनाओं और रंग-बिरंगे वस्त्रों के साथ।

solution.en:
Kamsale is performed by male devotees of Lord Male Mahadeshwara, who clash the bronze Kamsale while singing his praises; its vigorous, rhythmic movements combine devotion with a martial energy. It is not silent, instrument-free or a Sankranti harvest dance.


Related exam facts
1. The Kamsale instrument is a cymbal in one hand and a bronze disc in the other.
2. It is traditionally performed by the Haalu Kuruba / Kuruba Gowda community; the initiated singers are called Devara Guddas.
3. The Male Mahadeshwara Hills temple is in Chamarajanagar district (Kollegal taluk), Karnataka.
4. The Kannada songs narrate the legends of Mahadeshwara; the form is common around Mysuru, Mandya, Chamarajanagar and Bengaluru.
solution.hi:
कंसाले भगवान माले महादेश्वर के पुरुष भक्त करते हैं, जो कांसे के कंसाले बजाते हुए उनकी स्तुति गाते हैं; इसकी ऊर्जावान लयबद्ध गतियों में भक्ति के साथ युद्ध-नृत्य जैसी शक्ति होती है। यह मौन, वाद्य-रहित या संक्रांति का फसल-नृत्य नहीं है।


संबंधित परीक्षा-तथ्य
1. कंसाले वाद्य में एक हाथ में झांझ और दूसरे में कांसे की चकती होती है।
2. इसे परंपरागत रूप से हालु कुरुबा / कुरुबा गौड़ा समुदाय करता है; दीक्षित गायकों को देवर गुड्डा कहते हैं।
3. माले महादेश्वर पहाड़ियों का मंदिर कर्नाटक के चामराजनगर ज़िले (कोल्लेगल तालुक) में है।
4. कन्नड़ गीत महादेश्वर की कथाएँ सुनाते हैं; यह मैसूरु, मांड्या, चामराजनगर और बेंगलुरु क्षेत्र में प्रचलित है।

questions.topic: Static GK: Folk Dances and Festivals

question.en: Which folk dance of India is performed during Navratri and involves rhythmic clapping and circular group formations? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: भारत का कौन-सा लोकनृत्य नवरात्रि के दौरान किया जाता है और जिसमें तालबद्ध ताली और गोलाकार समूह संरचनाएँ शामिल होती हैं? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Garba, Gujarat’s Navratri dance, is performed in circles around a lamp or an image of the Goddess, with rhythmic clapping and songs. Bihu is from Assam, Ghoomar from Rajasthan and Lavani from Maharashtra.


Related exam facts
1. The name is linked to the garbo, an earthen pot with a lamp inside, symbolising life.
2. “Garba of Gujarat” was inscribed on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in December 2023.
3. Dandiya Raas, also danced during Navratri, uses decorated sticks.
4. The dance honours the goddess Amba / Durga over the nine nights.
solution.hi:
गुजरात का नवरात्रि नृत्य गरबा दीपक या देवी की प्रतिमा के चारों ओर वृत्ताकार घेरे में तालियों और गीतों के साथ किया जाता है। बिहू असम, घूमर राजस्थान और लावणी महाराष्ट्र का नृत्य है।


संबंधित परीक्षा-तथ्य
1. नाम गरबो से जुड़ा है — भीतर दीपक वाला मिट्टी का घड़ा, जो जीवन का प्रतीक है।
2. “गुजरात का गरबा” दिसंबर 2023 में यूनेस्को की मानवता की अमूर्त सांस्कृतिक विरासत की प्रतिनिधि सूची में शामिल हुआ।
3. नवरात्रि में होने वाले डांडिया रास में सजी हुई डंडियों का प्रयोग होता है।
4. यह नृत्य नौ रातों तक देवी अंबा / दुर्गा की आराधना से जुड़ा है।

questions.topic: Static GK: Folk Dances and Festivals

question.en: Which of the following festivals is celebrated to commemorate the birth of Lord Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा उत्सव जैन धर्म के 24वें तीर्थंकर भगवान महावीर के जन्मोत्सव के रूप में मनाया जाता है? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Mahavir Jayanti celebrates the birth of Vardhamana Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara, on Chaitra Shukla Trayodashi. Paryushana is a period of fasting and forgiveness, Diwali marks his nirvana for Jains, and Navapad Oli is a nine-day observance.


Related exam facts
1. Mahavira was born at Kundagrama near Vaishali (Bihar).
2. He attained nirvana at Pavapuri; Jains observe Diwali as his nirvana day.
3. Paryushana ends with Samvatsari, when followers seek forgiveness with “Micchami Dukkadam”.
4. Rishabhanatha is the first Tirthankara and Parshvanatha the 23rd.
solution.hi:
महावीर जयंती 24वें तीर्थंकर वर्धमान महावीर के जन्म का उत्सव है, जो चैत्र शुक्ल त्रयोदशी को मनाया जाता है। पर्युषण उपवास और क्षमा का पर्व है, जैन दिवाली को महावीर के निर्वाण के रूप में मनाते हैं और नवपद ओली नौ दिन का व्रत है।


संबंधित परीक्षा-तथ्य
1. महावीर का जन्म वैशाली (बिहार) के निकट कुंडग्राम में हुआ।
2. उन्हें पावापुरी में निर्वाण प्राप्त हुआ; जैन दिवाली को उनका निर्वाण-दिवस मानते हैं।
3. पर्युषण संवत्सरी पर समाप्त होता है, जब अनुयायी “मिच्छामि दुक्कड़म्” कहकर क्षमा माँगते हैं।
4. ऋषभनाथ प्रथम और पार्श्वनाथ 23वें तीर्थंकर हैं।

questions.topic: Static GK: Folk Dances and Festivals

question.en: Which of the following festivals marks the beginning of the harvest season in Tamil Nadu and is closely associated with sun worship? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा उत्सव तमिलनाडु में फसल ऋतु की शुरुआत का प्रतीक है और सूर्य पूजन से गहराई से जुड़ा हुआ है? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Pongal, Tamil Nadu’s harvest festival in the month of Thai, thanks the Sun God for the harvest; new rice is boiled with milk and jaggery until it overflows (“pongal”). Ugadi is the new-year festival of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, and Vishu is Kerala’s new year.


Related exam facts
1. Its four days are Bhogi, Thai (Surya) Pongal, Mattu Pongal and Kaanum Pongal.
2. Mattu Pongal honours cattle.
3. Jallikattu, the bull-taming sport, is associated with the Pongal season.
4. Makar Sankranti marks the Sun’s entry into Capricorn (Makara).
solution.hi:
तमिलनाडु का फसल-उत्सव पोंगल थाई मास में मनाया जाता है और फसल के लिए सूर्य देव के प्रति कृतज्ञता प्रकट करता है; नए चावल को दूध और गुड़ के साथ उफान आने तक पकाया जाता है (“पोंगल”)। उगादि कर्नाटक, आंध्र प्रदेश और तेलंगाना का नववर्ष है तथा विषु केरल का नववर्ष है।


संबंधित परीक्षा-तथ्य
1. इसके चार दिन हैं: भोगी, थाई (सूर्य) पोंगल, मट्टू पोंगल और कानुम पोंगल।
2. मट्टू पोंगल पशुओं के सम्मान में है।
3. बैल-नियंत्रण का खेल जल्लीकट्टू पोंगल के समय से जुड़ा है।
4. मकर संक्रांति सूर्य के मकर राशि में प्रवेश का प्रतीक है।

questions.topic: Static GK: Music and Musical Instruments

question.en: In what ways do Manganiyar and Langas musical traditions reflect the complex interplay of social hierarchy, patronage, and cultural transmission in Rajasthan's folk music landscape? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: राजस्थान की मंगनियार और लंगा संगीत परंपराएँ सामाजिक पदानुक्रम, संरक्षण (patronage) और सांस्कृतिक संचरण के जटिल संबंध को किस प्रकार दर्शाती हैं? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

1.en: By being independent of any patronage system and performed solely in public festivals
1.hi: किसी भी संरक्षक व्यवस्था से स्वतंत्र रहकर केवल सार्वजनिक उत्सवों में प्रस्तुत किए जाने द्वारा

2.en: By historically relying on the patronage of Rajput and Muslim elites, these communities preserved and transmitted a rich repertoire of songs praising rulers, deities, and local legends, thus blending diverse cultural influences and sustaining their social identity through music
2.hi: राजपूत और मुस्लिम अभिजात वर्ग के संरक्षण पर ऐतिहासिक रूप से निर्भर रहकर, इन समुदायों ने शासकों, देवी-देवताओं और स्थानीय लोककथाओं की प्रशंसा में समृद्ध गीत-संग्रह को संरक्षित और आगे बढ़ाया; इस प्रकार विविध सांस्कृतिक प्रभावों का मिश्रण हुआ और संगीत के माध्यम से सामाजिक पहचान बनी रही।

3.en: By exclusively performing classical Hindustani music without any folk elements
3.hi: केवल शास्त्रीय हिंदुस्तानी संगीत प्रस्तुत करना, बिना किसी लोक तत्व के

4.en: By rejecting all traditional instruments and focusing only on vocal performances
4.hi: सभी पारंपरिक वाद्ययंत्रों को अस्वीकार कर केवल गायन पर ध्यान केंद्रित करके

solution.en:
The Manganiyars and Langas are hereditary Muslim musician communities of western Rajasthan who sustained their art through hereditary patrons (jajmans): Rajputs for the Manganiyars and Sindhi-Sipahis (Muslim Rajputs) for the Langas. Their songs praise patrons, deities and local legends, blending Hindu and Muslim traditions; the other options deny patronage, folk content or instruments.


Related exam facts
1. They are concentrated in the Barmer–Jaisalmer region of the Thar Desert.
2. The Manganiyars’ signature bowed instrument is the kamaicha, made of mango wood with a goatskin resonator.
3. The khartal, a pair of wooden clappers, keeps the rhythm.
4. Folklorist Komal Kothari helped bring these musicians to wider audiences from the late 1970s.
solution.hi:
मांगणियार और लंगा पश्चिमी राजस्थान के वंशानुगत मुस्लिम संगीतकार समुदाय हैं, जिन्होंने वंशानुगत संरक्षकों (जजमानों) के सहारे अपनी कला बचाई: मांगणियारों के लिए राजपूत और लंगाओं के लिए सिंधी-सिपाही (मुस्लिम राजपूत)। इनके गीत संरक्षकों, देवी-देवताओं और लोककथाओं की प्रशंसा करते हैं और हिंदू-मुस्लिम परंपराओं को जोड़ते हैं; अन्य विकल्प संरक्षण, लोक-तत्व या वाद्यों को नकारते हैं।


संबंधित परीक्षा-तथ्य
1. ये थार मरुस्थल के बाड़मेर–जैसलमेर क्षेत्र में केंद्रित हैं।
2. मांगणियारों का प्रमुख गज-वाद्य कमायचा है, जो आम की लकड़ी और बकरी की खाल से बनता है।
3. लकड़ी के दो टुकड़ों वाला खड़ताल ताल देता है।
4. लोकविद् कोमल कोठारी ने 1970 के दशक के अंत से इन्हें व्यापक मंच दिलाने में सहायता की।

questions.topic: Static GK: Music and Musical Instruments

question.en: The padams of Kshetrayya are known for which of the following features? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: क्षेत्रय्या के पादम निम्नलिखित में से किस विशेषता के लिए प्रसिद्ध हैं? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

3.hi: श्रृंगार रस, नायिका-नायक भाव के साथ

4.hi: केवल संस्कृत के प्रयोग तक सीमित रहकर

solution.en:
Kshetrayya perfected the Telugu padam, in which devotion to Krishna is expressed through sringara rasa — the devotee as the nayika longing for the Lord as the nayaka (madhura bhakti). His padams are neither abstract philosophy nor Sanskrit compositions.


Related exam facts
1. His signature (mudra) is “Muvva Gopala”, the Krishna of his village Muvva (Movva), Andhra Pradesh.
2. He lived in the 17th century; his original name is given as Varadayya.
3. His padams are central to abhinaya in Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi.
4. He is associated with the courts of Nayaka rulers such as Tirumala Nayaka and Vijayaraghava Nayaka.
solution.hi:
क्षेत्रय्या ने तेलुगु पदम को परिपूर्ण किया, जिसमें कृष्ण-भक्ति श्रृंगार रस से व्यक्त होती है — भक्त नायिका और प्रभु नायक (मधुर भक्ति)। उनके पदम न तो अमूर्त दर्शन हैं और न संस्कृत रचनाएँ।


संबंधित परीक्षा-तथ्य
1. उनकी मुद्रा (हस्ताक्षर) “मुव्व गोपाल” है — आंध्र प्रदेश के उनके गाँव मुव्वा (मोव्वा) के कृष्ण।
2. वे 17वीं शताब्दी में हुए; उनका मूल नाम वरदय्या बताया जाता है।
3. उनके पदम भरतनाट्यम और कुचिपुड़ी के अभिनय का केंद्रीय अंग हैं।
4. वे तिरुमला नायक और विजयराघव नायक जैसे नायक शासकों के दरबार से जुड़े थे।

question.en: Who is the young Indian chess prodigy that recently defeated World No.1 Magnus Carlsen in a classical game, signaling a generational shift in world chess? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]
question.hi: वह युवा भारतीय शतरंज प्रतिभा कौन है जिसने हाल ही में विश्व नंबर 1 मैग्नस कार्लसन को एक शास्त्रीय मुकाबले में हराया, जिससे विश्व शतरंज में पीढ़ीगत बदलाव का संकेत मिला? [SSC Steno 09/09/26 Shift 1]

solution.en:
R. Praggnanandhaa beat world No. 1 Magnus Carlsen in classical chess for the first time at Norway Chess 2024 (Stavanger), a result widely seen as a sign of India’s rising generation.


Related exam facts
1. Praggnanandhaa was runner-up to Carlsen at the 2023 FIDE World Cup in Baku.
2. D. Gukesh became the youngest undisputed World Champion by beating Ding Liren in Singapore in December 2024; he also defeated Carlsen in classical chess at Norway Chess 2025.
3. Praggnanandhaa won the Tata Steel Masters 2025 after a tiebreak against Gukesh.
4. Divya Deshmukh won the 2025 FIDE Women’s World Cup, beating Koneru Humpy in the final.


Latest verified updates
• Divya Deshmukh won the FIDE Women's World Cup 2025 at Batumi (Georgia), beating Koneru Humpy in the tie-break final; she is India's 4th woman Grandmaster and earned a 2026 Candidates berth.
• D. Gukesh beat Magnus Carlsen in a classical game for the first time at Norway Chess 2025 (Stavanger, 1 June 2025).
solution.hi:
आर. प्रज्ञानानंदा ने नॉर्वे शतरंज 2024 (स्टावेंजर) में विश्व नंबर 1 मैग्नस कार्लसन को क्लासिकल शतरंज में पहली बार हराया; इसे भारत की उभरती पीढ़ी के संकेत के रूप में देखा गया।


संबंधित परीक्षा-तथ्य
1. प्रज्ञानानंदा बाकू में 2023 FIDE विश्व कप में कार्लसन के बाद उपविजेता रहे।
